import html
from io import StringIO

from csv2md.table import Table


def _render_markdown_cell(cell):
    """Approximate the relevant markdown table escaping rules."""
    rendered = []
    index = 0

    while index < len(cell):
        if (
            cell[index] == "\\"
            and index + 1 < len(cell)
            and cell[index + 1] in ("\\", "|")
        ):
            rendered.append(cell[index + 1])
            index += 2
        else:
            rendered.append(cell[index])
            index += 1

    return html.unescape("".join(rendered))


def _render_markdown_row(line):
    """Split a markdown row only at pipes that are actual delimiters."""
    assert line.startswith("| ")
    assert line.endswith(" |")

    content = line[2:-2]
    cells = []
    start = 0

    for index, character in enumerate(content):
        if character != "|":
            continue

        preceding_backslashes = 0
        cursor = index - 1
        while cursor >= 0 and content[cursor] == "\\":
            preceding_backslashes += 1
            cursor -= 1

        # A pipe with an odd number of preceding backslashes is escaped.
        if preceding_backslashes % 2 == 0:
            cells.append(_render_markdown_cell(content[start:index].strip()))
            start = index + 1

    cells.append(_render_markdown_cell(content[start:].strip()))
    return cells


def test_markdown_escapes_unescaped_pipe_in_csv_cell():
    table = Table.parse_csv(StringIO('"name","value"\n"test|with|pipes","baz"\n'))

    lines = table.markdown().splitlines()

    assert r"test\|with\|pipes" in lines[2]
    assert _render_markdown_row(lines[2]) == ["test|with|pipes", "baz"]


def test_markdown_preserves_backslashes_while_escaping_pipe_delimiters():
    # A CSV value can contain literal backslashes before a pipe. Markdown must
    # preserve those backslashes while ensuring the pipe remains escaped; an
    # even run of backslashes immediately before a pipe would expose it as a
    # table delimiter.
    csv_data = (
        '"left","right"\n'
        r'"one\|slash","value"' + "\n"
        r'"two\\|slashes","value"' + "\n"
        '"html|entity","value"\n'
    )

    lines = Table.parse_csv(StringIO(csv_data)).markdown().splitlines()

    assert _render_markdown_row(lines[2]) == [r"one\|slash", "value"]
    assert _render_markdown_row(lines[3]) == [r"two\\|slashes", "value"]
    assert _render_markdown_row(lines[4]) == ["html|entity", "value"]

import pytest

from parsel import Selector


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("encoding", "body", "expected_title"),
    [
        (
            "b'utf8'",
            b"<html><head><title>caf\xc3\xa9</title></head></html>",
            "café",
        ),
        (
            'b"utf8"',
            b"<html><head><title>caf\xc3\xa9</title></head></html>",
            "café",
        ),
        (
            "b'latin-1'",
            b"<html><head><title>ol\xe1</title></head></html>",
            "olá",
        ),
        (
            'b"latin-1"',
            b"<html><head><title>ol\xe1</title></head></html>",
            "olá",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_css_selection_accepts_stringified_bytes_encoding(
    encoding, body, expected_title
):
    """lxml must receive the actual encoding name, not a bytes repr."""
    selector = Selector(body=body, encoding=encoding)

    assert selector.css("title::text").get() == expected_title


def test_invalid_stringified_bytes_encoding_is_not_silently_replaced():
    """Only a valid encoding contained in a bytes repr may be normalized."""
    with pytest.raises(LookupError):
        Selector(
            body=b"<html><head><title>Example</title></head></html>",
            encoding="b'not-a-real-encoding'",
        )

import pytest

import add_trailing_comma


def _rewrite_once_and_assert_idempotent(tmp_path, source, expected):
    filename = tmp_path / 'example.py'
    filename.write_text(source, encoding='UTF-8')

    # The complete trailing-comma result must be produced on this first pass.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 1
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected

    # The output of that first pass must already be stable.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 0
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
        (
            "f(x='long'\n"
            "    'literal')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    x='long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  # the literals are still implicitly concatenated\n"
            "  'literal')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    # the literals are still implicitly concatenated\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicit_string_call_argument_is_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path, source, expected,
):
    _rewrite_once_and_assert_idempotent(tmp_path, source, expected)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        (
            "callbacks[0]('long'\n"
            "             'literal')\n",
            "callbacks[0](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
        (
            "get_callback()('long'\n"
            "               'literal')\n",
            "get_callback()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicit_string_argument_for_any_callable_is_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path, source, expected,
):
    # Valid Python call targets are not restricted to bare names.  The AST
    # represents these exactly as calls, so they need the same single-pass
    # formatting behavior.
    _rewrite_once_and_assert_idempotent(tmp_path, source, expected)

import pytest

from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture
def store(tmp_path):
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        # Include nesting so filtering is also checked during recursive listing.
        levels={"objects": (0, 1)},
    )
    store.create()
    with store:
        yield store
    store.destroy()


def test_list_separates_normal_and_soft_deleted_items_and_preserves_suffix(store):
    names_to_delete = ["objects/delete-flat", "objects/delete-nested"]
    normal_names = ["objects/keep-flat", "objects/keep-nested"]

    for name in names_to_delete + normal_names:
        store.store(name, name.encode())

    for name in names_to_delete:
        store.move(name, delete=True)

    normal_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=False))
    deleted_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=True))

    normal_result_names = {item.name for item in normal_items}
    deleted_result_names = {item.name for item in deleted_items}

    # False must not expose soft-deleted objects.
    assert normal_result_names == {"keep-flat", "keep-nested"}
    assert all(not item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for item in normal_items)

    # True must not include normal objects, and it must retain the suffix so
    # callers can identify returned objects as soft-deleted.
    assert deleted_result_names == {"delete-flat.del", "delete-nested.del"}
    assert all(item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for item in deleted_items)


def test_list_handles_names_that_contain_del_without_being_soft_deleted(store):
    # Only the exact suffix denotes soft deletion. A normal name which merely
    # contains ".del" must remain in the normal listing.
    store.store("objects/report.del.backup", b"normal")
    store.store("objects/removed", b"deleted")
    store.move("objects/removed", delete=True)

    assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == [
        "report.del.backup"
    ]
    assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)] == [
        "removed.del"
    ]


def test_list_existing_empty_namespace_has_no_normal_or_deleted_objects(store):
    # Establish the namespace through the public Store API, then remove its
    # only object. Listing an existing namespace with no objects should yield
    # no objects for either filter value.
    store.store("objects/temporary", b"value")
    store.delete("objects/temporary")

    assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=False)) == []
    assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=True)) == []

        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template_path)],

def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_check_without_reason(tmp_path):
    """CloudFormation resources should honor the documented skip-comment syntax."""
    template = tmp_path / "suppressed_security_group.yaml"
    template.write_text(
        """
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
  SecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SSH access is intentionally managed elsewhere
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""".lstrip()
    )

    report = _run_cloudformation_template(template, ["CKV_AWS_24"])

    assert not report.failed_checks
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SecurityGroup"


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_with_reason_is_scoped_to_its_resource(tmp_path):
    """
    A directive immediately above one CloudFormation resource suppresses that
    resource only, preserves its reason, and must not suppress a subsequent
    resource that has no directive.
    """
    template = tmp_path / "scoped_suppression.yaml"
    template.write_text(
        """
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is required by this legacy host
  SuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Deliberately allows SSH
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: This resource has no suppression
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""".lstrip()
    )

    report = _run_cloudformation_template(template, ["CKV_AWS_24"])

    assert {
        (record.resource, record.check_id) for record in report.skipped_checks
    } == {("AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SuppressedSecurityGroup", "CKV_AWS_24")}
    assert {
        (record.resource, record.check_id) for record in report.failed_checks
    } == {("AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.UnsuppressedSecurityGroup", "CKV_AWS_24")}
    assert (
        report.skipped_checks[0].check_result["suppress_comment"]
        == " SSH access is required by this legacy host"
    )

def test_event_set_outside_async_context_is_immediately_observable() -> None:
    """
    Event.set() must work when neither an async library nor an asyncio event loop is
    currently running (the use case from the issue report).
    """
    event = anyio.Event()

    assert event.is_set() is False
    assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

    event.set()

    assert event.is_set() is True
    assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

    # Setting an already-set event is part of normal Event semantics and must not
    # reintroduce a dependency on an active async context.
    event.set()
    assert event.is_set() is True

from pathlib import Path

from setuptools_scm import Configuration
from setuptools_scm.version import format_version, meta


def test_qualified_scheme_names_import_source_tree_modules(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Qualified scheme names must work without an installed entry point."""
    package_name = f"source_only_scheme_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    package = tmp_path / package_name
    package.mkdir()

    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """
            def version_scheme(version):
                assert version.distance == 3
                return "4.5.6.dev3"

            def local_scheme(version):
                assert version.node == "deadbeef"
                return "+source-tree"
            """
        )
    )

    # This mirrors a source checkout during a build: it is importable from the
    # source tree, but is not installed and cannot provide an entry point.
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme=f"{package_name}.versioning.version_scheme",
        local_scheme=f"{package_name}.versioning.local_scheme",
    )
    version = meta(
        tag="4.5.6",
        distance=3,
        node="deadbeef",
        dirty=False,
        config=config,
    )

    assert (
        format_version(
            version,
            version_scheme=config.version_scheme,
            local_scheme=config.local_scheme,
        )
        == "4.5.6.dev3+source-tree"
    )


@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("git") is None, reason="git is required for SCM integration")
def test_pyproject_qualified_scheme_works_before_project_is_installed(tmp_path):
    """A pyproject-qualified function must work while building from its source tree."""
    project = tmp_path / "project"
    project.mkdir()
    package = project / "uninstalled_demo"
    package.mkdir()

    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """
            def source_tree_version(version):
                # A distinctive value proves that this source-tree function,
                # rather than an installed entry point, was called.
                return "9.8.7.dev42"

            def source_tree_local(version):
                return "+built-from-source"
            """
        )
    )

    # The SCM configuration is intentionally outside setup.py, matching the
    # reported chicken-and-egg scenario.
    (project / "setup.py").write_text("from setuptools import setup\nsetup()\n")
    (project / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """
            [build-system]
            requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools_scm"]
            build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

            [project]
            name = "uninstalled-qualified-scheme-demo"
            dynamic = ["version"]

            [tool.setuptools_scm]
            version_scheme = "uninstalled_demo.versioning.source_tree_version"
            local_scheme = "uninstalled_demo.versioning.source_tree_local"
            """
        )
    )

    def git(*args):
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args],
            cwd=project,
            check=True,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
        )

    git("init")
    git("config", "user.email", "tests@example.invalid")
    git("config", "user.name", "Test User")
    git("add", ".")
    git("commit", "-m", "initial")
    git("tag", "v1.0.0")

    # Make this checkout's setuptools_scm importable, but do not install the
    # temporary project itself. Its qualified function must still be found.
    source_root = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "src")
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = (
        source_root
        if not env.get("PYTHONPATH")
        else source_root + os.pathsep + env["PYTHONPATH"]
    )
    env.pop("SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION", None)

    completed = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "setup.py", "--version"],
        cwd=project,
        env=env,
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )

    # setuptools normalizes local-version separators for PEP 440 metadata.
    assert "9.8.7.dev42+built.from.source" in completed.stdout

"""Regression tests for upload-safe multi-base charm artifact names."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from zipfile import ZipFile

from charmcraft.services import package


def _package_service(
    project_dir: Path, platform_name: str
) -> package.PackageService:
    """Create the small portion of a package service needed to pack a charm."""
    service = object.__new__(package.PackageService)
    service._platform = platform_name
    service._project = SimpleNamespace(name="mysql-router-k8s", type="charm")
    service.project_dir = project_dir
    return service


def test_multibase_charm_artifacts_are_upload_safe_and_distinct(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch
) -> None:
    """Multi-base platforms must not put ':' in artifact names or overwrite each other."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(package.emit, "progress", lambda *_args, **_kwargs: None)

    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    destination = tmp_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    platforms = (
        "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
        "ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
    )
    artifacts = [
        _package_service(tmp_path, platform_name).pack(prime_dir, destination)[0]
        for platform_name in platforms
    ]

    # Both platforms from a multi-base recipe must produce separate artifacts.
    assert len({artifact.name for artifact in artifacts}) == len(platforms)

    for artifact, platform_name in zip(artifacts, platforms):
        architecture = platform_name.rsplit(":", 1)[1]

        assert artifact.parent == destination
        assert artifact.suffix == ".charm"
        assert ":" not in artifact.name
        assert architecture in artifact.stem
        assert artifact.is_file()

        # Confirm that the returned upload-safe path is the path that was actually packed.
        with ZipFile(artifact) as charm_archive:
            assert charm_archive.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

    # The package list consumed by downstream automation must also contain safe names.
    recorded_names = (tmp_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text().splitlines()
    assert recorded_names == [artifact.name for artifact in artifacts]
    assert all(":" not in name for name in recorded_names)

class RecordingClient:
    def __init__(self):
        self.calls = []

    def values_get(self, spreadsheet_id, range_name, params=None):
        self.calls.append(("values_get", spreadsheet_id, range_name, params))
        return {
            "range": range_name,
            "majorDimension": "ROWS",
            "values": [["value"]],
        }

    def values_batch_get(self, spreadsheet_id, ranges, params=None):
        self.calls.append(("values_batch_get", spreadsheet_id, ranges, params))
        return {
            "valueRanges": [
                {
                    "range": range_name,
                    "majorDimension": "ROWS",
                    "values": [["value"]],
                }
                for range_name in ranges
            ]
        }

    def values_update(self, spreadsheet_id, range_name, params=None, body=None):
        self.calls.append(
            ("values_update", spreadsheet_id, range_name, params, body)
        )
        return {"updatedRange": range_name}

    def values_batch_update(self, spreadsheet_id, body=None):
        self.calls.append(("values_batch_update", spreadsheet_id, body))
        return {"totalUpdatedCells": 1}


@pytest.fixture
def worksheet():
    client = RecordingClient()
    sheet = Worksheet(
        "spreadsheet-id",
        client,
        {
            "sheetId": 123,
            "title": "Sheet1",
            "index": 0,
            "gridProperties": {"rowCount": 100, "columnCount": 26},
        },
    )
    return sheet, client

"""Regression tests for filtering soft-deleted objects in Store.list."""

from borgstore.store import Store


def test_list_separates_live_and_soft_deleted_items(tmp_path):
    """The two values of ``deleted`` must return disjoint object sets."""
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={"objects": [0]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            store.store("objects/live-a", b"live-a")
            store.store("objects/deleted-a", b"deleted-a")
            store.store("objects/live-b", b"live-b")
            store.store("objects/deleted-b", b"deleted-b")

            store.move("objects/deleted-a", delete=True)
            store.move("objects/deleted-b", delete=True)

            # The default remains the normal, non-deleted view.
            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects")] == ["live-a", "live-b"]
            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == [
                "live-a",
                "live-b",
            ]

            # Deleted objects are the only objects in the deleted view, and
            # retain their suffix so callers can identify their status.
            deleted_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=True))
            assert [item.name for item in deleted_items] == [
                "deleted-a.del",
                "deleted-b.del",
            ]
            assert all(item.name.endswith(".del") for item in deleted_items)
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def test_list_deleted_filter_works_for_recursively_nested_items(tmp_path):
    """The filter must also be passed through Store.list's directory recursion."""
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={"objects": [1]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            # Different first bytes ensure these objects are in different
            # nesting directories and thus exercise recursive listing.
            store.store("objects/00000000", b"live")
            store.store("objects/ff000000", b"deleted")
            store.move("objects/ff000000", delete=True)

            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == [
                "00000000"
            ]
            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)] == [
                "ff000000.del"
            ]
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def test_list_handles_namespace_containing_only_soft_deleted_items(tmp_path):
    """A fully deleted namespace has no live results and restores on undelete."""
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={"objects": [0]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            store.store("objects/only-item", b"value")
            store.move("objects/only-item", delete=True)

            assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=False)) == []
            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)] == [
                "only-item.del"
            ]

            store.move("objects/only-item", undelete=True)

            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == [
                "only-item"
            ]
            assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=True)) == []
    finally:
        store.destroy()

import time
import warnings

import nltk


def test_unknown_numeric_characters_do_not_modify_configured_vowels():
    """Numbers are treated as temporary vowels, not permanently added to state."""
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()
    configured_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for token in ("99", "123", "007", "42", "9876543210"):
            syllables = tokenizer.tokenize(token)

            # Syllabification must never lose or alter input characters.
            assert "".join(syllables) == token
            # The source of the performance regression was mutation here.
            assert tokenizer.vowels == configured_vowels

    # Repeated processing must likewise leave tokenizer configuration unchanged.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for _ in range(100):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")

    assert tokenizer.vowels == configured_vowels


def test_unknown_characters_are_temporary_for_custom_hierarchies_too():
    """The fix must not merely special-case the default English hierarchy."""
    hierarchy = ["a", "lmnrw", "zvsf", "bcdgtkpqxhj"]
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer(sonority_hierarchy=hierarchy)
    configured_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        for token in ("11", "a1a", "12-34"):
            assert "".join(tokenizer.tokenize(token)) == token

    assert tokenizer.vowels == configured_vowels


def test_repeated_numbers_have_bounded_runtime():
    """
    Repeated numeric tokens must not get progressively slower.

    The former implementation appended every unknown digit to ``vowels``.
    Validation then built an increasingly large regular expression on every
    call, making this loop quadratic.  The limit is deliberately generous for
    slow CI workers while the fixed implementation should complete far below it.
    """
    tokenizer = nltk.SyllableTokenizer()
    iterations = 1500

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        started = time.perf_counter()
        results = [tokenizer.tokenize("99") for _ in range(iterations)]
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started

    assert results == [["99"]] * iterations
    assert tokenizer.vowels == "aeiouy"
    assert elapsed < 3.0, (
        f"Tokenizing {iterations} numeric tokens took {elapsed:.3f}s; "
        "numeric tokenization appears to have quadratic growth."
    )

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def _log_to_tty_like_sink(*, no_color=None, colorize_argument=None, loguru_colorize=None):
    """Run in a fresh interpreter so Loguru's environment defaults are reloaded."""
    if colorize_argument is None:
        add_call = 'logger.add(TtySink(), format="<red>{message}</red>")'
    else:
        add_call = (
            'logger.add(TtySink(), format="<red>{message}</red>", '
            "colorize=%s)" % colorize_argument
        )

    code = """
import sys
from loguru import logger


class TtySink:
    def write(self, message):
        sys.stdout.write(str(message))

    def flush(self):
        sys.stdout.flush()

    def isatty(self):
        return True


logger.remove()
%s
logger.info("colored message")
""" % add_call

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.pop("NO_COLOR", None)
    env.pop("LOGURU_COLORIZE", None)

    if no_color is not None:
        env["NO_COLOR"] = no_color
    if loguru_colorize is not None:
        env["LOGURU_COLORIZE"] = loguru_colorize

    pythonpath = env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(ROOT) + (os.pathsep + pythonpath if pythonpath else "")

    return subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        cwd=str(ROOT),
        env=env,
        check=True,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
    ).stdout


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "0", "false", "any non-empty value"])
def test_non_empty_no_color_disables_automatic_ansi_output(value):
    output = _log_to_tty_like_sink(no_color=value)

    # NO_COLOR is enabled by its non-empty presence, not by boolean parsing.
    assert "colored message" in output
    assert "\x1b[" not in output


def test_empty_no_color_does_not_disable_automatic_ansi_output():
    output = _log_to_tty_like_sink(no_color="")

    # https://no-color.org/: an empty NO_COLOR value must be ignored.
    assert "\x1b[" in output


def test_explicit_colorize_argument_overrides_no_color():
    output = _log_to_tty_like_sink(no_color="1", colorize_argument="True")

    # Explicit per-sink color configuration takes precedence over NO_COLOR.
    assert "\x1b[" in output


def test_explicit_loguru_colorize_configuration_overrides_no_color():
    output = _log_to_tty_like_sink(no_color="1", loguru_colorize="true")

    # LOGURU_COLORIZE is Loguru's explicit user configuration and must take
    # precedence over the generic NO_COLOR default.
    assert "\x1b[" in output

import pytest

from ucumvert import PintUcumRegistry


@pytest.fixture
def ureg():
    return PintUcumRegistry()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ucum_code", "reference_code", "expected_scale"),
    [
        # Reported cases: the prefix belongs to [IU], not to a separate meter.
        ("m[IU]/L", "[IU]/L", 1e-3),
        ("k[IU]/L", "[IU]/L", 1e3),
        # Prefix handling must not be limited to just milli and kilo.
        ("u[IU]/L", "[IU]/L", 1e-6),
        # A prefixed special unit must also work outside a compound expression.
        ("m[IU]", "[IU]", 1e-3),
        # Prefixes in both numerator and denominator retain their independent
        # meanings: milli-IU per milli-liter equals IU per liter.
        ("m[IU]/mL", "[IU]/L", 1.0),
    ],
)
def test_prefixed_international_units_have_correct_dimension_and_scale(
    ureg, ucum_code, reference_code, expected_scale
):
    converted = ureg.from_ucum(ucum_code)
    reference = ureg.from_ucum(reference_code)

    # In particular, m[IU]/L must be compatible with [IU]/L.  The old
    # interpretation, meter * international_unit / liter, is not.
    converted_in_reference_units = converted.to(reference.units)

    ratio = converted_in_reference_units / reference
    assert ratio.to("").magnitude == pytest.approx(expected_scale)

import logging
import re
from types import SimpleNamespace

from requests.structures import CaseInsensitiveDict

from google.cloud.storage.blob import Blob
from google.cloud.storage.bucket import Bucket
from google.cloud.storage import transfer_manager


class _RawResponse:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self._data = data

    def stream(self, chunk_size, decode_content=False):
        yield self._data


class _DownloadResponse:
    def __init__(self, data, start, end, total_size):
        self.status_code = 206
        self.headers = CaseInsensitiveDict(
            {
                "content-range": f"bytes {start}-{end}/{total_size}",
                "content-length": str(len(data)),
            }
        )
        self.raw = _RawResponse(data)


def test_download_chunks_concurrently_does_not_log_missing_checksum_per_range(
    tmp_path, caplog
):
    """Concurrent ranged downloads must not validate a whole-object checksum.

    Composite objects do not return an MD5 checksum.  A concurrent download
    consists of byte ranges, for which a whole-object checksum is not usable,
    so this API must disable checksum validation rather than logging the
    missing-checksum message once per range.
    """
    object_contents = b"abcdefghij"
    requested_ranges = []

    def request(*args, **kwargs):
        headers = kwargs.get("headers")
        if headers is None and len(args) >= 3:
            headers = args[2]

        range_header = next(
            value for key, value in headers.items() if key.lower() == "range"
        )
        match = re.fullmatch(r"bytes=(\d+)-(\d+)", range_header)
        assert match, "parallel workers should request bounded byte ranges"

        start, end = map(int, match.groups())
        requested_ranges.append((start, end))
        return _DownloadResponse(
            object_contents[start : end + 1],
            start,
            end,
            len(object_contents),
        )

    client = SimpleNamespace(
        project="test-project",
        _http=SimpleNamespace(request=request),
        _connection=SimpleNamespace(user_agent="test-agent"),
        _extra_headers={},
    )
    bucket = Bucket(client, "test-bucket")
    blob = Blob("composite-object", bucket)
    blob._properties = {
        "size": str(len(object_contents)),
        "generation": "1",
    }
    blob._get_download_url = lambda *args, **kwargs: "https://example.invalid/media"

    destination = tmp_path / "downloaded-object"

    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="google.resumable_media._helpers")
    transfer_manager.download_chunks_concurrently(
        blob,
        str(destination),
        chunk_size=4,
        max_workers=2,
        worker_type=transfer_manager.THREAD,
    )

    assert destination.read_bytes() == object_contents
    assert sorted(requested_ranges) == [(0, 3), (4, 7), (8, 9)]
    assert not [
        record
        for record in caplog.records
        if record.name == "google.resumable_media._helpers"
        and "checksum was returned from the service while downloading"
        in record.getMessage()
    ]

from textual.app import App
from textual.widget import Widget


@pytest.mark.asyncio
@pytest.mark.parametrize("position", ["before", "after"])
async def test_move_child_relative_to_itself_is_a_noop(position: str) -> None:
    """Moving a child before or after the same child leaves the order unchanged."""
    children = [Widget(id=f"child-{number}") for number in range(5)]
    parent = Widget(*children)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(parent)

        original_nodes = list(parent._nodes)
        child = children[2]

        parent.move_child(child, **{position: child})

        assert list(parent._nodes) == original_nodes
        assert child.parent is parent


@pytest.mark.asyncio
@pytest.mark.parametrize("position", ["before", "after"])
async def test_move_child_index_relative_to_itself_is_a_noop(position: str) -> None:
    """The no-op applies when both references identify the same indexed child."""
    children = [Widget(id=f"child-{number}") for number in range(3)]
    parent = Widget(*children)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(parent)

        original_nodes = list(parent._nodes)

        parent.move_child(1, **{position: 1})

        assert list(parent._nodes) == original_nodes

        assert children[1] in parent._nodes

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def _expected_shifted_masks(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: tuple[int, int], resolution_wh: tuple[int, int]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Translate masks by (dx, dy), clipping pixels outside the output canvas."""
    width, height = resolution_wh
    dx, dy = offset
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for mask_index, y, x in zip(*np.where(masks)):
        shifted_x = x + dx
        shifted_y = y + dy
        if 0 <= shifted_x < width and 0 <= shifted_y < height:
            expected[mask_index, shifted_y, shifted_x] = True

    return expected


def test_move_masks_supports_negative_offsets_for_multiple_masks() -> None:
    masks = np.zeros((2, 4, 5), dtype=bool)
    masks[0, 0, 1] = True
    masks[0, 1, 3] = True
    masks[0, 3, 4] = True
    masks[1, 1, 0] = True
    masks[1, 2, 2] = True
    masks[1, 3, 3] = True

    offset = (-2, -1)
    resolution_wh = (5, 4)

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.array(offset, dtype=np.int32),
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = _expected_shifted_masks(masks, offset, resolution_wh)

    assert result.dtype == np.bool_
    assert result.shape == (2, 4, 5)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)

import subprocess

import pytest

from streamlink_cli import output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    (
        "",
        "A title with spaces",
        """An O'Reilly "quoted" title""",
        "--a-title-that-looks-like-an-option",
    ),
)
def test_mpv_title_is_a_single_unquoted_equals_option_on_posix(monkeypatch, title):
    """
    mpv requires --title=value syntax for a double-dash option.

    PlayerOutput passes an argv list to subprocess on POSIX, so shell quoting
    must not be embedded in the argv value. Otherwise quote characters become
    part of the title displayed by mpv.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", False)

    output = PlayerOutput("/usr/bin/mpv", title=title, quiet=False)

    assert output._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title={0}".format(title),
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_on_windows_command_line(monkeypatch):
    """
    Windows needs command-line quoting for subprocess, but that quoting belongs
    to list2cmdline, not in the value supplied to mpv's --title option.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", True)

    title = """An O'Reilly "quoted" title"""
    output = PlayerOutput("/usr/bin/mpv", title=title, quiet=False)

    expected_argv = ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title={0}".format(title), "-"]
    assert output._create_arguments() == subprocess.list2cmdline(expected_argv)

"""Regression tests for filtering soft-deleted objects in Store.list."""

from borgstore.store import Store

from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend


def test_list_separates_live_and_soft_deleted_items_and_preserves_marker(tmp_path):
    """The deleted flag selects exactly one state and deleted names stay identifiable."""
    store = Store(
        backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path),
        levels={"flat/": [0], "nested/": [1]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            # Exercise both direct and recursively nested backend listings.
            store.store("flat/live", b"live")
            store.store("flat/removed", b"removed")
            store.move("flat/removed", delete=True)

            store.store("nested/01000000", b"nested-live")
            store.store("nested/02000000", b"nested-removed")
            store.move("nested/02000000", delete=True)

            flat_live = list(store.list("flat", deleted=False))
            flat_deleted = list(store.list("flat", deleted=True))
            nested_live = list(store.list("nested", deleted=False))
            nested_deleted = list(store.list("nested", deleted=True))

            assert [item.name for item in flat_live] == ["live"]
            assert [item.name for item in flat_deleted] == ["removed.del"]

            assert [item.name for item in nested_live] == ["01000000"]
            assert [item.name for item in nested_deleted] == ["02000000.del"]

            # Listing deleted entries must not normalize away the marker: consumers
            # need to be able to tell their state from the returned ItemInfo.
            for item in flat_live + nested_live:
                assert not item.name.endswith(".del")
                assert item.directory is False
            for item in flat_deleted + nested_deleted:
                assert item.name.endswith(".del")
                assert item.directory is False
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def test_list_returns_empty_for_the_nonmatching_deletion_state(tmp_path):
    """A namespace containing only one state must not leak into the other list."""
    store = Store(
        backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path),
        levels={"objects/": [0]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            store.store("objects/only-deleted", b"value")
            store.move("objects/only-deleted", delete=True)

            assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=False)) == []
            deleted_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=True))
            assert [item.name for item in deleted_items] == ["only-deleted.del"]

            store.move("objects/only-deleted", undelete=True)

            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=False)] == [
                "only-deleted"
            ]
            assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=True)) == []
    finally:
        store.destroy()

from __future__ import absolute_import
from __future__ import unicode_literals

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "obj.format_message('long'\n"
            "                   'literal')",
            "obj.format_message(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # A function call's callable may be an expression rather than a bare
        # name.  The implicitly concatenated strings are still one argument.
        (
            "get_formatter()('long'\n"
            "                'literal')",
            "get_formatter()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicit_string_call_is_fixed_in_one_pass(src, expected):
    ret = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)

    assert ret == expected
    # The trailing comma must be produced during the same invocation that
    # unhugs the call, rather than requiring a second formatter run.
    assert _fix_src(ret, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_parenthesized_expression_after_name_on_prior_line_is_not_a_call():
    # The newline terminates the `func` expression.  The parentheses begin a
    # separate parenthesized string expression, not an invocation; adding a
    # comma would change that expression into a tuple.
    src = (
        'func\n'
        '(\n'
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal'\n"
        ')'
    )

    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == src

import sys
import uuid
from pathlib import Path

from setuptools_scm import Configuration
from setuptools_scm.version import format_version, meta


def _version(tag, distance, config):
    return meta(
        tag=tag,
        distance=distance,
        node="abcdef1234567890",
        dirty=False,
        config=config,
    )


def test_pyproject_qualified_version_scheme_loads_from_uninstalled_source_tree(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """A project must be able to import its own scheme before it is installed.

    This models a flat-layout project being built from its checkout: the
    project's source root is importable, but there is no installed distribution
    or project entry point yet.
    """
    package = f"source_project_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    package_dir = tmp_path / package
    package_dir.mkdir()

    (package_dir / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package_dir / "versioning.py").write_text(
        """
def from_source_tree(version):
    # Deliberately use both values supplied by setuptools_scm so that this is
    # demonstrably the project's callable, not an entry point with the same
    # name.
    return "{}.from_source{}".format(version.tag, version.distance)
""".strip()
    )

    qualified_name = f"{package}.versioning.from_source_tree"
    pyproject = tmp_path / "pyproject.toml"
    pyproject.write_text(
        f"""
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools_scm"]

[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_scheme = "{qualified_name}"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"
""".strip()
    )

    # A build backend runs while the checkout is available on sys.path.  Do not
    # import the project package ourselves: resolving the configured qualified
    # name is the behavior under test.
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
    for name in list(sys.modules):
        if name == package or name.startswith(package + "."):
            del sys.modules[name]

    config = Configuration.from_file(str(pyproject))

    assert config.version_scheme == qualified_name
    rendered = format_version(
        _version("2.5.0", 7, config),
        version_scheme=config.version_scheme,
        local_scheme=config.local_scheme,
    )

    assert rendered == "2.5.0.from_source7"


def test_qualified_scheme_does_not_replace_existing_entry_point_schemes():
    """Existing short entry-point names remain valid configuration values."""
    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme="guess-next-dev",
        local_scheme="no-local-version",
    )

    rendered = format_version(
        _version("1.0.0", 3, config),
        version_scheme=config.version_scheme,
        local_scheme=config.local_scheme,
    )

    assert rendered == "1.0.1.dev3"

from __future__ import annotations

import tomlkit
import pytest

from pdm.core import Core


def _make_project(tmp_path, pyproject_content: str):
    (tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(pyproject_content, encoding="utf-8")
    return Core().create_project(tmp_path)


def _add_dev_requirement(project, group: str, requirement: str) -> None:
    dependencies, setter = project.use_pyproject_dependencies(group, dev=True)
    setter([*dependencies, requirement])
    project.pyproject.write()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("target_group", ["dev", "lint"])
def test_adding_dev_dependency_does_not_duplicate_legacy_editable_groups(tmp_path, target_group):
    """Legacy groups containing editables must remain outside PEP 735 groups."""
    project = _make_project(
        tmp_path,
        """
[project]
name = "demo"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.8"
dependencies = []

[dependency-groups]
existing = ["coverage"]

[tool.pdm.dev-dependencies]
editable-only = [
    "-e ./packages/editable-only",
]
mixed = [
    "-e ./packages/editable-and-normal",
    "pytest>=8",
]
""",
    )

    _add_dev_requirement(project, target_group, "ruff")

    data = tomlkit.parse((tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    dependency_groups = data["dependency-groups"]
    legacy_groups = data["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"]

    # The requested group must receive the new requirement. In particular, a
    # group from the legacy table must not replace the requested group name.
    assert list(dependency_groups[target_group]) == ["ruff"]

    # Existing PEP 735 groups are retained, but legacy groups with editable
    # requirements must not be duplicated in dependency-groups at all.
    assert list(dependency_groups["existing"]) == ["coverage"]
    assert "editable-only" not in dependency_groups
    assert "mixed" not in dependency_groups

    # The source legacy table is unchanged.
    assert list(legacy_groups["editable-only"]) == ["-e ./packages/editable-only"]
    assert list(legacy_groups["mixed"]) == [
        "-e ./packages/editable-and-normal",
        "pytest>=8",
    ]

[tool.pdm.dev-dependencies]

]

import io
import re
import sys

import pytest

from loguru import logger


@pytest.mark.parametrize("diagnose", [False, True])
def test_recursion_error_traceback_compacts_repeated_recursive_frames(diagnose):
    # ``depth`` intentionally changes in every frame. With diagnosis enabled,
    # the rendered value annotations therefore differ, but frames from the same
    # recursive call site must still be recognized as repeated.
    def recurse(depth):
        return recurse(depth + 1)

    stream = io.StringIO()
    handler_id = logger.add(
        stream,
        format="{message}",
        colorize=False,
        backtrace=False,
        diagnose=diagnose,
    )

    old_recursion_limit = sys.getrecursionlimit()
    had_traceback_limit = hasattr(sys, "tracebacklimit")
    old_traceback_limit = getattr(sys, "tracebacklimit", None)

    frame_depth = 0
    frame = sys._getframe()
    while frame is not None:
        frame_depth += 1
        frame = frame.f_back

    try:
        # Keep the test fast, while producing sufficiently many frames for
        # traceback repetition formatting.
        sys.setrecursionlimit(frame_depth + 80)
        sys.tracebacklimit = 10000

        try:
            recurse(0)
        except RecursionError:
            recursive_frame_count = 0
            traceback = sys.exc_info()[2]

            while traceback is not None:
                if traceback.tb_frame.f_code is recurse.__code__:
                    recursive_frame_count += 1
                traceback = traceback.tb_next

            logger.exception("Oups")
    finally:
        logger.remove(handler_id)
        sys.setrecursionlimit(old_recursion_limit)
        if had_traceback_limit:
            sys.tracebacklimit = old_traceback_limit
        else:
            del sys.tracebacklimit

    output = stream.getvalue()
    recursive_headers = re.findall(
        r'^  File ".*", line \d+, in recurse$',
        output,
        flags=re.MULTILINE,
    )

    assert recursive_frame_count > 3
    assert "Traceback (most recent call last):" in output
    assert "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded" in output

    # Retain the first three instances and replace all following occurrences
    # of the same recursive call site with Python's standard summary line.
    assert len(recursive_headers) == 3
    assert (
        "  [Previous line repeated {} more times]".format(recursive_frame_count - 3)
        in output
    )

import typing

import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError, create_model
from pydantic.dataclasses import dataclass
from shapely import LineString, MultiLineString, MultiPoint, MultiPolygon, Point, Polygon

from pydantic_shapely import GeometryField

Annotated = typing.Annotated


def test_pydantic_dataclass_accepts_polygons_for_multipolygon_field():
    """The reported use case: component geometries can build a MultiPolygon."""
    polygon_with_hole = Polygon(
        shell=((0, 0), (0, 4), (4, 4), (4, 0), (0, 0)),
        holes=[((1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 2), (2, 1), (1, 1))],
    )
    second_polygon = Polygon(((10, 10), (10, 11), (11, 11), (10, 10)))

    @dataclass
    class Shape:
        polys: Annotated[MultiPolygon, GeometryField()]

    value = Shape(polys=[polygon_with_hole, second_polygon])

    assert isinstance(value.polys, MultiPolygon)
    assert value.polys.equals_exact(
        MultiPolygon([polygon_with_hole, second_polygon]), tolerance=0
    )
    assert len(value.polys.geoms[0].interiors) == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("multi_type", "parts"),
    [
        (
            MultiPolygon,
            [
                Polygon(((0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (0, 0))),
                Polygon(((2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3), (2, 2))),
            ],
        ),
        (MultiPoint, [Point(0, 0), Point(1, 2)]),
        (
            MultiLineString,
            [
                LineString(((0, 0), (1, 1))),
                LineString(((2, 2), (3, 4))),
            ],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_component_geometry_lists_build_the_corresponding_multi_geometry(
    multi_type, parts
):
    """All Shapely Multi* geometries should accept their component geometries."""
    model = create_model(
        f"{multi_type.__name__}Container",
        geometry=(Annotated[multi_type, GeometryField()], ...),
    )

    value = model(geometry=parts)

    assert type(value.geometry) is multi_type
    assert value.geometry.equals_exact(multi_type(parts), tolerance=0)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("multi_type", [MultiPolygon, MultiPoint, MultiLineString])
def test_empty_component_list_builds_an_empty_multi_geometry(multi_type):
    model = create_model(
        f"Empty{multi_type.__name__}Container",
        geometry=(Annotated[multi_type, GeometryField()], ...),
    )

    value = model(geometry=[])

    assert type(value.geometry) is multi_type
    assert value.geometry.is_empty


def test_list_created_multipolygon_still_obeys_z_value_configuration():
    polygon_3d = Polygon(
        ((0, 0, 7), (0, 1, 7), (1, 1, 7), (0, 0, 7)),
    )
    model = create_model(
        "TwoDimensionalMultiPolygon",
        geometry=(Annotated[MultiPolygon, GeometryField(z_values="strip")], ...),
    )

    value = model(geometry=[polygon_3d])

    assert isinstance(value.geometry, MultiPolygon)
    assert not value.geometry.has_z
    assert value.geometry.equals_exact(
        MultiPolygon([Polygon(((0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (0, 0)))]),
        tolerance=0,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("multi_type", "invalid_parts"),
    [
        (MultiPolygon, [Polygon(((0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (0, 0))), Point(1, 1)]),
        (MultiPoint, [Point(0, 0), LineString(((0, 0), (1, 1)))]),
        (MultiLineString, [LineString(((0, 0), (1, 1))), Point(1, 1)]),
    ],
)
def test_component_lists_must_match_the_requested_multi_geometry(
    multi_type, invalid_parts
):
    model = create_model(
        f"Invalid{multi_type.__name__}Container",
        geometry=(Annotated[multi_type, GeometryField()], ...),
    )

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        model(geometry=invalid_parts)

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _run_cloudformation_template(tmp_path, content, checks):
    template = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template.write_text(content)

    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=checks),
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_only_annotated_resource(tmp_path):
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is intentionally allowed
  SuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SSH access is intentionally allowed
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: This resource must still be checked
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""",
        ["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1

    skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
    failed = report.failed_checks[0]

    assert skipped.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert skipped.resource.endswith(".SuppressedSecurityGroup")
    assert skipped.check_result["suppress_comment"] == (
        " SSH access is intentionally allowed"
    )

    assert failed.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert failed.resource.endswith(".UnsuppressedSecurityGroup")


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_with_empty_reason_matches_issue_example(tmp_path):
    """A trailing colon with no explanation is the documented issue's syntax."""
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
  SecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Security group from the issue example
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""",
        ["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert report.failed_checks == []
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource.endswith(".SecurityGroup")


def test_cloudformation_resource_can_suppress_each_of_multiple_checks(tmp_path):
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is required for this test instance
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_25: RDP access is required for this test instance
  OpenManagementSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Management access security group
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 3389
          ToPort: 3389
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""",
        ["CKV_AWS_24", "CKV_AWS_25"],
    )

    assert report.failed_checks == []
    assert {record.check_id for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "CKV_AWS_24",
        "CKV_AWS_25",
    }
    assert all(
        record.resource.endswith(".OpenManagementSecurityGroup")
        for record in report.skipped_checks
    )

    suppress_comments = {
        record.check_id: record.check_result["suppress_comment"]
        for record in report.skipped_checks
    }
    assert suppress_comments == {
        "CKV_AWS_24": " SSH access is required for this test instance",
        "CKV_AWS_25": " RDP access is required for this test instance",
    }

"""Regression tests for filtering soft-deleted objects in Store.list."""

import pytest

from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.mark.parametrize("level", [0, 1])
def test_list_separates_live_and_soft_deleted_items(tmp_path, level):
    """Both flat and recursively nested listings must apply the same filter."""
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={"objects": [level]},
    )
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            live_keys = ["00000002", "00000004"]
            deleted_keys = ["00000001", "00000003"]

            for key in live_keys + deleted_keys:
                store.store(f"objects/{key}", key.encode())

            for key in deleted_keys:
                store.move(f"objects/{key}", delete=True)

            live_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=False))
            deleted_items = list(store.list("objects", deleted=True))

            # False must exclude every soft-deleted object.
            assert [item.name for item in live_items] == live_keys

            # True must exclude every live object and retain the suffix which
            # identifies the returned objects as soft-deleted.
            assert [item.name for item in deleted_items] == [
                key + DEL_SUFFIX for key in deleted_keys
            ]
            assert all(item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX) for item in deleted_items)

            # The two modes must be disjoint even when both kinds coexist.
            assert {item.name for item in live_items}.isdisjoint(
                item.name for item in deleted_items
            )
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def test_list_handles_namespaces_containing_only_soft_deleted_items(tmp_path):
    store = Store(url=f"file://{tmp_path}", levels={"objects": [0]})
    store.create()

    try:
        with store:
            keys = ["first", "second"]
            for key in keys:
                store.store(f"objects/{key}", b"value")
                store.move(f"objects/{key}", delete=True)

            assert list(store.list("objects", deleted=False)) == []
            assert [item.name for item in store.list("objects", deleted=True)] == [
                key + DEL_SUFFIX for key in keys
            ]
    finally:
        store.destroy()

import pytest

from parsel import Selector


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("encoding", "body", "expected_title"),
    [
        (
            "b'utf8'",
            b"<html><head><title>Snowman \xe2\x98\x83</title></head></html>",
            "Snowman \u2603",
        ),
        (
            "b'latin1'",
            b"<html><head><title>caf\xe9</title></head></html>",
            "café",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_css_selection_accepts_stringified_byte_encoding_name(
    encoding: str, body: bytes, expected_title: str
) -> None:
    """An encoding represented as ``str(bytes_encoding)`` must be usable by lxml."""
    selector = Selector(body=body, encoding=encoding)

    assert selector.css("title").get() == f"<title>{expected_title}</title>"
    assert selector.css("title::text").get() == expected_title

import time
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_unknown_numeric_characters_do_not_mutate_vowel_configuration():
    """Numbers are unknown phonemes, but must not become permanent vowels."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    configured_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        first_result = tokenizer.tokenize("0123456789")
        second_result = tokenizer.tokenize("0123456789")
        tokenizer.tokenize("99")
        tokenizer.tokenize("1234567890")

    # Unknown characters may be treated as vowels for one token, but the
    # tokenizer's configured hierarchy must remain reusable and unchanged.
    assert tokenizer.vowels == configured_vowels
    assert first_result == second_result
    assert "".join(first_result) == "0123456789"

    # Normal syllabification must still use the original English inventory.
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]


def test_repeated_number_tokenization_remains_fast_and_does_not_accumulate_state():
    """Repeated numeric tokens must not exhibit the former quadratic slowdown."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    configured_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    # The old implementation appended both digits to ``self.vowels`` on every
    # call.  That made the regex used for validation grow on every iteration.
    iterations = 1500
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(iterations):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    assert tokenizer.vowels == configured_vowels

    # A correct implementation takes only a small fraction of a second here;
    # the reported buggy implementation takes several seconds at this scale and
    # continues getting slower as the loop proceeds.
    assert elapsed < 2.0, (
        f"tokenizing a short number {iterations} times took {elapsed:.3f}s; "
        "numeric tokenization appears to retain the quadratic slowdown"
    )

_fixture_key = f"fixture-isolation:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"


@pytest.fixture
def fake_redis_client():
    return fakeredis.FakeRedis()


def test_a_function_scoped_default_client_stores_data(fake_redis_client):
    """The first pytest case can write to its own default client."""
    assert fake_redis_client.get(_fixture_key) is None
    assert fake_redis_client.set(_fixture_key, "written-by-test-a")
    assert fake_redis_client.get(_fixture_key) == b"written-by-test-a"


def test_b_function_scoped_default_client_starts_empty(fake_redis_client):
    """A new default client in a later pytest case must not see test A's data."""
    assert fake_redis_client.get(_fixture_key) is None


def test_separately_constructed_default_clients_are_isolated():
    """Isolation must hold even while both independent clients still exist."""
    key = f"default-client-isolation:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()

    first_client.set(key, "first")

    assert first_client.get(key) == b"first"
    assert second_client.get(key) is None


def test_clients_with_an_explicit_same_host_and_port_still_share_state():
    """Default isolation must not remove intentional endpoint-based sharing."""
    host = f"explicit-host-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    key = f"explicit-host-key:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host=host, port=6379)
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host=host, port=6379)

    first_client.set(key, "shared")

    assert second_client.get(key) == b"shared"


def test_clients_given_the_same_explicit_server_still_share_state():
    """Providing FakeServer remains an explicit way to share a fake Redis."""
    server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    key = f"explicit-server-key:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)

    first_client.set(key, "shared")

    assert second_client.get(key) == b"shared"

import asyncio
from contextlib import contextmanager

import anyio
import pytest

from anyio._backends import _asyncio as asyncio_backend


@pytest.fixture
def anyio_backend():
    return "asyncio"


@contextmanager
def _simulate_current_task_not_matching_asyncio_task(monkeypatch):
    """
    Simulate the reported condition where current_task() returns the native
    _asyncio.Task while asyncio.Task refers to the pure-Python Task class.

    This distinction exists on CPython versions exposing asyncio.tasks._PyTask
    and is relevant because AnyIO stores state for the task returned by
    current_task().
    """
    python_task_type = getattr(asyncio.tasks, "_PyTask", None)
    native_task_type = getattr(__import__("_asyncio"), "Task", None)
    task = asyncio.current_task()

    if python_task_type is None or native_task_type is None or task is None:
        pytest.skip("this Python version does not expose both Task implementations")

    if not isinstance(task, native_task_type) or isinstance(task, python_task_type):
        pytest.skip("the running loop does not use a native _asyncio.Task")

    # asyncio is a module object, so patching this reproduces the incompatible
    # Task facade used by TaskStateStore's runtime type check.
    with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
        patch.setattr(asyncio_backend.asyncio, "Task", python_task_type)
        yield


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_native_current_task_supports_checkpoint_and_effective_deadline(
    monkeypatch,
):
    with anyio.CancelScope(deadline=anyio.current_time() + 60) as scope:
        with _simulate_current_task_not_matching_asyncio_task(monkeypatch):
            await anyio.lowlevel.checkpoint_if_cancelled()
            assert anyio.current_effective_deadline() == scope.deadline


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_native_current_task_checkpoint_detects_cancellation(monkeypatch):
    with anyio.CancelScope() as scope:

            scope.cancel()
            with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await anyio.lowlevel.checkpoint_if_cancelled()

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from typing import Any

from anyio import Event, run


def _set_event_without_current_asyncio_loop(event: Event) -> None:
    """
    Simulate the outside-async-context state of a freshly started Python 3.12 process,
    where asyncio does not provide an implicit current loop.
    """
    original_policy = asyncio.get_event_loop_policy()
    try:
        asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.DefaultEventLoopPolicy())
        asyncio.set_event_loop(None)
        event.set()
    finally:
        asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(original_policy)


def test_event_set_works_outside_an_async_event_loop() -> None:
    event = Event()

    assert not event.is_set()
    assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

    _set_event_without_current_asyncio_loop(event)

    assert event.is_set()
    assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

    # Like native event implementations, repeated set() calls are harmless.
    _set_event_without_current_asyncio_loop(event)
    assert event.is_set()


def test_event_set_outside_loop_can_be_waited_on_later(
    anyio_backend_name: str, anyio_backend_options: dict[str, Any]
) -> None:
    """
    Since an Event created and set outside async code has no selected backend yet, its
    signalled state must remain usable when it is later consumed by an AnyIO backend.
    """
    event = Event()
    _set_event_without_current_asyncio_loop(event)

    async def use_event() -> None:
        assert event.is_set()
        await event.wait()
        assert event.is_set()
        assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

    run(use_event, backend=anyio_backend_name, backend_options=anyio_backend_options)

"""Regression tests for safe multi-base charm artifact names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import zipfile

from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


def test_pack_multi_base_charm_uses_github_artifact_safe_filenames(
    tmp_path: pathlib.Path, service_factory
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not put ':' in produced charm filenames.

    GitHub Actions artifacts and GitHub releases reject filenames containing a
    colon. Each platform must still produce its own, distinguishable artifact.
    """
    project_dir = tmp_path / "project"
    project_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")
    destination = tmp_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    platform_labels = (
        "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
        "ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
    )
    charm = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A multi-base charm",
            "description": "A charm used to test package filenames.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {label: None for label in platform_labels},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    packages = []
    for platform_label, architecture in zip(
        platform_labels, ("amd64", "arm64"), strict=True
    ):
        build_plan = [
            BuildInfo(
                platform=platform_label,
                build_on=architecture,
                build_for=architecture,
                base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
            )
        ]
        package_service = services.PackageService(
            app=APP_METADATA,
            project=charm,
            services=service_factory,
            project_dir=project_dir,
            build_plan=build_plan,
        )

        created = package_service.pack(prime_dir, destination)

        assert len(created) == 1
        package = created[0]
        packages.append(package)

        assert package.exists()
        assert package.suffix == ".charm"
        assert ":" not in package.name
        assert "ubuntu" in package.name
        assert "22.04" in package.name
        assert architecture in package.name
        assert not (destination / f"multi-base-charm_{platform_label}.charm").exists()

        with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as archive:
            assert archive.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

    assert len(set(packages)) == 2

    recorded_packages = (
        project_dir / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    ).read_text().splitlines()
    assert set(recorded_packages) == {package.name for package in packages}
    assert all(":" not in package_name for package_name in recorded_packages)

"""Regression tests for failures reported by ``charmcraft publish-lib``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from craft_cli.errors import CraftError

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands


LIBRARY_ID = "123e4567-e89b-42d3-a456-426614174000"


class _PublishedRevision:
    """A previously published revision newer than the local library."""

    api = 0
    patch = 100
    revision = 100
    library_id = LIBRARY_ID
    lib_id = LIBRARY_ID
    name = "example"

    def __bool__(self):
        return True

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter((self,))

    def __len__(self):
        return 1

    def __getitem__(self, _key):
        return self

    def __getattr__(self, _name):
        return self

    def get(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
        return self


class _StoreWithStaleLibrary:
    """Fake Charmhub store where the submitted LIBPATCH is stale."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.published_revision = _PublishedRevision()
        self.create_called = False

    def create_library_revision(self, *_args, **_kwargs):
        self.create_called = True
        raise AssertionError("A stale library revision must not be published")

    def __getattr__(self, _name):
        # publish-lib queries existing revisions before creating a new one.
        # Return a collection containing a revision whose patch is newer than
        # the local LIBPATCH, irrespective of the precise lookup method used.
        def lookup(*_args, **_kwargs):
            return [self.published_revision]

        return lookup


def _publish_args(command: store_commands.PublishLibCommand, library_path):
    """Build arguments from the command's public parser."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    command.fill_parser(parser)

    library_action = next(
        (
            action
            for action in parser._actions
            if action.dest in {"library", "libraries", "lib", "libs"}
        ),
        None,
    )

    argv = []
    if library_action is not None:
        if library_action.option_strings:
            argv = [library_action.option_strings[0], str(library_path)]
        else:
            argv = [str(library_path)]

    return parser.parse_args(argv)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
def test_publish_lib_fails_when_libpatch_is_not_bumped(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, output_format
):
    """A rejected library publication must produce a non-successful command."""
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "example" / "v0" / "example.py"
    library_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library_path.write_text(
        f'''"""Example charm library."""

LIBID = "{LIBRARY_ID}"
LIBAPI = 0
LIBPATCH = 1
'''
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    fake_store = _StoreWithStaleLibrary()
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", lambda *_args, **_kwargs: fake_store)

    command = object.__new__(store_commands.PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = SimpleNamespace(
        store=fake_store,
        # publish-lib obtains the charm name from the project before it
        # analyses the library.  Supplying it avoids requiring charmcraft.yaml
        # and matches normal command execution for a named project.
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="example"),
    )
    parsed_args = _publish_args(command, library_path)
    parsed_args.format = output_format

    try:
        result = command.run(parsed_args)
    except CraftError:
        # CraftError is translated by the command framework into a non-zero
        # process exit code.
        result = None
    else:
        assert result not in (None, 0), (
            "publish-lib reported an invalid/stale LIBPATCH but exited "
            "successfully"
        )

    assert not fake_store.create_called

    """A project-local qualified scheme must work during setuptools version lookup.

    No entry point is declared and the project is deliberately not installed.  This
    mirrors the build/install chicken-and-egg case: setuptools_scm must import the
    function from the source tree while evaluating ``pyproject.toml``.
    """
    if shutil.which("git") is None:
        pytest.skip("git is required to create SCM metadata for this integration test")

    project = tmp_path / "project"
    package = project / "uninstalled_demo_pkg"
    package.mkdir(parents=True)

    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        """
def source_tree_scheme(version):
    # Make both use of this function and the SCM distance observable.
    assert version.distance == 1
    return "42.0.%d" % version.distance
""".lstrip()
    )

    # There is intentionally no use_scm_version/version_scheme in setup.py and no
    # entry-point declaration.  The only configuration is the pyproject table.
    (project / "setup.py").write_text(
        "from setuptools import setup\n\nsetup()\n"
    )
    (project / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        """
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools", "setuptools_scm"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "uninstalled-qualified-scheme-demo"
dynamic = ["version"]

[tool.setuptools_scm]
version_scheme = "uninstalled_demo_pkg.versioning.source_tree_scheme"
local_scheme = "no-local-version"
""".lstrip()
    )
    (project / "README.md").write_text("initial\n")

    git_env = os.environ.copy()
    git_env.update(
        {
            "GIT_AUTHOR_NAME": "Test User",
            "GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL": "test@example.invalid",
            "GIT_COMMITTER_NAME": "Test User",
            "GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL": "test@example.invalid",
        }
    )
    _run(["git", "init", "-q"], project, git_env)
    _run(["git", "add", "."], project, git_env)
    _run(["git", "commit", "-qm", "initial"], project, git_env)
    _run(["git", "tag", "1.0.0"], project, git_env)

    # One commit after the tag gives the scheme a deterministic nonzero distance.
    (project / "README.md").write_text("one commit after tag\n")
    _run(["git", "add", "README.md"], project, git_env)
    _run(["git", "commit", "-qm", "after tag"], project, git_env)

    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(
        filter(None, [str(repo_root / "src"), env.get("PYTHONPATH")])
    )

    result = _run([sys.executable, "setup.py", "--version"], project, env)

    # setup.py asks setuptools_scm for the version before this project could have
    # been installed.  A pre-fix implementation only looks for an entry point and
    # therefore cannot find this project-local function.
    assert result.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1] == "42.0.1"

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from loguru._colorama import should_colorize


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


class TtyStream:
    def isatty(self):
        return True


SCRIPT = r"""
from loguru import logger


class TtySink:
    def __init__(self):
        self.output = []

    def isatty(self):
        return True

    def write(self, message):
        self.output.append(str(message))

    def flush(self):
        pass


sink = TtySink()
logger.remove()
logger.add(sink, format="<red>{message}</red>", colorize=COLORIZE_ARGUMENT)
logger.info("message")

print("colored" if "\x1b[" in "".join(sink.output) else "plain")
"""


def run_loguru(*, no_color=None, colorize_argument="None", loguru_colorize=None):
    environment = os.environ.copy()
    environment.pop("NO_COLOR", None)
    environment.pop("LOGURU_COLORIZE", None)
    environment["LOGURU_AUTOINIT"] = "true"
    environment["LOGURU_LEVEL"] = "TRACE"

    if no_color is not None:
        environment["NO_COLOR"] = no_color
    if loguru_colorize is not None:
        environment["LOGURU_COLORIZE"] = loguru_colorize

    completed = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", SCRIPT.replace("COLORIZE_ARGUMENT", colorize_argument)],
        cwd=str(ROOT),
        env=environment,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return completed.stdout.strip()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "0", "false", "any non-empty value"])
def test_non_empty_no_color_disables_automatic_tty_colors(value):
    """Every non-empty NO_COLOR value disables automatically selected ANSI colors."""
    assert run_loguru(no_color=value) == "plain"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "0", "false", "any non-empty value"])
def test_non_empty_no_color_disables_color_detection(monkeypatch, value):
    """NO_COLOR also applies to Loguru's stream color-detection behavior."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("NO_COLOR", value)
    assert should_colorize(TtyStream()) is False


def test_empty_no_color_does_not_disable_automatic_tty_colors(monkeypatch):
    """The no-color.org specification explicitly excludes an empty value."""
    monkeypatch.setenv("NO_COLOR", "")

    assert should_colorize(TtyStream()) is True
    assert run_loguru(no_color="") == "colored"


def test_explicit_colorize_true_overrides_no_color():
    """A per-sink explicit color choice takes precedence over NO_COLOR."""
    assert run_loguru(no_color="1", colorize_argument="True") == "colored"


def test_explicit_loguru_colorize_default_overrides_no_color():
    """Explicit Loguru default configuration is a user-level color preference."""
    assert run_loguru(no_color="1", loguru_colorize="true") == "colored"
