import numpy as np
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose

from nilearn.regions import HierarchicalKMeans


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_uses_samples_by_features_convention():
    """Fit, transform, and inverse_transform operate on feature columns."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    X_train = rng.randn(9, 6)
    X_test = rng.randn(4, 6)

    estimator = HierarchicalKMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=0)
    estimator.fit(X_train)

    # There must be one cluster assignment for each input feature, not sample.
    assert estimator.labels_.shape == (X_train.shape[1],)

    X_reduced = estimator.transform(X_test)
    assert X_reduced.shape == (X_test.shape[0], estimator.n_clusters)

    # Reduction is the mean of the feature columns belonging to each cluster.
    expected_reduced = np.column_stack(
        [
            X_test[:, estimator.labels_ == label].mean(axis=1)
            for label in range(estimator.n_clusters)
        ]
    )
    assert_allclose(X_reduced, expected_reduced)

    X_restored = estimator.inverse_transform(X_reduced)
    assert X_restored.shape == X_test.shape
    assert_allclose(X_restored, X_reduced[:, estimator.labels_])


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_cluster_limit_is_number_of_features():
    """More clusters than samples is valid when enough features are present."""
    # This deliberately has fewer samples than requested clusters.  The
    # estimator must regard columns as the objects being clustered.
    X = np.array(
        [
            [0.0, 0.1, 10.0, 10.1, 20.0],
            [0.1, 0.0, 10.2, 9.9, 20.1],
            [0.0, 0.2, 9.8, 10.0, 19.9],
        ]
    )

    estimator = HierarchicalKMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=0).fit(X)

    assert estimator.labels_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert estimator.n_clusters == 4
    assert np.unique(estimator.labels_).size == 4

    reduced = estimator.transform(X)
    assert reduced.shape == (X.shape[0], 4)

import pytest

from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture()
def store(tmp_path):
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={
            "flat": [0],
            "nested": [1],
        },
    )
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def list_names(store, namespace, *, deleted):
    return [item.name for item in store.list(namespace, deleted=deleted)]


def test_list_returns_disjoint_normal_and_soft_deleted_populations(store):
    """The flag selects a population; it must not mean "include deleted too"."""
    with store:
        store.store("flat/normal-a", b"normal-a")
        store.store("flat/normal-b", b"normal-b")
        store.store("flat/removed-a", b"removed-a")
        store.store("flat/removed-b", b"removed-b")
        store.move("flat/removed-a", delete=True)
        store.move("flat/removed-b", delete=True)

        normal_names = list_names(store, "flat", deleted=False)
        deleted_names = list_names(store, "flat", deleted=True)

        assert normal_names == ["normal-a", "normal-b"]
        assert deleted_names == ["removed-a.del", "removed-b.del"]

        # The .del suffix is retained so a caller can identify deleted entries.
        assert all(not name.endswith(".del") for name in normal_names)
        assert all(name.endswith(".del") for name in deleted_names)
        assert set(normal_names).isdisjoint(deleted_names)


def test_list_filters_deleted_items_during_recursive_nested_listing(store):
    """Filtering must apply to files reached through nesting directories too."""
    with store:
        store.store("nested/00aa", b"deleted")
        store.store("nested/00bb", b"normal")
        store.store("nested/ffaa", b"also-deleted")
        store.move("nested/00aa", delete=True)
        store.move("nested/ffaa", delete=True)

        assert list_names(store, "nested", deleted=False) == ["00bb"]
        assert set(list_names(store, "nested", deleted=True)) == {
            "00aa.del",
            "ffaa.del",
        }


def test_list_handles_namespaces_containing_only_one_population(store):
    with store:
        store.store("flat/only-deleted", b"value")
        store.move("flat/only-deleted", delete=True)

        assert list_names(store, "flat", deleted=False) == []
        assert list_names(store, "flat", deleted=True) == ["only-deleted.del"]

        store.move("flat/only-deleted", undelete=True)

        assert list_names(store, "flat", deleted=False) == ["only-deleted"]
        assert list_names(store, "flat", deleted=True) == []

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'callee',
    (
        'f',
        'obj.method',
        # Calls can use arbitrary callable expressions, not only a bare name.
        '(f)',
        'callbacks[0]',
    ),
)
def test_adjacent_multiline_string_call_gets_comma_in_one_pass(callee):
    src = "{}('long'\n  'literal')".format(callee)
    expected = "{}(\n    'long'\n    'literal',\n)".format(callee)

    ret = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)

    assert ret == expected
    # This regression must be fully resolved after the first invocation.
    assert _fix_src(ret, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_adjacent_multiline_strings_with_comment_get_comma_in_one_pass():

    expected = (

        "    'long'  # still one implicitly-concatenated argument\n"
        "    'literal',\n"
        ')'

    assert ret == expected
    assert _fix_src(ret, py35_plus=False) == expected

import subprocess

import pytest

from streamlink_cli import output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize("is_win32", [False, True])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "",
        "A title with spaces",
        "Rock 'n' Roll",
        "Title with $property and shell-looking; characters",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_passed_as_unquoted_equals_option(monkeypatch, is_win32, title):
    """
    Recent mpv versions require --title=VALUE, rather than separate --title
    and VALUE arguments. Since Streamlink starts the player without a shell,
    POSIX shell quoting must not become literal content of the title argument.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output_module, "is_win32", is_win32)

    command = "mpv.exe --no-terminal" if is_win32 else "/usr/bin/mpv --no-terminal"
    stream_url = "https://example.com/stream.m3u8"
    player = PlayerOutput(
        command,
        args="--stream={filename}",
        filename=stream_url,
        quiet=False,
        title=title,
    )

    escaped_title = PlayerOutput._mpv_title_escape(title)
    title_option = "--title={0}".format(escaped_title)

    if is_win32:
        # Windows PlayerOutput returns one command-line string. The platform
        # command-line quoting here is solely to preserve title_option as one
        # child-process argv item.
        expected = " ".join([
            command,
            subprocess.list2cmdline([title_option]),
            "--stream={0}".format(stream_url),
        ])
    else:
        expected = [
            "/usr/bin/mpv",
            "--no-terminal",
            title_option,
            "--stream={0}".format(stream_url),
        ]

    assert player._create_arguments() == expected

from typing import Tuple

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def _translated_and_clipped(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: Tuple[int, int], resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the expected result of translating mask pixels within a canvas."""
    dx, dy = offset
    width, height = resolution_wh
    result = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for source_y in range(masks.shape[1]):
        for source_x in range(masks.shape[2]):
            destination_x = source_x + dx
            destination_y = source_y + dy

            if 0 <= destination_x < width and 0 <= destination_y < height:
                result[:, destination_y, destination_x] = masks[
                    :, source_y, source_x
                ]

    return result


@pytest.fixture
def masks() -> np.ndarray:
    return np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, False, True, False],
                [False, True, True, False, False],
                [True, False, True, False, True],
                [False, False, True, True, False],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, False, True],
                [True, False, False, True, False],
                [False, True, True, False, False],
                [True, False, True, False, True],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "offset,resolution_wh",
    [
        # Negative offsets must be accepted and crop pixels at the top/left edge.
        ((-2, -1), (5, 4)),
        # Offsets can be negative in one dimension and positive in the other. Pixels
        # that leave either canvas edge must be cropped without raising.
        ((2, -1), (5, 4)),
        # Cropping must work when the requested output canvas is smaller than the
        # source mask after applying a negative offset.
        ((-1, -1), (2, 2)),
        # Existing positive movement remains supported when the output is larger.
        ((2, 1), (8, 6)),
        # It is valid for a negative movement to move every pixel out of view.
        ((-10, -10), (5, 4)),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_translates_and_clips_masks_in_all_directions(
    masks: np.ndarray,
    offset: Tuple[int, int],
    resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int],
) -> None:
    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.asarray(offset, dtype=np.int32),
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = _translated_and_clipped(
        masks=masks, offset=offset, resolution_wh=resolution_wh
    )

import pytest

import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import MissingRequiredClaimError


SECRET = "secret"


def test_null_audience_is_ignored_when_no_audience_is_requested():
    """A null aud claim must decode exactly like an omitted aud claim."""
    payload = {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")

    assert jwt.decode(token, SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"]) == payload


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "audience",
    [
        "expected-audience",
        ["other-audience", "expected-audience"],
    ],
)
def test_null_audience_behaves_like_omitted_audience_when_audience_is_requested(
    audience,
):
    """A null audience must not be treated as a malformed audience claim.

    Since an omitted aud claim cannot satisfy an explicitly requested audience,
    aud: null must raise the same missing-claim exception.
    """
    absent_audience_token = jwt.encode(
        {"sub": "user-123"}, SECRET, algorithm="HS256"
    )
    null_audience_token = jwt.encode(
        {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}, SECRET, algorithm="HS256"
    )

    for token in (absent_audience_token, null_audience_token):
        with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
            jwt.decode(
                token,
                SECRET,
                algorithms=["HS256"],
                audience=audience,
            )

        assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _run_cloudformation_template(tmp_path, content, checks):
    template = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template.write_text(content)

    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=checks),
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_only_annotated_resource(tmp_path):
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
  SuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: SSH access is intentionally public
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: This resource has no suppression annotation
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""",
        ["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1

    skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
    failed = report.failed_checks[0]

    assert skipped.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert skipped.resource.endswith(".SuppressedSecurityGroup")
    assert failed.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert failed.resource.endswith(".UnsuppressedSecurityGroup")


def test_cloudformation_resource_honors_all_preceding_skip_annotations(tmp_path):
    """Every skip annotation directly above a resource must be passed to its checks."""
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is required for administration
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_25: RDP access is required for administration
  RemoteAccessSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Remote administration security group
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 3389
          ToPort: 3389
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""",
        ["CKV_AWS_24", "CKV_AWS_25"],
    )

    assert not report.failed_checks
    assert {record.check_id for record in report.skipped_checks} == {
        "CKV_AWS_24",
        "CKV_AWS_25",
    }
    assert all(
        record.resource.endswith(".RemoteAccessSecurityGroup")
        for record in report.skipped_checks
    )

import pathlib

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


@pytest.mark.parametrize("architecture", ["amd64", "arm64"])
def test_pack_multibase_charm_artifact_name_has_no_colon(
    new_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    architecture: str,
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not leak ':' into produced artifact names."""
    platform = f"ubuntu@22.04:{architecture}"
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "mysql-router-k8s",
            "summary": "Test charm",
            "description": "Test charm used to verify artifact naming.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {platform: None},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]

    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=new_path,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )

    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, new_path)

    assert len(packages) == 1
    artifact = packages[0]
    assert artifact.is_file()
    assert artifact.suffix == ".charm"
    assert ":" not in artifact.name
    assert "ubuntu@22.04" in artifact.name
    assert architecture in artifact.name

    # Consumers of charmcraft's package output file must receive the safe name too.
    assert (new_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text() == (
        f"{artifact.name}\n"
    )

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def _unescaped_pipe_count(text):
    """Count table delimiter pipes, excluding backslash-escaped pipes."""
    count = 0
    for index, character in enumerate(text):
        if character != "|":
            continue

        preceding_backslashes = 0
        cursor = index - 1
        while cursor >= 0 and text[cursor] == "\\":
            preceding_backslashes += 1
            cursor -= 1

        if preceding_backslashes % 2 == 0:
            count += 1
    return count


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_headers_and_cell_values():
    csv_text = (
        '"head|er","plain"\n'
        '"|leading","trailing|"\n'
        '"many|pipes|inside","ok"\n'
        '"entity|encoded","ok"\n'
    )

    markdown = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_text)).markdown()
    lines = markdown.splitlines()

    # This is a two-column table: each line must contain only the opening,
    # inter-column, and closing structural Markdown pipes.
    assert all(_unescaped_pipe_count(line) == 3 for line in lines)

    # Literal item pipes, including those in headers and at value boundaries,
    # must be represented safely instead of becoming table delimiters.
    assert r"head\|er" in lines[0] or "head|er" in lines[0]
    assert r"\|leading" in lines[2] or "|leading" in lines[2]
    assert r"trailing\|" in lines[2] or "trailing|" in lines[2]
    assert (
        r"many\|pipes\|inside" in lines[3]
        or "many|pipes|inside" in lines[3]
    )

    # Existing HTML entity escaping is already valid Markdown table content.

import time
import warnings

import pytest

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_numeric_unknown_characters_are_temporary_and_do_not_mutate_vowels():
    """Unknown numeric characters must not accumulate in tokenizer state."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="Character not defined"):
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]

    # Tokenization of unknown characters should retain its per-token behavior,
    # while the configured vowel inventory remains the one supplied at creation.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        for token in ("9", "99", "123", "9876543210") * 20:
            syllables = tokenizer.tokenize(token)
            assert "".join(syllables) == token
            assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    assert tokenizer.vowels == "aeiouy"


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_has_bounded_runtime_and_state():
    """Repeated number tokenization must not exhibit the former quadratic slowdown."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    # The pre-fix implementation continually appended "9" to ``vowels``.
    # Besides changing public state, that made the regex used on subsequent
    # calls increasingly expensive.  A correct implementation should handle
    # this many calls comfortably even on slower CI machines.
    iterations = 1500
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        start = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(iterations):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels
    assert elapsed < 2.0, (
        f"{iterations} numeric tokenizations took {elapsed:.3f}s; "
        "numeric input appears to retain quadratic behavior"
    )

import pytest

from borgstore.constants import DEL_SUFFIX
from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture
def store(tmp_path):
    store = Store(
        url=f"file://{tmp_path}",
        levels={"flat/": [0], "nested/": [1]},
    )
    store.create()
    try:
        with store:
            yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def names(store, namespace, *, deleted):
    return [item.name for item in store.list(namespace, deleted=deleted)]


def test_list_partitions_active_and_soft_deleted_items_and_preserves_marker(store):
    # Exercise both ordinary and nested storage; list() must apply the same
    # filtering while recursing into nesting directories.
    store.store("flat/active", b"active")
    store.store("flat/removed", b"removed")
    store.move("flat/removed", delete=True)

    store.store("nested/aa000001", b"active nested")
    store.store("nested/bb000002", b"removed nested")
    store.move("nested/bb000002", delete=True)

    assert names(store, "flat", deleted=False) == ["active"]
    assert names(store, "flat", deleted=True) == [f"removed{DEL_SUFFIX}"]

    assert names(store, "nested", deleted=False) == ["aa000001"]
    assert names(store, "nested", deleted=True) == [f"bb000002{DEL_SUFFIX}"]

    # The deleted result must retain its storage marker.  Otherwise callers
    # cannot distinguish it from an active item with the same logical name.
    deleted_item = next(store.list("flat", deleted=True))
    assert deleted_item.name.endswith(DEL_SUFFIX)
    assert deleted_item.exists
    assert not deleted_item.directory


def test_list_handles_all_deleted_items_and_undelete_without_overlap(store):
    store.store("flat/first", b"1")
    store.store("flat/second", b"2")
    store.move("flat/first", delete=True)
    store.move("flat/second", delete=True)

    # True means deleted-only, rather than active plus deleted.
    assert names(store, "flat", deleted=False) == []
    assert names(store, "flat", deleted=True) == [
        f"first{DEL_SUFFIX}",
        f"second{DEL_SUFFIX}",
    ]

    # Once restored, the object must move back to the active-only listing and
    # must no longer appear in the deleted-only listing.
    store.move("flat/first", undelete=True)

    assert names(store, "flat", deleted=False) == ["first"]
    assert names(store, "flat", deleted=True) == [f"second{DEL_SUFFIX}"]

        holes=[[(1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 2), (2, 1), (1, 1)]],

    second_polygon = Polygon(

    assert len(container.polygons.geoms) == 2
    assert container.polygons.geoms[0] == polygon_with_hole

import pytest

from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
from textual.containers import Container
from textual.widgets import Static


class ChildMovingApp(App):
    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield Container(
            Static("first", id="first"),
            Static("middle", id="middle"),
            Static("last", id="last"),
            id="parent",
        )


@pytest.mark.asyncio
@pytest.mark.parametrize("position", ["before", "after"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("child_id", ["first", "middle", "last"])
async def test_moving_child_before_or_after_itself_is_a_no_op(
    position: str, child_id: str
) -> None:
    """A child may be used as its own relative target without changing order."""
    async with ChildMovingApp().run_test() as pilot:
        parent = pilot.app.query_one("#parent", Container)
        child = parent.query_one(f"#{child_id}", Static)
        original_children = list(parent.children)

        parent.move_child(child, **{position: child})

        assert list(parent.children) == original_children
        assert [widget.id for widget in parent.children] == ["first", "middle", "last"]

import io
import sys

from loguru import logger


def _log_recursive_exception(*, changing_depth):
    stream = io.StringIO()
    sink_id = logger.add(
        stream,
        format="{message}",
        colorize=False,
        backtrace=False,
        diagnose=True,
    )
    previous_limit = sys.getrecursionlimit()

    def recurse(depth):
        if changing_depth:
            recurse(depth + 1)
        else:
            recurse(depth)

    try:
        # Keep the traceback manageable while ensuring it contains enough
        # recursive frames to require traceback compaction.
        sys.setrecursionlimit(100)

        try:
            recurse(0)
        except RecursionError as error:
            traceback = error.__traceback__
            recursive_frames = 0

            while traceback is not None:
                if traceback.tb_frame.f_code is recurse.__code__:
                    recursive_frames += 1
                traceback = traceback.tb_next

            logger.exception("Oups")
    finally:
        sys.setrecursionlimit(previous_limit)
        logger.remove(sink_id)

    return stream.getvalue(), recursive_frames


def test_recursion_error_traceback_compacts_repeated_frames():
    output, recursive_frames = _log_recursive_exception(changing_depth=False)

    assert recursive_frames > 3
    assert "Oups" in output
    assert "Traceback (most recent call last):" in output
    assert "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded" in output

    repeated = "  [Previous line repeated {} more times]\n".format(recursive_frames - 3)
    assert output.count(repeated) == 1

    recursive_locations = [
        line for line in output.splitlines() if ", in recurse" in line
    ]
    assert len(recursive_locations) == 3


def test_recursion_error_compaction_uses_frame_location_not_diagnosed_values():
    # Every recursive frame executes the same source location, but ``depth``
    # has a distinct local value in each frame. Those diagnostic annotations
    # must not prevent the traceback locations from being recognized as
    # repeated frames.
    output, recursive_frames = _log_recursive_exception(changing_depth=True)

    assert recursive_frames > 3
    assert "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded" in output

    repeated = "  [Previous line repeated {} more times]\n".format(recursive_frames - 3)
    assert output.count(repeated) == 1

    recursive_locations = [
        line for line in output.splitlines() if ", in recurse" in line
    ]
    assert len(recursive_locations) == 3

import asyncio
import math

import anyio
import pytest


@pytest.mark.parametrize("operation", ["checkpoint", "deadline"])
def test_native_current_task_is_accepted_when_asyncio_task_is_replaced(
    monkeypatch, operation
):
    """
    A native ``_asyncio.Task`` can remain the current task after an integration
    replaces ``asyncio.Task`` with its pure-Python implementation. AnyIO's task
    state lookup must not reject that current task merely because it is no
    longer an instance of the currently exported ``asyncio.Task`` class.
    """
    python_task_class = getattr(asyncio.tasks, "_PyTask", None)
    if python_task_class is None:
        pytest.skip("This Python implementation has no pure-Python Task class")

    async def native_task() -> None:
        current = asyncio.current_task()
        assert current is not None
        if type(current).__module__ != "_asyncio":
            pytest.skip("The event loop does not create native _asyncio.Task objects")

        with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
            # Simulate libraries such as nest_asyncio replacing asyncio.Task
            # while a native task created before that replacement is running.
            patch.setattr(asyncio, "Task", python_task_class)

            if operation == "checkpoint":
                # An untracked native asyncio task has no cancel scope, so this
                # should simply be a no-op rather than raising AssertionError.
                await anyio.lowlevel.checkpoint_if_cancelled()
            else:
                # Likewise, an untracked task has no deadline.
                assert math.isinf(anyio.current_effective_deadline())

    async def exercise() -> None:
        # The task must be created before asyncio.Task is replaced, so it is a
        # native _asyncio.Task rather than an instance of _PyTask.
        await asyncio.create_task(native_task())

    anyio.run(exercise, backend="asyncio")

"""Regression tests for HierarchicalKMeans input orientation."""

import numpy as np
import pytest
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose

from nilearn.regions import HierarchicalKMeans


def _feature_means(X, labels, n_clusters):
    """Compute the expected feature-wise cluster averages."""
    return np.column_stack(
        [X[:, labels == label].mean(axis=1) for label in range(n_clusters)]
    )


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_uses_sklearn_sample_feature_orientation():
    """A standard (samples, features) matrix must produce feature labels."""
    X = np.array(
        [
            [0.0, 0.1, 10.0, 10.1],
            [1.0, 1.1, 9.0, 9.1],
            [2.0, 2.1, 8.0, 8.1],
            [3.0, 3.1, 7.0, 7.1],
            [4.0, 4.1, 6.0, 6.1],
            [5.0, 5.1, 5.0, 5.1],
            [6.0, 6.1, 4.0, 4.1],
            [7.0, 7.1, 3.0, 3.1],
        ]
    )

    clustering = HierarchicalKMeans(n_clusters=2, random_state=0)
    reduced = clustering.fit_transform(X)

    # Labels describe input features, not input samples.
    assert clustering.labels_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert reduced.shape == (X.shape[0], 2)

    expected_reduced = _feature_means(
        X, clustering.labels_, clustering.n_clusters
    )
    assert_allclose(reduced, expected_reduced)

    # Inverse transformation expands cluster signals along the feature axis.
    assert_allclose(
        clustering.inverse_transform(reduced),
        expected_reduced[:, clustering.labels_],
    )


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_scaling_uses_cluster_axis_for_standard_input():
    """Scaling and inverse scaling must preserve the samples-first layout."""
    X = np.arange(45, dtype=float).reshape(9, 5)

    clustering = HierarchicalKMeans(
        n_clusters=3, random_state=0, scaling=True
    ).fit(X)
    reduced = clustering.transform(X)

    unscaled = _feature_means(X, clustering.labels_, clustering.n_clusters)
    expected_scaled = unscaled * np.sqrt(clustering.sizes_)[np.newaxis, :]

    assert reduced.shape == (X.shape[0], clustering.n_clusters)
    assert_allclose(reduced, expected_scaled)
    assert_allclose(
        clustering.inverse_transform(reduced),
        unscaled[:, clustering.labels_],
    )


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_limits_clusters_by_number_of_features():
    """The feature count, rather than sample count, bounds n_clusters."""
    X = np.arange(27, dtype=float).reshape(9, 3)

    clustering = HierarchicalKMeans(n_clusters=6, random_state=0)
    with pytest.warns(
        UserWarning, match="n_clusters should be at most the number of features"
    ):
        clustering.fit(X)

    assert clustering.n_clusters == X.shape[1]
    assert clustering.labels_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert clustering.transform(X).shape == (X.shape[0], X.shape[1])

import fakeredis


@pytest.fixture()
def fake_redis_client():
    """Match the function-scoped fixture pattern from the reported regression."""
    return fakeredis.FakeRedis()


def test_fixture_client_starts_empty_and_can_write_a(fake_redis_client):
    # This intentionally leaves data behind. A later function-scoped fixture
    # must still receive a completely independent FakeRedis instance.
    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == []

    fake_redis_client.set("ttg-fixture-a", "1")

    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == [b"ttg-fixture-a"]


def test_next_fixture_client_does_not_see_previous_case_data(fake_redis_client):
    # Together with the preceding test, this is the issue's pytest-case
    # reproduction: a newly constructed default FakeRedis must be empty.
    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == []

    fake_redis_client.set("ttg-fixture-b", "1")

    assert fake_redis_client.keys("*") == [b"ttg-fixture-b"]


def test_default_fake_redis_instances_are_isolated_while_both_are_alive():
    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
    key = f"ttg-default-isolation-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    first_client.set(key, "value")

    assert first_client.get(key) == b"value"
    assert second_client.get(key) is None


def test_explicit_same_host_still_intentionally_shares_state():
    # Isolation of implicit/default instances must not discard the established
    # ability to share a fake server by explicitly selecting the same address.
    host = f"ttg-explicit-host-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host=host, port=6379)
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host=host, port=6379)
    key = f"ttg-explicit-host-key-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    try:
        first_client.set(key, "value")

        assert second_client.get(key) == b"value"
    finally:
        first_client.flushdb()


def test_explicit_fake_server_still_shares_state():
    server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    first_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    second_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    key = f"ttg-explicit-server-key-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    first_client.set(key, "value")

    assert second_client.get(key) == b"value"

import pytest


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "prepare",
    [
        "",
        """
        import asyncio
        asyncio.set_event_loop(None)
        """,
    ],
    ids=["fresh_python_process", "no_current_asyncio_loop"],
)
def test_event_set_works_without_an_active_async_context(prepare: str) -> None:
    """
    Event.set() is synchronous and must work outside an async context.

    Run in a separate interpreter so this test exercises the reported "newly
    started Python" use case without a loop or backend leaked by the test suite.
    The second case also verifies that the behavior does not accidentally depend
    on asyncio having created a current (but non-running) loop.
    """
    code = dedent(
        f"""
        from anyio import Event

        {prepare}

        event = Event()
        assert not event.is_set()
        assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

        event.set()

        assert event.is_set()
        assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0
        """
    )

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(
        path for path in (os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "src"), env.get("PYTHONPATH")) if path
    )
    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        cwd=os.getcwd(),
        env=env,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr

"""Regression tests for safe multi-base charm artifact names."""

import pathlib
import zipfile

from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


def test_pack_multibase_charms_uses_colon_free_distinct_artifact_names(
    new_path: pathlib.Path, service_factory
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not make GitHub-incompatible artifact names."""
    platforms = ["ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "ubuntu@22.04:arm64"]
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A test charm",
            "description": "A test charm for multi-base packaging.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {platform: None for platform in platforms},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "test-file").write_text("charm contents")

    destination = new_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    packages = []
    for platform in platforms:
        architecture = platform.rsplit(":", maxsplit=1)[1]
        package_service = services.PackageService(
            app=APP_METADATA,
            project=project,
            services=service_factory,
            project_dir=new_path,
            build_plan=[
                BuildInfo(
                    platform=platform,
                    build_on=architecture,
                    build_for=architecture,
                    base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
                )
            ],
        )

        packages.extend(package_service.pack(prime_dir, destination))

    # Each platform produces an independently uploadable artifact.  In
    # particular, ':' is rejected by GitHub Actions artifact/release uploads.
    assert len(packages) == len(platforms)
    assert len({package.name for package in packages}) == len(platforms)
    assert all(package.parent == destination for package in packages)
    assert all(package.suffix == ".charm" for package in packages)
    assert all(":" not in package.name for package in packages)
    assert all(package.is_file() for package in packages)

    # Ensure the renamed paths are the paths actually used for packed charms,
    # rather than merely names returned by path-generation logic.
    for package in packages:
        assert zipfile.is_zipfile(package)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as charm:
            assert charm.read("test-file") == b"charm contents"

    recorded_packages = (
        new_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    ).read_text().splitlines()
    assert set(recorded_packages) == {package.name for package in packages}
    assert all(":" not in package_name for package_name in recorded_packages)

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from loguru._colorama import should_colorize


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


class TtyStream:
    def isatty(self):
        return True


def colorized_output_with_environment(no_color, *, colorize=None, loguru_colorize=None):
    """Run in a fresh interpreter so import-time Loguru defaults are reloaded."""
    environment = os.environ.copy()

    for key in list(environment):
        if key.startswith("LOGURU_"):
            environment.pop(key)

    environment["LOGURU_AUTOINIT"] = "false"

    if no_color is None:
        environment.pop("NO_COLOR", None)
    else:
        environment["NO_COLOR"] = no_color

    if loguru_colorize is not None:
        environment["LOGURU_COLORIZE"] = loguru_colorize

    environment["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(
        filter(None, (str(ROOT), environment.get("PYTHONPATH")))
    )

    script = f"""
import io

from loguru import logger


class TtyStream(io.StringIO):
    def isatty(self):
        return True


stream = TtyStream()
logger.remove()
logger.add(stream, colorize={colorize!r}, format="<red>{{message}}</red>")
logger.info("message")

print("COLORIZED=" + str("\\x1b[" in stream.getvalue()))
"""

    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", script],
        cwd=str(ROOT),
        env=environment,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    assert result.stdout in ("COLORIZED=True\n", "COLORIZED=False\n")
    return result.stdout == "COLORIZED=True\n"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "0", "false", "anything"])
def test_non_empty_no_color_disables_automatic_colorization(value):
    # no-color.org specifies that every non-empty value disables ANSI output,
    # rather than parsing the variable as a boolean.
    assert colorized_output_with_environment(value) is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "0", "false", "anything"])
def test_non_empty_no_color_disables_tty_detection_immediately(monkeypatch, value):
    # Detection must also honor NO_COLOR when the environment changes after
    # Loguru itself has already been imported.
    monkeypatch.setenv("NO_COLOR", value)
    assert should_colorize(TtyStream()) is False


def test_empty_no_color_does_not_disable_tty_detection(monkeypatch):
    # The convention applies only when NO_COLOR is present *and non-empty*.
    monkeypatch.setenv("NO_COLOR", "")
    assert should_colorize(TtyStream()) is True


def test_empty_no_color_does_not_disable_automatic_colorization():
    assert colorized_output_with_environment("") is True


def test_no_color_absent_keeps_normal_automatic_colorization():
    assert colorized_output_with_environment(None) is True


def test_explicit_colorize_true_overrides_no_color():
    # no-color.org allows explicit per-instance user configuration to override
    # the environment convention.
    assert colorized_output_with_environment("1", colorize=True) is True


def test_loguru_colorize_configuration_overrides_no_color():
    # LOGURU_COLORIZE is Loguru's explicit user configuration for the default
    # colorization behavior, and therefore must take precedence as well.
    assert (
        colorized_output_with_environment(
            "1",
            loguru_colorize="true",
        )
        is True
    )

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _column(statement, name):
    return next(
        column
        for column in statement.find_all(exp.ColumnDef)
        if column.this.name.lower() == name.lower()
    )


def test_mysql_serial_in_create_table_with_primary_key_and_other_columns():
    sql = """
    CREATE TABLE temp
    (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        label VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
    );
    """

    rendered = sqlglot.transpile(
        sql,
        read="mysql",
        write="mysql",
        pretty=True,
        comments=False,
    )

    assert len(rendered) == 1

    # Most importantly, SERIAL must be parsed as a column type rather than
    # causing PRIMARY KEY (or the following column) to be left unparsed.
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(rendered[0], read="mysql")
    id_column = _column(reparsed, "id")
    label_column = _column(reparsed, "label")

    assert label_column.kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR
    assert "PRIMARY KEY" in rendered[0].upper()

    # A MySQL generator may preserve SERIAL or expand its documented alias.
    # In either case, the resulting declaration must retain SERIAL's meaning.
    id_type = id_column.kind.sql(dialect="mysql").upper()
    if id_type == "SERIAL":
        assert "SERIAL" in rendered[0].upper()
    else:
        assert id_type == "BIGINT UNSIGNED"
        upper_sql = rendered[0].upper()
        assert "NOT NULL" in upper_sql
        assert "AUTO_INCREMENT" in upper_sql
        assert "UNIQUE" in upper_sql


def test_mysql_serial_without_explicit_constraints_keeps_mysql_alias_semantics():
    rendered = sqlglot.transpile(
        "CREATE TABLE counters (counter_id serial)",
        read="mysql",
        write="mysql",
        comments=False,
    )[0]

    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, read="mysql")
    column = _column(reparsed, "counter_id")
    column_type = column.kind.sql(dialect="mysql").upper()

    # SERIAL is a MySQL alias for BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE.
    # Keeping the SERIAL spelling is valid; if it is canonicalized, all of the
    # alias's implied properties must be represented in the generated DDL.
    if column_type == "SERIAL":
        assert "SERIAL" in rendered.upper()
    else:
        assert column_type == "BIGINT UNSIGNED"
        upper_sql = rendered.upper()

"""Regression tests for encoding values serialized as byte literals."""

import pytest

from parsel import Selector


@pytest.mark.parametrize("selector_type", ["html", "xml"])
def test_byte_literal_encoding_allows_css_selection(selector_type: str) -> None:
    """A serialized ``b'utf8'`` encoding must be normalized before lxml parses."""
    body = "<html><head><title>Café example</title></head></html>".encode("utf8")

    selector = Selector(body=body, type=selector_type, encoding="b'utf8'")

    assert selector.css("title::text").get() == "Café example"


def test_byte_literal_encoding_is_normalized_on_text_body_path() -> None:
    """The encoding must work on paths which decode the body without lxml."""
    selector = Selector(
        body="Café example".encode("utf8"),
        type="text",
        encoding="b'utf8'",
    )

    assert selector.get() == "Café example"


def test_byte_literal_utf8_encoding_keeps_json_autodetection() -> None:
    """Normalization must occur before behavior which checks for ``utf8``."""
    selector = Selector(
        body='{"title": "Café example"}'.encode("utf8"),
        encoding="b'utf8'",
    )

    assert selector.type == "json"
    assert selector.jmespath("title").get() == "Café example"

"""Regression tests for GNU df binary block-size suffixes."""

import pytest

import jc
from jc.utils import convert_size_to_int


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("suffix", "power"),
    [
        ("k", 1),
        ("K", 1),
        ("m", 2),
        ("M", 2),
        ("g", 3),
        ("G", 3),
        ("t", 4),
        ("T", 4),
        ("p", 5),
        ("P", 5),
        ("e", 6),
        ("E", 6),
        ("z", 7),
        ("Z", 7),
        ("y", 8),
        ("Y", 8),
    ],
)
def test_gnu_df_short_block_size_suffixes_are_binary(suffix, power):
    """GNU df's bare block-size suffixes use powers of 1024."""
    assert convert_size_to_int(f"2{suffix}") == 2 * 1024**power


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("size", "expected"),
    [
        ("2KB", 2_000),
        ("2MB", 2_000_000),
        ("2GB", 2_000_000_000),
        ("2KiB", 2 * 1024),
        ("2MiB", 2 * 1024**2),
        ("2GiB", 2 * 1024**3),
    ],
)
def test_explicit_decimal_and_iec_units_retain_their_meaning(size, expected):
    assert convert_size_to_int(size) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("heading", "size_key", "block_size"),
    [
        ("1K-blocks", "1k_blocks", 1024),
        ("1M-blocks", "1m_blocks", 1024**2),
    ],
)
def test_df_parser_interprets_short_block_heading_as_binary(
    heading, size_key, block_size
):
    """df output must scale block count fields according to GNU suffix rules."""
    data = (
        f"Filesystem     {heading}      Used Available Use% Mounted on\n"
        "/dev/example         17         5        12  30% /example\n"
    )

    parsed = jc.parse("df", data, quiet=True)

    assert parsed == [
        {
            "filesystem": "/dev/example",
            size_key: 17 * block_size,
            "used": 5 * block_size,
            "available": 12 * block_size,
            "use_percent": 30,
            "mounted_on": "/example",
        }
    ]

"""Regression tests for suspect/corrupt copy cleaning."""

from unittest.mock import patch

from alpenhorn.db import ArchiveFile, ArchiveFileCopy, ArchiveAcq, StorageGroup, StorageNode


def test_node_clean_include_bad_marks_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(clidb, cli):
    """The CLI must provide an explicit opt-in for scheduling bad copies."""

    group = StorageGroup.create(name="group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="node", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="acq")

    good_file = ArchiveFile.create(name="good", acq=acq, size_b=1)
    suspect_file = ArchiveFile.create(name="suspect", acq=acq, size_b=1)
    corrupt_file = ArchiveFile.create(name="corrupt", acq=acq, size_b=1)

    good = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node, file=good_file, has_file="Y", wants_file="Y"
    )
    suspect = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node, file=suspect_file, has_file="M", wants_file="Y"
    )
    corrupt = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node, file=corrupt_file, has_file="X", wants_file="Y"
    )

    # Bad copies are deliberately excluded from ordinary cleaning.
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "node", "--force"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(good.id).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "Y"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "Y"

    # Explicitly including bad copies schedules both suspect and corrupt data.
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "node", "--force", "--include-bad"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "M"


def test_node_clean_include_bad_now_releases_bad_copies(clidb, cli):
    """--include-bad works with immediate cleaning as well as deferred cleaning."""

    group = StorageGroup.create(name="group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="node", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="acq")

    suspect = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="suspect", acq=acq, size_b=1),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    corrupt = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="corrupt", acq=acq, size_b=1),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="Y",
    )

    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "node", "--now", "--include-bad", "--force"])

    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "N"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "N"


def test_daemon_deletes_released_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(
    mockgroupandnode, simpleacq, archivefile, archivefilecopy
):
    """Deletion candidates include Y/M/X copies whose wants_file is N."""

    mockio, _, updateable_node = mockgroupandnode

    valid = archivefilecopy(
        node=updateable_node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="valid", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="Y",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    suspect = archivefilecopy(
        node=updateable_node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="suspect", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=updateable_node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="N",
    )

    # A missing DB copy has no local file to remove.
    archivefilecopy(
        node=updateable_node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="missing", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="N",
        wants_file="N",
    )

    updateable_node.update_delete()

    deleted = {
        copy.id
        for delete_call in mockio.node.delete.call_args_list
        for copy in delete_call.args[0]
    }
    assert deleted == {valid.id, suspect.id, corrupt.id}


def test_daemon_skips_check_for_suspect_copy_released_for_deletion(
    mockgroupandnode, simpleacq, archivefile, archivefilecopy
):
    """Suspect copies with wants_file=N are deleted rather than checked."""

    mockio, _, updateable_node = mockgroupandnode
    mockio.node.before_update.return_value = True

    released = archivefilecopy(
        node=updateable_node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="released", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    needs_check = archivefilecopy(
        node=updateable_node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="needs-check", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )

    with (
        patch.object(updateable_node, "update_free_space"),
        patch.object(updateable_node, "update_delete"),
        patch("alpenhorn.daemon.update.auto_import.update_observer"),
        patch("alpenhorn.daemon.update.RemoteNode"),
    ):
        updateable_node.update()

    checked_ids = [call.args[0].id for call in mockio.node.check.call_args_list]
    assert checked_ids == [needs_check.id]
    assert released.id not in checked_ids

from __future__ import absolute_import
from __future__ import unicode_literals

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # The implicit-concatenation argument can contain more than two
        # physical string literals.
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'er'\n"
            "  ' literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'er'\n"
            "    ' literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Comments and blank lines do not prevent adjacent literals from being
        # one implicitly-concatenated argument.
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  # explanation\n"
            "\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    # explanation\n"
            "\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # A call target need not be a bare NAME.  This is still a call with
        # the same multiline implicit-string argument.
        (
            "factory()('long'\n"
            "          'literal')",
            "factory()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "(factory)('long'\n"
            "          'literal')",
            "(factory)(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "factories[0]('long'\n"
            "             'literal')",
            "factories[0](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_call_argument_fixed_in_one_pass(
        src, expected,
):
    ret = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)

    assert ret == expected
    # The required comma must be present after the first pass, making the
    # formatter idempotent rather than requiring the reported second pass.
    assert _fix_src(ret, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_multiline_implicitly_concatenated_string_expression_is_not_a_call():
    src = (
        "value = ('long'\n"
        "         'literal')"
    )
    expected = (
        "value = (\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal'\n"
        ")"
    )

    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == expected

) -> None:
    """Moving any child relative to itself must not alter the child order."""
    children = [Widget() for _ in range(3)]
    parent = Widget(*children)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(parent)

        child = children[position]
        original_children = tuple(parent.children)

        parent.move_child(child, **{placement: child})

        assert tuple(parent.children) == original_children
        assert all(widget.parent is parent for widget in children)

import textwrap

from setuptools_scm import Configuration
from setuptools_scm.version import format_version
from setuptools_scm.version import meta


def test_qualified_version_scheme_loads_from_project_source_before_install(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """A pyproject-style dotted callable name needs no installed entry point."""
    project_source = tmp_path / "source_only_project"
    project_source.mkdir()
    (project_source / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (project_source / "versioning.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """
            def source_tree_scheme(version):
                return "source-%s.dev%s" % (version.tag, version.distance)
            """
        )
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    scheme = "source_only_project.versioning.source_tree_scheme"
    config = Configuration(version_scheme=scheme, local_scheme="no-local-version")
    version = meta(
        tag="2.4.0",
        distance=3,
        node="abcdef",
        dirty=False,
        config=config,
    )

    assert (
        format_version(
            version,
            version_scheme=scheme,
            local_scheme="no-local-version",
        )
        == "source-2.4.0.dev3"
    )


def test_qualified_name_works_for_the_local_scheme_hook_too(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Qualified names are resolved by the common scheme-hook mechanism."""
    project_source = tmp_path / "source_only_local_scheme_project"
    project_source.mkdir()
    (project_source / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (project_source / "versioning.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """
            def version_scheme(version):
                return "5.0.dev%s" % version.distance

            def local_scheme(version):
                return "+from-source-tree"
            """
        )
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    version_scheme = "source_only_local_scheme_project.versioning.version_scheme"
    local_scheme = "source_only_local_scheme_project.versioning.local_scheme"
    config = Configuration(version_scheme=version_scheme, local_scheme=local_scheme)
    version = meta(
        tag="5.0",
        distance=1,
        node="123456",
        dirty=False,
        config=config,
    )

    assert (
        format_version(
            version,
            version_scheme=version_scheme,
            local_scheme=local_scheme,
        )
        == "5.0.dev1+from-source-tree"
    )


def test_existing_entry_point_scheme_names_remain_supported():
    """Adding dotted imports must not stop normal setuptools_scm schemes working."""
    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme="guess-next-dev",
        local_scheme="no-local-version",
    )
    version = meta(
        tag="1.0.0",
        distance=2,
        node="abcdef",
        dirty=False,
        config=config,
    )

    assert (
        format_version(
            version,
            version_scheme="guess-next-dev",
            local_scheme="no-local-version",
        )
        == "1.0.1.dev2"
    )

def _run_template(tmp_path, content, checks):
    template = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template.write_text(content)

    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        external_checks_dir=None,
        files=[str(template)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=checks),
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_only_annotated_resource(tmp_path):
    report = _run_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
Resources:
  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH access is intentionally allowed
  SuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: A deliberately public SSH group
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: This group must still be reported
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 22
          ToPort: 22
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
""",
        ["CKV_AWS_24"],

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"

    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1

import typing

import pytest
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError
from pydantic.dataclasses import dataclass
from shapely import LineString, MultiLineString, MultiPoint, MultiPolygon, Point, Polygon

from pydantic_shapely import GeometryField


def test_pydantic_dataclass_builds_multipolygon_from_polygon_objects():
    """The reported dataclass use case accepts Polygon objects as MultiPolygon parts."""

    @dataclass
    class Model:
        polygons: typing.Annotated[MultiPolygon, GeometryField()]

    polygon_with_hole = Polygon(
        shell=((0, 0), (0, 4), (4, 4), (4, 0)),
        holes=[((1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 2), (2, 1))],
    )
    other_polygon = Polygon(((10, 10), (10, 11), (11, 11), (11, 10)))

    result = Model(polygons=[polygon_with_hole, other_polygon])

    assert isinstance(result.polygons, MultiPolygon)
    assert len(result.polygons.geoms) == 2
    assert result.polygons.geoms[0].equals(polygon_with_hole)
    assert result.polygons.geoms[1].equals(other_polygon)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("multi_type", "component_type", "components"),
    [
        (
            MultiPolygon,
            Polygon,
            [
                Polygon(((0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1), (1, 0))),
                Polygon(((2, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3), (3, 2))),
            ],
        ),
        (
            MultiPoint,
            Point,
            [Point(0, 0), Point(1, 1)],
        ),
        (
            MultiLineString,
            LineString,
            [
                LineString(((0, 0), (1, 1))),
                LineString(((2, 2), (3, 3))),
            ],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_multi_geometry_fields_accept_lists_of_component_geometry_objects(
    multi_type, component_type, components
):
    class Model(BaseModel):
        geometry: typing.Annotated[multi_type, GeometryField()]

    result = Model(geometry=components)

    assert isinstance(result.geometry, multi_type)
    assert len(result.geometry.geoms) == len(components)
    assert all(
        isinstance(component, component_type) for component in result.geometry.geoms
    )
    assert all(
        actual.equals(expected)
        for actual, expected in zip(result.geometry.geoms, components)
    )


def test_component_list_conversion_applies_configured_z_value_processing():
    class Model(BaseModel):
        geometry: typing.Annotated[MultiPolygon, GeometryField(z_values="strip")]

    polygon_3d = Polygon(((0, 0, 7), (0, 1, 7), (1, 1, 7), (1, 0, 7)))

    result = Model(geometry=[polygon_3d])

    assert isinstance(result.geometry, MultiPolygon)
    assert not result.geometry.has_z
    assert len(result.geometry.geoms[0].exterior.coords[0]) == 2


def test_multi_geometry_component_list_rejects_wrong_geometry_types():
    class Model(BaseModel):
        geometry: typing.Annotated[MultiPolygon, GeometryField()]

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Model(geometry=[Point(0, 0)])


def test_empty_component_list_creates_an_empty_multi_geometry():
    class Model(BaseModel):
        geometry: typing.Annotated[MultiPolygon, GeometryField()]

    result = Model(geometry=[])

    assert isinstance(result.geometry, MultiPolygon)
    assert result.geometry.is_empty

    """Build a publish-lib command with local library discovery mocked."""

    command = object.__new__(PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = SimpleNamespace(
        store=store,
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="example-charm"),

import streamlink_cli.output as output
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "A title with spaces",
        "O'Reilly's stream",
        "",
        'A "quoted" title',
        "price $5",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_one_unquoted_equals_argument_on_posix(monkeypatch, title):
    """
    POSIX subprocess invocation receives an argv list directly. Therefore,
    shell quoting must not be embedded in the --title=value argument: quotes
    would be displayed by mpv as part of the title.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output, "is_win32", False)

    player = PlayerOutput("mpv", args="{filename}", title=title, quiet=False)
    escaped_title = PlayerOutput._mpv_title_escape(title)

    assert player._create_arguments() == [
        "mpv",
        "--title={0}".format(escaped_title),
        "-",
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "A title with spaces",
        "O'Reilly's stream",
        "",
        'A "quoted" title',
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_on_windows(monkeypatch, title):
    """
    Windows needs command-line quoting for an argument containing whitespace,
    but that quoting must be generated from the complete --title=value argv
    element rather than inserted as literal POSIX shell quotes in its value.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(output, "is_win32", True)

    player = PlayerOutput("mpv.exe", args="{filename}", title=title, quiet=False)
    escaped_title = PlayerOutput._mpv_title_escape(title)
    title_argument = "--title={0}".format(escaped_title)

    assert player._create_arguments() == " ".join([
        "mpv.exe",
        subprocess.list2cmdline([title_argument]),
        "-",
    ])

import numpy as np

def _expected_translated_masks(
    masks: np.ndarray,
    offset: Tuple[int, int],
    resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int],
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Translate pixels by (dx, dy), discarding pixels outside output bounds."""
    width, height = resolution_wh
    dx, dy = offset
    expected = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for mask_index in range(masks.shape[0]):
        for source_y in range(masks.shape[1]):
            for source_x in range(masks.shape[2]):
                destination_x = source_x + dx
                destination_y = source_y + dy
                if 0 <= destination_x < width and 0 <= destination_y < height:
                    expected[mask_index, destination_y, destination_x] = masks[
                        mask_index, source_y, source_x
                    ]

    return expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "offset,resolution_wh",
    [
        pytest.param((0, 0), (4, 3), id="zero-offset"),
        pytest.param((1, 1), (7, 6), id="positive-offset-with-padding"),
        pytest.param(
            (1, 1),
            (4, 3),
            id="positive-offset-crops-right-and-bottom",
        ),
        pytest.param((-1, -1), (5, 4), id="negative-offset-crops-top-left"),
        pytest.param((1, -1), (5, 4), id="mixed-offset-crops-top"),
        pytest.param((-2, 1), (5, 4), id="mixed-offset-crops-left"),
        pytest.param(
            (-10, 0),
            (5, 4),
            id="offset-completely-outside-output-is-empty",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_translates_each_mask_and_clips_to_output_bounds(
    offset: Tuple[int, int], resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int]
) -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, True, False, False],
                [True, True, False, True],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, False, True, True],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.array(offset, dtype=np.int32),
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    expected = _expected_translated_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=offset,
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    assert result.dtype == bool
    assert result.shape == (masks.shape[0], resolution_wh[1], resolution_wh[0])
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)

import pytest

import fakeredis


@pytest.mark.parametrize("client_class", [fakeredis.FakeRedis, fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis])
def test_default_clients_created_for_separate_fixture_invocations_are_isolated(
    client_class,
):
    """A client created without an explicit server must not reuse prior state."""
    key = f"fixture-isolation:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    # These represent the clients returned by two separate function-scoped
    # pytest fixture invocations.
    first_case_client = client_class()
    second_case_client = client_class()

    first_case_client.set(key, "written-in-first-case")

    assert second_case_client.get(key) is None

    second_case_client.set(key, "written-in-second-case")
    assert first_case_client.get(key) == b"written-in-first-case"
    assert second_case_client.get(key) == b"written-in-second-case"


def test_clients_with_an_explicit_server_still_share_state():
    """Isolation by default must not break the documented explicit sharing API."""
    server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    writer = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    reader = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    key = f"explicit-server-sharing:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    writer.set(key, "shared")

    assert reader.get(key) == b"shared"


def test_clients_with_the_same_explicit_host_still_share_state():
    """Supplying a connection target explicitly should continue to select one server."""
    host = f"explicit-host-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    writer = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host=host, port=6379, db=0)
    reader = fakeredis.FakeRedis(host=host, port=6379, db=0)
    key = f"explicit-host-sharing:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

    writer.set(key, "shared")

    assert reader.get(key) == b"shared"

import pytest

from ucumvert import PintUcumRegistry, ucum_preprocessor


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("prefix", "scale"),
    [
        ("m", 1e-3),
        ("k", 1e3),
        ("u", 1e-6),
    ],
)
def test_prefixed_international_units_are_scaled_not_multiplied_by_meter(
    prefix, scale
):
    """A UCUM prefix must apply to [IU], not become a separate unit."""
    ureg = PintUcumRegistry()

    unprefixed = ureg.from_ucum("[IU]/L")
    converted = ureg.from_ucum(f"{prefix}[IU]/L")

    # In the reported regression, m[IU]/L became
    # meter * international_unit / liter. Conversion to the unprefixed unit
    # verifies both dimensionality and prefix scale.
    assert converted.to(unprefixed.units) == scale * unprefixed


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("prefix", "scale"),
    [
        ("m", 1e-3),
        ("k", 1e3),
        ("u", 1e-6),
    ],
)
def test_ucum_preprocessor_produces_parseable_prefixed_international_units(
    prefix, scale
):
    """The public UCUM-to-Pint string path must support the same expressions."""
    ureg = PintUcumRegistry()
    ureg.preprocessors.append(ucum_preprocessor)

    converted = ureg(f"{prefix}[IU]/L")
    unprefixed = ureg("[IU]/L")

    assert converted.to(unprefixed.units) == scale * unprefixed

import base64
import logging

import google_crc32c
from google.auth.credentials import AnonymousCredentials
from google.cloud import storage
from google.cloud.storage import transfer_manager
from google.cloud.storage.blob import Blob


def test_download_chunks_concurrently_disables_checksum_logging_for_every_chunk(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, caplog
):
    """Concurrent range downloads must not request a checksum for each range.

    Individual range responses do not carry an object-level checksum, especially
    for composite objects.  Requesting one causes resumable-media to emit the
    "No MD5 checksum" INFO warning once per chunk.
    """
    contents = b"x" * 12
    object_crc32c = base64.b64encode(google_crc32c.value(contents).to_bytes(4, "big")).decode(
        "ascii"
    )

    client = storage.Client(
        project="test-project",
        credentials=AnonymousCredentials(),
    )
    blob = Blob("large-composite-object", client.bucket("test-bucket"))
    blob._properties = {
        "size": len(contents),
        # The transfer manager performs one final object-level CRC32C validation.
        # Supply valid metadata so the test remains local and reaches the
        # assertion about per-chunk download behavior.
        "crc32c": object_crc32c,
    }

    # download_chunks_concurrently reloads metadata before splitting the object
    # into ranges. Keep the test offline while retaining the metadata above.
    monkeypatch.setattr(Blob, "reload", lambda self, *args, **kwargs: None)

    checksums_seen = []
    helper_logger = logging.getLogger("google.resumable_media._helpers")

    def fake_prep_and_do_download(self, file_obj, *args, **kwargs):
        checksum = kwargs.get("checksum")
        checksums_seen.append(checksum)

        # This is the warning emitted by resumable-media when a checksum was
        # requested but a range response has no checksum header.
        if checksum is not None:
            helper_logger.info(
                "No MD5 checksum was returned from the service while downloading "
                "the object, so client-side content integrity checking is not "
                "being performed."
            )

        start = kwargs["start"]
        end = kwargs["end"]
        file_obj.write(contents[start : end + 1])

    monkeypatch.setattr(Blob, "_prep_and_do_download", fake_prep_and_do_download)
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="google.resumable_media._helpers")

    destination = tmp_path / "downloaded-object"
    transfer_manager.download_chunks_concurrently(
        blob,
        str(destination),
        chunk_size=4,
        worker_type=transfer_manager.THREAD,
        max_workers=1,
    )

    # Multiple chunks ensure checksum validation is disabled for every range,
    # rather than only avoiding one warning for a single-chunk object.
    assert checksums_seen == [None, None, None]
    assert destination.read_bytes() == contents
    assert not [
        record
        for record in caplog.records
        if record.name == "google.resumable_media._helpers"
        and "No MD5 checksum was returned" in record.getMessage()
    ]

import time
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_unknown_numeric_characters_do_not_modify_vowel_configuration():
    """Unknown characters may be treated as vowels for one token, but not retained."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        # These outputs are the normal SSP behavior for unknown characters:
        # they are temporarily assigned maximum sonority for this token.
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

        assert tokenizer.tokenize("12345") == ["12", "3", "4", "5"]
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

        # Repeated and distinct numeric input must not accumulate in the
        # tokenizer's configured vowel inventory.
        for token in ("0", "42", "8675309", "٣١٤", "99", "1234567890"):
            tokenizer.tokenize(token)
            assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_unknown_characters_are_local_to_each_tokenizer_call():
    """A call containing an unknown character must not alter future tokenization state."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        tokenizer.tokenize("é9")
        tokenizer.tokenize("999")
        tokenizer.tokenize("abc123xyz")

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    # The configured vowel string is also user-customizable and must remain
    # intact when the tokenizer encounters unknown numeric characters.
    custom = SyllableTokenizer(sonority_hierarchy=["ae", "iou", "bc"])
    custom_vowels = custom.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        assert custom.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        assert custom.tokenize("12345") == ["12", "3", "4", "5"]

    assert custom.vowels == custom_vowels


def test_repeated_number_tokenization_has_no_quadratic_state_growth():
    """
    Reusing one tokenizer for numeric tokens was the reported pathological case.

    This intentionally checks both the public configuration invariant and a
    generous CPU-time bound.  A linear implementation completes this loop in a
    small fraction of a second; the former implementation continuously grew
    ``vowels`` and repeatedly searched an ever-growing expression.
    """
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        started = time.process_time()
        for _ in range(1500):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        elapsed = time.process_time() - started

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels
    assert elapsed < 1.0, (
        "Repeated numeric tokenization should not become progressively slower; "
        f"1500 calls used {elapsed:.3f}s of CPU time"
    )

import numpy as np
import nibabel as nib
import pytest
from nilearn.maskers import NiftiMasker

from fmralign.template_alignment import TemplateAlignment


def _make_img(value, shape=(4, 4, 4)):
    return nib.Nifti1Image(
        np.full(shape, value, dtype=np.float32),
        affine=np.eye(4),
    )


def _fitted_estimator_with_one_sample_template():
    """Build the minimum fitted state needed by TemplateAlignment.transform."""
    mask = nib.Nifti1Image(np.ones((4, 4, 4), dtype=np.uint8), np.eye(4))
    masker = NiftiMasker(mask_img=mask).fit()

    estimator = TemplateAlignment(alignment_method="identity", n_pieces=1)
    estimator.masker_ = masker
    # TemplateAlignment stores even one contrast as a one-sample 4D Niimg.
    estimator.template = nib.Nifti1Image(
        np.ones((4, 4, 4, 1), dtype=np.float32),
        np.eye(4),
    )
    return estimator


def test_transform_accepts_3d_target_for_one_sample_4d_template():
    """A 3D target image represents one contrast and matches train_index=[0]."""
    estimator = _fitted_estimator_with_one_sample_template()

    predicted = estimator.transform(
        [_make_img(2)],
        train_index=[0],
        test_index=[0],
    )

    assert len(predicted) == 1
    assert predicted[0].shape == (4, 4, 4, 1)


def test_transform_rejects_3d_target_for_multiple_training_samples():
    """The final spatial dimension of a 3D image must not be treated as samples."""
    estimator = _fitted_estimator_with_one_sample_template()

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="same length as the length of train_index"):
        estimator.transform(
            [_make_img(2)],
            train_index=[0, 0],
            test_index=[0],
        )

import io
import re
import sys

from loguru import logger


def _capture_exception_output(callback):
    stream = io.StringIO()
    handler_id = logger.add(
        stream,
        format="{message}",
        colorize=False,
        diagnose=False,
        backtrace=False,
    )
    try:
        callback()
    finally:
        logger.remove(handler_id)

    return stream.getvalue()


def test_recursion_error_traceback_compacts_repeated_frames(monkeypatch):
    # Ensure the formatter receives every traceback frame, independently of a
    # traceback limit possibly configured by another test or the environment.
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "tracebacklimit", 10000, raising=False)

    def _recursive_call_for_traceback_formatting():
        _recursive_call_for_traceback_formatting()

    traceback_length = None

    def log_recursion_error():
        nonlocal traceback_length

        try:
            _recursive_call_for_traceback_formatting()
        except RecursionError as error:
            traceback = error.__traceback__
            traceback_length = 0

            while traceback is not None:
                traceback_length += 1
                traceback = traceback.tb_next

            logger.exception("Oups")

    output = _capture_exception_output(log_recursion_error)

    assert "Oups" in output
    assert "Traceback (most recent call last):" in output
    assert "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded" in output

    repeated_frames = re.findall(
        r'  File ".*?", line \d+, in _recursive_call_for_traceback_formatting\n'
        r"    _recursive_call_for_traceback_formatting\(\)\n",
        output,
    )
    assert len(repeated_frames) == 3

    match = re.search(r"  \[Previous line repeated (\d+) more times\]\n", output)
    assert match is not None

    # The traceback has one outer frame which invoked the recursive function;
    # all remaining frames are identical recursive calls. Three are displayed
    # and the rest must be accounted for by the summary.
    assert int(match.group(1)) == traceback_length - 4


def test_recursion_error_does_not_compact_non_consecutive_frames():
    def first():
        second()

    def second():
        first()

    def log_recursion_error():
        try:
            first()
        except RecursionError:
            logger.exception("Oups")

    output = _capture_exception_output(log_recursion_error)

    assert "RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded" in output
    assert "[Previous line repeated" not in output
