import pytest

from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture
def nested_store(tmp_path):
    """A real file-backed store whose listing must recurse into nesting dirs."""
    store = Store(url=f"file://{tmp_path}", levels={"items/": [1]})
    store.create()
    try:
        with store:
            yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def _listed_by_name(store, *, deleted):
    return {item.name: item for item in store.list("items", deleted=deleted)}


def test_list_deleted_flag_partitions_normal_and_soft_deleted_items(nested_store):
    normal_key = "items/bb000000"
    deleted_key_1 = "items/aa000000"
    deleted_key_2 = "items/cc000000"

    nested_store.store(normal_key, b"normal")
    nested_store.store(deleted_key_1, b"first deleted")
    nested_store.store(deleted_key_2, b"second deleted")
    nested_store.move(deleted_key_1, delete=True)
    nested_store.move(deleted_key_2, delete=True)

    normal_items = _listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=False)
    deleted_items = _listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=True)

    # The two modes must be disjoint views of the store, including when list()
    # has to recurse through automatic nesting directories.
    assert set(normal_items) == {"bb000000"}
    assert set(deleted_items) == {"aa000000", "cc000000"}
    assert set(normal_items).isdisjoint(deleted_items)

    # Deleted names are presented through the Store API without the internal
    # soft-delete suffix, while retaining their ordinary item metadata.
    assert deleted_items["aa000000"].size == len(b"first deleted")
    assert deleted_items["cc000000"].size == len(b"second deleted")
    assert all(not name.endswith(".del") for name in deleted_items)


def test_list_deleted_flag_handles_empty_category_and_undelete(nested_store):
    first_key = "items/11000000"
    second_key = "items/22000000"

    nested_store.store(first_key, b"one")
    nested_store.store(second_key, b"two")

    # A store containing only live objects has no entries in the deleted view.
    assert set(_listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=False)) == {"11000000", "22000000"}
    assert _listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=True) == {}

    nested_store.move(first_key, delete=True)
    nested_store.move(second_key, delete=True)

    # Conversely, when every object is soft-deleted, the normal view is empty.
    assert _listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=False) == {}
    assert set(_listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=True)) == {"11000000", "22000000"}

    nested_store.move(first_key, undelete=True)

    assert set(_listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=False)) == {"11000000"}
    assert set(_listed_by_name(nested_store, deleted=True)) == {"22000000"}

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def _has_ansi_output(*, no_color=None, colorize=None):
    if colorize is None:
        add_handler = 'logger.add(stream, format="<red>{message}</red>")'
    else:
        add_handler = (
            'logger.add(stream, format="<red>{message}</red>", colorize=%s)' % colorize
        )

    code = textwrap.dedent(
        """
        from io import StringIO
        from loguru import logger

        class TtyStream(StringIO):
            def isatty(self):
                return True

        stream = TtyStream()
        logger.remove()
        %s
        logger.info("message")

        print("HAS_ANSI=" + str("\\x1b[" in stream.getvalue()))
        """
        % add_handler
    )

    env = os.environ.copy()
    env.pop("NO_COLOR", None)
    env.pop("LOGURU_COLORIZE", None)
    env["LOGURU_AUTOINIT"] = "false"

    if no_color is not None:
        env["NO_COLOR"] = no_color

    result = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        cwd=str(ROOT),
        env=env,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
    return "HAS_ANSI=True" in result.stdout


@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", ["1", "0", "false", "any arbitrary value"])
def test_non_empty_no_color_disables_default_tty_colors(value):
    # NO_COLOR is value-agnostic: every non-empty value disables default color.
    assert _has_ansi_output(no_color=value) is False


def test_empty_no_color_does_not_disable_default_colors():
    # Per no-color.org, NO_COLOR only applies when it is present and non-empty.
    assert _has_ansi_output(no_color="") is True


def test_explicit_colorize_true_overrides_no_color():
    # NO_COLOR controls colors added by default; an explicit user configuration
    # requesting colors takes precedence.
    assert _has_ansi_output(no_color="1", colorize="True") is True


def test_explicit_colorize_false_remains_disabled_with_no_color():
    assert _has_ansi_output(no_color="1", colorize="False") is False

"""Regression tests for charm artifact names generated from platform labels."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
import zipfile

from charmcraft.services.package import PackageService


def _package_service(project_dir: Path, platform: str) -> PackageService:
    """Create a package service with the minimum state needed to pack a charm."""
    service = object.__new__(PackageService)
    service._project = SimpleNamespace(name="mysql-router-k8s", type="charm")
    service._platform = platform
    service.project_dir = project_dir
    return service


def test_multibase_charm_artifacts_have_github_safe_unique_names(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """Platforms differing only by architecture must produce uploadable artifacts.

    GitHub Actions rejects artifact names containing ``:``, while multi-base
    platform labels use that character to separate the base from the architecture.
    """
    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "dispatch").write_text("#!/bin/sh\n")

    destination = tmp_path / "artifacts"
    destination.mkdir()

    platforms = ("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "ubuntu@22.04:arm64")
    packages = [
        _package_service(tmp_path, platform).pack(prime_dir, destination)[0]
        for platform in platforms
    ]

    package_names = [package.name for package in packages]

    # The two platform builds must remain separate artifacts rather than being
    # collapsed into one name during filename sanitization.
    assert len(set(package_names)) == len(platforms)

    for package, architecture in zip(packages, ("amd64", "arm64"), strict=True):
        assert package.exists()
        assert package.suffix == ".charm"
        assert ":" not in package.name
        assert "ubuntu@22.04" in package.name
        assert architecture in package.name
        assert zipfile.is_zipfile(package)

    # The package paths consumed by callers that request arbitrary output
    # directories must also refer to the safe artifact names.
    reported_packages = (
        tmp_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    ).read_text().splitlines()
    assert reported_packages == package_names
    assert all(":" not in package_name for package_name in reported_packages)

import pytest

from jwt.api_jwt import PyJWT
from jwt.exceptions import MissingRequiredClaimError


@pytest.fixture
def jwt():
    return PyJWT()


def test_decode_ignores_null_audience_when_no_audience_is_expected(jwt):
    payload = {"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret", algorithm="HS256")

    # A null audience must validate like an omitted audience claim, rather than
    # raising InvalidAudienceError merely because the claim key is present.
    assert jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"]) == payload


@pytest.mark.parametrize("audience", ["urn:expected", ["urn:other", "urn:expected"]])
def test_null_audience_behaves_like_omitted_audience_when_audience_is_required(
    jwt, audience
):
    token = jwt.encode({"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}, "secret", algorithm="HS256")

    # An omitted aud claim cannot satisfy an application-supplied audience.
    # Null must have the same result (MissingRequiredClaimError), not be treated
    # as a malformed or mismatched audience claim.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            audience=audience,
        )

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"


def test_null_audience_is_missing_when_audience_claim_is_required(jwt):
    token = jwt.encode({"sub": "user-123", "aud": None}, "secret", algorithm="HS256")

    # Since null aud is equivalent to an unspecified aud claim, it must not
    # satisfy explicit required-claim validation either.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            options={"require": ["aud"]},
        )

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"

"""Regression tests for HierarchicalKMeans input orientation."""

import numpy as np
import pytest
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose

from nilearn.regions import HierarchicalKMeans
from nilearn.regions.hierarchical_kmeans_clustering import hierarchical_k_means


def _feature_oriented_data():
    """Return data with more samples than features and separable features."""
    samples = np.arange(7, dtype=float)
    return np.column_stack(
        [
            samples,
            samples + 0.1,
            100 + samples,
            100 + samples + 0.1,
            -100 + samples,
            -100 + samples + 0.1,
        ]
    )


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_clusters_columns_of_standard_input():
    """Standard (n_samples, n_features) input must yield feature labels."""
    X = _feature_oriented_data()

    labels = hierarchical_k_means(X, n_clusters=3, random_state=0)
    assert labels.shape == (X.shape[1],)

    estimator = HierarchicalKMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=0).fit(X)

    assert estimator.labels_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert estimator.sizes_.sum() == X.shape[1]

    reduced = estimator.transform(X)
    assert reduced.shape == (X.shape[0], estimator.n_clusters)

    expected_reduced = np.column_stack(
        [
            X[:, estimator.labels_ == label].mean(axis=1)
            for label in range(estimator.n_clusters)
        ]
    )
    assert_allclose(reduced, expected_reduced)

    expanded = estimator.inverse_transform(reduced)
    assert expanded.shape == X.shape
    assert_allclose(expanded, expected_reduced[:, estimator.labels_])


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scaling", [False, True])
def test_hierarchical_kmeans_transform_and_inverse_keep_sample_axis(scaling):
    """Reduction and reconstruction operate on features, not samples."""
    X = _feature_oriented_data()
    estimator = HierarchicalKMeans(
        n_clusters=3, scaling=scaling, random_state=0
    ).fit(X)

    reduced = estimator.transform(X)
    unscaled_reduced = np.column_stack(
        [
            X[:, estimator.labels_ == label].mean(axis=1)
            for label in range(estimator.n_clusters)
        ]
    )

    if scaling:
        assert_allclose(
            reduced,
            unscaled_reduced * np.sqrt(estimator.sizes_)[np.newaxis, :],
        )
    else:
        assert_allclose(reduced, unscaled_reduced)

    assert_allclose(
        estimator.inverse_transform(reduced),
        unscaled_reduced[:, estimator.labels_],
    )


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_limits_clusters_by_feature_count():
    """The maximum meaningful number of clusters is the number of columns."""
    X = np.arange(32, dtype=float).reshape(8, 4)

    estimator = HierarchicalKMeans(n_clusters=10, random_state=0)
    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="at most the number of features"):
        estimator.fit(X)

    assert estimator.n_clusters == X.shape[1]
    assert estimator.labels_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert estimator.transform(X).shape == (X.shape[0], X.shape[1])

import importlib

from setuptools_scm import _entrypoints


def test_qualified_version_scheme_is_imported_without_entry_point(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """A project-local qualified name must work before the project is installed."""
    module_name = "project_local_versioning"
    (tmp_path / f"{module_name}.py").write_text(
        """
def custom_version_scheme(version):
    return "7.8.9"
""".lstrip(),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()

    def entry_point_lookup_must_not_be_used(*args, **kwargs):
        raise AssertionError("qualified names must not require an installed entry point")

    monkeypatch.setattr(_entrypoints, "_get_ep", entry_point_lookup_must_not_be_used)

    version = object()
    result = _entrypoints._call_version_scheme(
        version,
        "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
        f"{module_name}:custom_version_scheme",
        default=None,
    )

    assert result == "7.8.9"

def test_region_country_validation_collects_errors_for_all_regions(tmp_path):

    (tmp_path / "regions.yaml").write_text(
        """
- countries:
  - Invalid country-name region:
      countries:
        - Austria
        - Definitely Not A Country
  - Invalid ISO3 region:
      iso3_codes:

        - ZZZ
""",

    # contributed their country-validation errors.
    assert "Invalid country-name region" in message
    assert "Definitely Not A Country" in message
    assert "Invalid ISO3 region" in message
    assert "ZZZ" in message

    assert "uses non-standard country name(s)" in message
    assert "has invalid ISO3 country code(s)" in message

import subprocess
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

import streamlink_cli.output as output_module
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "Test Title",
        "Title with several spaces",
        'Title with "double quotes"',
        "O'Reilly's title",
        "",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_one_equals_style_argument_without_shell_quotes(title):
    """
    mpv requires --title=<value>. PlayerOutput passes an argv list to
    subprocess on POSIX, so shell quotes must not become literal characters in
    mpv's title value.
    """
    with patch.object(output_module, "is_win32", False):
        player = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="{filename}",
            title=title,
            quiet=False,
        )

        assert player._create_arguments() == [
            "/usr/bin/mpv",
            "--title={0}".format(title),
            "-",
        ]


def test_mpv_title_preserves_property_expansion_escaping_with_equals_syntax():
    """
    Existing mpv dollar escaping must remain in effect, while the resulting
    value is supplied directly after '=' in one argument.
    """
    with patch.object(output_module, "is_win32", False):
        player = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="/usr/bin/mpv",
            args="{filename}",
            title="Price is $5",
            quiet=False,
        )

        assert player._create_arguments() == [
            "/usr/bin/mpv",
            "--title=Price is $$5",
            "-",
        ]


def test_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax_on_windows():
    """
    On Windows, PlayerOutput creates a command string. list2cmdline performs
    the command-line quoting needed for a title containing spaces; POSIX-style
    quote characters must not be added to the title itself.
    """
    title = "Title with spaces"

    with patch.object(output_module, "is_win32", True):
        player = PlayerOutput(
            cmd="mpv.exe",
            args="{filename}",
            title=title,
            quiet=False,
        )

        assert player._create_arguments() == " ".join([
            "mpv.exe",
            subprocess.list2cmdline(["--title={0}".format(title)]),
            "-",
        ])

    assert first_client.get("only-on-first") == b"value"
    assert second_client.get("only-on-first") is None

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from textual.app import App
from textual.widget import Widget


@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ["before", "after"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "child_as_index,target_as_index",
    [
        (False, False),
        (False, True),
        (True, False),
        (True, True),
    ],
)
async def test_move_child_relative_to_itself_is_a_no_op(
    direction: str, child_as_index: bool, target_as_index: bool
) -> None:
    """All supported references to the same child must leave the order unchanged."""
    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        children = [Widget(id=f"child-{index}") for index in range(3)]
        container = Widget(*children)
        await pilot.app.mount(container)

        child = 1 if child_as_index else children[1]
        target = 1 if target_as_index else children[1]
        original_children = tuple(container.children)

        container.move_child(child, **{direction: target})

        assert tuple(container.children) == original_children
        assert tuple(container.children) == tuple(children)

import asyncio

import anyio
import pytest

import anyio._backends._asyncio as asyncio_backend


class _DifferentPublicTaskType:
    """A Task type that differs from the implementation returned by current_task()."""


def test_checkpoint_if_cancelled_handles_current_task_type_mismatch(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    async def main() -> None:
        task = asyncio.current_task()
        assert task is not None

        # Model environments where current_task() returns a native _asyncio.Task
        # while the Task class used by AnyIO's bookkeeping is a different type.
        # The task has no cancel scope, so checkpoint_if_cancelled() must simply
        # return rather than raising from its internal task-state lookup.
        with monkeypatch.context() as context:
            context.setattr(asyncio_backend.asyncio, "Task", _DifferentPublicTaskType)
            assert not isinstance(task, asyncio_backend.asyncio.Task)

            await anyio.lowlevel.checkpoint_if_cancelled()

    anyio.run(main, backend="asyncio")


def test_current_effective_deadline_handles_current_task_type_mismatch(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    async def main() -> None:
        deadline = anyio.current_time() + 60

        # Register genuine AnyIO state for the current task before emulating
        # the mismatch. This exercises lookup of an existing task state too.
        with anyio.CancelScope(deadline=deadline):
            task = asyncio.current_task()
            assert task is not None

            with monkeypatch.context() as context:
                context.setattr(
                    asyncio_backend.asyncio, "Task", _DifferentPublicTaskType
                )
                assert not isinstance(task, asyncio_backend.asyncio.Task)

                observed_deadline = anyio.current_effective_deadline()

            assert observed_deadline == pytest.approx(deadline)

    anyio.run(main, backend="asyncio")

import textwrap

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


def _run_cloudformation_template(tmp_path, template, checks):
    template_file = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template_file.write_text(textwrap.dedent(template))

    return Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template_file)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(checks=checks),
    )


def test_cloudformation_skip_comment_suppresses_annotated_resource_only(tmp_path):
    """CloudFormation supports the documented skip syntax without leaking to peers."""
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:
          SuppressedSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: SSH is intentionally exposed
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

          UnsuppressedSecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: SSH is not suppressed here
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        """,
        checks=["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert (
        report.skipped_checks[0].resource
        == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.SuppressedSecurityGroup"
    )

    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
    assert report.failed_checks[0].check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert (
        report.failed_checks[0].resource
        == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.UnsuppressedSecurityGroup"
    )


def test_cloudformation_considers_each_skip_annotation_before_a_resource(tmp_path):
    """
    A resource may have several skip annotations. An annotation for an unrelated
    check must not hide an earlier annotation for the check currently being run.
    """
    report = _run_cloudformation_template(
        tmp_path,
        """
        Resources:
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24: SSH is required for this legacy host
          #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_999: This is an unrelated policy annotation
          LegacySecurityGroup:
            Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
            Properties:
              GroupDescription: Legacy administration access
              SecurityGroupIngress:
                - IpProtocol: tcp
                  FromPort: 22
                  ToPort: 22
                  CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
        """,
        checks=["CKV_AWS_24"],
    )

    assert report.failed_checks == []
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1

    skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
    assert skipped.check_id == "CKV_AWS_24"
    assert skipped.resource == "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup.LegacySecurityGroup"
    assert (
        skipped.check_result["suppress_comment"]
        == " SSH is required for this legacy host"
    )

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import expressions as exp


def test_mysql_serial_is_parsed_and_expanded_in_create_table():
    sql = """
    CREATE TABLE temp
    (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
    );
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="mysql")
    column = expression.find(exp.ColumnDef)

    assert column is not None
    assert column.kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.SERIAL

    assert sqlglot.transpile(
        sql,
        read="mysql",
        write="mysql",
        pretty=True,
        comments=False,
    ) == [
        """CREATE TABLE temp (
  id BIGINT UNSIGNED PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE
)"""
    ]


def test_mysql_serial_expansion_preserves_following_columns():
    sql = """
    CREATE TABLE temp (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
    )
    """

    assert sqlglot.transpile(sql, read="mysql", write="mysql", comments=False) == [
        "CREATE TABLE temp ("
        "id BIGINT UNSIGNED PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE, "
        "name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL)"
    ]


def test_mysql_serial_does_not_duplicate_explicit_alias_constraints():
    sql = """
    CREATE TABLE temp (
        id SERIAL NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE
    )
    """

    result = sqlglot.transpile(sql, read="mysql", write="mysql", comments=False)[0]

    assert result == (
        "CREATE TABLE temp (id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT UNIQUE)"
    )
    assert result.count("NOT NULL") == 1
    assert result.count("AUTO_INCREMENT") == 1
    assert result.count("UNIQUE") == 1

from abc import abstractmethod
from typing import Protocol

from dishka import Provider, Scope, WithParents, make_container, provide_all


def test_provide_all_with_parents_registers_implementation_and_protocol_at_request_scope():
    class Encoder(Protocol):
        @abstractmethod
        def __call__(self, data: bytes) -> bytes: ...

    class ReverseEncoder(Encoder):
        def __call__(self, data: bytes) -> bytes:
            return data[::-1]

    # This is the usage from the reported issue: the error used to occur while
    # the provider class was being created/instantiated.
    class EncoderProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.REQUEST

        encoders = provide_all(WithParents[ReverseEncoder])

    provider = EncoderProvider()
    container = make_container(provider)

    with container() as request_container:
        implementation = request_container.get(ReverseEncoder)
        protocol = request_container.get(Encoder)

        assert isinstance(implementation, ReverseEncoder)
        assert implementation(b"dishka") == b"akhsid"
        assert protocol is implementation


def test_provide_all_with_parents_keeps_all_parent_aliases_and_other_entries():
    class BaseService:
        def base_name(self) -> str:
            return "base"

    class FirstCapability(Protocol):
        def first(self) -> str: ...

    class SecondCapability(Protocol):
        def second(self) -> str: ...

    class MultiService(BaseService, FirstCapability, SecondCapability):
        created = 0

        def __init__(self) -> None:
            type(self).created += 1

        def first(self) -> str:
            return "first"

        def second(self) -> str:
            return "second"

    class OtherBase:
        pass

    class OtherService(OtherBase):
        pass

    class PlainService:
        pass

    class ServicesProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP

        services = provide_all(
            WithParents[MultiService],
            WithParents[OtherService],
            PlainService,
        )

    container = make_container(ServicesProvider())

    multi = container.get(MultiService)

    # WithParents must expose every relevant parent as an alias to the same
    # concrete factory, rather than trying to construct a ProvideMultiple marker.
    assert container.get(BaseService) is multi
    assert container.get(FirstCapability) is multi
    assert container.get(SecondCapability) is multi
    assert multi.first() == "first"
    assert multi.second() == "second"
    assert multi.base_name() == "base"

    # The aliases must not result in separate construction of the implementation.
    assert MultiService.created == 1

    other = container.get(OtherService)
    assert container.get(OtherBase) is other

    plain = container.get(PlainService)
    assert isinstance(plain, PlainService)

import pytest

from borgstore.store import Store


@pytest.fixture()
def store(tmp_path):
    # Use nesting so listing must also apply the deleted filter while recursing
    # through backend-created subdirectories.
    store = Store(url=tmp_path.as_uri(), levels={"objects/": [1]})
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def _listed_sizes(store, *, deleted=False):
    return {info.name: info.size for info in store.list("objects", deleted=deleted)}


def test_list_separates_live_and_soft_deleted_items(store):
    """deleted=False and deleted=True must expose mutually exclusive states."""
    with store:
        # A normal object that was never deleted.
        store.store("objects/aa00", b"live")

        # An object that exists only as a soft-deleted object.
        store.store("objects/bb00", b"gone")
        store.move("objects/bb00", delete=True)

        # Both states may exist for one logical key: soft-delete an old version,
        # then write a new live version at the original name.
        store.store("objects/cc00", b"old")
        store.move("objects/cc00", delete=True)
        store.store("objects/cc00", b"newer")

        expected_live = {
            "aa00": len(b"live"),
            "cc00": len(b"newer"),
        }
        expected_deleted = {
            "bb00": len(b"gone"),
            "cc00": len(b"old"),
        }

        # The default behavior is the same as explicitly requesting live items.
        assert {info.name: info.size for info in store.list("objects")} == expected_live
        assert _listed_sizes(store, deleted=False) == expected_live

        # Requesting deleted objects must not also include live-only objects.
        # Returned names remain logical names rather than backend ".del" names.
        assert _listed_sizes(store, deleted=True) == expected_deleted
        assert all(not name.endswith(".del") for name in _listed_sizes(store, deleted=True))

from typing import Tuple

import numpy as np
import pytest

from supervision.detection.utils import move_masks


def _expected_shift(
    masks: np.ndarray, offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Reference translation that clips pixels falling outside the output canvas."""
    width, height = resolution_wh
    result = np.zeros((masks.shape[0], height, width), dtype=bool)

    for source_y in range(masks.shape[1]):
        for source_x in range(masks.shape[2]):
            destination_x = source_x + offset[0]
            destination_y = source_y + offset[1]

            if 0 <= destination_x < width and 0 <= destination_y < height:
                result[:, destination_y, destination_x] = masks[
                    :, source_y, source_x
                ]

    return result


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "offset,resolution_wh",
    [
        pytest.param(
            np.array([-1, -1]),
            (2, 2),
            id="negative_xy_offset_crops_left_top_and_output_right_bottom",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            np.array([-1, 0]),
            (2, 3),
            id="negative_x_offset_with_horizontal_cropping",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            np.array([0, -1]),
            (4, 2),
            id="negative_y_offset_with_vertical_cropping",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            np.array([-10, -10]),
            (4, 3),
            id="negative_offset_moves_mask_completely_off_canvas",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_move_masks_accepts_negative_offsets_and_clips_to_resolution(
    offset: np.ndarray, resolution_wh: Tuple[int, int]
) -> None:
    # Two different masks verify that every mask is translated independently.
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, True, False, False],
            ],
            [
                [False, True, False, True],
                [True, False, True, False],
                [False, False, True, True],
            ],
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=offset,
        resolution_wh=resolution_wh,
    )

    assert result.dtype == np.bool_
    assert result.shape == (len(masks), resolution_wh[1], resolution_wh[0])
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(
        result,
        _expected_shift(masks=masks, offset=offset, resolution_wh=resolution_wh),
    )


def test_move_masks_negative_offset_preserves_the_correct_remaining_pixels() -> None:
    masks = np.array(
        [
            [
                [True, False, False],
                [False, False, True],
                [False, True, False],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    result = move_masks(
        masks=masks,
        offset=np.array([-1, -1]),
        resolution_wh=(3, 3),
    )

    expected = np.array(
        [
            [
                [False, True, False],
                [True, False, False],
                [False, False, False],
            ]
        ],
        dtype=bool,
    )

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result, expected)

import io
import re
import sys

from loguru import logger


def _log_exception(callable_, *, diagnose):
    stream = io.StringIO()
    handler_id = logger.add(
        stream,
        format="{message}",
        colorize=False,
        backtrace=False,
        diagnose=diagnose,
    )

    try:
        try:
            callable_()
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Recursion failed")
    finally:
        logger.remove(handler_id)

    return stream.getvalue()


def test_recursion_error_traceback_compacts_repeated_frames():
    def recursive_without_locals():
        recursive_without_locals()

    previous_limit = sys.getrecursionlimit()
    try:
        sys.setrecursionlimit(100)
        output = _log_exception(recursive_without_locals, diagnose=True)
    finally:
        sys.setrecursionlimit(previous_limit)

    match = re.search(r"^  \[Previous line repeated (\d+) more times\]$", output, re.MULTILINE)

    assert "RecursionError:" in output
    assert match is not None
    assert int(match.group(1)) > 0

    # The standard traceback convention is to retain three copies of a
    # repeated location before emitting the summary.
    assert len(re.findall(r"in recursive_without_locals\n", output)) == 3


def test_recursion_is_compacted_when_diagnosis_values_differ_per_frame():
    def recursive_with_changing_local(value):
        recursive_with_changing_local(value + 1)

    previous_limit = sys.getrecursionlimit()
    try:
        sys.setrecursionlimit(100)
        output = _log_exception(lambda: recursive_with_changing_local(0), diagnose=True)
    finally:
        sys.setrecursionlimit(previous_limit)

    # Every frame has a different local ``value`` and therefore different
    # diagnostic-arrow output. Repetition is a property of traceback
    # locations, however, so these frames must still be summarized.
    match = re.search(r"^  \[Previous line repeated (\d+) more times\]$", output, re.MULTILINE)

    assert "RecursionError:" in output
    assert match is not None
    assert int(match.group(1)) > 0
    assert len(re.findall(r"in recursive_with_changing_local\n", output)) == 3


def test_four_identical_locations_keep_three_and_summarize_one():
    def limited_recursion(remaining):
        if remaining:
            limited_recursion(remaining - 1)
        raise ValueError("stop")

    output_with_three_calls = _log_exception(lambda: limited_recursion(3), diagnose=False)
    output_with_four_calls = _log_exception(lambda: limited_recursion(4), diagnose=False)

    assert "[Previous line repeated" not in output_with_three_calls
    assert "[Previous line repeated 1 more times]" in output_with_four_calls

    # Do not count the final ``raise`` frame: it has the same function name
    # but is a distinct traceback location from the recursive call.
    recursive_call_frame = (
        r'  File ".*", line \d+, in limited_recursion\n'
        r"    limited_recursion\(remaining - 1\)\n"
    )
    assert len(re.findall(recursive_call_frame, output_with_four_calls)) == 3

import time
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def test_numeric_tokens_remain_fast_after_many_previous_numeric_tokens():
    """Repeated unknown numeric characters must not make later calls slower.

    The tokenizer instance is intentionally reused: the reported regression was
    caused by work accumulating across calls to ``tokenize("99")``.
    """
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    # Numeric input remains a single syllable/token when there are no configured
    # vowels, including a longer number containing several distinct digits.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("1234567890") == ["1234567890"]

        def tokenize_repeatedly(count):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            for _ in range(count):
                assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
            return time.perf_counter() - start

        # Measure an early batch, then move the same tokenizer far enough into
        # its lifetime that the former accumulating-state implementation shows
        # its quadratic slowdown.
        early_batch_time = tokenize_repeatedly(100)
        tokenize_repeatedly(700)
        late_batch_time = tokenize_repeatedly(100)

    # Allow generous room for timing noise and slow machines, while requiring
    # that equivalent batches have comparable cost.  The regression makes the
    # late batch dramatically slower because every prior digit is retained.
    assert late_batch_time <= early_batch_time * 10 + 0.05

import logging
from unittest import mock

from google.cloud.storage import transfer_manager
from google.cloud.storage.blob import Blob
from google.cloud.storage.bucket import Bucket


def test_download_chunks_concurrently_disables_checksum_for_every_range(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, caplog
):
    """Concurrent range downloads must not request unavailable MD5 checksums."""
    client = mock.Mock()
    bucket = Bucket(client=client, name="test-bucket")

    chunk_size = 256 * 1024
    # Create enough data for multiple full ranges and a final partial range.
    blob = Blob(
        "large-composite-object",
        bucket,
        properties={"size": str(chunk_size * 3 + 1)},
    )

    requested_checksums = []
    resumable_media_logger = logging.getLogger("google.resumable_media._helpers")

    def fake_prep_and_do_download(self, file_obj, *args, **kwargs):
        checksum = kwargs.get("checksum", "md5")
        requested_checksums.append(checksum)

        # Simulate the warning emitted by resumable-media for a range response
        # without the requested object-level checksum.
        if checksum is not None:
            resumable_media_logger.info(
                "No %s checksum was returned from the service while downloading "
                "the object, so client-side content integrity checking is not "
                "being performed.",
                checksum.upper(),
            )

        file_obj.write(b"x")

    monkeypatch.setattr(Blob, "_prep_and_do_download", fake_prep_and_do_download)
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="google.resumable_media._helpers")

    transfer_manager.download_chunks_concurrently(
        blob,
        str(tmp_path / "downloaded-object"),
        chunk_size=chunk_size,
        max_workers=2,
        worker_type=transfer_manager.THREAD,
    )

    assert len(requested_checksums) == 4
    assert requested_checksums == [None] * 4
    assert not [
        record
        for record in caplog.records
        if record.name == "google.resumable_media._helpers"
        and "checksum was returned from the service" in record.getMessage()
    ]

import pytest
from nilearn.image import concat_imgs
from nilearn.maskers import NiftiMasker
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose

from fmralign.template_alignment import TemplateAlignment
from fmralign.tests.utils import random_niimg


def _fit_single_sample_template():
    """Create the singleton-4D template used for a one-contrast alignment."""
    source_3d, mask_img = random_niimg((5, 4, 3))
    source_4d = concat_imgs([source_3d])

    masker = NiftiMasker(mask_img=mask_img).fit()
    estimator = TemplateAlignment(
        alignment_method="identity",
        mask=masker,
        n_iter=1,
    )
    estimator.fit([source_4d, source_4d])

    assert estimator.template.ndim == 4
    assert estimator.template.shape[-1] == 1
    return estimator, source_3d


def test_transform_aligns_single_3d_contrast_to_singleton_4d_template():
    """A one-contrast target may be a 3D image although template is 4D."""
    estimator, target_3d = _fit_single_sample_template()

    predictions = estimator.transform(
        [target_3d, target_3d],
        train_index=[0],
        test_index=[0],
    )

    assert len(predictions) == 2
    for prediction in predictions:
        assert prediction.shape == estimator.template.shape
        assert_allclose(prediction.get_fdata(), estimator.template.get_fdata())


def test_transform_does_not_treat_a_spatial_dimension_as_sample_count():
    """A 3D image has one sample regardless of its final spatial dimension."""
    estimator, target_3d = _fit_single_sample_template()

    # target_3d.shape[-1] is 3, but it still represents only one contrast.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="same length"):
        estimator.transform(
            [target_3d],
            train_index=[0, 0],
            test_index=[0],
        )

import gzip
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pytest
import zarr


def _crc32c(data: bytes) -> int:
    """Compute the CRC-32C (Castagnoli) checksum used by the v3 crc32c codec."""
    crc = 0xFFFFFFFF
    polynomial = 0x82F63B78
    for byte in data:
        crc ^= byte
        for _ in range(8):
            crc = (crc >> 1) ^ polynomial if crc & 1 else crc >> 1
    return crc ^ 0xFFFFFFFF


def _write_foreign_sharded_array(path: Path, *, gzip_compressed: bool) -> np.ndarray:
    """Create a sharded v3 fixture without using zarr's sharding writer.

    This deliberately writes the on-disk format described in the issue:
    start-located index, big-endian uint64 index entries protected by CRC32C,
    transpose followed by little-endian bytes, and optionally gzip.
    """
    shape = (10, 15, 20)
    inner_chunk_shape = (5, 3, 5)
    chunks_per_shard = (2, 5, 4)

    codecs: list[dict[str, object]] = [
        {"name": "transpose", "configuration": {"order": [2, 0, 1]}},
        {"name": "bytes", "configuration": {"endian": "little"}},
    ]
    if gzip_compressed:
        codecs.append({"name": "gzip", "configuration": {"level": 5}})

    metadata = {
        "zarr_format": 3,
        "node_type": "array",
        "shape": list(shape),
        "data_type": "float64",
        "fill_value": -float("inf"),
        "chunk_grid": {
            "name": "regular",
            "configuration": {"chunk_shape": list(shape)},
        },
        "chunk_key_encoding": {
            "name": "default",
            "configuration": {"separator": "/"},
        },
        "codecs": [
            {
                "name": "sharding_indexed",
                "configuration": {
                    "chunk_shape": list(inner_chunk_shape),
                    "index_location": "start",
                    "index_codecs": [
                        {"name": "bytes", "configuration": {"endian": "big"}},
                        {"name": "crc32c"},
                    ],
                    "codecs": codecs,
                },
            }
        ],
        "attributes": {},
    }
    (path / "zarr.json").write_text(json.dumps(metadata))

    expected = (
        np.arange(np.prod(shape), dtype=np.float64).reshape(shape) / 11.0
        + np.arange(shape[0], dtype=np.float64)[:, None, None] * 100_000
    )

    # The encoded index consists of two uint64 entries for each inner chunk,
    # then the crc32c codec's four-byte checksum.
    index = np.full(chunks_per_shard + (2,), 2**64 - 1, dtype=np.uint64)
    encoded_index_size = index.nbytes + 4
    offset = encoded_index_size
    payloads: list[bytes] = []

    for coords in np.ndindex(chunks_per_shard):
        selection = tuple(
            slice(coord * chunk, (coord + 1) * chunk)
            for coord, chunk in zip(coords, inner_chunk_shape, strict=True)
        )
        # Encoding pipeline: transpose, then serialize C-order values as
        # little-endian float64 bytes, then optional gzip.
        payload = np.transpose(expected[selection], (2, 0, 1)).astype("<f8").tobytes()
        if gzip_compressed:
            payload = gzip.compress(payload, compresslevel=5, mtime=0)

        index[coords] = (offset, len(payload))
        payloads.append(payload)
        offset += len(payload)

    big_endian_index = index.astype(">u8", copy=False).tobytes(order="C")
    # numcodecs' crc32c codec stores its checksum as a little-endian uint32.
    encoded_index = big_endian_index + _crc32c(big_endian_index).to_bytes(4, "little")

    shard = path / "c" / "0" / "0" / "0"
    shard.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    shard.write_bytes(encoded_index + b"".join(payloads))
    return expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("gzip_compressed", [False, True], ids=["plain", "gzip"])
def test_reads_partial_selection_from_foreign_start_index_shard(
    tmp_path: Path, gzip_compressed: bool
) -> None:
    """A partial read must honor index offsets from another implementation.

    This is intentionally not a zarr write/read round trip.  In particular,
    the selected region intersects several non-cubic inner chunks, which is
    the layout that exposed the reported partial-decode failure.
    """

@pytest.mark.parametrize("architecture", ["amd64", "arm64"])
def test_pack_multibase_charm_uses_colon_free_artifact_name(
    tmp_path, service_factory, architecture
):
    """Multi-base platform labels must not leak ':' into produced charm filenames.

    A colon is part of the shorthand platform syntax (``ubuntu@22.04:amd64``),
    but is not accepted in GitHub Actions artifact and release filenames.
    """
    amd64_platform = "ubuntu@22.04:amd64"
    arm64_platform = "ubuntu@22.04:arm64"
    platform = f"ubuntu@22.04:{architecture}"

    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A charm with multiple bases.",
            "description": "A charm with multiple bases.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {
                amd64_platform: None,
                arm64_platform: None,
            },
            "parts": {},
        }
    )

    service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=tmp_path,
        build_plan=[
            BuildInfo(
                platform=platform,
                build_on=architecture,
                build_for=architecture,
                base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
            )
        ],
    )

    prime_dir = tmp_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    packages = service.pack(prime_dir, tmp_path)

    expected_name = f"multi-base-charm_ubuntu@22.04-{architecture}.charm"

import pytest

from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title, expected_title_argument",
    [
        ("A title with spaces", "--title=A title with spaces"),
        ('A "quoted" title', '--title=A "quoted" title'),
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_a_single_equals_option_argument(title, expected_title_argument):
    """
    mpv 0.31.1+ requires long option values to be passed using ``=``.

    PlayerOutput launches players with an argv list rather than through a shell,
    so shell quoting must not become part of the actual argument received by
    mpv. In particular, a title containing spaces must be one argv item of the
    form ``--title=<value>``, not ``--title <value>`` and not an argument with
    literal shell quote characters.
    """
    output = PlayerOutput(
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        args="{filename}",
        title=title,
        quiet=False,
    )

    try:
        arguments = output._create_arguments()
    finally:
        output.stdout.close()
        output.stderr.close()

    assert arguments == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        expected_title_argument,
        "-",
    ]
    assert "--title" not in arguments
    assert all(not argument.startswith("--title='") for argument in arguments)

import pytest

import jc
from jc.utils import convert_size_to_int


@pytest.mark.parametrize("suffix", ["k", "K"])
def test_df_block_size_suffix_k_is_binary_in_size_conversion(suffix):
    """GNU df treats bare k/K block-size suffixes as KiB."""
    assert convert_size_to_int(f"1{suffix}") == 1024
    assert convert_size_to_int(f"1.5{suffix}") == 1536
    assert convert_size_to_int(f"2{suffix}") == convert_size_to_int("2KiB")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("suffix", ["k", "K"])
def test_df_parser_converts_bare_kilo_suffixed_size_columns_as_binary(suffix):
    # This is representative of GNU df -h-style aligned output, where the
    # displayed values can use compact size suffixes.
    output = f"""Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda1       2.0{suffix}  1.0{suffix}  1.0{suffix}  50% /
"""

    result = jc.parse("df", output, quiet=True)

    assert result == [{
        "filesystem": "/dev/sda1",
        "size": 2048,
        "used": 1024,
        "available": 1024,
        "use_percent": 50,
        "mounted_on": "/",
    }]


def test_explicit_kb_remains_decimal_while_bare_k_is_binary():
    """Only the bare GNU k/K suffix has the special binary meaning."""
    assert convert_size_to_int("2KB") == 2000
    assert convert_size_to_int("2k") == 2048
    assert convert_size_to_int("2K") == 2048

def _run_cloudformation_template(tmp_path, template):
    template_file = Path(tmp_path) / "template.yaml"

        root_folder=None,
        files=[str(template_file)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(),
    )


def _failed_check_ids(report):
    return {record.check_id for record in report.failed_checks}


def _skipped_records(report):
    return getattr(report, "skipped_checks", [])

import tomlkit

from pdm.models.specifiers import PySpecSet


def _set_legacy_editable_group(project, name: str, dependencies: list[str]) -> None:
    project.pyproject.settings.setdefault("dev-dependencies", {})[name] = dependencies
    project.pyproject.write(show_message=False)


def _read_pyproject(project):
    return tomlkit.parse((project.root / "pyproject.toml").read_text("utf-8"))


def test_add_dev_uses_dev_group_without_copying_legacy_editable_group(project, pdm, repository):
    """`pdm add -d` must not reuse or duplicate a legacy editable group."""
    project.environment.python_requires = PySpecSet(">=3.6")
    legacy_dependencies = ["-e git+https://github.com/test-root/demo.git#egg=demo"]
    _set_legacy_editable_group(project, "workspaces", legacy_dependencies)

    pdm(["add", "--no-sync", "-d", "urllib3"], obj=project, strict=True)

    pyproject = _read_pyproject(project)
    assert pyproject["tool"]["pdm"]["dev-dependencies"]["workspaces"] == legacy_dependencies

    dependency_groups = pyproject["dependency-groups"]
    assert dependency_groups["dev"] == ["urllib3>=1.22"]
    assert "workspaces" not in dependency_groups

    urllib3 = next(package for package in project.lockfile["package"] if package["name"] == "urllib3")
    assert "dev" in urllib3["groups"]

import pytest

from textual.app import App
from textual.widget import Widget


@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ("before", "after"))
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "child_by_index,target_by_index",
    (
        (False, False),
        (False, True),
        (True, False),
        (True, True),
    ),
)
async def test_move_child_relative_to_itself_is_a_noop(
    direction: str, child_by_index: bool, target_by_index: bool
) -> None:
    """A child may be referred to by either its widget or its index when moved to itself."""

    children = [Widget(id=f"child-{index}") for index in range(3)]
    container = Widget(*children)
    child_index = 1
    child = children[child_index]
    original_children = list(container._nodes)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(container)

        child_reference = child_index if child_by_index else child
        target_reference = child_index if target_by_index else child
        container.move_child(child_reference, **{direction: target_reference})

        assert list(container._nodes) == original_children
        assert list(container._nodes) == children
        assert child.parent is container

import pytest

import add_trailing_comma


def _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(tmp_path, source, expected):
    filename = tmp_path / 'example.py'
    filename.write_text(source, encoding='UTF-8')

    # A single invocation must produce the final formatting, including the
    # trailing comma that previously required a second invocation.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 1
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected

    # The first pass must already be stable.
    assert add_trailing_comma.main([str(filename)]) == 0
    assert filename.read_text(encoding='UTF-8') == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('source', 'expected'),
    (
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
        (
            "def function():\n"
            "    f('long'\n"
            "      'literal')\n",
            "def function():\n"
            "    f(\n"
            "        'long'\n"
            "        'literal',\n"
            "    )\n",
        ),
        (
            "f('long'  # adjacent strings may be separated by a comment\n"
            "  'literal')\n",
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'  # adjacent strings may be separated by a comment\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
        # Calls are not limited to bare-name callables.  A subscripted
        # callable still has one multiline implicit-string argument.
        (
            "handlers['message']('long'\n"
            "                    'literal')\n",
            "handlers['message'](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
        # Likewise, a parenthesized callable expression is a call and must
        # not need a follow-up run to receive its trailing comma.
        (
            "(lambda value: value)('long'\n"
            "                      'literal')\n",
            "(lambda value: value)(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")\n",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_implicit_string_call_is_fully_fixed_in_one_pass(
        tmp_path, source, expected,
):
    _assert_fixed_in_one_pass(tmp_path, source, expected)

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _column_definition(expression, name):
    for column in expression.find_all(exp.ColumnDef):
        if column.name == name:
            return column
    raise AssertionError(f"Column {name!r} was not parsed as a column definition")


def test_mysql_serial_is_parsed_as_a_data_type_and_round_trips_create_table():
    sql = """
    CREATE TABLE temp
    (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
    );
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="mysql")
    column = _column_definition(expression, "id")

    # SERIAL must be understood as a type, rather than being treated as an
    # identifier that leaves PRIMARY KEY unparsed.
    assert column.kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.SERIAL

    rendered = sqlglot.transpile(
        sql, read="mysql", write="mysql", pretty=True, comments=False
    )
    assert len(rendered) == 1

    # The generated MySQL DDL must itself remain valid MySQL and retain the
    # primary-key constraint. Implementations may retain SERIAL spelling or
    # expand MySQL's SERIAL alias to its underlying integer type.
    round_tripped = sqlglot.parse_one(rendered[0], read="mysql")
    rendered_column = _column_definition(round_tripped, "id")
    assert rendered_column.kind.this in {
        exp.DataType.Type.SERIAL,
        exp.DataType.Type.UBIGINT,
    }
    assert any(
        isinstance(constraint.kind, exp.PrimaryKeyColumnConstraint)
        for constraint in rendered_column.args.get("constraints", [])
    )


def test_mysql_serial_does_not_break_following_columns_or_constraints():
    sql = """
    CREATE TABLE serial_examples (
      id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
      external_id SERIAL UNIQUE,
      label VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
    )
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="mysql")

    assert _column_definition(expression, "id").kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.SERIAL
    assert _column_definition(expression, "external_id").kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.SERIAL

    rendered = sqlglot.transpile(sql, read="mysql", write="mysql", comments=False)[0]
    round_tripped = sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, read="mysql")

    assert _column_definition(round_tripped, "label").kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR
    assert any(
        isinstance(constraint.kind, exp.NotNullColumnConstraint)
        for constraint in _column_definition(round_tripped, "label").args.get("constraints", [])
    )

import io
import re

from csv2md.table import Table


def _markdown_cells(row):
    """Split a Markdown table row on pipe delimiters not escaped by backslashes."""
    assert row.startswith("|") and row.endswith("|")

    cells = []
    current = []
    preceding_backslashes = 0

    for char in row[1:-1]:
        if char == "|" and preceding_backslashes % 2 == 0:
            cells.append("".join(current).strip())
            current = []
            preceding_backslashes = 0
            continue

        current.append(char)
        if char == "\\":
            preceding_backslashes += 1
        else:
            preceding_backslashes = 0

    cells.append("".join(current).strip())
    return cells


def _render_markdown_cell(source):
    """Decode the Markdown escaping relevant to literal pipes and backslashes."""
    rendered = []
    index = 0

    while index < len(source):
        if source[index] == "\\" and index + 1 < len(source):
            following = source[index + 1]
            if following in ("\\", "|"):
                rendered.append(following)
                index += 2
                continue

        rendered.append(source[index])
        index += 1

    return re.sub(r"|", "|", "".join(rendered))


def test_csv_items_and_headers_with_pipes_remain_single_markdown_cells():
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"column|name","other"\n'
            '"value|with|pipes","plain"\n'
        )
    )

    lines = table.markdown().splitlines()
    header_cells = _markdown_cells(lines[0])
    data_cells = _markdown_cells(lines[2])

    assert len(header_cells) == 2
    assert len(data_cells) == 2
    assert _render_markdown_cell(header_cells[0]) == "column|name"
    assert _render_markdown_cell(data_cells[0]) == "value|with|pipes"
    assert _render_markdown_cell(data_cells[1]) == "plain"


def test_pipe_escaping_preserves_literal_backslashes_before_pipe():
    # Backslashes in CSV are literal data. To represent two literal backslashes
    # followed by a literal pipe in Markdown, the final pipe must still be
    # escaped after the literal backslashes have been preserved.
    table = Table.parse_csv(
        io.StringIO(
            '"value","other"\n'
            '"test\\|with\\|pipe","one"\n'
            '"slashes\\\\|pipe","two"\n'
        )
    )

    markdown_rows = table.markdown().splitlines()
    one_backslash_cells = _markdown_cells(markdown_rows[2])
    two_backslash_cells = _markdown_cells(markdown_rows[3])

    assert len(one_backslash_cells) == 2
    assert _render_markdown_cell(one_backslash_cells[0]) == r"test\|with\|pipe"
    assert _render_markdown_cell(one_backslash_cells[1]) == "one"

    # The pipe must not turn into a delimiter merely because the input happened
    # to contain an even number of literal backslashes before it.
    assert len(two_backslash_cells) == 2
    assert _render_markdown_cell(two_backslash_cells[0]) == r"slashes\\|pipe"
    assert _render_markdown_cell(two_backslash_cells[1]) == "two"


def test_existing_html_pipe_entities_are_left_intact():
    original = "test|with|escaped|pipe"
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO('"value"\n"{}"\n'.format(original)))

    source_cell = _markdown_cells(table.markdown().splitlines()[2])[0]

    assert source_cell == original
    assert _render_markdown_cell(source_cell) == "test|with|escaped|pipe"

    concrete = container.get(Concrete)
    assert container.get(Middle) is concrete
    assert container.get(Base) is concrete


def test_provide_all_with_parents_handles_multiple_protocol_parents():
    class FirstProtocol(Protocol):
        def first(self) -> str: ...

    class SecondProtocol(Protocol):
        def second(self) -> str: ...

    class Implementation(FirstProtocol, SecondProtocol):
        def first(self) -> str:
            return "first"

        def second(self) -> str:
            return "second"

    class TestProvider(Provider):
        scope = Scope.APP
        dependencies = provide_all(WithParents[Implementation])

    container = make_container(TestProvider())

    implementation = container.get(Implementation)
    first = container.get(FirstProtocol)
    second = container.get(SecondProtocol)

    assert first is implementation
    assert second is implementation
    assert first.first() == "first"
    assert second.second() == "second"

import parsel.selector as selector_module
from lxml import html

from parsel import Selector


def _require_canonical_utf8_parser(received_encodings):
    """Model lxml builds which reject the ``utf8`` codec spelling."""

    def parser_factory(*args, **kwargs):
        encoding = kwargs.get("encoding")
        received_encodings.append(encoding)
        if encoding != "utf-8":
            raise LookupError(f"unknown encoding: {encoding!r}")
        return html.HTMLParser(*args, **kwargs)

    return parser_factory


def test_default_encoding_is_portable_for_eager_and_lazy_css_parsing(monkeypatch):
    """The default must work on lxml installations that reject ``utf8``."""
    received_encodings = []
    monkeypatch.setitem(
        selector_module._ctgroup["html"],
        "_parser",
        _require_canonical_utf8_parser(received_encodings),
    )

    document = "<html><head><title>Grüße</title></head><body></body></html>"

    # HTML is parsed eagerly for the normal HTML selector path.
    assert Selector(text=document).css("title::text").get() == "Grüße"

    # A text selector parses lazily when CSS/XPath is first requested.
    assert Selector(text=document, type="text").css("title::text").get() == "Grüße"

    # Bytes input has a separate construction path.
    assert (
        Selector(body=document.encode("utf-8")).css("title::text").get() == "Grüße"
    )

    assert received_encodings
    assert set(received_encodings) == {"utf-8"}


def test_utf8_alias_remains_usable_for_html_input(monkeypatch):
    """A previously accepted Python codec alias must not trigger an lxml error."""
    received_encodings = []
    monkeypatch.setitem(
        selector_module._ctgroup["html"],
        "_parser",
        _require_canonical_utf8_parser(received_encodings),
    )

    markup = "<html><head><title>Title</title></head><body></body></html>"

    assert Selector(text=markup, encoding="utf8").css("title::text").get() == "Title"
    assert (
        Selector(body=markup.encode("utf-8"), encoding="utf8")
        .css("title::text")
        .get()
        == "Title"
    )
    assert received_encodings == ["utf-8", "utf-8"]


def test_utf8_alias_keeps_json_autodetection_compatibility():
    """Changing the default spelling must not regress existing ``utf8`` callers."""
    body = b'{"title": "Parsel", "items": [1, 2]}'

    default_selector = Selector(body=body)
    utf8_selector = Selector(body=body, encoding="utf8")

    assert default_selector.type == "json"
    assert utf8_selector.type == "json"
    assert default_selector.jmespath("title").get() == "Parsel"
    assert utf8_selector.jmespath("title").get() == "Parsel"
    assert utf8_selector.jmespath("items").getall() == ["1", "2"]

def _git(project, *args):
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],

        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )


def test_version_scheme_can_be_qualified_name_from_uninstalled_source_tree(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """A project-local scheme must be importable before the project is installed."""
    if not subprocess.run(
        ["git", "--version"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL
    ).returncode == 0:
        pytest.skip("git is required to create an SCM versioned project")

    project = tmp_path / "project"
    project.mkdir()

    package_name = f"project_versioning_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    package = project / package_name
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "constants.py").write_text('VERSION = "9.8.7"\n')
    (package / "versioning.py").write_text(
        """
from .constants import VERSION

calls = []


def version_scheme(scm_version):
    calls.append(scm_version)
    return VERSION
"""
    )

    _git(project, "init")
    _git(project, "config", "user.email", "tests@example.invalid")
    _git(project, "config", "user.name", "Test User")
    _git(project, "add", ".")
    _git(project, "commit", "-m", "initial commit")
    _git(project, "tag", "v1.0.0")

    # This is the state during project configuration/build: source is importable
    # from the checkout, but there is no installed distribution or entry point
    # for this package.
    monkeypatch.chdir(project)
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(project))

    result = get_version(
        root=str(project),
        version_scheme=f"{package_name}.versioning:version_scheme",
        local_scheme="no-local-version",
    )

    assert result == "9.8.7"

    versioning = importlib.import_module(f"{package_name}.versioning")
    assert versioning.calls, "the project-local qualified version scheme was not run"

import os

def test_event_set_in_fresh_synchronous_python_process() -> None:
    """
    Match the reported use case: Event.set() must work in a newly started Python
    process, before any asynchronous event loop has been started.
    """
    source_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src"
    environment = os.environ.copy()
    environment["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join(
        filter(None, (str(source_dir), environment.get("PYTHONPATH")))
    )

    result = subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            "-c",
            """
from anyio import Event

event = Event()
assert not event.is_set()
event.set()
assert event.is_set()
assert event.statistics().tasks_waiting == 0

# Like asyncio.Event and trio.Event, setting an already-set event is harmless.
event.set()
assert event.is_set()
print("event was set")
""",
        ],
        cwd=source_dir.parent,
        env=environment,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )

    assert result.returncode == 0, (
        f"fresh synchronous Event.set() failed\n"
        f"stdout:\n{result.stdout}\n"
        f"stderr:\n{result.stderr}"
    )
    assert result.stdout == "event was set\n"

    """The clean client must explicitly support scheduling M and X copies."""

    group = StorageGroup.create(name="group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="node", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="acq")

    good_file = ArchiveFile.create(name="good", acq=acq, size_b=1)
    suspect_file = ArchiveFile.create(name="suspect", acq=acq, size_b=1)
    corrupt_file = ArchiveFile.create(name="corrupt", acq=acq, size_b=1)

    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=good_file, has_file="Y", wants_file="Y")
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=suspect_file, has_file="M", wants_file="Y")
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(node=node, file=corrupt_file, has_file="X", wants_file="Y")

    # Bad copies are not implicitly included in an ordinary cleaning request.
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "node", "--force"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=good_file).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=suspect_file).wants_file == "Y"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get(node=node, file=corrupt_file).wants_file == "Y"

    # The requested option must make both suspect and corrupt copies eligible.
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "node", "--include-bad", "--force"])

import pytest

from wemake_python_styleguide.violations import complexity
from wemake_python_styleguide.visitors.ast.complexity.function import (
    FunctionComplexityVisitor,
)


def _run_visitor(code, parse_ast_tree, default_options):
    """Run the WPS210 visitor using the project's standard test options."""
    visitor = FunctionComplexityVisitor(
        default_options,
        tree=parse_ast_tree(code),
    )
    visitor.run()
    return visitor


def test_nested_function_and_class_locals_do_not_count_for_outer_function(
    assert_errors,
    parse_ast_tree,
    default_options,
):
    """
    Locals belonging to nested lexical scopes must not inflate the outer count.

    Every individual scope remains below the default WPS210 limit, whereas
    counting all nested assignments as outer locals would exceed it.
    """
    visitor = _run_visitor(
        """
def outer():
    outer_first = 1

    def nested_function():
        function_first = 1
        function_second = 2
        function_third = 3

    class NestedClass:
        class_first = 1
        class_second = 2
        class_third = 3

    outer_second = 2
""",
        parse_ast_tree,
        default_options,
    )

    assert_errors(visitor, [])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'nested_scope',
    [
        """
        def nested_function():
            first = 1
            second = 2
            third = 3
            fourth = 4
        """,
        """
        async def nested_function():
            first = 1
            second = 2
            third = 3
            fourth = 4
        """,
        """
        class NestedClass:
            first = 1
            second = 2
            third = 3
            fourth = 4
        """,
    ],
)
def test_scopes_nested_in_control_flow_do_not_count_as_outer_locals(
    assert_errors,
    parse_ast_tree,
    default_options,
    nested_scope,
):
    """
    Nested scopes retain their boundary when they occur below an ``if`` node.

    This prevents an implementation which only recognizes functions/classes
    directly inside the containing function body.
    """
    visitor = _run_visitor(
        """
def outer(condition):
    outer_first = 1
    if condition:
{0}
    outer_second = 2
""".format(nested_scope),
        parse_ast_tree,
        default_options,
    )

    assert_errors(visitor, [])


def test_outer_function_locals_are_still_reported(
    assert_errors,
    parse_ast_tree,
    default_options,
):
    """The scope exclusion must not stop WPS210 from checking outer locals."""
    visitor = _run_visitor(
        """
def outer():
    first = 1
    second = 2
    third = 3
    fourth = 4
    fifth = 5
    sixth = 6
""",
        parse_ast_tree,
        default_options,
    )

    assert_errors(visitor, [complexity.TooManyLocalsViolation])

"""Regression test for publish-lib command failure status."""

import pathlib
from argparse import Namespace
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from craft_cli.errors import CraftError

import charmcraft.application.commands.store as store_commands
from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand


class _UnavailableLibraryStore:
    """Store double that reports every queried library as unavailable."""

    def __getattr__(self, _name):
        return lambda *args, **kwargs: None


def test_publish_lib_returns_an_error_when_library_cannot_be_published(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """A library validation failure (such as a stale LIBPATCH) must fail CI.

    The command performs validation before attempting to create the revision.
    Reporting that the library cannot be found causes that validation to add an
    error to its per-library analysis, which previously was only printed while
    the command still exited successfully.
    """
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "example" / "v1" / "example.py"
    library_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library_path.write_text("LIBPATCH = 4\n")

    library = SimpleNamespace(
        owner="owner",
        name="example",
        api=1,
        patch=4,
        filepath=library_path,
        path=library_path,
        lib_id=None,
    )

    # The command imports charm-library discovery through charmcraft.utils.
    # Patch the discovery helper actually referenced by run(), without making
    # assumptions about its exported spelling across charmcraft versions.
    discovery_helpers = [
        name
        for name in PublishLibCommand.run.__code__.co_names
        if "lib" in name.lower()
        and hasattr(store_commands.utils, name)
        and callable(getattr(store_commands.utils, name))
    ]
    assert discovery_helpers, "PublishLibCommand.run must use a library discovery helper"

    for helper_name in discovery_helpers:
        monkeypatch.setattr(
            store_commands.utils,
            helper_name,
            lambda *args, **kwargs: [library],
        )

    command = object.__new__(PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = SimpleNamespace(store=_UnavailableLibraryStore())

    # Namespace deliberately supplies None for all command options other than
    # format, as this test exercises automatic discovery rather than selecting
    # one particular library on the command line.
    class Args(Namespace):
        def __getattr__(self, _name):
            return None

    with pytest.raises(CraftError, match="Failed to publish one or more libraries"):
        command.run(Args(format=None))

"""Regression tests for safe multi-base charm artifact names."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
import zipfile

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


@pytest.mark.parametrize("architecture", ["amd64", "arm64"])
def test_pack_multibase_charm_uses_github_artifact_safe_filename(
    new_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    architecture: str,
):
    """Packed multi-base charms must not use ':' in their artifact filename.

    A platform label such as ``ubuntu@22.04:amd64`` is valid charmcraft input, but
    GitHub Actions cannot upload an artifact whose filename contains a colon.
    """
    platform = f"ubuntu@22.04:{architecture}"
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "multi-base-charm",
            "summary": "A test charm",
            "description": "A test charm used to verify artifact naming.",
            "type": "charm",
            "platforms": {platform: None},
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]

    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=new_path,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )
    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, new_path)

    assert len(packages) == 1
    charm_path = packages[0]

    # This is the externally-consumed filename used by artifact and release
    # upload actions, so it must itself be portable rather than merely logging
    # a sanitized representation.
    assert charm_path.exists()
    assert charm_path.suffix == ".charm"
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name
    assert charm_path.name.startswith("multi-base-charm_")

    # Sanitizing the unsafe separator must not discard the platform information:
    # artifacts for the two architectures need distinguishable, meaningful names.
    assert "ubuntu" in charm_path.name
    assert "22.04" in charm_path.name
    assert architecture in charm_path.name

    with zipfile.ZipFile(charm_path) as charm:
        assert charm.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

    # The package path recorded for subsequent command/output handling must be
    # the same upload-safe artifact name.
    recorded_paths = (new_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text().splitlines()
    assert recorded_paths == [charm_path.name]

"""Regression tests for HierarchicalKMeans sample/feature orientation."""

import numpy as np
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose

from nilearn.regions import HierarchicalKMeans
from nilearn.regions.hierarchical_kmeans_clustering import hierarchical_k_means


def test_hierarchical_kmeans_uses_sklearn_sample_feature_orientation():
    """Features, rather than samples, must be clustered on rectangular data.

    Requesting more clusters than samples must be possible when the input has
    enough features. Before the fix, the implementation treated the samples
    as items to cluster and this input could not be handled correctly.
    """
    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
    n_samples, n_features, n_clusters = 3, 8, 5
    X = rng.standard_normal((n_samples, n_features))

    estimator = HierarchicalKMeans(
        n_clusters=n_clusters,
        random_state=0,
        n_init=3,
    ).fit(X)

    # One label describes each input feature, not each input sample.
    assert estimator.labels_.shape == (n_features,)

    X_reduced = estimator.transform(X)
    assert X_reduced.shape == (n_samples, estimator.n_clusters)

    # Reduction averages columns (features) belonging to each cluster.
    expected_reduced = np.column_stack(
        [
            X[:, estimator.labels_ == label].mean(axis=1)
            for label in range(estimator.n_clusters)
        ]
    )
    assert_allclose(X_reduced, expected_reduced)

    # The reduced representation must expand back along the feature axis.
    assert_allclose(
        estimator.inverse_transform(X_reduced),
        X_reduced[:, estimator.labels_],
    )


def test_hierarchical_k_means_and_scaling_follow_feature_axis():
    """The functional API and scaling must use the same orientation as fit."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    X = rng.standard_normal((4, 7))

    labels = hierarchical_k_means(X, n_clusters=3, random_state=0, n_init=3)
    assert labels.shape == (X.shape[1],)

    unscaled = HierarchicalKMeans(
        n_clusters=3, random_state=0, n_init=3, scaling=False
    ).fit(X)
    scaled = HierarchicalKMeans(
        n_clusters=3, random_state=0, n_init=3, scaling=True
    ).fit(X)

    # Both estimators cluster the input columns identically; scaling only
    # changes the reduced values, not what constitutes a feature cluster.
    assert np.array_equal(unscaled.labels_, scaled.labels_)

    X_reduced = unscaled.transform(X)
    X_reduced_scaled = scaled.transform(X)
    assert X_reduced.shape == X_reduced_scaled.shape == (X.shape[0], 3)

    assert_allclose(
        X_reduced_scaled,
        X_reduced * np.sqrt(scaled.sizes_)[np.newaxis, :],
    )
    assert_allclose(
        scaled.inverse_transform(X_reduced_scaled),
        unscaled.inverse_transform(X_reduced),
    )
