import numpy as np
import pytest
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.modeling import models

from specutils import Spectrum1D
from specutils.fitting import fit_lines


class _RecordingFitter:
    """Minimal public fitter interface which records fit_lines input samples."""

    def __call__(self, model, x, y, weights=None, **kwargs):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        return model


def _fit_coordinates(spectrum, model, window):
    fitter = _RecordingFitter()
    fit_lines(spectrum, model, fitter=fitter, window=window)
    return fitter.x.to_value(u.AA)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "continuum_first",
    [False, True],
    ids=["gaussian_plus_continuum", "continuum_plus_gaussian"],
)
def test_quantity_window_selects_same_samples_as_explicit_bounds(
    continuum_first,
):
    """
    A single Quantity window is a half-width centered on the line model.

    In particular, this must work for the Gaussian-plus-constant compound
    model from the reported example, rather than silently fitting the entire
    spectrum.
    """
    spectral_axis = (6500.25 + 0.5 * np.arange(200)) * u.AA
    spectrum = Spectrum1D(
        spectral_axis=spectral_axis,
        flux=np.ones(spectral_axis.size) * u.Jy,
    )

    center = 6563 * u.AA
    window = 10 * u.AA
    gaussian = models.Gaussian1D(
        amplitude=2000 * u.Jy,
        mean=center,
        stddev=3 * u.AA,
    )
    continuum = models.Const1D(amplitude=0 * u.Jy)
    model = gaussian + continuum if not continuum_first else continuum + gaussian

    scalar_window_samples = _fit_coordinates(spectrum, model, window)

    # This is the documented manual form of the same window.  The chosen
    # sampling has no point exactly on either endpoint, so endpoint convention
    # cannot affect this comparison.
    explicit_model = (
        gaussian + continuum if not continuum_first else continuum + gaussian
    )
    explicit_window_samples = _fit_coordinates(
        spectrum, explicit_model, (center - window, center + window)
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(scalar_window_samples, explicit_window_samples)
    assert scalar_window_samples.size < spectral_axis.size
    assert scalar_window_samples.min() > (center - window).to_value(u.AA)
    assert scalar_window_samples.max() < (center + window).to_value(u.AA)

from types import SimpleNamespace

from xsdata.codegen.mappers.definitions import DefinitionsMapper
from xsdata.codegen.models import Class
from xsdata.models.enums import Tag


SOAP_ENV_NS = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"
SERVICE_NS = "urn:example:soap-service"


def build_output_envelope():
    """Build the portion of an output envelope relevant to SOAP responses."""
    envelope = Class(
        qname=f"{{{SERVICE_NS}}}GetThingOutput",
        tag=Tag.BINDING_MESSAGE,
        location="service.wsdl",
        namespace=SOAP_ENV_NS,
    )
    body = DefinitionsMapper.build_inner_class(envelope, "Body", SOAP_ENV_NS)
    response = DefinitionsMapper.build_attr(
        "GetThingResponse",
        f"{{{SERVICE_NS}}}GetThingResponse",
        namespace=SERVICE_NS,
    )
    body.attrs.append(response)

    return envelope, body, response


def test_output_envelope_fault_is_optional_while_response_remains_required():
    """A successful SOAP response must be valid without a Fault element."""
    envelope, body, response = build_output_envelope()

    DefinitionsMapper.build_envelope_fault(
        definitions=None,
        port_type_operation=SimpleNamespace(faults=[]),
        target=envelope,
    )

    fault = next(attr for attr in body.attrs if attr.name == "Fault")

    # A SOAP Body contains either the normal response payload or a Fault.
    # In particular, generated keyword-only/Pydantic models must not require
    # Fault when a normal response payload is present.
    assert fault.restrictions.min_occurs == 0

    # Making Fault optional must not accidentally make the actual response
    # payload optional too.
    assert response.restrictions.min_occurs is None

    fault_class = next(inner for inner in body.inner if inner.name == "Fault")
    assert [attr.name for attr in fault_class.attrs] == [
        "faultcode",
        "faultstring",
        "faultactor",
        "detail",
    ]


def test_fault_is_optional_even_when_wsdl_operation_declares_faults():
    """Declared operation faults describe fault contents, not Body requirements."""
    envelope, body, _ = build_output_envelope()

    definitions = SimpleNamespace(
        find_message=lambda name: SimpleNamespace(parts=[]),
    )
    operation = SimpleNamespace(
        faults=[SimpleNamespace(message="tns:KnownServiceFault")],
    )

    DefinitionsMapper.build_envelope_fault(
        definitions=definitions,
        port_type_operation=operation,
        target=envelope,
    )

    fault = next(attr for attr in body.attrs if attr.name == "Fault")
    fault_class = next(inner for inner in body.inner if inner.name == "Fault")

    # WSDL-declared faults must not cause a normal successful response to fail
    # validation merely because it has no SOAP Fault element.
    assert fault.restrictions.min_occurs == 0
    assert [attr.name for attr in fault_class.attrs] == [
        "faultcode",
        "faultstring",
        "faultactor",
        "detail",
    ]

from spinta.manifests.xsd2.helpers import XSDReader


def _read_xsd(tmp_path, contents):
    path = tmp_path / "schema.xsd"
    path.write_text(textwrap.dedent(contents), encoding="utf-8")

    reader = XSDReader(str(path), dataset_name="ignored")
    reader.start()
    return reader


def test_post_process_refs_resolves_prefixed_element_ref_to_later_element_model(tmp_path):
    reader = _read_xsd(
        tmp_path,
        """\
        <xs:schema xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
                   xmlns:tns="urn:example"
                   targetNamespace="urn:example">
          <!-- The referenced element is deliberately declared later. -->
          <xs:complexType name="EmployeeType">
            <xs:choice>
              <xs:element ref="tns:Office" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded"/>
            </xs:choice>
          </xs:complexType>

          <xs:element name="Office">
            <xs:complexType mixed="true"/>
          </xs:element>
        </xs:schema>
        """,
    )

    employee = next(
        model
        for model in reader.models
        if model.is_root_model and model.xsd_name == "EmployeeType"
    )
    office = reader.top_level_element_models["Office"]
    office_property = next(
        prop for prop in employee.properties.values() if prop.xsd_ref_to == "tns:Office"
    )

    # XSD ref values are QNames.  The namespace prefix must not prevent lookup

import re

from luaparser import ast


def test_array_style_table_fields_render_as_bracketed_numeric_keys():
    source = 'local Table = {"a", "b", "c"};'

    rendered = ast.to_lua_source(ast.parse(source))

    assert re.search(r'\[1\]\s*=\s*"a"', rendered)
    assert re.search(r'\[2\]\s*=\s*"b"', rendered)
    assert re.search(r'\[3\]\s*=\s*"c"', rendered)
    assert not re.search(r'(?m)^\s*[123]\s*=', rendered)

    # The rendered source must itself be valid Lua source. In particular,
    # `1 = "a"` is not a valid table field, while `[1] = "a"` is.
    ast.parse(rendered)


def test_implicit_fields_keep_sequential_indices_in_mixed_tables():
    source = '''
        local values = {
            "first",
            name = "named field",
            "second",
            [99] = "explicit numeric field",
        }
    '''

    rendered = ast.to_lua_source(ast.parse(source))

    # Named and explicitly indexed fields do not consume implicit array slots.
    assert re.search(r'\[1\]\s*=\s*"first"', rendered)
    assert re.search(r'name\s*=\s*"named field"', rendered)
    assert re.search(r'\[2\]\s*=\s*"second"', rendered)
    assert re.search(r'\[99\]\s*=\s*"explicit numeric field"', rendered)
    assert not re.search(r'\[\s*name\s*\]\s*=', rendered)

    ast.parse(rendered)


def test_nested_array_style_tables_render_valid_numeric_keys_at_every_level():
    source = '''
        local nested = {
            "outer value",
            {"inner one", "inner two"},
        }
    '''

    rendered = ast.to_lua_source(ast.parse(source))

    # Both the outer table and the nested constructor have implicit fields.
    # Every generated numeric key needs square brackets.
    assert re.findall(r'\[(\d+)\]\s*=', rendered) == ["1", "2", "1", "2"]
    assert not re.search(r'(?m)^\s*[12]\s*=', rendered)

    ast.parse(rendered)

import punq


class KeywordOnlyDependency:
    pass


class KeywordOnlyConsumer:
    def __init__(self, *, dependency: KeywordOnlyDependency, label: str = "default"):
        self.dependency = dependency
        self.label = label


class UnregisteredKeywordOnlyDependency:
    pass


DEFAULT_DEPENDENCY = UnregisteredKeywordOnlyDependency()


class ConsumerWithKeywordOnlyDefault:
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        dependency: UnregisteredKeywordOnlyDependency = DEFAULT_DEPENDENCY,
    ):
        self.dependency = dependency


def test_resolve_supplies_keyword_only_resolution_arguments_alongside_dependencies():
    """Keyword-only parameters must accept values passed to resolve()."""
    container = punq.Container()
    container.register(KeywordOnlyDependency)
    container.register(KeywordOnlyConsumer)

    consumer = container.resolve(KeywordOnlyConsumer, label="configured at resolution")

    assert isinstance(consumer.dependency, KeywordOnlyDependency)
    assert consumer.label == "configured at resolution"


def test_keyword_only_annotated_dependency_uses_its_default_when_unregistered():
    """An optional keyword-only dependency should retain its declared default."""
    container = punq.Container()
    container.register(ConsumerWithKeywordOnlyDefault)

    consumer = container.resolve(ConsumerWithKeywordOnlyDefault)

    assert consumer.dependency is DEFAULT_DEPENDENCY


def test_factory_accepts_keyword_only_resolution_arguments():
    """Keyword-only arguments must work for registered factory callables too."""
    container = punq.Container()

    def build_service(*, prefix, number=0):
        return f"{prefix}-{number}"

    container.register("service", build_service)

    assert container.resolve("service", prefix="item", number=3) == "item-3"

        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Microsoft Sans Serif;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Microsoft YaHei;}"
        r"{\f2\fnil Microsoft Sans Serif;}"
        r"}"
        r"{\*\generator Riched20 10.0.19041}"
        r"\viewkind4\uc1 "
        r"\pard\ltrpar\f0\fs17 [HEADER]\par"
        r"[/HEADER]\par"
        r"[BODY]\par"
        r"[1]\par"
        r"00:00:44:22\par"
        r"00:00:48:05\par"
        r"\f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd\'d5\'e6\'ca\'b8\'b9\'cc\'ca\'c2\'b4\'b4\'d7\'f7\f0\par"
        r"}"
    )

    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == (
        "[HEADER]\n"
        "[/HEADER]\n"
        "[BODY]\n"
        "[1]\n"
        "00:00:44:22\n"
        "00:00:48:05\n"
        "根据真矢固事创作\n"
    )


def test_font_changes_decode_each_section_and_group_scope_restores_font():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Western;}"
        r"{\f1\fnil\fcharset134 Chinese;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f0\'e9"
        r"{\f1\'b8\'f9}"
        r"\'e9"
        r"}"
    )

    # The first and final bytes are selected by f0 (cp1252), whereas the
    # nested section selects f1 (GBK). RTF formatting state is group-scoped.
    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "é根é"


def test_font_table_parsing_survives_nested_font_metadata_groups():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0{\*\panose 02020603050405020304}Western;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134{\*\panose 02010600030101010101}Chinese;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f1\'b8\'f9"
        r"}"
    )

    # Font definitions commonly contain nested ignorable metadata. It must not
    # prematurely end font-table processing or leak names/metadata to output.
    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "根"

import json

import pytest

from keyring import cli


def test_cli_get_returns_password_previously_set_for_username(monkeypatch, capsys):
    """
    The default ``get`` mode obtains a password-only (anonymous)
    credential, so emitting it must not attempt to read a username.
    """
    passwords = {}

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli.CommandLineTool,
        'input_password',
        lambda self, prompt: 'stored-secret',
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli,
        'set_password',
        lambda service, username, password: passwords.__setitem__(
            (service, username), password
        ),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli,
        'get_password',
        lambda service, username: passwords.get((service, username)),
    )

    cli.main(['set', 'example-service', 'example-user'])
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''

    cli.main(['get', 'example-service', 'example-user'])

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == 'stored-secret\n'


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('password', 'expected_output'),
    [
        ('a password with spaces', 'a password with spaces\n'),
        ('', '\n'),
    ],
)
def test_cli_get_plain_handles_anonymous_passwords(
    monkeypatch, capsys, password, expected_output
):
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, 'get_password', lambda service, username: password)

    cli.main(['get', 'service', 'user'])

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == expected_output


def test_cli_get_json_handles_anonymous_credential_without_username(
    monkeypatch, capsys
):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli, 'get_password', lambda service, username: 'json-password'
    )

    cli.main(['get', 'service', 'user', '--output', 'json'])

    payload = json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)
    assert payload == {'password': 'json-password'}

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, table_name, alias",
    [
        (
            """
            INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c) VALUES (1, 2, 3)
            ON CONFLICT (c)
            DO UPDATE
              SET a = t.a + 1
            WHERE t.a < 1
            """,
            "newtable",
            "t",
        ),
        (
            """
            INSERT INTO inventory i (id, quantity) VALUES (1, 10)
            ON CONFLICT (id)
            DO UPDATE
              SET quantity = i.quantity
            WHERE i.quantity < 100
            """,
            "inventory",
            "i",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_insert_target_alias_with_columns_and_conflict_where(sql, table_name, alias):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    tables = list(expression.find_all(exp.Table))
    assert [table.name for table in tables] == [table_name]

    conflict = expression.args["conflict"]
    assert isinstance(conflict, exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict.args["action"] == "UPDATE"

    # References in the DO UPDATE expression and its WHERE predicate must be
    # parsed as qualified references to the INSERT target alias.
    qualified_columns = [
        column
        for column in conflict.find_all(exp.Column)
        if column.table == alias
    ]
    assert len(qualified_columns) == 2


def test_postgres_insert_target_as_alias_without_target_column_list():
    expression = parse_one(
        """
        INSERT INTO newtable AS t VALUES (1, 2, 3)
        ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET a = t.a
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    tables = list(expression.find_all(exp.Table))
    assert [table.name for table in tables] == ["newtable"]

    conflict = expression.args["conflict"]
    assert isinstance(conflict, exp.OnConflict)
    assert [
        (column.table, column.name) for column in conflict.find_all(exp.Column)
    ] == [("t", "a")]

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _with_fill(expression):
    with_fill = expression.find(exp.WithFill)
    assert with_fill is not None, "WITH FILL clause was not retained in the parsed expression"
    return with_fill


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_bare_column_with_datetime_bounds():
    sql = """
    SELECT
        1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
        'test' interp
    ORDER BY DATETIME
    WITH FILL
    FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
    TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
    STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
    INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)

    assert with_fill.args["from"] is not None
    assert with_fill.args["to"] is not None
    assert with_fill.args["step"] is not None
    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 1

    # The generated ClickHouse SQL must itself remain parseable with its
    # INTERPOLATE clause intact, regardless of AST canonicalization.
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse"), read="clickhouse")
    assert len(_with_fill(reparsed).args["interpolate"]) == 1


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_accepts_multiple_bare_and_explicit_columns():
    sql = """
    SELECT ts, carry_a, calculated_b, carry_c
    FROM events
    ORDER BY ts
    WITH FILL
    FROM 0
    TO 10
    STEP 1
    INTERPOLATE (carry_a, calculated_b AS calculated_b + 1, carry_c)
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    interpolate = _with_fill(expression).args["interpolate"]

    # Bare column names are valid alongside the pre-existing `column AS
    # expression` form, and none of the entries may be discarded.
    assert len(interpolate) == 3

    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "INTERPOLATE" in rendered.upper()
    assert "calculated_b + 1" in rendered

    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, read="clickhouse")
    assert len(_with_fill(reparsed).args["interpolate"]) == 3

"""Regression tests for WPS210 local-variable scope boundaries."""

from wemake_python_styleguide.violations.complexity import (
    TooManyLocalsViolation,
)
from wemake_python_styleguide.visitors.ast.complexity.function import (
    FunctionComplexityVisitor,
)


def _outer_assignments(limit: int) -> str:
    """Build exactly as many outer locals as the configured limit allows."""
    return ''.join(
        '    outer_{0} = {0}\n'.format(number)
        for number in range(limit)
    )


def _run_wps210(
    code: str,
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
) -> list[object]:
    """Run the function-complexity visitor and return WPS210 violations."""
    tree = parse_ast_tree(code)
    visitor = FunctionComplexityVisitor(default_options, tree=tree)
    visitor.run()

    return [
        violation
        for violation in visitor.violations
        if isinstance(violation, TooManyLocalsViolation)
    ]


def test_nested_function_in_conditional_does_not_count_for_outer_function(
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
) -> None:
    """
    Ensures a nested function remains a separate scope inside control flow.

    Its parent in the AST is an ``if`` statement rather than the outer
    function directly, but its assignments must still not increase the
    outer function's WPS210 local-variable count.
    """
    code = (
        'def outer(condition):\n'
        + _outer_assignments(default_options.max_local_variables)
        + '    if condition:\n'
        + '        def nested():\n'
        + '            nested_local = 1\n'
    )

    violations = _run_wps210(code, default_options, parse_ast_tree)

    assert violations == []


def test_nested_class_in_conditional_does_not_count_for_outer_function(
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
) -> None:
    """
    Ensures class-body assignments do not count for an enclosing function.

    This covers a local class nested through a control-flow node, rather than
    only a class that is an immediate child of the function body.
    """
    code = (
        'def outer(condition):\n'
        + _outer_assignments(default_options.max_local_variables)
        + '    if condition:\n'
        + '        class Nested:\n'
        + '            first_attribute = 1\n'
        + '            second_attribute = 2\n'
    )

    violations = _run_wps210(code, default_options, parse_ast_tree)

    assert violations == []

"""Regression tests for cleaning and deleting suspect/corrupt file copies."""

from unittest.mock import patch

from alpenhorn.db import ArchiveAcq, ArchiveFile, ArchiveFileCopy, StorageGroup, StorageNode


def test_clean_include_bad_flags_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(clidb, cli):
    """Bad copies are candidates only when --include-bad is requested."""

    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    valid = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="valid", acq=acq, size_b=100),
        has_file="Y",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    suspect = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="suspect", acq=acq, size_b=100),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    corrupt = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=ArchiveFile.create(name="corrupt", acq=acq, size_b=100),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )

    # The option must be opt-in: normal clean behavior excludes bad copies.
    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(valid.id).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "Y"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "Y"

    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force", "--include-bad"])
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(suspect.id).wants_file == "M"
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(corrupt.id).wants_file == "M"


def test_daemon_deletes_released_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(
    mockgroupandnode, simpleacq, archivefile, archivefilecopy
):
    """The daemon dispatches delete work for unwanted X and M copies."""

    mockio, _group, node = mockgroupandnode

    valid = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="valid", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="Y",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    suspect = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="suspect", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    corrupt = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="N",
    )

    # Controls: nonexistent copies cannot be removed, and a copy still wanted
    # by the scheduler must not be deleted merely because it is suspect.
    absent = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="absent", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="N",
        wants_file="N",
    )
    wanted_suspect = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="wanted-suspect", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="X",
        wants_file="Y",
    )

    mockio.node.delete.reset_mock()
    node.update_delete()

    dispatched_ids = {
        copy.id
        for call in mockio.node.delete.call_args_list
        for copy in call[0][0]
    }

    assert {valid.id, suspect.id, corrupt.id} <= dispatched_ids
    assert absent.id not in dispatched_ids
    assert wanted_suspect.id not in dispatched_ids


def test_daemon_skips_checking_released_corrupt_copies(
    mockgroupandnode, simpleacq, archivefile, archivefilecopy
):
    """A corrupt copy released for deletion is not sent through integrity check."""

    mockio, _group, node = mockgroupandnode

    wanted = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="wanted-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="Y",
    )
    deferred = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="deferred-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="M",
    )
    released = archivefilecopy(
        node=node.db,
        file=archivefile(name="released-corrupt", acq=simpleacq),
        has_file="M",
        wants_file="N",
    )

    mockio.node.before_update.return_value = True
    mockio.node.check.reset_mock()

    # Isolate the integrity-check part of a normal daemon update.  Deletion
    # dispatch is tested above; it need not run to establish that this copy
    # was not checked first.
    with patch.object(node, "update_free_space"), patch.object(node, "update_delete"):
        node.update()

    checked_ids = {call[0][0].id for call in mockio.node.check.call_args_list}

    assert wanted.id in checked_ids
    assert deferred.id in checked_ids
    assert released.id not in checked_ids

import ast
from typing import Any, Iterable

import pytest

from func_adl import ObjectStream
from func_adl.type_based_replacement import remap_by_types


class Item:
    def pt(self) -> float: ...


class Event:
    def Items(self) -> Iterable[Item]: ...


def _expression(source: str) -> ast.AST:
    return ast.parse(source, mode="eval").body


def _stream() -> ObjectStream:
    return ObjectStream(ast.Name(id="e", ctx=ast.Load()), Event)


def test_unknown_function_on_dictionary_expression_has_any_type():
    """A backend-defined function such as Zip must not be treated as a dict key."""
    _, _, expression_type = remap_by_types(
        _stream(),
        "e",
        Event,
        _expression("{'pt': e.Items()}.Zip()"),
    )

    assert expression_type is Any


def test_zip_dictionary_function_can_be_used_in_a_collection_chain():
    """The AGC-style Zip/Where/Count expression must type trace successfully."""
    _, _, expression_type = remap_by_types(
        _stream(),
        "e",
        Event,
        _expression(
            "{'pt': e.Items()}.Zip()"
            ".Where(lambda item: item.pt > 30)"
            ".Count()"
        ),
    )

    assert expression_type is Any


def test_unknown_dictionary_field_is_still_reported_as_a_typo():
    """Known dictionary structure must continue to catch misspelled field names."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="itemss"):
        remap_by_types(
            _stream(),
            "e",
            Event,
            _expression("{'items': e.Items()}.itemss"),
        )


def test_unknown_field_on_typed_dictionary_result_is_still_reported():
    """Dictionary type information propagated through Select must remain strict."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ptt"):
        remap_by_types(
            _stream(),
            "e",
            Event,
            _expression(
                "e.Items()"
                ".Select(lambda item: {'pt': item.pt()})"
                ".Select(lambda record: record.ptt)"
            ),
        )

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot.errors import ParseError


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected",
    [
        (
            "SELECT 'hello' || 'world' FROM t",
            "SELECT 'hello' + 'world' FROM t",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT first_name || last_name FROM users",
            "SELECT first_name + last_name FROM users",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name FROM users",
            "SELECT first_name + ' ' + last_name FROM users",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT prefix || (a + b) FROM t",
            "SELECT prefix + (a + b) FROM t",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_string_concatenation_uses_plus_in_tsql(sql, expected):
    assert sqlglot.transpile(sql, read="postgres", write="tsql") == [expected]


def test_tsql_does_not_accept_double_pipe_as_string_concatenation():
    # || is only available in Azure SQL Database, not the general T-SQL dialect.
    # In particular, it must not be parsed into a string-concatenation expression.
    with pytest.raises(ParseError):
        sqlglot.parse_one("SELECT first_name || last_name FROM users", dialect="tsql")

import json

import pytest

from streamlink import Streamlink
from streamlink.plugins.kick import Kick


TOKEN = "kick-xsrf-token"
HLS_URL = "https://video.example.test/master.m3u8"
HLS_PLAYLIST = """#EXTM3U
#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=1500000,RESOLUTION=1280x720
720p.m3u8
"""


def _register_token_page(requests_mock):
    requests_mock.get(
        "https://kick.com/",
        text="<html><body>Kick</body></html>",
        cookies={"XSRF-TOKEN": TOKEN},
    )


def _assert_browser_navigation_headers(request):
    # Kick requires a browser-like initial request before its API endpoints
    # accept subsequent requests.
    assert request.headers["User-Agent"].startswith("Mozilla/5.0")
    assert request.headers["Accept-Language"].startswith("en-US")
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-Dest"] == "document"
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-Mode"] == "navigate"
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-Site"] == "none"
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-User"] == "?1"


def _assert_api_headers(request, referer):
    # These are the headers of the same-origin XHR request made by the
    # browser after loading the Kick page. A request missing them is what
    # Kick's security policy rejects with HTTP 403.
    assert request.headers["User-Agent"].startswith("Mozilla/5.0")
    assert request.headers["Accept"] == "application/json"
    assert request.headers["Accept-Language"].startswith("en-US")
    assert request.headers["Referer"] == referer
    assert request.headers["Authorization"] == f"Bearer {TOKEN}"
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-Dest"] == "empty"
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-Mode"] == "cors"
    assert request.headers["Sec-Fetch-Site"] == "same-origin"
    assert request.headers["X-Requested-With"] == "XMLHttpRequest"


def _security_protected_response(expected_referer, payload, status_code=200):
    """Return a mock Kick endpoint which only accepts browser-like requests."""

    def callback(request, context):
        required = {
            "Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}",
            "Referer": expected_referer,
            "Accept": "application/json",
            "Sec-Fetch-Dest": "empty",
            "Sec-Fetch-Mode": "cors",
            "Sec-Fetch-Site": "same-origin",
            "X-Requested-With": "XMLHttpRequest",
        }

        if (
            not request.headers.get("User-Agent", "").startswith("Mozilla/5.0")
            or not request.headers.get("Accept-Language", "").startswith("en-US")
            or any(request.headers.get(name) != value for name, value in required.items())
        ):
            context.status_code = 403
            return json.dumps({"message": "Request blocked by security policy"})

        context.status_code = status_code
        return json.dumps(payload)

    return callback


def _plugin(url):
    session = Streamlink()
    return Kick(session, url)


def test_kick_live_request_uses_browser_session_and_can_open_stream(requests_mock):
    url = "https://kick.com/zmok"
    api_url = "https://kick.com/api/v2/channels/zmok/livestream"

    _register_token_page(requests_mock)
    requests_mock.get(
        api_url,
        text=_security_protected_response(
            url,
            {
                "data": {
                    "playback_url": HLS_URL,
                    "id": 123,
                    "category": {"name": "Gaming"},
                    "session_title": "Live title",
                },
            },
        ),
    )
    requests_mock.get(HLS_URL, text=HLS_PLAYLIST)

    plugin = _plugin(url)
    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert streams
    assert plugin.author == "zmok"
    assert plugin.id == 123
    assert plugin.category == "Gaming"
    assert plugin.title == "Live title"

    homepage_request = next(
        request for request in requests_mock.request_history if request.url == "https://kick.com/"
    )
    api_request = next(request for request in requests_mock.request_history if request.url == api_url)
    _assert_browser_navigation_headers(homepage_request)
    _assert_api_headers(api_request, url)


def test_kick_vod_request_uses_browser_session_and_can_open_stream(requests_mock):
    vod_id = "4acba712-a1cd-45b0-8ce0-4b534d4c271f"
    url = f"https://kick.com/kukudota2/videos/{vod_id}"
    api_url = f"https://kick.com/api/v1/video/{vod_id}"

    _register_token_page(requests_mock)
    requests_mock.get(
        api_url,
        text=_security_protected_response(
            url,
            {
                "source": HLS_URL,
                "livestream": {
                    "session_title": "Recorded stream",
                    "channel": {"user": {"username": "kukudota2"}},
                },
            },
        ),
    )
    requests_mock.get(HLS_URL, text=HLS_PLAYLIST)

    plugin = _plugin(url)
    streams = plugin.streams()

    assert streams
    assert plugin.id == vod_id
    assert plugin.author == "kukudota2"
    assert plugin.title == "Recorded stream"

    api_request = next(request for request in requests_mock.request_history if request.url == api_url)
    _assert_api_headers(api_request, url)


def test_kick_offline_channel_returns_no_streams_instead_of_a_403(requests_mock):
    url = "https://kick.com/offlinechannel"
    api_url = "https://kick.com/api/v2/channels/offlinechannel/livestream"

    _register_token_page(requests_mock)
    requests_mock.get(
        api_url,
        text=_security_protected_response(
            url,
            {"message": "Channel is not live"},
            status_code=404,
        ),
    )

    plugin = _plugin(url)

    assert plugin.streams() == {}

    api_request = next(request for request in requests_mock.request_history if request.url == api_url)
    _assert_api_headers(api_request, url)

def ureg():

@pytest.mark.parametrize("magnitude", (1.1, -1.1, 1.5, 2.5))
def test_round_quantity_without_ndigits_matches_scalar_rounding(ureg, magnitude):
    quantity = magnitude * ureg.kilogram

    result = round(quantity)
    expected = round(magnitude)

    assert result.units == ureg.kilogram
    assert result.magnitude == expected
    assert type(result.magnitude) is type(expected)
    assert isinstance(result.magnitude, int)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("magnitude", (1.1, -1.1, 1.5, 2.5))
def test_round_quantity_with_explicit_none_matches_scalar_rounding(ureg, magnitude):
    quantity = magnitude * ureg.meter

    result = round(quantity, None)
    expected = round(magnitude, None)

    assert result.units == ureg.meter
    assert result.magnitude == expected
    assert type(result.magnitude) is type(expected)
    assert isinstance(result.magnitude, int)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("ndigits", (-1, 0, 1))
def test_round_quantity_with_ndigits_preserves_scalar_round_behavior(ureg, ndigits):
    magnitude = 12.34
    quantity = magnitude * ureg.second

    result = round(quantity, ndigits)
    expected = round(magnitude, ndigits)

    assert result.units == ureg.second
    assert result.magnitude == expected
    assert type(result.magnitude) is type(expected)

import pytest


CPPLINT = Path(__file__).with_name("cpplint.py")

_CPP_SPECIFIC_SOURCE = """\
int main() {

def _run_cpplint(path: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    # Uppercase extensions are not necessarily part of cpplint's default input
    # extension list, so explicitly enable every extension covered by .[cChH].
    # This tests their language-specific behavior rather than whether a project
    # has opted into linting them.
    return subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            str(CPPLINT),
            "--extensions=c,C,h,H,cc",
            "--filter=-,+readability/casting,+runtime/int",
            str(path),
        ],
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("extension", [".c", ".C", ".h", ".H"])
def test_c_extensions_skip_cpp_casting_and_integer_warnings(
    tmp_path: Path, extension: str
) -> None:
    """Every extension in .[cChH] is treated as C for these rules."""
    source = tmp_path / f"c_source{extension}"
    source.write_text(_CPP_SPECIFIC_SOURCE)

    result = _run_cpplint(source)
    output = result.stdout + result.stderr

    assert "Ignoring" not in output
    assert "[readability/casting]" not in output
    assert "[runtime/int]" not in output
    assert result.returncode == 0


def test_cpp_file_still_reports_cpp_casting_and_integer_warnings(
    tmp_path: Path,
) -> None:
    """Suppressing the rules for C must not suppress them for C++."""
    source = tmp_path / "cpp_source.cc"
    source.write_text(_CPP_SPECIFIC_SOURCE)

    result = _run_cpplint(source)
    output = result.stdout + result.stderr

    assert "[readability/casting]" in output
    assert "[runtime/int]" in output
    assert result.returncode != 0

def in_memory_keyring(monkeypatch):
    passwords = {}

    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, 'set_password', set_password)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, 'get_password', get_password)
    return passwords


def test_get_returns_password_that_was_set_without_accessing_anonymous_username(
    monkeypatch, capsys, in_memory_keyring
):
    """
    The default get mode obtains a password and wraps it in an
    AnonymousCredential. Its lack of a username must not prevent the CLI from
    printing the password.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli.CommandLineTool,
        'input_password',
        lambda self, prompt: 'stored-password',
    )

    cli.main(['set', 'aaaa', 'bbbb'])
    cli.main(['get', 'aaaa', 'bbbb'])

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == 'stored-password\n'


def test_get_json_for_password_mode_does_not_require_anonymous_username(
    monkeypatch, capsys, in_memory_keyring
):
    """
    JSON output is another formatter for the same anonymous credential and
    should likewise expose the password without inventing or reading a
    username.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        cli.CommandLineTool,
        'input_password',
        lambda self, prompt: 'json-password',
    )

    cli.main(['set', 'service', 'user'])
    cli.main(['get', 'service', 'user', '--output=json'])

    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out) == {'password': 'json-password'}

        'input_password',
        lambda self, prompt: '',
    )

    cli.main(['set', 'empty-service', 'empty-user'])
    cli.main(['get', 'empty-service', 'empty-user'])

    assert capsys.readouterr().out == '\n'

from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import streaming_pull_manager
from google.pubsub_v1 import types as gapic_types


def _make_manager():
    scheduler = mock.Mock(name="scheduler")
    manager = streaming_pull_manager.StreamingPullManager(
        mock.Mock(name="subscriber_client"),
        "projects/test-project/subscriptions/test-subscription",
        scheduler=scheduler,
        await_callbacks_on_shutdown=True,
    )

    manager._callback = mock.Mock(name="message_callback")
    manager._consumer = mock.Mock(name="consumer")
    manager._consumer.is_active = True
    manager._consumer.is_paused = False

    manager._dispatcher = mock.Mock(name="dispatcher")
    manager._leaser = mock.Mock(name="leaser")
    manager._leaser.message_count = 0
    manager._leaser.bytes = 0
    manager._heartbeater = mock.Mock(name="heartbeater")

    return manager, scheduler


def _response():
    return gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse(
        received_messages=[
            gapic_types.ReceivedMessage(
                ack_id="ack-id",
                message=gapic_types.PubsubMessage(
                    data=b"message-data",
                    message_id="message-id",
                ),
            )
        ]
    )


def test_response_is_ignored_when_shutdown_has_removed_scheduler():
    """A bidi response arriving after scheduler teardown must not crash.

    ``close()`` clears helpers in several stages. This represents the state at
    the reported failure: the scheduler has been removed while the bidi thread
    is still able to invoke ``_on_response``. The response must be discarded
    rather than reaching an assertion or trying to schedule a callback.
    """
    manager, scheduler = _make_manager()
    manager._scheduler = None

    manager._on_response(_response())

    scheduler.schedule.assert_not_called()
    assert manager._messages_on_hold.size == 0


def test_response_and_scheduler_teardown_race_does_not_raise():
    """Scheduler teardown between response receipt and callback dispatch is safe."""
    manager, scheduler = _make_manager()
    response_started = threading.Event()
    permit_dispatch = threading.Event()
    errors = []
    original_put = manager._messages_on_hold.put

    def pause_before_dispatch(message):
        response_started.set()
        assert permit_dispatch.wait(2), "test did not release response processing"
        return original_put(message)

    def invoke_response():
        try:
            manager._on_response(_response())
        except BaseException as exc:
            errors.append(exc)

    with mock.patch.object(
        manager._messages_on_hold, "put", side_effect=pause_before_dispatch
    ):
        response_thread = threading.Thread(target=invoke_response, daemon=True)
        response_thread.start()

        assert response_started.wait(2), "_on_response did not begin processing"

        # This is the operation performed by shutdown that caused the reported
        # assertion. Keep other helpers intact: they are unrelated to the
        # scheduler race and allow this test to isolate it.
        manager._scheduler = None
        permit_dispatch.set()

        response_thread.join(2)

    assert not response_thread.is_alive(), "_on_response did not finish"
    assert errors == []
    scheduler.schedule.assert_not_called()

import pytest

from xsdata.codegen.mappers import DefinitionsMapper
from xsdata.models.wsdl import (
    BindingMessage,
    BindingOperation,
    Definitions,
    Message,
    Part,
    PortTypeMessage,
    PortTypeOperation,
)


def build_message(name: str, part_name: str, element_name: str) -> Message:
    message = Message(
        name=name,
        parts=[Part(name=part_name, element=f"tns:{element_name}")],
    )
    message.ns_map["tns"] = "urn:example"
    message.parts[0].ns_map["tns"] = "urn:example"
    return message


@pytest.mark.parametrize("style", ["document", "rpc"])
def test_soap_output_fault_is_optional_but_response_content_is_not(style: str):
    """SOAP responses may contain either normal body content or a SOAP Fault.

    The generated output envelope must therefore retain the Fault model while
    making the Fault element optional. This is especially important for
    kw-only/Pydantic generated classes, where a missing min_occurs=0 would
    otherwise turn Fault into a required constructor/validation field.
    """

    definitions = Definitions(target_namespace="urn:example")
    definitions.messages.extend(
        [
            build_message("RequestMessage", "request", "Request"),
            build_message("ResponseMessage", "response", "Response"),
        ]
    )

    input_binding_message = BindingMessage(
        extended=[],
        location="service.wsdl",
    )
    output_binding_message = BindingMessage(
        extended=[],
        location="service.wsdl",
    )

    # A soap:body extension is all the mapper needs to create the Body inner
    # class. The local name is intentionally used here, as in parsed WSDL
    # extension elements.
    from xsdata.formats.dataclass.models.generics import AnyElement

    input_binding_message.extended.append(AnyElement(qname="body"))
    output_binding_message.extended.append(AnyElement(qname="body"))

    binding_operation = BindingOperation(
        name="GetValue",
        input=input_binding_message,
        output=output_binding_message,
    )
    port_operation = PortTypeOperation(
        input=PortTypeMessage(message="tns:RequestMessage", location="service.wsdl"),
        output=PortTypeMessage(message="tns:ResponseMessage", location="service.wsdl"),
    )

    generated = list(
        DefinitionsMapper.map_binding_operation_messages(
            definitions=definitions,
            binding_operation=binding_operation,
            port_type_operation=port_operation,
            name="Example_GetValue",
            style=style,
            namespace="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/",
        )
    )

    envelopes = [obj for obj in generated if obj.meta_name == "Envelope"]
    assert len(envelopes) == 2

    input_envelope, output_envelope = envelopes
    input_body = next(inner for inner in input_envelope.inner if inner.name == "Body")
    output_body = next(inner for inner in output_envelope.inner if inner.name == "Body")

    # Fault is a SOAP response construct; requests must not gain a spurious
    # fault field merely because the operation has an output.
    assert all(attr.name != "Fault" for attr in input_body.attrs)

    fault_attr = next(attr for attr in output_body.attrs if attr.name == "Fault")
    response_attrs = [attr for attr in output_body.attrs if attr.name != "Fault"]

    # The normal response still follows the WSDL's normal required semantics.
    assert len(response_attrs) == 1
    assert response_attrs[0].restrictions.min_occurs is None

    # A normal SOAP response without a Fault is valid. min_occurs=0 is the
    # codegen-level representation that produces an optional field for both
    # dataclass and kw-only/Pydantic output formats.
    assert fault_attr.default is None
    assert fault_attr.restrictions.min_occurs == 0

    # Optional must not mean that the SOAP Fault schema disappears: callers
    # still need a typed Fault model when a fault response is actually sent.
    fault_class = next(inner for inner in output_body.inner if inner.name == "Fault")
    assert {attr.name for attr in fault_class.attrs} >= {
        "faultcode",
        "faultstring",
        "faultactor",
        "detail",
    }

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _with_fill(query):
    with_fill = query.find(exp.WithFill)
    assert with_fill is not None, "WITH FILL should be represented in the parsed expression tree"
    return with_fill


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_shorthand_with_datetime_bounds():
    sql = """
    SELECT
        1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
        'test' interp
    ORDER BY DATETIME
    WITH FILL
    FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
    TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
    STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
    INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """

    query = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = _with_fill(query)

    # The fill range must remain intact; INTERPOLATE must not consume any of
    # the preceding WITH FILL clauses.
    assert with_fill.args["from"] is not None
    assert with_fill.args["to"] is not None
    assert with_fill.args["step"] is not None
    assert "toDateTime64" in with_fill.args["from"].sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "toDateTime64" in with_fill.args["to"].sql(dialect="clickhouse")

    interpolate = with_fill.args["interpolate"]
    assert len(interpolate) == 1

    # ClickHouse permits INTERPOLATE(column) as shorthand for using the
    # column itself as the interpolation expression. In particular, this
    # must not create an Alias without its required "this" expression.
    item = interpolate[0]
    assert isinstance(item, exp.Alias)
    assert item.alias == "interp"
    assert item.this is not None
    assert item.this.name == "interp"

    # Generated ClickHouse SQL must also remain parseable.
    rendered = query.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    reparsed_fill = _with_fill(sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, read="clickhouse"))
    assert len(reparsed_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 1


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_supports_shorthand_and_explicit_expressions():
    sql = """
    SELECT ts, value, label
    FROM events
    ORDER BY ts
    WITH FILL
    FROM 0 TO 10 STEP 1
    INTERPOLATE (
        value,
        label AS COALESCE(label, 'missing')
    )
    """

import pytest
from apispec import APISpec
from apispec.ext.marshmallow import MarshmallowPlugin
from marshmallow import Schema, fields


def make_spec(version):
    return APISpec(
        title="Nullable nested schemas",
        version="1.0.0",
        openapi_version=version,
        plugins=[MarshmallowPlugin()],
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("version", ["3.0.0", "3.0.3"])
def test_openapi_30_nullable_nested_reference_is_object_or_reference(version):
    """OpenAPI 3.0 must not use the OpenAPI-3.1-only type:null syntax."""

    class FooSchema(Schema):
        bar = fields.Integer(required=True)

    class MySchema(Schema):
        foo = fields.Nested(FooSchema, allow_none=True)

    spec = make_spec(version)
    spec.components.schema("Foo", schema=FooSchema)
    spec.components.schema("MySchema", schema=MySchema)

    foo = spec.to_dict()["components"]["schemas"]["MySchema"]["properties"]["foo"]

    # nullable applies only to a type in its own Schema Object. It cannot be
    # placed beside an allOf containing Foo's type assertion.
    assert foo == {
        "anyOf": [
            {"type": "object", "nullable": True},
            {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Foo"},
        ]
    }


def test_openapi_30_nullable_nested_reference_with_sibling_properties():
    """The same valid nullable form is required when nesting uses allOf.

    A Nested field with metadata has sibling Schema Object properties, so the
    converter normally represents the reference through allOf.  Nullable must
    still be represented by a separate locally typed object alternative.
    """

    class FooSchema(Schema):
        bar = fields.Integer(required=True)

    class MySchema(Schema):
        foo = fields.Nested(
            FooSchema,
            allow_none=True,
            metadata={"description": "A Foo or null"},
        )

    spec = make_spec("3.0.3")
    spec.components.schema("Foo", schema=FooSchema)
    spec.components.schema("MySchema", schema=MySchema)

    foo = spec.to_dict()["components"]["schemas"]["MySchema"]["properties"]["foo"]

    assert foo["description"] == "A Foo or null"
    assert "nullable" not in foo
    assert "allOf" not in foo
    assert foo["anyOf"] == [
        {"type": "object", "nullable": True},
        {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/Foo"},
    ]


def test_openapi_30_nullable_non_reference_keeps_local_type_and_nullable():
    """Ordinary nullable fields retain OpenAPI 3.0's local nullable syntax."""

    class MySchema(Schema):
        name = fields.String(allow_none=True)

    spec = make_spec("3.0.3")
    spec.components.schema("MySchema", schema=MySchema)

    name = spec.to_dict()["components"]["schemas"]["MySchema"]["properties"]["name"]

    assert name == {"type": "string", "nullable": True}
    assert "anyOf" not in name

from striprtf.striprtf import rtf_to_text


def test_font_table_charsets_are_applied_per_selected_font_and_not_emitted():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Western Font;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese Font;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f0caf\'e9 "
        r"\f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd\'d5\'e6\'ca\'b8\'b9\'cc\'ca\'c2\'b4\'b4\'d7\'f7"
        r"\f0!}"
    )

    # Font-table contents are metadata, while the selected font's charset
    # determines the decoding of following \'xx escapes.
    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "café 根据真矢固事创作!"


def test_font_selection_and_its_encoding_are_restored_after_a_group():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Western Font;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese Font;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f0\'e9"
        r"{\f1\'b8\'f9}"
        r"\'e9}"
    )

    # RTF character properties are scoped to groups.  After the f1 group ends,
    # the final byte must again be decoded using the surrounding f0 charset.
    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "é根é"


def test_switching_between_font_charsets_decodes_each_section_independently():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Latin;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f1\'b8\'f9"
        r"\f0\'e9"
        r"\f1\'be\'dd}"
    )

    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "根é据"

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pytest

import zarr
from zarr.codecs import BytesCodec, GzipCodec, ShardingCodec, TransposeCodec
from zarr.codecs.crc32c_ import Crc32cCodec
from zarr.storage import MemoryStore, StorePath


def _create_partially_populated_sharded_array(
    *,
    compressed: bool,
) -> tuple[zarr.Array, np.ndarray]:
    """Create a shard with populated and implicit-fill inner chunks.

    This uses the layout from the interoperability report: a sharding-indexed
    codec with a nontrivial transpose, little-endian payload bytes, and a
    big-endian CRC-protected shard index.
    """
    path = StorePath(MemoryStore(mode="w")) / "interoperability-array"

    inner_codecs = [
        TransposeCodec(order=(2, 0, 1)),
        BytesCodec(endian="little"),
    ]
    if compressed:
        inner_codecs.append(GzipCodec(level=5))

    array = zarr.Array.create(
        path,
        shape=(100, 100, 50),
        chunk_shape=(10, 15, 20),
        dtype="float64",
        fill_value=-np.inf,
        codecs=[
            ShardingCodec(
                chunk_shape=(5, 3, 5),
                codecs=inner_codecs,
                index_codecs=[BytesCodec(endian="big"), Crc32cCodec()],
                index_location="start",
            )
        ],
    )

    expected = np.full(array.shape, -np.inf, dtype=np.float64)

    # Only populate a narrow strip. This leaves absent inner chunks in each
    # touched shard while placing data in multiple inner chunks and at multiple
    # byte offsets in the shard payload.
    values = (
        np.arange(30 * 2 * 50, dtype=np.float64).reshape(30, 2, 50) * 0.25 + 0.125
    )
    array[:30, 10:12, :] = values
    expected[:30, 10:12, :] = values

    # Read through a newly opened array, as a consumer of persisted data would.
    return zarr.Array.open(path), expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("compressed", "selection"),
    [
        # The exact partial read from the issue.
        (False, (slice(0, 20), slice(10, 11), slice(None))),
        # Includes both written and implicit-fill chunks, and crosses inner
        # chunk boundaries in every relevant dimension.
        (False, (slice(4, 26), slice(8, 14), slice(2, 47))),
        # Reads chunks at later offsets within the shard payload.
        (False, (slice(21, 30), slice(11, 12), slice(0, 50))),
        # The issue reports a separate failure when a compression codec is
        # included in the inner sharding pipeline.
        (True, (slice(0, 20), slice(10, 11), slice(None))),
        (True, (slice(4, 26), slice(8, 14), slice(2, 47))),
        (True, (slice(21, 30), slice(11, 12), slice(0, 50))),
    ],
    ids=[
        "uncompressed-reported-selection",
        "uncompressed-fill-and-boundaries",
        "uncompressed-later-payload-offset",
        "gzip-reported-selection",
        "gzip-fill-and-boundaries",
        "gzip-later-payload-offset",
    ],
)
def test_partial_decode_of_transposed_shards_preserves_values(
    compressed: bool,
    selection: tuple[slice, slice, slice],
) -> None:
    array, expected = _create_partially_populated_sharded_array(compressed=compressed)

    observed = array[selection]

    assert observed.shape == expected[selection].shape
    assert observed.dtype == np.dtype("float64")
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(observed, expected[selection])

from keyring import cli

def test_get_prints_password_for_anonymous_credential(
    stored_password, expected_output, capsys
):
    """
    ``get`` retrieves passwords through an AnonymousCredential, whose username
    property intentionally raises ValueError. The CLI must still print the
    password rather than attempting to read that username.
    """
    with mock.patch("keyring.cli.get_password", return_value=stored_password) as get:
        result = cli.main(["get", "service-name", "account-name"])

    assert result is None
    get.assert_called_once_with("service-name", "account-name")
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == expected_output


def test_get_json_prints_anonymous_password_without_accessing_username(capsys):
    """
    The JSON output path must also support password-mode credentials, even
    though such credentials have no username.
    """
    with mock.patch("keyring.cli.get_password", return_value="secret-value") as get:
        result = cli.main(
            ["--output", "json", "get", "service-name", "account-name"]
        )

    assert result is None
    get.assert_called_once_with("service-name", "account-name")

    output = capsys.readouterr().out
    payload = json.loads(output)
    assert payload["password"] == "secret-value"

"""Regression tests for the exit status of ``charmcraft publish-lib``."""

from argparse import Namespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands
from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand
from charmcraft.store.models import Library


class _PublishLibArgs(Namespace):
    """Arguments accepted by publish-lib across its supported invocation forms."""

    def __init__(self, output_format=None):
        super().__init__(format=output_format, libraries=[])

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        # publish-lib has historically supported both explicit libraries and
        # discovery from ``lib/``.  Defaults for optional parser arguments are
        # intentionally harmless for either form.
        if name in {"library", "libraries"}:
            return []
        return None


def _write_library(tmp_path, patch):
    """Create a discoverable charm library with the requested LIBPATCH."""
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "test_charm" / "v0" / "example.py"
    library_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    library_path.write_text(
        f'''"""A test charm library."""

LIBID = "12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc"
LIBAPI = 0
LIBPATCH = {patch}
'''
    )
    return library_path


def _published_library(patch):
    """Return the remotely published version of the test library."""
    return Library(
        lib_id="12345678-1234-1234-1234-123456789abc",
        charm_name="test-charm",
        lib_name="example",
        api=0,
        patch=patch,
        content="published library contents",
        content_hash="published-content-hash",
    )


def _run_publish_lib(monkeypatch, tmp_path, remote_libraries, output_format=None):
    """Run publish-lib against a fully local fake Store."""
    _write_library(tmp_path, patch=0)
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    fake_store = MagicMock()
    fake_store.list_libraries.return_value = remote_libraries

    # The command's analysis has used these Store queries in different
    # charmcraft releases.  They all describe the same already-published
    # library for this regression scenario.
    fake_store.get_library.return_value = (
        remote_libraries[0] if remote_libraries else None
    )
    fake_store.get_library_revision.return_value = (
        remote_libraries[0] if remote_libraries else None
    )
    fake_store.list_library_revisions.return_value = remote_libraries

    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", lambda *args, **kwargs: fake_store)

    command = PublishLibCommand.__new__(PublishLibCommand)
    result = command.run(_PublishLibArgs(output_format))
    return result, fake_store


@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
def test_publish_lib_fails_when_libpatch_was_not_bumped(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path, output_format
):
    """A rejected publication must have a non-zero command exit status."""
    result, fake_store = _run_publish_lib(
        monkeypatch,
        tmp_path,
        [_published_library(patch=0)],
        output_format,
    )

    assert result != 0
    fake_store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()


def test_publish_lib_fails_when_one_of_multiple_libraries_is_rejected(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """A partial publish must still fail, so CI cannot overlook the rejection."""
    _write_library(tmp_path, patch=0)
    second_library = (
        tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "test_charm" / "v0" / "second_example.py"
    )
    second_library.write_text(
        '''LIBID = "87654321-4321-4321-4321-cba987654321"
LIBAPI = 0
LIBPATCH = 1
'''
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    fake_store = MagicMock()
    fake_store.list_libraries.return_value = [_published_library(patch=0)]
    fake_store.get_library.return_value = _published_library(patch=0)
    fake_store.get_library_revision.return_value = _published_library(patch=0)
    fake_store.list_library_revisions.return_value = [_published_library(patch=0)]
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", lambda *args, **kwargs: fake_store)

    command = PublishLibCommand.__new__(PublishLibCommand)

    assert command.run(_PublishLibArgs()) != 0


def test_publish_lib_succeeds_when_no_library_is_rejected(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """The non-zero status is reserved for publication failures."""
    result, fake_store = _run_publish_lib(monkeypatch, tmp_path, [])

    assert result in (None, 0)
    fake_store.create_library_revision.assert_called()

"""Regression tests for single-contrast (3D) template-alignment inputs."""

import numpy as np
from nibabel import Nifti1Image

from fmralign.template_alignment import TemplateAlignment


SHAPE = (4, 5, 6)
AFFINE = np.eye(4)


def _contrast(value):
    """Create a spatial 3D contrast image."""
    data = np.arange(np.prod(SHAPE), dtype=float).reshape(SHAPE) + value
    return Nifti1Image(data, AFFINE)


def _model():
    return TemplateAlignment(
        alignment_method="identity",
        n_pieces=1,
        n_iter=1,
        mask=Nifti1Image(np.ones(SHAPE, dtype=np.int8), AFFINE),
    )


def test_template_fit_accepts_3d_single_contrast_subjects():
    """3D source images must be compatible with the singleton-4D template."""
    model = _model()

    model.fit([_contrast(1), _contrast(2)])

    # A template inferred from one contrast per subject has one sample.
    assert model.template.shape == SHAPE + (1,)


def test_template_alignment_predicts_from_3d_single_contrast_inputs():
    """A 3D target contrast represents one sample, not ``shape[-1]`` samples.

    The public transform API documents a list of 3D target images.  Therefore
    it must accept that form when mapping/predicting the sole contrast of a
    singleton-4D template.
    """
    model = _model()
    model.fit([_contrast(1), _contrast(2)])

    predictions = model.transform(
        [_contrast(3), _contrast(4)],
        train_index=[0],
        test_index=[0],
    )

    assert len(predictions) == 2
    assert all(prediction.shape == SHAPE + (1,) for prediction in predictions)


def test_template_alignment_predicts_from_singleton_lists_of_3d_contrasts():
    """The list-of-3D input form also supports subjects with one contrast."""
    model = _model()
    model.fit([[_contrast(1)], [_contrast(2)]])

    predictions = model.transform(
        [[_contrast(3)], [_contrast(4)]],
        train_index=[0],
        test_index=[0],
    )

    assert len(predictions) == 2
    assert all(prediction.shape == SHAPE + (1,) for prediction in predictions)

"""Regression tests for language-specific C++ warnings in C files."""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


CPPLINT = Path(__file__).with_name("cpplint.py")

# Each construct reliably produces one of the C++-specific warnings that must
# not be emitted for .c/.C/.h/.H files.
_SOURCE = """\
double get_value(void);

int convert_value(void) {
  double value = get_value();
  int converted = (int)value;
  long long wide_value = 0;
  return converted + (int)wide_value;
}
"""

_TARGET_CATEGORIES = ("readability/casting", "runtime/int")


def _lint(*filenames: Path) -> str:
    """Run cpplint with only the categories relevant to this behavior enabled."""
    command = [
        sys.executable,
        str(CPPLINT),
        "--extensions=c,C,h,H,cc",
        "--filter=-,+readability/casting,+runtime/int",
        *(str(filename) for filename in filenames),
    ]
    result = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=CPPLINT.parent,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )
    return result.stdout + result.stderr


def _category_lines(output: str, filename: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Return selected-category diagnostics reported for one file."""
    prefix = f"{filename}:"
    return [
        line
        for line in output.splitlines()
        if line.startswith(prefix)
        and any(f"[{category}]" in line for category in _TARGET_CATEGORIES)
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("extension", ("c", "C", "h", "H"))
def test_cpp_specific_warnings_are_skipped_only_for_c_extensions(
    tmp_path: Path,
    extension: str,
) -> None:
    """C spelling variants suppress these warnings without suppressing C++ files.

    Linting both files in one invocation also verifies that a suppression for a
    C file does not leak into the C++ file that follows it.
    """
    c_file = tmp_path / f"implementation.{extension}"
    cpp_file = tmp_path / "implementation.cc"
    c_file.write_text(_SOURCE, encoding="utf-8")
    cpp_file.write_text(_SOURCE, encoding="utf-8")

    output = _lint(c_file, cpp_file)

    assert _category_lines(output, c_file) == [], output

    cpp_diagnostics = _category_lines(output, cpp_file)
    for category in _TARGET_CATEGORIES:
        assert any(f"[{category}]" in line for line in cpp_diagnostics), output

import ast
from typing import Any, Iterable

import pytest

from func_adl import ObjectStream
from func_adl.type_based_replacement import remap_by_types


class Jet:
    def pt(self) -> float: ...


class Event:
    def Jets(self) -> Iterable[Jet]: ...


def _expression(source: str) -> ast.AST:
    return ast.parse(source).body[0].value


def _stream() -> ObjectStream[Event]:
    return ObjectStream[Event](ast.Name(id="e", ctx=ast.Load()))


def test_dict_zip_function_lookup_returns_any_instead_of_failing():
    """Zip is a backend function rather than a dictionary key."""
    query = _expression("{'pt': 1, 'eta': 2}.Zip()")

    _, _, expression_type = remap_by_types(_stream(), "e", Event, query)

    assert expression_type is Any


def test_dict_zip_function_lookup_allows_complete_expression_to_be_traced():
    """The type fallback for Zip must allow its result to be used normally."""
    query = _expression(
        "{'pt': 1, 'eta': 2}.Zip()"
        ".Where(lambda particle: particle.pt > 30 and abs(particle.eta) < 2.1)"
        ".Count() == 1"
    )

    _, _, expression_type = remap_by_types(_stream(), "e", Event, query)

    assert expression_type is bool


def test_unknown_dictionary_key_still_reports_a_typo():
    """Backend method support must not hide misspelled typed dictionary keys.

    ``jetsss`` is an attribute lookup, not a call itself. Thus it cannot be
    treated as an unknown backend function such as ``Zip()``.
    """
    query = _expression("{'jets': e.Jets()}.jetsss.Select(lambda jet: jet.pt())")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="jetsss"):
        remap_by_types(_stream(), "e", Event, query)


def test_known_dictionary_key_keeps_its_inferred_type():
    """The special handling for unknown functions must preserve known fields."""
    query = _expression("{'jets': e.Jets()}.jets.Select(lambda jet: jet.pt())")

    _, _, expression_type = remap_by_types(_stream(), "e", Event, query)

    assert expression_type == Iterable[float]

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_postgres_insert_target_alias_with_conflict_update_where():
    sql = """
    INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c) VALUES (1, 2, 3)
    ON CONFLICT (c)
    DO UPDATE
       SET a = t.a + 1
    WHERE t.a < 1
    """

    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    assert isinstance(expression, exp.Insert)
    assert [table.name for table in expression.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["newtable"]

    conflict = expression.find(exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict is not None

    # Both references to the INSERT target alias must parse as qualified columns:
    # one in the assignment and one in the conflict-update predicate.
    aliased_columns = [
        column for column in expression.find_all(exp.Column) if column.table == "t"
    ]
    assert [column.name for column in aliased_columns] == ["a", "a"]

    # SQL generated from the parsed tree must retain a valid target alias before
    # the INSERT column list, and must remain parseable by the Postgres reader.
    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c)" in rendered
    reparsed = parse_one(rendered, read="postgres")
    assert [
        column.name for column in reparsed.find_all(exp.Column) if column.table == "t"
    ] == ["a", "a"]


def test_postgres_insert_target_alias_before_column_list():
    """The alias belongs to the target table, not to an INSERT column."""
    expression = parse_one(
        "INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c) VALUES (1, 2, 3)",
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert isinstance(expression, exp.Insert)
    assert [table.name for table in expression.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["newtable"]

    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c)" in rendered
    parse_one(rendered, read="postgres")

class RecordingFitter:
    """A fitter substitute that records the data supplied to the fitter."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.dispersion = None
        self.flux = None

    def __call__(self, model, dispersion, flux, weights=None, **kwargs):
        self.dispersion = dispersion
        self.flux = flux
        return model


def _selected_dispersion(spectrum, model, window):
    fitter = RecordingFitter()
    fit_lines(spectrum, model, fitter=fitter, window=window)
    return np.asarray(fitter.dispersion.value)


def _spectrum_and_compound_gaussian():
    spectral_axis = np.arange(0, 21) * u.AA
    spectrum = Spectrum1D(
        spectral_axis=spectral_axis,
        flux=np.arange(spectral_axis.size) * u.Jy,
    )

    # This is the Gaussian plus constant model from the reported use case.
    model = (
        models.Gaussian1D(
            amplitude=5 * u.Jy,
            mean=10 * u.AA,
            stddev=1 * u.AA,
        )
        + models.Const1D(amplitude=0 * u.Jy)
    )
    return spectrum, model

def test_resolve_supplies_runtime_values_to_keyword_only_constructor_arguments():
    class EndpointClient:
        def __init__(self, *, endpoint):
            self.endpoint = endpoint

    container = punq.Container()
    container.register(EndpointClient)

    client = container.resolve(EndpointClient, endpoint="https://example.test")

    assert client.endpoint == "https://example.test"


def test_keyword_only_dependencies_and_defaults_are_used_when_building_an_implementation():
    class Connection:
        pass

    default_retries = 3

    class Worker:
        def __init__(
            self,
            connection: Connection,
            *,
            backup_connection: Connection,
            retries: int = default_retries,
            name: str,
        ):
            self.connection = connection
            self.backup_connection = backup_connection
            self.retries = retries
            self.name = name

    container = punq.Container()
    container.register(Connection)
    container.register(Worker)

    worker = container.resolve(Worker, name="import-job")

    assert isinstance(worker.connection, Connection)
    assert worker.backup_connection is worker.connection
    assert worker.retries == default_retries
    assert worker.name == "import-job"


def test_registration_arguments_can_configure_a_self_registered_keyword_only_argument():
    class RetryPolicy:
        def __init__(self, *, retries: int):
            self.retries = retries

    container = punq.Container()
    container.register(RetryPolicy, retries=7)

    policy = container.resolve(RetryPolicy)

    assert policy.retries == 7

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _with_fill(expression):
    with_fill = expression.find(exp.WithFill)
    assert with_fill is not None, "WITH FILL should be represented in the parsed expression tree"
    return with_fill


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_bare_column_with_datetime_bounds():
    sql = """
        SELECT
            1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
            'test' interp
        ORDER BY DATETIME
        WITH FILL
        FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
        TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
        STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
        INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)

    # The complete WITH FILL clause must remain attached to ORDER BY, rather
    # than merely accepting INTERPOLATE and losing its bounds or step.
    assert with_fill.args["from"] is not None
    assert with_fill.args["to"] is not None
    assert with_fill.args["step"] is not None
    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 1

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "WITH FILL" in generated
    assert "INTERPOLATE (" in generated

    # Generated ClickHouse SQL must remain parseable; this also guards against
    # creating an invalid Alias node for a bare interpolation column.
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read="clickhouse")
    assert len(_with_fill(reparsed).args["interpolate"]) == 1


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_preserves_explicit_expression_syntax():
    sql = """
        SELECT n, inter
        FROM numbers(1)
        ORDER BY n
        WITH FILL
        INTERPOLATE (inter AS inter + 1)
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)
    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 1

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")

    # ClickHouse's syntax is <column> AS <expression>, not the normal SQL
    # alias order. Supporting a bare item must not reverse existing explicit
    # interpolation expressions.
    assert "INTERPOLATE (inter AS inter + 1)" in generated
    sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read="clickhouse")


def test_clickhouse_interpolate_allows_bare_and_explicit_items_together():
    sql = """
        SELECT a, b, c
        FROM t
        ORDER BY a
        WITH FILL
        INTERPOLATE (a AS a + 1, b, c AS 'fallback')
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)
    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 3

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "a AS a + 1" in generated
    assert "c AS 'fallback'" in generated

    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read="clickhouse")
    assert len(_with_fill(reparsed).args["interpolate"]) == 3

def _properties_with_reference(reader, attribute, value):
    return [

        for model in reader.models
        for prop in model.properties.values()

    ]


def test_xsd_reader_resolves_qualified_element_ref_after_target_is_created(tmp_path):
    schema = tmp_path / "qualified-ref.xsd"
    schema.write_text(
        """\
        <xs:schema
            xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema"
            xmlns:tns="urn:example"
            targetNamespace="urn:example">

          <!-- The referenced declaration comes after its user. -->
          <xs:element name="HasAddress">
            <xs:complexType>
              <xs:choice>
                <xs:element ref="tns:Address"/>
              </xs:choice>
            </xs:complexType>
          </xs:element>

          <xs:element name="Address">
            <xs:complexType/>
          </xs:element>
        </xs:schema>
        """,
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    reader = XSDReader(str(schema), dataset_name="example")
