import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _stream_tables(expression):
    return [table for table in expression.find_all(exp.Table) if table.name.lower() == "stream"]


def test_create_table_as_with_cte_named_stream_is_a_normal_cte_reference():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo AS
        WITH stream AS (
            SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT * FROM stream;
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(expression, exp.Create)
    query = expression.expression
    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)

    assert len(query.ctes) == 1
    cte = query.ctes[0]
    assert cte.alias_or_name.lower() == "stream"
    assert isinstance(cte.this, exp.Select)

    # Both the source inside the CTE and the CTE reference itself must be tables,
    # rather than the special Stream expression.
    assert sorted(table.name.lower() for table in query.find_all(exp.Table)) == ["bar", "stream"]
    assert not list(query.find_all(exp.Stream))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("cte_name", ["stream", "STREAM", "StReAm"])
def test_cte_name_stream_is_valid_for_all_unquoted_casings(cte_name):
    query = sqlglot.parse_one(
        f"""
        WITH {cte_name} AS (
            SELECT 1 AS value
        )
        SELECT {cte_name}.value
        FROM {cte_name}
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)
    assert len(query.ctes) == 1
    assert query.ctes[0].alias_or_name.lower() == "stream"

    stream_tables = _stream_tables(query)
    assert len(stream_tables) == 1
    assert stream_tables[0].name.lower() == "stream"

    column = next(query.find_all(exp.Column))
    assert column.table.lower() == "stream"
    assert not list(query.find_all(exp.Stream))


def test_stream_cte_can_be_used_with_other_ctes_and_a_table_alias():
    query = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        WITH seed AS (
            SELECT 1 AS id
        ),
        stream AS (
            SELECT id FROM seed
        ),
        result AS (
            SELECT s.id FROM stream AS s
        )
        SELECT * FROM result
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)
    assert [cte.alias_or_name.lower() for cte in query.ctes] == ["seed", "stream", "result"]

    stream_tables = _stream_tables(query)
    assert len(stream_tables) == 1
    assert stream_tables[0].alias_or_name.lower() == "s"
    assert not list(query.find_all(exp.Stream))


def test_unquoted_stream_remains_a_valid_regular_table_name():
    query = sqlglot.parse_one("SELECT * FROM stream AS s")

    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)
    stream_tables = _stream_tables(query)
    assert len(stream_tables) == 1
    assert stream_tables[0].alias_or_name == "s"
    assert not list(query.find_all(exp.Stream))

    plugin = Kick(session, url)
    requests = []

    def get(request_url, **kwargs):
        requests.append((request_url, kwargs))

        if request_url == "https://kick.com/":
            return type("Response", (), {"cookies": {"XSRF-TOKEN": "csrf-token"}})()

        assert request_url == api_url
        return api_result

    monkeypatch.setattr(session.http, "get", get)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "streamlink.plugins.kick.HLSStream.parse_variant_playlist",
        lambda _session, _url: {"source": DummyHLSStream()},
    )

    streams = plugin.streams()

    # Plugin.streams() adds the best/worst aliases to parsed streams.
    assert {"best", "worst"} <= set(streams)
    assert [request[0] for request in requests] == ["https://kick.com/", api_url]

    # The initial request which obtains the XSRF token needs browser navigation
    # headers, rather than Streamlink's generic HTTP-client defaults.
    assert session.http.headers["User-Agent"].startswith("Mozilla/")
    assert "text/html" in session.http.headers["Accept"]
    assert session.http.headers["Sec-Fetch-Dest"] == "document"
    assert session.http.headers["Sec-Fetch-Mode"] == "navigate"
    assert session.http.headers["Sec-Fetch-Site"] == "none"
    assert session.http.headers["Sec-Fetch-User"] == "?1"

    api_kwargs = requests[1][1]
    assert api_kwargs["acceptable_status"] == (200, 404)

    api_headers = api_kwargs["headers"]
    assert api_headers["Accept"] == "application/json"
    assert api_headers["Accept-Language"].startswith("en-US")
    assert api_headers["Referer"] == url
    assert api_headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer csrf-token"
    assert api_headers["Sec-Fetch-Dest"] == "empty"
    assert api_headers["Sec-Fetch-Mode"] == "cors"
    assert api_headers["Sec-Fetch-Site"] == "same-origin"
    assert api_headers["X-Requested-With"] == "XMLHttpRequest"

    for attribute, value in expected_metadata.items():
        assert getattr(plugin, attribute) == value


def test_kick_does_not_send_an_empty_bearer_token(monkeypatch):
    """A failed token lookup must not produce an invalid ``Authorization`` header."""
    plugin = Kick(Streamlink(), "https://kick.com/live_channel")

    def get(request_url, **kwargs):
        assert request_url == "https://kick.com/"
        return type("Response", (), {"cookies": {}})()

    monkeypatch.setattr(plugin.session.http, "get", get)

    headers = plugin._get_api_headers()

    assert headers["Accept"] == "application/json"
    assert headers["Referer"] == "https://kick.com/live_channel"
    assert "Authorization" not in headers

"""Tests for reporting the JWST software version at pipeline completion."""

import logging

from jwst import __version__
from jwst.stpipe import core
from jwst.stpipe.core import JwstPipeline
from stdatamodels.jwst import datamodels


class _LoggingTestPipeline(JwstPipeline):
    """A pipeline with no reference-file lookups or processing side effects."""

    def process(self, input_model):
        self.log.info("TEST: pipeline processing has completed")
        return input_model


def test_pipeline_logs_installed_jwst_version_after_crds_context(monkeypatch, caplog):
    """
    A pipeline completion summary must include the installed JWST version
    directly beside the existing CRDS context summary.

    No reference files are requested by this pipeline.  Pipeline-level output
    must nevertheless state which JWST software produced its result.
    """
    context = "jwst_test_context_for_version_logging"
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        core.crds_client,
        "get_context_used",
        lambda observatory: context,
    )

    model = datamodels.ImageModel((2, 2))
    pipeline = _LoggingTestPipeline()

    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger=core.__name__)
    try:
        result = pipeline.run(model)

        messages = [record.getMessage() for record in caplog.records]
        processing_index = messages.index("TEST: pipeline processing has completed")
        context_message = f"Results used CRDS context: {context}"

        # Logging configurations can cause a LogRecord to be observed more
        # than once.  The final CRDS report is the pipeline's completion
        # summary, so assess the message immediately following that report.
        context_indices = [
            index
            for index, message in enumerate(messages)
            if message == context_message
        ]
        assert context_indices
        context_index = context_indices[-1]

        # This is completion information, not a startup/configuration message.
        assert context_index > processing_index

        # The version is intentionally placed at the end, alongside the
        # existing CRDS context report.  Verify the real package version rather
        # than merely accepting a generic "version" message.
        assert context_index + 1 < len(messages)
        version_message = messages[context_index + 1]
        assert "jwst" in version_message.lower()
        assert "version" in version_message.lower()
        assert __version__ in version_message
    finally:
        if "result" in locals() and result is not model:
            result.close()
        model.close()

import sqlglot


def test_duckdb_unpacks_columns_inside_struct_pack_and_round_trips():
    sql = r"""
        SELECT id, struct_pack(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements
        FROM many_measurements
    """

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, dialect="duckdb")
    generated = expression.sql(dialect="duckdb")

    assert generated == (
        r"SELECT id, STRUCT_PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements FROM many_measurements"
    )
    assert sqlglot.parse_one(generated, dialect="duckdb").sql(dialect="duckdb") == generated


def test_duckdb_unpacks_columns_for_other_function_calls():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT coalesce(*COLUMNS('first_|last_'), 'unknown') FROM people",
        dialect="duckdb",
    )

    assert expression.sql(dialect="duckdb") == (
        "SELECT COALESCE(*COLUMNS('first_|last_'), 'unknown') FROM people"
    )


def test_duckdb_existing_star_function_arguments_remain_supported():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT struct_pack(*) FROM measurements",
        dialect="duckdb",
    )

    assert expression.sql(dialect="duckdb") == "SELECT STRUCT_PACK(*) FROM measurements"

"""Regression tests for the exit status of ``charmcraft publish-lib``."""

from argparse import Namespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands
from charmcraft.application.commands.store import PublishLibCommand
from charmcraft.store.models import Library
from charmcraft.utils import charmlibs


def _library(name: str, patch: int) -> Library:
    """Create metadata representing a local or published charm library."""
    return Library(
        charm_name="test-charm",
        lib_name=name,
        lib_id=f"test-charm.{name}.v0",
        api=0,
        patch=patch,
        content=f"# Library {name}\n",
        content_hash=f"hash-for-{name}-{patch}",
    )


def _args(**overrides) -> Namespace:
    """Build arguments accepted by ``PublishLibCommand.run``."""
    values = {
        "format": None,
        "library": None,
        "libraries": None,
    }
    values.update(overrides)
    return Namespace(**values)


def _command(monkeypatch, local_libraries, remote_libraries):
    """Set up the command with local library and store interactions isolated."""
    store = MagicMock()
    store.list_libraries.return_value = remote_libraries
    store.get_libraries.return_value = remote_libraries

    # Library discovery has moved between these utility entry points in
    # Charmcraft versions; patch both so the command is tested without reading
    # a charm project from disk.
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        store_commands.utils,
        "get_libs",
        lambda *args, **kwargs: local_libraries,
        raising=False,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        charmlibs,
        "get_libs",
        lambda *args, **kwargs: local_libraries,
        raising=False,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", lambda *args, **kwargs: store)

    return PublishLibCommand(MagicMock()), store


def test_publish_lib_returns_nonzero_when_patch_was_not_bumped(monkeypatch, emitter):
    """An unchanged LIBPATCH rejected by Charmhub must fail the command."""
    local = _library("mylib", patch=4)
    remote = _library("mylib", patch=4)
    command, store = _command(monkeypatch, [local], [remote])

    result = command.run(_args())

    assert result != 0
    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()


def test_publish_lib_returns_nonzero_when_patch_goes_back(monkeypatch, emitter):
    """A local LIBPATCH lower than the published revision must fail."""
    local = _library("mylib", patch=4)
    remote = _library("mylib", patch=5)
    command, store = _command(monkeypatch, [local], [remote])

    result = command.run(_args())

    assert result != 0
    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()


def test_publish_lib_fails_batch_when_one_library_is_rejected(monkeypatch, emitter):
    """A partial publish must still have a failing status for CI."""
    publishable = _library("publishable", patch=2)
    stale = _library("stale", patch=4)
    remote_publishable = _library("publishable", patch=1)
    remote_stale = _library("stale", patch=5)
    command, store = _command(
        monkeypatch,
        [publishable, stale],
        [remote_publishable, remote_stale],
    )

    result = command.run(_args())

    assert result != 0
    assert store.create_library_revision.call_count == 1


def test_publish_lib_with_bumped_patch_remains_successful(monkeypatch, emitter):
    """A valid new library revision must not be reported as a failure."""
    local = _library("mylib", patch=2)
    remote = _library("mylib", patch=1)
    command, store = _command(monkeypatch, [local], [remote])

    result = command.run(_args())

    assert result in (None, 0)
    assert store.create_library_revision.call_count == 1

import ast
import textwrap
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Iterable

import pytest

from func_adl import ObjectStream
from func_adl.type_based_replacement import remap_by_types


@dataclass
class Event:
    Electron_pt: Iterable[float]
    Electron_eta: Iterable[float]
    Electron_cutBased: Iterable[int]
    Electron_sip3d: Iterable[float]

    Muon_pt: Iterable[float]
    Muon_eta: Iterable[float]
    Muon_tightId: Iterable[bool]
    Muon_sip3d: Iterable[float]
    Muon_pfRelIso04_all: Iterable[float]

    Jet_pt: Iterable[float]
    Jet_eta: Iterable[float]
    Jet_jetId: Iterable[int]
    Jet_btagCSVV2: Iterable[float]


def expression(source: str) -> ast.AST:
    return ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(source), mode="eval").body


def remap(source: str, variable_name: str = "e", variable_type=Event):
    stream = ObjectStream(ast.Name(id=variable_name, ctx=ast.Load()), variable_type)
    return remap_by_types(stream, variable_name, variable_type, expression(source))


def test_zip_on_typed_dictionary_is_treated_as_a_function_lookup():
    """Zip is not a dictionary key, even though the dictionary fields are typed."""
    _, _, result_type = remap("{'pt': e.Electron_pt, 'eta': e.Electron_eta}.Zip()")

    # Zip is backend-defined, so type tracing must fall back rather than fail.
    assert result_type is Any


def test_zip_can_be_used_in_the_agc_style_selection_chain():
    """Regression test for the nested Zip/Where/Count pattern from the report."""
    query = """
        events.Where(
            lambda e:
                {'pt': e.Electron_pt,
                 'eta': e.Electron_eta,
                 'cutBased': e.Electron_cutBased,
                 'sip3d': e.Electron_sip3d}.Zip()
                .Where(lambda electron:
                    electron.pt > 30
                    and abs(electron.eta) < 2.1
                    and electron.cutBased == 4
                    and electron.sip3d < 4)
                .Count()
                +
                {'pt': e.Muon_pt,
                 'eta': e.Muon_eta,
                 'tightId': e.Muon_tightId,
                 'sip3d': e.Muon_sip3d,
                 'pfRelIso04_all': e.Muon_pfRelIso04_all}.Zip()
                .Where(lambda muon:
                    muon.pt > 30
                    and abs(muon.eta) < 2.1
                    and muon.tightId
                    and muon.pfRelIso04_all < 0.15)
                .Count() == 1
        ).Where(
            lambda f:
                {'pt': f.Jet_pt,
                 'eta': f.Jet_eta,
                 'jetId': f.Jet_jetId}.Zip()
                .Where(lambda jet:
                    jet.pt > 25 and abs(jet.eta) < 2.4 and jet.jetId == 6)
                .Count() >= 4
        ).Where(
            lambda g:
                {'pt': g.Jet_pt,
                 'eta': g.Jet_eta,
                 'btagCSVV2': g.Jet_btagCSVV2,
                 'jetId': g.Jet_jetId}.Zip()
                .Where(lambda jet:
                    jet.btagCSVV2 > 0.5
                    and jet.pt > 25
                    and abs(jet.eta) < 2.4
                    and jet.jetId == 6)
                .Count() >= 1
        )
    """

    stream = ObjectStream(ast.Name(id="events", ctx=ast.Load()), Event)
    _, _, result_type = remap_by_types(
        stream, "events", Iterable[Event], expression(query)
    )

    assert result_type == Iterable[Event]


def test_dictionary_typing_still_rejects_misspelled_keys_and_methods():
    """Allowing Zip must not turn genuine typed-dictionary typos into Any."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ptt"):
        remap("{'pt': e.Electron_pt, 'eta': e.Electron_eta}.ptt")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Zipp"):
        remap("{'pt': e.Electron_pt, 'eta': e.Electron_eta}.Zipp()")

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields

from xsdata.formats.dataclass.filters import Filters
from xsdata.formats.dataclass.parsers import XmlParser
from xsdata.models.config import GeneratorConfig
from xsdata.models.enums import DataType
from xsdata.utils.testing import AttrFactory, ClassFactory


def test_generated_ignore_fields_do_not_break_repr_of_parsed_models():
    """Generated prohibited fields must be omitted from dataclass repr.

    ``type=Ignore`` fields are generated with ``init=False`` and are not set
    on parsed instances. Dataclass repr must consequently exclude them.
    """
    filters = Filters(GeneratorConfig())
    model = ClassFactory.create(qname="generated")

    prohibited = AttrFactory.native(DataType.STRING)
    prohibited.restrictions.max_occurs = 0
    ignored_definition = filters.field_definition(model, prohibited, None)

    namespace = {"dataclass": dataclass, "field": field}
    exec(
        "\n".join(
            [
                "@dataclass",
                "class Generated:",
                '    value: str = field(metadata={"type": "Element"})',
                f"    ignored_one: object = {ignored_definition}",
                f"    ignored_two: object = {ignored_definition}",
            ]
        ),
        namespace,
    )
    generated_type = namespace["Generated"]

    parsed = XmlParser().from_string(
        "<Generated><value>available</value></Generated>",
        generated_type,
    )

    ignored_fields = fields(generated_type)[1:]
    assert all(item.metadata["type"] == "Ignore" for item in ignored_fields)
    assert all(item.init is False for item in ignored_fields)
    assert all(item.repr is False for item in ignored_fields)
    assert not hasattr(parsed, "ignored_one")
    assert not hasattr(parsed, "ignored_two")

    assert repr(parsed) == "Generated(value='available')"

    @dataclass
    class Parent:
        child: generated_type

    nested_representation = repr(Parent(parsed))
    assert "child=Generated(value='available')" in nested_representation
    assert "ignored_one" not in nested_representation
    assert "ignored_two" not in nested_representation

import threading
import time
from unittest import mock

from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import client
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber import scheduler
from google.cloud.pubsub_v1.subscriber._protocol import streaming_pull_manager
from google.pubsub_v1 import types as gapic_types


def _response():
    return gapic_types.StreamingPullResponse(
        received_messages=[
            gapic_types.ReceivedMessage(
                ack_id="ack-id",
                message=gapic_types.PubsubMessage(
                    data=b"message data",
                    message_id="message-id",
                ),
            )
        ]
    )


def _manager_with_running_helpers():
    manager = streaming_pull_manager.StreamingPullManager(
        mock.create_autospec(client.Client, instance=True),
        "projects/project/subscriptions/subscription",
        scheduler=scheduler.ThreadScheduler(),
    )

    manager._consumer = mock.Mock()
    manager._consumer.is_active = True
    manager._consumer.is_paused = False
    manager._dispatcher = mock.Mock()
    manager._heartbeater = mock.Mock()
    manager._callback = mock.Mock()

    leaser_ = mock.Mock()
    leaser_.message_count = 0
    leaser_.bytes = 0
    manager._leaser = leaser_

    # Avoid lease-extension details unrelated to the scheduler shutdown race.
    manager._send_lease_modacks = mock.Mock(return_value=set())
    manager._maybe_release_messages = mock.Mock()

    return manager


def test_on_response_does_not_use_scheduler_torn_down_by_concurrent_close():
    """An in-flight response must not observe shutdown halfway through processing.

    The response is paused after entering _on_response's scheduling critical
    section. Closing the manager at that point must not set _scheduler to None
    while _on_response can subsequently use it.
    """
    manager = _manager_with_running_helpers()
    response_in_critical_section = threading.Event()
    allow_response_to_continue = threading.Event()
    response_errors = []

    def pause_response_processing():
        # This is invoked from _on_response after it enters the
        # _pause_resume_lock-protected block and before scheduler.queue is used.
        response_in_critical_section.set()
        assert allow_response_to_continue.wait(timeout=5)
        return False

    manager._exactly_once_delivery_enabled = pause_response_processing

    def invoke_response():
        try:
            manager._on_response(_response())
        except BaseException as exc:
            response_errors.append(exc)

    response_thread = threading.Thread(target=invoke_response)
    response_thread.start()
    assert response_in_critical_section.wait(timeout=5)

    # close() starts the regular shutdown worker which tears down scheduler and
    # leaser. In the broken implementation this occurs despite _on_response
    # already having passed its None check.
    manager.close()

    deadline = time.monotonic() + 1
    while manager._scheduler is not None and time.monotonic() < deadline:
        time.sleep(0.01)

    allow_response_to_continue.set()
    response_thread.join(timeout=5)
    assert not response_thread.is_alive()

    shutdown_thread = manager._regular_shutdown_thread
    if shutdown_thread is not None:
        shutdown_thread.join(timeout=5)
        assert not shutdown_thread.is_alive()

    assert response_errors == []


def test_on_response_ignores_response_after_shutdown_helpers_are_gone():
    """A late response after shutdown must be discarded instead of asserting."""
    manager = _manager_with_running_helpers()

    manager._scheduler = None
    manager._leaser = None

    manager._on_response(_response())

    # Modack handling occurs before received messages are scheduled. The
    # received message must not be dispatched once scheduling helpers are gone.
    manager._send_lease_modacks.assert_called_once()

    State,

def _model(reader, *, is_root=False, source=""):

    model.source = source
    return model


def _reference_property(name, *, ref_to=None, type_to=None):
    prop = XSDProperty(
        xsd_name=name,
        property_type=XSDType(name="ref"),
        source=name,
    )
    prop.name = name
    prop.xsd_ref_to = ref_to
    prop.xsd_type_to = type_to

def test_post_process_refs_links_root_properties_to_element_and_complex_type_models():
    reader = XSDReader("schema.xsd", "dataset")

    element_target = _model(reader)
    element_target.set_name("Person")

    complex_type_target = _model(reader)
    complex_type_target.set_name("Address")

    referring_model = _model(reader, is_root=True, source="Order")
    referring_model.properties["person"] = _reference_property(
        "person",
        ref_to="Person",

    referring_model.properties["address"] = _reference_property(
        "address",
        type_to="AddressType",

{\*\generator Riched20 10.0.19041}\viewkind4\uc1
\pard\ltrpar\f0\fs17 [HEADER]\par
[/HEADER]\par
[BODY]\par
[1]\par
00:00:44:22\par

\f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd\'d5\'e6\'ca\'b5\'b9\'ca\'ca\'c2\'b4\'b4\'d7\'f7\f0\par

        "00:00:48:05\n"

def test_font_charset_is_selected_per_font_and_font_table_text_is_ignored():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Latin Font;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese Font;}"
        r"{\f2\fnil\fcharset204 Cyrillic Font;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f0\'e9 \f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd \f2\'cf\'f0}"
    )

    # é is cp1252, 根据 is GB2312, and Пр is cp1251.
    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "é 根据 Пр"


def test_font_selection_is_restored_after_a_nested_group():
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Latin Font;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese Font;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f0\'e9 {\f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd} \'e9}"
    )

    # Character formatting, including the selected font, is scoped to an RTF
    # group. Leaving the f1 group restores f0 for the final hex escape.
    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "é 根据 é"

        r"}"
        r"\f0\'cf\'f0 \f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd}"

from conllu import parse


def parse_deps_value(deps):
    document = (
        "1\tRemoved\tremove\tVERB\t_\t_\t0\troot\t{}\t_\n\n"
    ).format(deps)
    return parse(document)[0][0]["deps"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

    [
        (
            "1:compound|6:ARG1|9:ARG1",
            [("compound", 1), ("ARG1", 6), ("ARG1", 9)],
        ),
        ("4:ARG1", [("ARG1", 4)]),
        ("5:measure", [("measure", 5)]),
        ("2:OBJ|3:NMOD", [("OBJ", 2), ("NMOD", 3)]),
        ("1:nsubj:pass|2:ARG1:theme", [("nsubj:pass", 1), ("ARG1:theme", 2)]),
        ("3.1:ARG1", [("ARG1", (3, ".", 1))]),
    ],
)
def test_deps_with_uppercase_and_numeric_relation_labels_are_parsed(deps, expected):
    """Valid enhanced dependencies must not be left as an unparsed string."""
    assert parse_deps_value(deps) == expected


def test_root_dependency_in_deps_column_is_parsed():
    """The DEPS column may point to the artificial root using head ID 0."""
    document = (
        "1\tRemoved\tremove\tVERB\t_\t_\t0\troot\t0:root\t_\n"
        "2\t.\t.\tPUNCT\t_\t_\t1\tpunct\t1:punct\t_\n\n"
    )

    sentence = parse(document)[0]

    assert sentence[0]["deps"] == [("root", 0)]
    assert sentence[1]["deps"] == [("punct", 1)]

import os

from click.testing import CliRunner

from reana_client.cli import cli


def test_upload_without_sources_uploads_entire_workspace_and_honours_ignores(
    monkeypatch,
):
    """Default upload includes all non-ignored files below the current directory."""
    uploaded_files = []

    def upload_to_server(workflow, filename, access_token):
        uploaded_files.append(os.path.relpath(filename, os.getcwd()))
        return [filename]

    # Only one input is declared on purpose. Files needed to load or execute
    # the workflow must be uploaded even if they are absent from inputs.files.
    def get_workflow_specification(workflow, access_token):
        return {
            "specification": {
                "inputs": {
                    "files": ["data/declared-input.txt"],
                }
            }
        }

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "reana_client.api.client.upload_to_server",
        upload_to_server,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "reana_client.api.client.get_workflow_specification",
        get_workflow_specification,
    )

    runner = CliRunner(env={"REANA_SERVER_URL": "http://localhost"})
    with runner.isolated_filesystem():

        def write_file(path, content="content"):
            directory = os.path.dirname(path)
            if directory:
                os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
            with open(path, "w") as stream:
                stream.write(content)

        write_file("reana.yaml", "version: 0.9.3\n")
        write_file("workflow.cwl", "class: CommandLineTool\n")
        write_file("lib/helpers.py")
        write_file("data/declared-input.txt")
        write_file("data/not-declared-input.csv")

        # This directory is unrelated to Git metadata. Its prefix must not
        # cause it to be treated as the excluded .git directory.
        write_file(".github/workflows/check.yml")

        write_file(".git/config", "repository metadata")
        write_file(
            ".gitignore",
            "ignored-by-git.txt\nignored-directory/\n",
        )
        write_file(".reanaignore", "ignored-by-reana.txt\nnested/*.secret\n")
        write_file("ignored-by-git.txt")
        write_file("ignored-directory/file.txt")
        write_file("ignored-by-reana.txt")
        write_file("nested/private.secret")
        write_file("nested/kept.txt")

        result = runner.invoke(
            cli,
            ["upload", "-t", "token", "--workflow", "workspace.1"],
        )

    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output

    expected_uploaded = {
        "reana.yaml",
        "workflow.cwl",
        "lib/helpers.py",
        "data/declared-input.txt",
        "data/not-declared-input.csv",
        ".github/workflows/check.yml",
        "nested/kept.txt",
    }
    assert expected_uploaded <= set(uploaded_files), uploaded_files

    assert "ignored-by-git.txt" not in uploaded_files
    assert "ignored-directory/file.txt" not in uploaded_files
    assert "ignored-by-reana.txt" not in uploaded_files
    assert "nested/private.secret" not in uploaded_files
    assert not any(
        path == ".git" or path.startswith(".git/") for path in uploaded_files
    )

def test_postgres_insert_target_as_alias_before_insert_column_list():
    statement = parse_one(
        "INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c) VALUES (1, 2, 3)",
        read="postgres",
    )

    target = statement.this
    assert isinstance(target, exp.Schema)
    assert isinstance(target.this, exp.Table)
    assert target.this.name == "newtable"
    assert [column.name for column in target.expressions] == ["a", "b", "c"]

    # The INSERT column list must not be consumed as alias-column syntax.
    alias = target.args.get("alias")
    assert isinstance(alias, exp.TableAlias)

import re

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _parse_clickhouse(sql):
    return sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")


def _with_fill(expression):
    with_fills = list(expression.find_all(exp.WithFill))
    assert len(with_fills) == 1, "WITH FILL should be represented by exactly one WithFill expression"
    return with_fills[0]


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_bare_interpolate_with_datetime_bounds_roundtrips():
    sql = """
        SELECT
            1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
            'test' interp
        ORDER BY DATETIME
        WITH FILL
        FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
        TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
        STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
        INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """

    expression = _parse_clickhouse(sql)
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)

    # The fill bounds and step must not be consumed or discarded while parsing
    # the following INTERPOLATE clause.
    assert with_fill.args.get("from") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("to") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("step") is not None
    assert with_fill.args.get("interpolate") is not None
    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 1

    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "WITH FILL" in rendered
    assert "FROM" in rendered
    assert "TO" in rendered
    assert "STEP" in rendered
    assert re.search(r"INTERPOLATE\s*\(\s*interp\s*\)", rendered)

    # Generated ClickHouse SQL must remain parseable, including the bare
    # INTERPOLATE column form that caused the original ParseError.
    reparsed = _parse_clickhouse(rendered)
    rerendered = reparsed.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert re.search(r"INTERPOLATE\s*\(\s*interp\s*\)", rerendered)


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_accepts_multiple_bare_columns():
    sql = """
        SELECT bucket, value, label
        ORDER BY bucket
        WITH FILL FROM 0 TO 10 STEP 1
        INTERPOLATE (value, label)
    """

    expression = _parse_clickhouse(sql)
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)

    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 2

    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert re.search(
        r"INTERPOLATE\s*\(\s*value\s*,\s*label\s*\)",
        rendered,
    )

    reparsed = _parse_clickhouse(rendered)
    assert len(_with_fill(reparsed).args["interpolate"]) == 2


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_supports_bare_and_as_expression_forms():
    sql = """
        SELECT bucket, value, label
        ORDER BY bucket
        WITH FILL FROM 0 TO 10 STEP 1
        INTERPOLATE (value, label AS label + 1)
    """

    expression = _parse_clickhouse(sql)
    with_fill = _with_fill(expression)

    # Both forms are valid in the same INTERPOLATE list. In particular, adding
    # support for a bare column must not regress the existing `column AS expr`
    # syntax.
    assert len(with_fill.args["interpolate"]) == 2

    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert re.search(
        r"INTERPOLATE\s*\(\s*value\s*,\s*label\s+AS\s+label\s*\+\s*1\s*\)",
        rendered,
    )

    reparsed = _parse_clickhouse(rendered)
    rerendered = reparsed.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert re.search(
        r"INTERPOLATE\s*\(\s*value\s*,\s*label\s+AS\s+label\s*\+\s*1\s*\)",
        rerendered,
    )

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected_table",
    [
        ("ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id", "ride"),
        ("ALTER TABLE ride DROP activity_id", "ride"),
        ("ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS activity_id", "ride"),
        ("ALTER TABLE `ride` DROP COLUMN `activity_id`", "ride"),
        ("ALTER TABLE warehouse.ride DROP COLUMN activity_id", "ride"),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_alter_drop_column_does_not_treat_column_as_table(sql, expected_table):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="mysql")

    # The target of ALTER TABLE is the only table reference. The dropped
    # column name must be represented as a field/identifier, not as a table.
    tables = list(expression.find_all(exp.Table))
    assert [table.name for table in tables] == [expected_table]

    drop = expression.find(exp.Drop)
    assert drop is not None
    assert drop.this.name == "activity_id"
    assert list(drop.find_all(exp.Table)) == []


def test_mysql_alter_drop_constraint_does_not_treat_constraint_name_as_table():
    expression = parse_one(
        "ALTER TABLE ride DROP CONSTRAINT fk_ride_activity",
        read="mysql",
    )

    assert [table.name for table in expression.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["ride"]

    drop = expression.find(exp.Drop)
    assert drop is not None
    assert drop.this.name == "fk_ride_activity"
    assert list(drop.find_all(exp.Table)) == []

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from xsdata.formats.dataclass.filters import Filters
from xsdata.formats.dataclass.parsers import XmlParser
from xsdata.models.config import GeneratorConfig
from xsdata.models.enums import DataType
from xsdata.utils.testing import AttrFactory, ClassFactory


def test_generated_ignore_fields_do_not_break_parsed_object_repr():
    """Generated prohibited fields must not be read by dataclass repr.

    Ignore fields are intentionally omitted from xsdata's parsed object state.
    A generated class containing more than one such field must therefore remain
    printable, including when it is populated by the XML parser.
    """
    filters = Filters(GeneratorConfig())
    parent = ClassFactory.create()

    prohibited = AttrFactory.native(DataType.STRING)
    prohibited.restrictions.max_occurs = 0

    ignored_field = filters.field_definition(parent, prohibited, None)

    namespace = {
        "Any": Any,
        "dataclass": dataclass,
        "field": field,
    }
    exec(
        "\n".join(
            [
                "@dataclass",
                "class GeneratedModel:",
                '    value: str = field(default="", metadata={"type": "Element"})',
                f"    first_ignored: Any = {ignored_field}",
                f"    second_ignored: Any = {ignored_field}",
            ]
        ),
        namespace,
    )
    model_type = namespace["GeneratedModel"]

    parsed = XmlParser().from_string(
        "<GeneratedModel><value>available</value></GeneratedModel>",
        model_type,
    )

    assert parsed.value == "available"
    assert not hasattr(parsed, "first_ignored")
    assert not hasattr(parsed, "second_ignored")

    # This was the reported failure: dataclass __repr__ attempted to read an
    # init=False Ignore field that xsdata deliberately did not initialize.
    assert repr(parsed) == "GeneratedModel(value='available')"

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pytest

import zarr
from zarr.codecs import BytesCodec, GzipCodec, ShardingCodec, TransposeCodec
from zarr.storage import LocalStore, StorePath


@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_gzip", [False, True])
def test_partial_read_sharded_transposed_array(
    tmp_path: Path, with_gzip: bool
) -> None:
    """
    Sharded arrays must correctly decode only the requested inner chunks.

    The configuration matches the interoperability report: a big-endian
    sharding index, transposed float64 inner chunks, little-endian payload
    bytes, and optionally gzip compression.
    """
    store = LocalStore(str(tmp_path / "foreign.zarr"), mode="w")
    root = StorePath(store)
    path = "some/group/another"

    inner_codecs = [
        TransposeCodec(order=(2, 0, 1)),
        BytesCodec(endian="little"),
    ]
    if with_gzip:
        inner_codecs.append(GzipCodec(level=5))

    array = zarr.Array.create(
        root / path,
        shape=(100, 100, 50),
        chunk_shape=(10, 15, 20),
        dtype="float64",
        fill_value=-np.inf,
        codecs=[
            ShardingCodec(
                chunk_shape=(5, 3, 5),
                codecs=inner_codecs,
                index_codecs=[
                    BytesCodec(endian="big"),
                    {"name": "crc32c"},
                ],
                index_location="start",
            )
        ],
    )

    # Unique values make an incorrect inner-chunk byte range or incorrect
    # transpose observable. This write spans several inner and outer chunks.
    x, y, z = np.indices((30, 2, 50))
    written = (x * 100_000 + (y + 10) * 100 + z).astype("float64")
    array[:30, 10:12, :] = written

    # Reopen after persistence, as a consumer of an independently produced
    # filesystem store would do.
    reopened = zarr.open_array(store=root, path=path)

    actual = reopened[:20, 10:11, :]
    assert actual.shape == (20, 1, 50)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(actual, written[:20, :1, :])

    # A nearby selection that contains no stored inner chunks must not receive
    # data from a neighbouring selected chunk.
    unwritten = reopened[:20, 7:9, :]
    assert np.all(np.isneginf(unwritten))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("corruption", ["trailing", "truncated"])
def test_bytes_codec_rejects_malformed_fixed_size_chunk(
    tmp_path: Path, corruption: str
) -> None:
    """
    BytesCodec must not hide malformed chunk data by discarding extra bytes.

    In particular, a sharding partial-range bug must be corrected by obtaining
    the correct inner-chunk range, rather than by making the general bytes
    decoder silently accept an oversized payload.
    """
    store_path = tmp_path / "bytes.zarr"
    store = LocalStore(str(store_path), mode="w")
    root = StorePath(store)

    array = zarr.Array.create(
        root,
        shape=(2,),
        chunk_shape=(2,),
        dtype="uint16",
        fill_value=0,
        codecs=[BytesCodec(endian="little")],
    )
    array[:] = np.array([11, 22], dtype="uint16")

    chunk_path = store_path / "c" / "0"
    original = chunk_path.read_bytes()

    if corruption == "trailing":
        # One additional uint16 keeps the payload dtype-aligned. Without
        # validation, truncation would return a plausible but corrupted prefix.
        chunk_path.write_bytes(original + np.array([999], dtype="<u2").tobytes())
    else:
        chunk_path.write_bytes(original[:-1])

    reopened = zarr.open_array(store=StorePath(LocalStore(str(store_path), mode="r")))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        reopened[:]

import numpy as np
from astropy import units as u
from astropy.modeling import models

from specutils import Spectrum1D
from specutils.fitting import fit_lines


class RecordingFitter:
    """Record the samples that fit_lines passes to its fitter."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.dispersion = None

    def __call__(self, model, dispersion, flux, weights=None, **kwargs):
        self.dispersion = np.asarray(dispersion)
        return model


def make_spectrum():
    spectral_axis = np.arange(6540.25, 6590.0, 0.5) * u.AA
    return Spectrum1D(
        spectral_axis=spectral_axis,
        flux=np.zeros(spectral_axis.size) * u.Jy,
    )


def selected_dispersion(model, window):
    fitter = RecordingFitter()
    fit_lines(make_spectrum(), model, fitter=fitter, window=window)
    return fitter.dispersion


def gaussian_plus_continuum(mean):
    # This is the compound-model form from the issue report.
    return (
        models.Gaussian1D(
            amplitude=2000 * u.Jy,
            mean=mean,
            stddev=3 * u.AA,
        )
        + models.Const1D(amplitude=0 * u.Jy)
    )


def test_quantity_window_on_compound_model_matches_explicit_bounds():
    """
    A scalar Quantity window is a half-width centered on the Gaussian mean.

    In particular, this must work for the Gaussian-plus-continuum compound
    model shown in the issue, rather than silently fitting the full spectrum.
    """
    automatic = selected_dispersion(
        gaussian_plus_continuum(6563 * u.AA),
        10 * u.AA,
    )
    explicit = selected_dispersion(
        gaussian_plus_continuum(6563 * u.AA),
        (6553 * u.AA, 6573 * u.AA),
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(automatic, explicit)
    assert automatic.size < make_spectrum().spectral_axis.size


def test_quantity_window_handles_equivalent_units():
    """Center and half-width may be expressed in units other than Angstrom."""
    automatic = selected_dispersion(
        gaussian_plus_continuum(656.3 * u.nm),
        1 * u.nm,
    )
    explicit = selected_dispersion(
        gaussian_plus_continuum(656.3 * u.nm),
        (6553 * u.AA, 6573 * u.AA),
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(automatic, explicit)

import pytest

from yarl import URL


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("port", "type_name"),
    [
        pytest.param("8080", "str", id="string"),
        pytest.param(12.5, "float", id="float"),
        pytest.param([], "list", id="list"),
    ],
)
def test_build_invalid_port_error_reports_actual_type_name(port, type_name):
    """Port validation should name the concrete invalid type readably."""
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as exc_info:
        URL.build(host="example.com", port=port)

    assert str(exc_info.value) == (
        f"The port is required to be int, got {type_name}."
    )


def test_build_port_none_remains_valid():
    """The optional port argument continues to accept its default None value."""
    url = URL.build(scheme="http", host="example.com", port=None)

    assert str(url) == "http://example.com"


def test_build_integer_port_remains_valid():
    """The improved error reporting must not affect valid integer ports."""
    url = URL.build(scheme="http", host="example.com", port=8080)

    assert str(url) == "http://example.com:8080"

import ast
from typing import Any

import pytest

from func_adl import ObjectStream
from func_adl.type_based_replacement import remap_by_types


def _remap(expression: str):
    """Type-remap an expression as it would occur inside a query lambda."""
    expression_ast = ast.parse(expression, mode="eval").body
    stream = ObjectStream(ast.Name(id="event", ctx=ast.Load()), Any)
    return remap_by_types(stream, "event", Any, expression_ast)


def test_zip_on_dictionary_is_an_unknown_function_return_not_a_missing_key():
    """Zip is a backend collection operation, rather than a dictionary field."""

    _, _, result_type = _remap(
        "{'pt': event.Electron_pt, 'eta': event.Electron_eta}.Zip()"
    )

    assert result_type is Any


def test_zip_dictionary_can_be_used_in_the_agc_style_query_chain():
    """The original failure occurred when Zip was followed by collection calls."""

    _, _, result_type = _remap(
        "{'pt': event.Electron_pt, 'eta': event.Electron_eta, "
        "'cutBased': event.Electron_cutBased, 'sip3d': event.Electron_sip3d}.Zip()"
        ".Where(lambda electron: (electron.pt > 30"
        " and abs(electron.eta) < 2.1"
        " and electron.cutBased == 4"
        " and electron.sip3d < 4))"
        ".Count() == 1"
    )

    assert result_type is bool


def test_unknown_dictionary_data_key_still_raises_to_catch_typos():
    """Permitting Zip must not make known dictionary-field typing disappear."""

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="jetsss"):
        _remap("{'jets': event.Jet_pt}.jetsss")

"""Regression tests for WPS210 local-variable scope handling."""

import ast

import pytest

from wemake_python_styleguide.transformations.ast_tree import transform
from wemake_python_styleguide.visitors.ast.complexity.function import (
    FunctionComplexityVisitor,
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'nested_function',
    [
        """
    def nested():
        nested_first = 1
        nested_second = 2
        nested_third = 3
""",
        """
    async def nested():
        nested_first = 1
        nested_second = 2
        nested_third = 3
""",
    ],
)
def test_wps210_does_not_count_nested_function_or_class_variables(
    assert_errors,
    default_options,
    nested_function,
):
    """
    Ensures locals in nested scopes cannot trigger WPS210 for their parent.

    The outer function has one local variable. The nested function and class
    each define three names: together these used to be incorrectly counted as
    seven locals of ``outer``.
    """
    code = """
def outer():
    outer_local = 1
{0}
    class Nested:
        class_first = 1
        class_second = 2
        class_third = 3
""".format(
        nested_function,
    )
    tree = transform(ast.parse(code))

    visitor = FunctionComplexityVisitor(default_options, tree=tree)
    visitor.run()

    assert_errors(visitor, [])

import pytest

from wemake_python_styleguide.violations.consistency import WalrusViolation
from wemake_python_styleguide.visitors.ast.operators import WalrusVisitor


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'code',
    [
        """
users = [
    user
    for user_id in user_ids
    if (user := get_user(user_id)) is not None
]
""",
        'users = [(user := get_user(user_id)) for user_id in user_ids]',
        'users = {(user := get_user(user_id)) for user_id in user_ids}',
        (
            'users = {'
            'user_id: (user := get_user(user_id)) '
            'for user_id in user_ids'
            '}'
        ),
        (
            'users = ('
            '(user := get_user(user_id)) '
            'for user_id in user_ids'
            ')'
        ),
        """
users = [
    user
    for group in groups
    for user_id in group
    if (user := get_user(user_id)) is not None
]
""",
    ],
)
def test_walrus_is_allowed_in_comprehensions_and_generators(
    assert_errors,
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
    code,
):
    """Assignment expressions are permitted in all comprehension forms."""
    visitor = WalrusVisitor(default_options, tree=parse_ast_tree(code))

    visitor.run()

    assert_errors(visitor, [])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    'code',
    [
        'user = (loaded_user := get_user(user_id))',
        """
if (loaded_user := get_user(user_id)) is not None:
    user = loaded_user
""",
        'users = [(loaded_user := get_user(user_id))]',
        """
def get_user_or_none(user_id):
    return (loaded_user := get_user(user_id))
""",
    ],
)
def test_walrus_is_still_forbidden_outside_comprehensions(
    assert_errors,
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
    code,
):
    """The comprehension exception must not permit ordinary walruses."""
    visitor = WalrusVisitor(default_options, tree=parse_ast_tree(code))

    visitor.run()

    assert_errors(visitor, [WalrusViolation])

import warnings

import h5py
import scipp as sc
import scippnexus as snx


def _timestamps():
    return sc.array(dims=["time"], unit="s", values=[1.0, 2.0, 3.0])


def _make_time_only_log(file):
    root = snx.Group(file, definitions=snx.base_definitions())
    entry = root.create_class("entry", snx.NXentry)
    log = entry.create_class("top_dead_center", snx.NXlog)
    log["time"] = _timestamps()
    return log


def _load_without_warnings(log, selection=()):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        # A timestamp-only NXlog is valid. In particular, loading it must not
        # trigger the "could not determine signal" warning.
        warnings.simplefilter("error")
        return log[selection]


def test_nxlog_with_only_time_uses_time_as_dataarray_signal():
    """A valid timestamp-only NXlog has time as its signal."""
    with h5py.File(
        "time-only-log.nxs", "w", driver="core", backing_store=False
    ) as file:
        loaded = _load_without_warnings(_make_time_only_log(file))

    assert isinstance(loaded, sc.DataArray)
    assert loaded.dims == ("time",)
    assert loaded.sizes == {"time": 3}
    assert loaded.data.dtype == sc.DType.datetime64
    assert sc.identical(loaded.data, sc.epoch(unit="s") + _timestamps())


def test_time_only_nxlog_supports_positional_selection():
    """Selecting the time dimension must work when time is the fallback signal."""
    with h5py.File(
        "time-only-log-selection.nxs", "w", driver="core", backing_store=False
    ) as file:
        loaded = _load_without_warnings(
            _make_time_only_log(file), ("time", slice(1, None))
        )

    assert isinstance(loaded, sc.DataArray)
    assert loaded.sizes == {"time": 2}
    assert sc.identical(
        loaded.data,
        sc.epoch(unit="s")
        + sc.array(dims=["time"], unit="s", values=[2.0, 3.0]),
    )


def test_time_only_nxlog_with_metadata_uses_time_as_dataarray_signal():
    """Non-value metadata must not make a timestamp-only NXlog invalid."""
    with h5py.File(
        "time-only-log-metadata.nxs", "w", driver="core", backing_store=False
    ) as file:
        log = _make_time_only_log(file)
        log["description"] = sc.scalar("top-dead-center chopper timestamps")
        loaded = _load_without_warnings(log)

    assert isinstance(loaded, sc.DataArray)
    assert loaded.data.dtype == sc.DType.datetime64
    assert loaded.coords["description"].value == "top-dead-center chopper timestamps"

import numpy as np
from nibabel import Nifti1Image
from nilearn.image import concat_imgs, index_img
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose

from fmralign.preprocessing import ParcellationMasker
from fmralign.template_alignment import TemplateAlignment


def _image(data):
    return Nifti1Image(np.asarray(data, dtype=float), np.eye(4))


def _mask(shape):
    return _image(np.ones(shape, dtype=np.uint8))


def _fitted_two_contrast_template():
    """Create an identity template with two contrasts."""
    spatial_shape = (4, 4, 4)
    base = np.arange(np.prod(spatial_shape)).reshape(spatial_shape) + 1
    contrast_0 = _image(base)
    contrast_1 = _image(2 * base + 3)

    subject_1 = concat_imgs([contrast_0, contrast_1])
    subject_2 = concat_imgs([_image(3 * base), _image(4 * base + 1)])

    alignment = TemplateAlignment(
        alignment_method="identity",
        n_iter=1,
        mask=_mask(spatial_shape),
    )
    alignment.fit([subject_1, subject_2])
    return alignment, contrast_0, spatial_shape


def test_parcellation_masker_accepts_mixed_3d_and_singleton_4d_images():
    """A one-contrast 3D image and its 4D representation are compatible."""
    spatial_shape = (4, 4, 4)
    data = np.arange(np.prod(spatial_shape)).reshape(spatial_shape) + 1
    image_3d = _image(data)
    image_4d = concat_imgs([image_3d])

    masker = ParcellationMasker(n_pieces=1, mask=_mask(spatial_shape))
    masker.fit([image_3d, image_4d])

    transformed = masker.transform([image_3d, image_4d])
    assert len(transformed) == 2
    assert transformed[0].data.shape == transformed[1].data.shape
    assert_allclose(transformed[0].data, transformed[1].data)


def test_template_alignment_fit_accepts_direct_3d_single_contrast_subjects():
    """Template fitting must align 3D subjects to the singleton-4D template."""
    spatial_shape = (4, 4, 4)
    first = _image(np.arange(np.prod(spatial_shape)).reshape(spatial_shape) + 1)
    second = _image(
        3 * np.arange(np.prod(spatial_shape)).reshape(spatial_shape) + 2
    )

    alignment = TemplateAlignment(
        alignment_method="identity",
        n_iter=1,
        mask=_mask(spatial_shape),
    )
    alignment.fit([first, second])

    assert alignment.template.shape == spatial_shape + (1,)
    assert_allclose(
        index_img(alignment.template, 0).get_fdata(),
        (first.get_fdata() + second.get_fdata()) / 2,
    )


def test_template_alignment_transform_accepts_singleton_list_of_3d_images():
    """A target subject represented by a one-image list is normalized to 4D."""
    alignment, contrast_0, spatial_shape = _fitted_two_contrast_template()

    predictions = alignment.transform(
        [[contrast_0]],
        train_index=[0],
        test_index=[1],
    )

    expected = index_img(alignment.template, 1).get_fdata()[..., np.newaxis]
    assert len(predictions) == 1
    assert predictions[0].shape == spatial_shape + (1,)
    assert_allclose(predictions[0].get_fdata(), expected)


def test_template_alignment_transform_accepts_direct_3d_single_contrast():
    """A direct 3D target is one known contrast, not a spatial-size time axis."""
    alignment, contrast_0, spatial_shape = _fitted_two_contrast_template()

    predictions = alignment.transform(
        [contrast_0],
        train_index=[0],
        test_index=[1],
    )

    expected = index_img(alignment.template, 1).get_fdata()[..., np.newaxis]
    assert len(predictions) == 1
    assert predictions[0].shape == spatial_shape + (1,)
    assert_allclose(predictions[0].get_fdata(), expected)

    """A late bidi response must be harmless once close has torn helpers down."""
    scheduler_ = mock.create_autospec(scheduler.Scheduler, instance=True)
    manager = _manager_with_running_helpers(scheduler_)

    # This is the state left by shutdown while the bidi response thread can
    # still call _on_response.
    manager._scheduler = None
    manager._leaser = None

    manager._on_response(_response())

    scheduler_.schedule.assert_not_called()
    manager._callback.assert_not_called()


def test_close_racing_with_an_inflight_response_does_not_crash_response_thread():
    """A response waiting on manager state must not assert during close()."""

    class RecordingScheduler:
        def __init__(self):
            self.shutdown_called = threading.Event()
            self.schedule_calls = []

        def schedule(self, callback, *args, **kwargs):
            self.schedule_calls.append((callback, args, kwargs))

        def shutdown(self, *args, **kwargs):
            self.shutdown_called.set()
            # StreamingPullManager._shutdown() counts messages dropped by the
            # scheduler, so a scheduler implementation must return a sequence.
            return []

    scheduler_ = RecordingScheduler()
    manager = _manager_with_running_helpers(scheduler_)
    response_errors = []

    # Keep _on_response suspended at its synchronization point while close
    # starts shutdown. This reproduces the window in which shutdown can clear
    # _scheduler before the response proceeds.
    manager._pause_resume_lock.acquire()
    try:
        response_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=_call_on_response,
            args=(manager, _response(), response_errors),
        )
        response_thread.start()

        deadline = time.monotonic() + 1
        while not response_thread.is_alive() and time.monotonic() < deadline:
            time.sleep(0.001)
        assert response_thread.is_alive()

        close_thread = threading.Thread(target=manager.close)
        close_thread.start()

        scheduler_.shutdown_called.wait(timeout=1)
    finally:
        manager._pause_resume_lock.release()

    response_thread.join(timeout=2)
    close_thread.join(timeout=2)

    if manager._regular_shutdown_thread is not None:
        manager._regular_shutdown_thread.join(timeout=2)

    assert not response_thread.is_alive()
    assert not close_thread.is_alive()
    assert response_errors == []


def _call_on_response(manager, response, errors):
    try:
        manager._on_response(response)
    except BaseException as exc:
        errors.append(exc)

        ),

    unknown_reference = reader.process_element(

            b'name="unknown" type="xs:MissingType"/>'

def test_generated_ignore_fields_do_not_break_nested_dataclass_repr():
    """Ignored prohibited fields are absent after construction but safe to repr."""
    filters = Filters(GeneratorConfig())
    owner = ClassFactory.create(qname="accessibility_limitation")

    ignored_field_definitions = []
    for name in (
        "validity_conditions_or_valid_between",
        "alternative_texts",
    ):
        attr = AttrFactory.native(DataType.STRING)
        attr.name = name
        attr.restrictions.max_occurs = 0
        ignored_field_definitions.append(filters.field_definition(owner, attr, None))

    namespace = {
        "dataclass": dataclass,
        "field": field,
        "Any": Any,
    }
    source = f"""
@dataclass
class AccessibilityLimitation:
    value: str
    validity_conditions_or_valid_between: Any = {ignored_field_definitions[0]}
    alternative_texts: Any = {ignored_field_definitions[1]}


@dataclass
class Limitations:
    accessibility_limitation: AccessibilityLimitation


@dataclass
class Assessment:
    limitations: Limitations
"""

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _tables(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="mysql")
    return expression, list(expression.find_all(exp.Table))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected_table, expected_column",
    [
        (
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP COLUMN activity_id",
            "ride",
            "activity_id",
        ),
        (
            "ALTER TABLE ride DROP activity_id",
            "ride",
            "activity_id",
        ),
        (
            "ALTER TABLE `ride` DROP COLUMN `activity_id`",
            "ride",
            "activity_id",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_alter_table_drop_column_does_not_expose_column_as_table(
    sql, expected_table, expected_column
):
    expression, tables = _tables(sql)

    # AST table traversal is public metadata behavior: only the table being
    # altered is a table reference, not the name of its dropped column.
    assert [table.name for table in tables] == [expected_table]

    action = expression.args["actions"][0]
    assert isinstance(action, exp.Drop)
    assert action.args["kind"] == "COLUMN"
    assert action.this.name == expected_column


def test_alter_table_drop_multiple_columns_does_not_add_table_references():
    expression, tables = _tables(
        "ALTER TABLE warehouse.ride "
        "DROP COLUMN activity_id, DROP COLUMN status"
    )

    assert [table.name for table in tables] == ["ride"]

    actions = expression.args["actions"]
    assert [action.this.name for action in actions] == ["activity_id", "status"]
    assert all(action.args["kind"] == "COLUMN" for action in actions)

def test_publish_lib_returns_nonzero_for_unbumped_or_decreased_libpatch(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, output_format
):
    """A rejected LIBPATCH must cause publish-lib to fail for CI consumers."""
    library_id = "01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef"
    library_name = "charms.my_charm.v0.example"
    library_path = tmp_path / "lib" / "charms" / "my_charm" / "v0"
    library_path.mkdir(parents=True)
    source_path = library_path / "example.py"
    source_path.write_text(
        f'''\
LIBID = "{library_id}"
LIBAPI = 0
LIBPATCH = 1
'''
    )
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)

    # Charmhub already contains a newer patch.  Publishing the local library
    # must be rejected rather than creating another revision.
    published_library = SimpleNamespace(
        id=library_id,
        lib_id=library_id,
        library_id=library_id,
        name=library_name,
        api=0,
        patch=2,
        content="",

    # None is translated to exit code zero by the command dispatcher; a

    assert result != 0

        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f0\'e9"
        r"\f1\'b8\'f9\'be\'dd"
        r"\f0\'f1"
        r"}"
    )

    assert rtf_to_text(rtf) == "é根据ñ"


def test_font_encoding_switches_are_scoped_to_their_rtf_group():
    # Font selection is a character property in RTF.  It must be restored after
    # a nested group finishes, rather than leaking into following text.
    rtf = (
        r"{\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252"
        r"{\fonttbl"
        r"{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Western;}"
        r"{\f1\fswiss\fcharset134 Chinese;}"
        r"}"
        r"\f1\'b8\'f9"
        r"{\f0\'e9}"
        r"\'be\'dd"
        r"}"
    )

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _parse_with_fill(sql):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="clickhouse")
    with_fill = expression.find(exp.WithFill)

    assert with_fill is not None, "Expected WITH FILL to be represented in the parsed expression"
    return expression, with_fill


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_simple_column_with_bounds():
    sql = """
        SELECT
            1730098800::DATETIME64 DATETIME,
            'test' interp
        ORDER BY DATETIME
        WITH FILL
        FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
        TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3) - INTERVAL 7 HOUR
        STEP toIntervalSecond(900)
        INTERPOLATE (interp)
    """

    expression, with_fill = _parse_with_fill(sql)

    interpolated = with_fill.args["interpolate"]
    assert len(interpolated) == 1
    assert isinstance(interpolated[0], exp.Identifier)
    assert interpolated[0].name == "interp"

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "WITH FILL" in generated
    assert "FROM toDateTime64(1730098800, 3)" in generated
    assert "TO toDateTime64(1730185140, 3)" in generated
    assert "STEP toIntervalSecond(900)" in generated
    assert "INTERPOLATE (interp)" in generated

    _, reparsed_with_fill = _parse_with_fill(generated)
    reparsed_interpolated = reparsed_with_fill.args["interpolate"]
    assert len(reparsed_interpolated) == 1
    assert isinstance(reparsed_interpolated[0], exp.Identifier)
    assert reparsed_interpolated[0].name == "interp"


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_multiple_simple_columns():
    sql = """
        SELECT
            1 AS bucket,
            'left' AS left_value,
            'right' AS "right value"
        ORDER BY bucket
        WITH FILL
        INTERPOLATE (left_value, "right value")
    """

    expression, with_fill = _parse_with_fill(sql)

    interpolated = with_fill.args["interpolate"]
    assert len(interpolated) == 2
    assert all(isinstance(item, exp.Identifier) for item in interpolated)
    assert [item.name for item in interpolated] == ["left_value", "right value"]
    assert interpolated[1].quoted

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert 'INTERPOLATE (left_value, "right value")' in generated

    _, reparsed_with_fill = _parse_with_fill(generated)
    assert [item.name for item in reparsed_with_fill.args["interpolate"]] == [
        "left_value",
        "right value",
    ]


def test_clickhouse_with_fill_interpolate_mixes_column_and_assignment():
    sql = """
        SELECT
            1 AS bucket,
            10 AS value,
            20 AS total
        ORDER BY bucket
        WITH FILL
        FROM 0 TO 10 STEP 1
        INTERPOLATE (value, total AS total + 1)
    """

    expression, with_fill = _parse_with_fill(sql)

    interpolated = with_fill.args["interpolate"]
    assert len(interpolated) == 2

    assert isinstance(interpolated[0], exp.Identifier)
    assert interpolated[0].name == "value"

    assignment = interpolated[1]
    assert isinstance(assignment, exp.Alias)
    assert assignment.alias_or_name == "total"
    assert isinstance(assignment.this, exp.Add)
    assert isinstance(assignment.this.this, exp.Column)
    assert assignment.this.this.name == "total"

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse")
    assert "INTERPOLATE (value, total AS total + 1)" in generated

    _, reparsed_with_fill = _parse_with_fill(generated)
    reparsed_values = reparsed_with_fill.args["interpolate"]
    assert isinstance(reparsed_values[0], exp.Identifier)
    assert reparsed_values[0].name == "value"
    assert isinstance(reparsed_values[1], exp.Alias)
    assert reparsed_values[1].alias_or_name == "total"

import logging

from stdatamodels.jwst import datamodels

from jwst import __version__
from jwst.stpipe.core import JwstPipeline, JwstStep


class _IdentityPipeline(JwstPipeline):
    """Minimal pipeline that returns its input model."""

    def process(self, model):
        return model


class _IdentityStep(JwstStep):
    """Minimal standalone step that returns its input model."""

    def process(self, model):
        return model


def _assert_context_and_version_are_adjacent(records, context):
    """
    The final CRDS summary emitted during result finalization must be followed
    immediately by the installed JWST version.

    Some stpipe execution paths emit an earlier CRDS-context message before
    JWST's finalization hook.  The issue specifically requires the new
    information beside the existing end-of-log context report, so inspect the
    final such report rather than an earlier one.
    """
    messages = [record.getMessage() for record in records]
    expected_context = f"Results used CRDS context: {context}"
    expected_version = f"JWST version: {__version__}"

    assert expected_context in messages
    context_index = len(messages) - 1 - messages[::-1].index(expected_context)

    assert messages[context_index + 1] == expected_version


def test_pipeline_logs_installed_jwst_version_next_to_crds_context(
    monkeypatch, caplog
):
    """
    Pipeline completion must append the actual installed JWST version after the
    final CRDS-context report, without requiring CRDS or network access.
    """
    context = "jwst_9999.pmap"
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "jwst.stpipe.core.crds_client.get_context_used",
        lambda observatory: context,
    )

    model = datamodels.ImageModel((2, 2))
    pipeline = _IdentityPipeline()
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="jwst.stpipe.core")

    try:
        result = pipeline.run(model)
        _assert_context_and_version_are_adjacent(caplog.records, context)
    finally:
        model.close()
        if "result" in locals() and result is not model:
            result.close()


def test_top_level_step_with_references_logs_version_next_to_crds_context(
    monkeypatch, caplog
):
    """
    The end-of-log summary for a standalone step using references must include
    the same JWST software version report as a pipeline.
    """
    context = "jwst_9999.pmap"
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "jwst.stpipe.core.crds_client.get_context_used",
        lambda observatory: context,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "jwst.stpipe.core.crds_client.get_svn_version",
        lambda: "test-crds-version",
    )

    model = datamodels.ImageModel((2, 2))
    step = _IdentityStep()
    caplog.set_level(logging.INFO, logger="jwst.stpipe.core")

    try:
        # Supplying a reference exercises the normal standalone-step
        # finalization branch while avoiding a CRDS reference lookup.
        step.finalize_result(model, [("flat", "flat_reference.fits")])
        _assert_context_and_version_are_adjacent(caplog.records, context)
    finally:
        model.close()

from sqlglot import exp


def test_duckdb_parses_and_generates_unpacked_columns_for_struct_pack():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        r"""
        SELECT id, struct_pack(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements
        FROM many_measurements
        """,
        dialect="duckdb",
    )

    unpack = expression.find(exp.Unpack)
    assert unpack is not None
    assert unpack.sql(dialect="duckdb") == r"*COLUMNS('m\d')"
    assert expression.sql(dialect="duckdb") == (
        r"SELECT id, STRUCT_PACK(*COLUMNS('m\d')) AS measurements FROM many_measurements"
    )

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        r"SELECT GREATEST(*COLUMNS('^metric_')) FROM measurements",
        dialect="duckdb",
    )

    assert expression.find(exp.Unpack) is not None
    assert expression.sql(dialect="duckdb") == (

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _assert_stream_cte_query(query):
    with_expression = query.args.get("with")
    assert with_expression is not None

    ctes = list(with_expression.find_all(exp.CTE))
    assert ctes
    assert any(cte.alias_or_name.lower() == "stream" for cte in ctes)

    stream_tables = [
        table
        for table in query.find_all(exp.Table)
        if table.name.lower() == "stream" and not table.db and not table.catalog
    ]
    assert stream_tables, "The CTE reference should be parsed as a table named stream"
    assert not list(query.find_all(exp.Stream))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        """
        WITH stream AS (
          SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT * FROM stream
        """,
        """
        WITH source AS (
          SELECT 1 AS id
        ), stream AS (
          SELECT * FROM source
        )
        SELECT * FROM stream
        """,
        """
        WITH stream AS (
          SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT s.* FROM stream AS s
        JOIN stream AS other ON s.id = other.id
        """,
        """
        WITH STREAM AS (
          SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT * FROM STREAM
        """,
    ],
)
def test_cte_named_stream_is_parsed_as_an_identifier(sql):
    query = parse_one(sql)

    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)
    _assert_stream_cte_query(query)


def test_create_table_as_query_can_reference_cte_named_stream():
    statement = parse_one(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo AS
        WITH stream AS (
            SELECT * FROM bar
        )
        SELECT * FROM stream
        """
    )

    assert isinstance(statement, exp.Create)
    assert statement.this.name == "foo"
    assert isinstance(statement.expression, exp.Select)
    _assert_stream_cte_query(statement.expression)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "SELECT * FROM stream",
        "SELECT * FROM stream AS s",
        "SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM stream) AS nested_stream",
    ],
)
def test_unquoted_stream_remains_a_valid_table_identifier(sql):
    query = parse_one(sql)

    assert isinstance(query, exp.Select)
    tables = [table for table in query.find_all(exp.Table) if table.name.lower() == "stream"]
    assert tables
    assert not list(query.find_all(exp.Stream))

import numpy as np
import pytest
import astropy.units as u
from astropy.modeling import models

from specutils.fitting import fit_lines
from specutils.spectra import Spectrum1D


class RecordingFitter:
    """A fitter stand-in that records precisely the samples fit_lines supplies."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.x = None
        self.y = None

    def __call__(self, model, x, y, weights=None, **kwargs):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        return model.copy()


def test_scalar_quantity_window_is_centered_on_compound_gaussian_mean():
    """
    A scalar Quantity window must select samples centered on the line model's
    initial mean, including when that Gaussian is part of a compound model and
    its units differ from the spectrum axis units.
    """
    axis = np.arange(6500.25, 6620.0, 0.5) * u.AA
    spectrum = Spectrum1D(flux=np.ones(axis.size) * u.Jy, spectral_axis=axis)

    # The mean and scalar window use nm, while the spectrum is in Angstrom.
    # This corresponds to the interval [6553, 6573) Angstrom.
    model = (
        models.Gaussian1D(
            amplitude=1 * u.Jy,
            mean=656.3 * u.nm,
            stddev=0.3 * u.nm,
        )
        + models.Const1D(0 * u.Jy)
    )

    scalar_fitter = RecordingFitter()
    bounds_fitter = RecordingFitter()

    fit_lines(spectrum, model.copy(), fitter=scalar_fitter, window=1 * u.nm)
    fit_lines(
        spectrum,
        model.copy(),
        fitter=bounds_fitter,
        window=(6553 * u.AA, 6573 * u.AA),
    )

    expected = axis[(axis >= 6553 * u.AA) & (axis < 6573 * u.AA)]

    # The manually specified bounds are the public reference behavior.
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        u.Quantity(scalar_fitter.x).to_value(u.AA),
        expected.to_value(u.AA),
    )
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        u.Quantity(bounds_fitter.x).to_value(u.AA),
        expected.to_value(u.AA),
    )

    # In particular, the fit must not receive the whole input spectrum.
    assert len(scalar_fitter.x) == len(expected)
    assert len(scalar_fitter.x) < len(axis)


def test_scalar_window_fit_matches_equivalent_explicit_bounds():
    """
    A real fit with ``window=10 * AA`` must use exactly the same data and
    produce the same result as the equivalent explicit bounds around mean.
    """
    axis = np.arange(6500.15, 6620.0, 0.2) * u.AA
    x = axis.to_value(u.AA)

    # The very strong distant feature makes using the full spectrum observably
    # different from fitting only the intended H-alpha neighborhood.
    flux = (
        80
        + 2000 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6563.0) / 2.8) ** 2)
        + 9000 * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - 6605.0) / 1.5) ** 2)
    ) * u.Jy
    spectrum = Spectrum1D(flux=flux, spectral_axis=axis)

    initial = (
        models.Gaussian1D(
            amplitude=1500 * u.Jy,
            mean=6563 * u.AA,
            stddev=3 * u.AA,
        )
        + models.Const1D(0 * u.Jy)
    )

    scalar_fit = fit_lines(spectrum, initial.copy(), window=10 * u.AA)
    bounds_fit = fit_lines(
        spectrum,
        initial.copy(),
        window=(6553 * u.AA, 6573 * u.AA),
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        scalar_fit[0].mean.quantity.to_value(u.AA),
        bounds_fit[0].mean.quantity.to_value(u.AA),
        rtol=0,
        atol=1e-8,
    )
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        scalar_fit[0].amplitude.quantity.to_value(u.Jy),
        bounds_fit[0].amplitude.quantity.to_value(u.Jy),
        rtol=0,
        atol=1e-8,
    )
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        scalar_fit[0].stddev.quantity.to_value(u.AA),
        bounds_fit[0].stddev.quantity.to_value(u.AA),
        rtol=0,
        atol=1e-8,
    )

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_postgres_insert_with_target_alias_and_conflict_update_where():
    sql = """
        INSERT INTO newtable AS t (a, b, c)
        VALUES (1, 2, 3)
        ON CONFLICT (c)
        DO UPDATE
           SET a = t.a + 1
        WHERE t.a < 1
    """

    statement = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    # This is the public traversal used in the reported reproduction.
    assert [table.name for table in statement.find_all(exp.Table)] == ["newtable"]

    # INSERT targets with a column list are represented as Schema nodes. The
    # target alias occurs before that list and therefore belongs to the schema.
    target_schema = statement.this
    assert isinstance(target_schema, exp.Schema)
    assert isinstance(target_schema.this, exp.Table)
    assert target_schema.this.name == "newtable"

    alias = target_schema.args.get("alias")
    assert isinstance(alias, exp.TableAlias)
    assert alias.this.name == "t"

    # Parsing must consume the complete ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE clause, including
    # the qualified alias references in its SET and WHERE expressions.
    conflict = statement.args.get("conflict")
    assert isinstance(conflict, exp.OnConflict)
    assert conflict.args.get("where") is not None

    qualified_a_references = [
        column
        for column in statement.find_all(exp.Column)
        if column.table == "t" and column.name == "a"
    ]
    assert len(qualified_a_references) == 2


def test_postgres_insert_target_alias_before_column_list_is_retained():

    )

    assert isinstance(target_schema, exp.Schema)
    assert target_schema.this.name == "newtable"

    alias = target_schema.args.get("alias")
    assert isinstance(alias, exp.TableAlias)
    assert alias.this.name == "target"

class Track:
    def pt(self) -> float:
        ...


class Event:
    def tracks(self) -> Iterable[Track]:
        ...


def _remap(expression: str):
    stream = ObjectStream[Event](ast.Name(id="e", ctx=ast.Load()))
    expression_ast = ast.parse(expression, mode="eval").body
    return remap_by_types(stream, "e", Event, expression_ast)


def test_dict_zip_method_lookup_is_untyped_not_missing_key():
    """Zip is a function lookup, not an attempted lookup of a dict field."""
    _, _, expression_type = _remap("{'pt': e.tracks(), 'eta': e.tracks()}.Zip()")

    assert expression_type is Any

    """The fallback must support the chained use shown in the issue report."""
    _, _, expression_type = _remap(
        "{'pt': e.tracks(), 'eta': e.tracks()}.Zip()"
        ".Where(lambda track: track.pt() > 30)"
        ".Count()"
    )

    assert expression_type is Any

    """Dictionary function names may be supplied by a backend.

    """
    _, _, expression_type = _remap(
        "{'pt': e.tracks(), 'eta': e.tracks()}.BackendSpecificZip()"
    )

    assert expression_type is Any


def test_dict_fields_remain_typed_and_misspelled_fields_still_fail():
    """Permitting function lookups must not hide ordinary dict-field typos."""
    _, _, expression_type = _remap(
        "{'tracks': e.tracks()}.tracks.Select(lambda track: track.pt())"
    )
    assert expression_type == Iterable[float]

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="trakcs"):
        _remap("{'tracks': e.tracks()}.trakcs")
