    """Return the resolver and child mapping used for a debugger expansion."""
    _type, _type_name, resolver = get_type(value)
    assert resolver is not None, "Debugger did not select a resolver"
    return resolver, resolver.get_dictionary(value)


def _indexed_children(children):
    return {name: value for name, value in children.items() if name.isdigit()}


def test_ctypes_array_from_buffer_is_expanded_like_a_sequence():
    """The example from the report must expose each item and its length."""
    backing = bytearray(b"\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05")
    array = (ctypes.c_uint8 * len(backing)).from_buffer(backing)

    _resolver, children = _debugger_children(array)

    assert children["len()"] == len(array)
    assert _indexed_children(children) == {
        "0": 1,
        "1": 2,
        "2": 3,
        "3": 4,
        "4": 5,
    }

    # The values displayed by the debugger must reflect the actual ctypes
    # buffer, rather than a one-time conversion to a Python sequence.
    backing[2] = 99
    _resolver, children = _debugger_children(array)
    assert _indexed_children(children)["2"] == 99


def test_ctypes_arrays_of_different_element_types_and_empty_arrays_expand():
    """Array handling must not be limited to the uint8 example in the report."""
    cases = [
        ((ctypes.c_int * 3)(-4, 0, 12), {"0": -4, "1": 0, "2": 12}),
        (
            (ctypes.c_char * 3)(b"a", b"b", b"c"),
            {"0": b"a", "1": b"b", "2": b"c"},
        ),
        ((ctypes.c_int * 0)(), {}),
    ]

    for array, expected_items in cases:
        _resolver, children = _debugger_children(array)

        assert children["len()"] == len(array)
        assert _indexed_children(children) == expected_items


def test_nested_ctypes_arrays_are_containers_at_each_level():
    """The debugger should be able to continue enumerating array children."""
    matrix = ((ctypes.c_int * 2) * 2)((10, 11), (20, 21))

    _resolver, outer_children = _debugger_children(matrix)

    assert outer_children["len()"] == 2
    assert set(_indexed_children(outer_children)) == {"0", "1"}

    _resolver, first_row_children = _debugger_children(outer_children["0"])
    assert first_row_children["len()"] == 2
    assert _indexed_children(first_row_children) == {"0": 10, "1": 11}

    _resolver, second_row_children = _debugger_children(outer_children["1"])
    assert second_row_children["len()"] == 2
    assert _indexed_children(second_row_children) == {"0": 20, "1": 21}

import os
from unittest import mock

from mobly.controllers import android_device


def test_cat_adb_log_uses_windows_safe_excerpt_filename(tmp_path):
    """The timestamp embedded in an adb excerpt name must not contain ':'."""
    ad = object.__new__(android_device.AndroidDevice)
    ad._log_path = str(tmp_path)
    ad.log = mock.MagicMock()
    ad.adb_logcat_file_path = str(
        tmp_path / "adblog,serial,02-29_14-02-19.123.txt"
    )
    ad.adb = mock.MagicMock()

    begin_time = "02-29 14:02:20.123"

    with mock.patch.object(android_device.utils, "create_dir"), mock.patch.object(
        android_device, "open", mock.mock_open()
    ) as output_file:
        ad.cat_adb_log(begin_time, "excerpt")

    excerpt_path = output_file.call_args[0][0]
    excerpt_name = os.path.basename(excerpt_path)

    # ':' is forbidden by Windows in filenames. The start timestamp is part of
    # the generated AdbLogExcerpts filename and therefore must be sanitized.
    assert ":" not in excerpt_name
    assert excerpt_name.startswith("excerpt,02-29 14-02-20.123,")
    assert excerpt_name.endswith(".txt")

import pytest

import esper


class Position:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


class Velocity:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


def test_create_entity_without_components_registers_an_empty_entity():
    world = esper.World()

    entity = world.create_entity()
    following_entity = world.create_entity()

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.components_for_entity(entity) == ()
    assert world.entity_exists(following_entity)
    assert following_entity == entity + 1


def test_empty_entity_can_be_built_up_with_components_later():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    position = Position(10, 20)
    velocity = Velocity(1, 2)
    world.add_component(entity, position)
    world.add_component(entity, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity
    assert world.has_components(entity, Position, Velocity)


def test_create_entity_with_components_still_registers_entity_and_components():
    world = esper.World()
    position = Position(1, 2)

    entity = world.create_entity(position)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.get_component(Position) == [(entity, position)]


def test_add_component_rejects_an_id_that_was_not_created():
    world = esper.World()
    nonexistent_entity = 123

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(nonexistent_entity, None)

    assert not world.entity_exists(nonexistent_entity)
    assert world.get_component(type(None)) == []


def test_empty_entity_can_be_deleted_and_cannot_be_reused_by_add_component():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    world.delete_entity(entity, immediate=True)

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Position())


def test_add_component_rejects_entity_marked_for_delayed_deletion():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    world.delete_entity(entity)

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Position())

    world.process()
    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)

from pyupgrade import _fix_escape_sequences


@pytest.mark.parametrize('newline', ('\n', '\r\n'))
def test_line_continuation_in_triple_quoted_string_is_not_made_raw(newline):
    source = (
        'value = """\\' + newline +
        '    import doesnotexist' + newline +
        newline +
        '    x = 1' + newline +
        '    """'
    )

    assert _fix_escape_sequences(source) == source


@pytest.mark.parametrize('newline', ('\n', '\r\n'))
def test_invalid_escape_with_line_continuation_is_escaped_not_raw(newline):
    # Adding a raw prefix would make the initial backslash and physical newline
    # part of the string value.  Keep the continuation intact and repair the
    # independently-invalid escape instead.
    source = (
        'value = """\\' + newline +
        '    pattern = \\d' + newline +
        '    """'
    )
    expected = (
        'value = """\\' + newline +
        '    pattern = \\\\d' + newline +
        '    """'
    )

    assert _fix_escape_sequences(source) == expected

from zarr.store import MemoryStore


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("method", "expected_value"),
    [
        ("empty", None),
        ("zeros", 0),
        ("ones", 1),
        ("full", 13),
        ("empty_like", None),
        ("zeros_like", 0),
        ("ones_like", 1),
        ("full_like", 7),

)
def test_group_creation_convenience_methods_create_children(
    method: str, expected_value: int | None
) -> None:
    """Group convenience methods retain the established name-based Group API."""
    root = Group.create(MemoryStore(mode="w"), zarr_format=3)
    group = root.create_group("nested")
    prototype = group.create_array(
        "prototype",
        shape=(2, 3),
        dtype="int16",
        fill_value=7,
    )
    name = f"{method}_result"

    if method == "full":
        result = group.full(name, shape=(2, 3), fill_value=13, dtype="int16")
    elif method.endswith("_like"):
        result = getattr(group, method)(name, prototype)
    else:
        result = getattr(group, method)(name, shape=(2, 3), dtype="int16")

    assert result.path == f"nested/{name}"
    assert group[name].path == f"nested/{name}"
    assert result.shape == (2, 3)

    if expected_value is not None:

import asyncio
import logging
import socket
import threading
import time

from aiosmtpd.controller import Controller
from aiosmtpd.handlers import Debugging


class SlowRCPTHandler(Debugging):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.started = threading.Event()
        self.cancelled = threading.Event()

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        self.started.set()
        try:
            await asyncio.sleep(30)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            self.cancelled.set()
            raise
        envelope.rcpt_tos.append(address)
        return "250 OK"


def _free_port():
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    try:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return sock.getsockname()[1]
    finally:
        sock.close()


def _readline(sock):
    sock.settimeout(2)
    data = b""
    while not data.endswith(b"\n"):
        chunk = sock.recv(1)
        assert chunk, "SMTP server unexpectedly closed the connection"
        data += chunk
    return data


def test_disconnect_during_slow_rcpt_cancels_handler_without_smtp_exception(
    caplog,
):
    """EOF during a command hook must cancel the session rather than recover.

    In particular, CancelledError must not be passed through the normal
    command-error handling path, which would log an SMTP session exception and
    attempt to send a 500 response to an already disconnected peer.
    """
    handler = SlowRCPTHandler()
    controller = Controller(
        handler, hostname="127.0.0.1", port=_free_port()
    )
    controller.start()

    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    try:
        with caplog.at_level(logging.ERROR, logger="mail.log"):
            sock.connect(("127.0.0.1", controller.port))
            assert _readline(sock).startswith(b"220 ")

            sock.sendall(
                b"HELO client.example\r\n"
                b"MAIL FROM:<sender@example.com>\r\n"
                b"RCPT TO:<recipient@example.com>\r\n"
            )
            assert _readline(sock).startswith(b"250 ")
            assert _readline(sock).startswith(b"250 ")

            assert handler.started.wait(2), "RCPT hook was not called"

            # Closing without reading the RCPT reply reproduces clients which
            # send input then ignore server responses.
            sock.close()
            assert handler.cancelled.wait(2), (
                "EOF did not cancel the command handler"
            )

            # Give the server task an opportunity to finish after cancellation.
            time.sleep(0.05)

        assert not any(
            "SMTP session exception" in record.getMessage()
            for record in caplog.records
        )
    finally:
        sock.close()
        controller.stop()


def test_pipelined_input_after_slow_rcpt_does_not_leave_server_stuck():
    """Queued DATA input after EOF must not cause an endless bad-syntax loop."""
    handler = SlowRCPTHandler()
    controller = Controller(
        handler, hostname="127.0.0.1", port=_free_port()
    )
    controller.start()

    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    try:
        sock.connect(("127.0.0.1", controller.port))
        assert _readline(sock).startswith(b"220 ")

        sock.sendall(
            b"HELO client.example\r\n"
            b"MAIL FROM:<sender@example.com>\r\n"
        )
        assert _readline(sock).startswith(b"250 ")
        assert _readline(sock).startswith(b"250 ")

        # Match the reported case: commands and message data are already
        # buffered while the RCPT hook is still awaiting external work.
        sock.sendall(
            b"RCPT TO:<recipient@example.com>\r\n"
            b"DATA\r\n"
            b"test message\r\n"
            b".\r\n"
        )
        assert handler.started.wait(2)
        sock.close()
        assert handler.cancelled.wait(2)

        # A server which swallowed cancellation can remain in a busy loop
        # processing EOF as empty SMTP commands.  It must instead remain able
        # to serve a new client promptly.
        probe = socket.create_connection(
            ("127.0.0.1", controller.port), timeout=2
        )
        try:
            assert _readline(probe).startswith(b"220 ")
            probe.sendall(b"QUIT\r\n")
            assert _readline(probe).startswith(b"221 ")
        finally:
            probe.close()
    finally:
        sock.close()
        controller.stop()

import pytest

from wemake_python_styleguide.violations.best_practices import (
    GettingElementByUnpackingViolation,
)
from wemake_python_styleguide.visitors.ast.builtins import (
    WrongAssignmentVisitor,
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize('code', [
    'name, *_ = get_address()',
    'names[0], *_ = get_address()',
    'self.name, *_ = get_address()',
    '(name, street), *_ = get_address()',
    'name, street, *_ = get_address()',
    'name, _, city, *_ = get_address()',
    'name, _, self.city, *_ = get_address()',
])
def test_wps472_detects_complex_unpacking_targets(
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
    code,
):
    """
    WPS472 is reported when ignored starred unpacking follows valid targets.

    Some complex assignment targets can also be subject to other assignment
    rules. This test specifically verifies the WPS472 behavior requested by
    this issue.
    """
    tree = parse_ast_tree(code)
    visitor = WrongAssignmentVisitor(default_options, tree=tree)

    visitor.run()

    assert any(
        isinstance(violation, GettingElementByUnpackingViolation)
        for violation in visitor.violations
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize('code', [
    'name, *remaining = get_address()',
    '*remaining, name = get_address()',
    'name, *_, city = get_address()',
])
def test_wps472_does_not_report_unpacking_that_keeps_the_remainder(
    default_options,
    parse_ast_tree,
    code,
):
    """WPS472 only applies when the discarded starred target is at an end."""
    tree = parse_ast_tree(code)
    visitor = WrongAssignmentVisitor(default_options, tree=tree)

    visitor.run()

    assert not any(
        isinstance(violation, GettingElementByUnpackingViolation)
        for violation in visitor.violations
    )

import json
from datetime import datetime

import pytest

from stix2 import FileSystemStore
from stix2.v21 import observables


_FILE_HASHES = {
    "SHA-256": (
        "841a8921140aba50671ebb0770fecc4ee308c4952cfeff8de154ab14eeef4649"
    ),
}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "observable",
    [
        observables.File(
            name="example.exe",
            size=68 * 1000,
            magic_number_hex="50000000",
            hashes=_FILE_HASHES,
        ),
        observables.IPv4Address(value="198.51.100.42"),
    ],
)
def test_filesystem_store_adds_sco_without_modified_or_file_timestamps(
    tmpdir, observable,
):
    """SCOs with no timestamp properties must be writable."""
    store = FileSystemStore(str(tmpdir))

    assert "modified" not in observable
    assert "mtime" not in observable
    assert "ctime" not in observable
    assert "atime" not in observable

    store.add(observable)

    object_dir = tmpdir / observable["type"] / observable["id"]
    written_files = list(object_dir.visit("*.json"))
    assert len(written_files) == 1

    with written_files[0].open() as stored_file:
        stored_data = json.load(stored_file)

    assert stored_data["id"] == observable["id"]
    assert stored_data["type"] == observable["type"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("timestamp_property", ["mtime", "ctime", "atime"])
def test_filesystem_store_adds_file_sco_with_available_file_timestamp(
    tmpdir, timestamp_property,
):
    """File SCO timestamp properties are valid alternatives to ``modified``."""
    timestamp = datetime(2020, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
    observable = observables.File(
        name="timestamped.exe",
        hashes=_FILE_HASHES,
        **{timestamp_property: timestamp}
    )
    store = FileSystemStore(str(tmpdir))

    store.add(observable)

    object_dir = tmpdir / observable["type"] / observable["id"]
    written_files = list(object_dir.visit("*.json"))
    assert len(written_files) == 1

    with written_files[0].open() as stored_file:
        assert json.load(stored_file)["id"] == observable["id"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "observable",
    [
        observables.File(name="no-times.exe", hashes=_FILE_HASHES),
        observables.IPv4Address(value="203.0.113.17"),
    ],
)
def test_filesystem_store_retrieves_stored_unversioned_sco(tmpdir, observable):
    """Retrieval must not assume that every stored object has ``modified``."""
    store = FileSystemStore(str(tmpdir))

    store.add(observable)

    retrieved = store.get(observable["id"])

    assert retrieved is not None
    assert retrieved["id"] == observable["id"]
    assert retrieved["type"] == observable["type"]

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, alias",
    [
        (
            """
            WITH arrayJoin([(1, [2, 3])]) AS arr
            SELECT arr
            """,
            "arr",
        ),
        (
            """
            WITH arrayJoin([1, 2, 3]) AS item
            SELECT item
            """,
            "item",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_clickhouse_with_arrayjoin_expression_alias_parses(sql, alias):
    query = parse_one(sql, dialect="clickhouse")

    assert len(query.ctes) == 1

    with_expression = query.ctes[0]
    assert with_expression.alias_or_name == alias
    assert isinstance(with_expression.this, exp.Explode)

    selected_expression = query.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(selected_expression, exp.Column)
    assert selected_expression.name == alias

import numpy as np
import pytest

from unyt import cm, unyt_array, unyt_quantity


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "take",
    [
        pytest.param(lambda array, index: array.take(index), id="method"),
        pytest.param(lambda array, index: np.take(array, index), id="numpy_function"),
    ],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("index", "expected"),
    [
        pytest.param(0, 1, id="python_integer"),
        pytest.param(np.int64(1), 2, id="numpy_integer"),
        pytest.param(-1, 3, id="negative_integer"),
        pytest.param(np.array(0), 1, id="zero_dimensional_integer_array"),
    ],
)
def test_take_scalar_index_preserves_units(take, index, expected):
    array = unyt_array([1, 2, 3], cm)

    result = take(array, index)

    assert isinstance(result, unyt_quantity)
    assert result.units == array.units
    assert result.value == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "take",
    [
        pytest.param(
            lambda array: array.take(1, axis=0),
            id="method",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            lambda array: np.take(array, 1, axis=0),
            id="numpy_function",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_take_scalar_index_along_axis_preserves_units(take):
    array = unyt_array([[1, 2], [3, 4]], cm)

    result = take(array)

    assert isinstance(result, unyt_array)
    assert result.units == array.units
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(result.value, [3, 4])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "take",
    [
        pytest.param(
            lambda array, out: array.take(1, out=out),
            id="method",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            lambda array, out: np.take(array, 1, out=out),
            id="numpy_function",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_take_scalar_index_with_out_returns_and_preserves_out(take):
    array = unyt_array([1, 2, 3], cm)
    out = unyt_array(np.empty((), dtype=int), cm)

    result = take(array, out)

    # NumPy's take contract returns the supplied output object. Supplying
    # ``out`` must not cause its units to be multiplied by the input units.
    assert result is out
    assert out.units == array.units
    assert out.value == 2

import numpy as np
import pytest
from numpy.testing import assert_array_equal

from unyt import unyt_array
from unyt.exceptions import UnitOperationError


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operation",
    [
        lambda base, exponent: base**exponent,
        np.power,
    ],
    ids=["operator", "numpy_power"],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "exponent",
    [
        np.array([1, 2, 3, 4]),
        unyt_array([1, 2, 3, 4]),
    ],
    ids=["ndarray", "dimensionless_unyt_array"],
)
def test_dimensionless_array_power_accepts_array_exponents(operation, exponent):
    """
    Array exponents must be evaluated elementwise, regardless of whether the
    dimensionless exponent is a NumPy array or a unyt array.
    """
    base = unyt_array([1, 2, 3, 4])

    result = operation(base, exponent)

    assert isinstance(result, unyt_array)
    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    assert_array_equal(result, [1, 4, 27, 256])


def test_array_power_with_array_exponent_follows_numpy_broadcasting():
    base = unyt_array([[2, 3, 4], [5, 6, 7]])
    exponent = unyt_array([0, 1, 2])

    result = base**exponent

    assert result.units.is_dimensionless
    assert_array_equal(result, [[1, 3, 16], [1, 6, 49]])


def test_dimensional_base_with_array_exponent_is_rejected():
    """
    A varying exponent on dimensional data cannot have one well-defined output
    unit, even when the exponent itself is dimensionless.
    """
    base = unyt_array([1, 2, 3], "m")
    exponent = unyt_array([1, 2, 3])

    with pytest.raises(UnitOperationError):
        base**exponent


def test_array_power_rejects_dimensional_array_exponent():
    base = unyt_array([1, 2, 3])
    exponent = unyt_array([1, 2, 3], "s")

    with pytest.raises(UnitOperationError):
        base**exponent

def _make_setuptools_egg(tmpdir, python_version):
    egg = tmpdir.join(

    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(egg), "w") as archive:
        archive.writestr(
            "EGG-INFO/PKG-INFO",
            "Metadata-Version: 1.0\n"
            "Name: example\n"
            "Version: 1.0\n"
            "Summary: test egg\n",
        )
    return str(egg)

        ("3.8", "cp38"),
    ],
)
def test_repackaged_setuptools_egg_uses_correct_cpython_abi_tag(
        tmpdir, python_version, expected_abi):
    egg = _make_setuptools_egg(tmpdir, python_version)
    platform = EPDPlatform.from_epd_string("win-64")

    metadata = SetuptoolsEggMetadata.from_egg(egg, platform)

    assert metadata.python_tag == "cp{0}".format(python_version.replace(".", ""))
    assert metadata.abi_tag == expected_abi

import json

import pytest

from stix2 import AttackPattern, Identity, Indicator
from stix2.common import COMMON_PROPERTIES
from stix2.exceptions import ExtraFieldsError, MissingFieldsError


def test_labels_is_not_a_universally_applied_common_property():
    """Only SDO types which define labels should expose the property."""
    assert "labels" not in COMMON_PROPERTIES

    with pytest.raises(ExtraFieldsError, match=r"labels"):
        AttackPattern(
            name="Spearphishing Attachment",
            labels=["phishing"],
        )


def test_labels_is_optional_when_an_sdo_declares_it_as_optional():
    identity_without_labels = Identity(
        name="Example Organization",
        identity_class="organization",
    )
    assert "labels" not in json.loads(str(identity_without_labels))

    identity_with_labels = Identity(
        name="Example Organization",
        identity_class="organization",
        labels=["partner", "trusted"],
    )
    assert json.loads(str(identity_with_labels))["labels"] == [
        "partner",
        "trusted",
    ]


def test_indicator_makes_its_labels_property_required():
    pattern = 'file:hashes.md5 = "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e"'

    with pytest.raises(MissingFieldsError, match=r"labels"):
        Indicator(pattern=pattern)

    indicator = Indicator(
        pattern=pattern,
        labels=["malicious-activity"],
    )
    assert json.loads(str(indicator))["labels"] == ["malicious-activity"]

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _cast_type(sql):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="duckdb")
    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)

    assert cast is not None
    return cast.to


def test_duckdb_cast_to_array_of_struct_parses_reported_query():
    data_type = _cast_type(
        "SELECT CAST([struct_pack(a := 1)] AS STRUCT(a BIGINT)[])"
    )

    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY

    struct_type = data_type.expressions[0]
    assert struct_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT
    assert len(struct_type.expressions) == 1

    field = struct_type.expressions[0]
    assert field.this.name == "a"
    assert field.kind.this == exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT


def test_duckdb_cast_to_array_of_struct_keeps_multiple_field_definitions():
    data_type = _cast_type(
        "SELECT CAST(NULL AS STRUCT(id BIGINT, name VARCHAR, scores DOUBLE[])[])"
    )

    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY

    struct_type = data_type.expressions[0]
    assert struct_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT

    fields = {field.this.name: field.kind for field in struct_type.expressions}
    assert fields["id"].this == exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT
    assert fields["name"].this == exp.DataType.Type.VARCHAR
    assert fields["scores"].this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY
    assert fields["scores"].expressions[0].this == exp.DataType.Type.DOUBLE

import re
from unittest.mock import patch

from mobilus_client.app import App
from mobilus_client.config import Config
from mobilus_client.messages.encryptor import MessageEncryptor
from mobilus_client.mqtt_client import MqttClient


CLIENT_ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^[0-9A-F]{12}$")


def make_config() -> Config:
    return Config(
        gateway_host="host",
        user_login="login",
        user_password="password",
    )


def client_id(client: MqttClient) -> str:
    return client._client_id.decode()


def test_config_does_not_generate_a_client_id() -> None:
    """Config may retain an optional compatibility field, but must not create IDs."""
    first_config = make_config()
    second_config = make_config()

    assert first_config.client_id is None
    assert second_config.client_id is None


def test_every_mqtt_client_initialization_generates_a_unique_valid_id() -> None:
    """The MQTT client itself owns generation of its per-connection identifier."""
    first_client = MqttClient()
    second_client = MqttClient()

    first_id = client_id(first_client)
    second_id = client_id(second_client)

    assert CLIENT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(first_id)
    assert CLIENT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(second_id)
    assert first_id != second_id


def test_apps_sharing_one_config_use_their_own_client_topics() -> None:
    """One Config must support multiple independent MQTT connections."""
    config = make_config()
    first_app = App(config)
    second_app = App(config)

    first_id = client_id(first_app.client)
    second_id = client_id(second_app.client)

    assert CLIENT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(first_id)
    assert CLIENT_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(second_id)
    assert first_id != second_id

    with patch.object(MqttClient, "subscribe", autospec=True) as subscribe:
        first_app.client.on_connect(
            first_app.client,
            first_app.client._userdata,
            None,
            0,
        )
        second_app.client.on_connect(
            second_app.client,
            second_app.client._userdata,
            None,
            0,
        )

    assert subscribe.call_args_list[0].args == (
        first_app.client,
        [(first_id, 0), ("clients", 0)],
    )
    assert subscribe.call_args_list[1].args == (
        second_app.client,
        [(second_id, 0), ("clients", 0)],
    )


def test_request_encryption_uses_the_mqtt_clients_own_id() -> None:
    """Protocol operations must use the ID associated with this MQTT client."""
    app = App(make_config())
    expected_client_id = client_id(app.client)

    with (
        patch.object(MqttClient, "is_connected", return_value=True),
        patch.object(MessageEncryptor, "encrypt", return_value=b"encrypted") as encrypt,
        patch.object(MqttClient, "publish", autospec=True) as publish,
    ):
        app.client.send_request(
            "login",
            login="login",
            password=app.config.user_key,
        )

    assert encrypt.call_args.args[1] == expected_client_id
    publish.assert_called_once_with(app.client, "module", b"encrypted")

import ctypes
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest


PYDEVD_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src" / "debugpy" / "_vendored" / "pydevd"
if str(PYDEVD_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(PYDEVD_ROOT))

from _pydevd_bundle.pydevd_xml import get_type


def _debugger_children(value):
    """Return the children that pydevd would expose for a value."""
    _, _, resolver = get_type(value)
    assert resolver is not None
    return resolver, resolver.get_dictionary(value)


def _indexed_children(children):
    return {name: value for name, value in children.items() if name.isdigit()}


def test_ctypes_array_from_writable_buffer_is_enumerated_with_length():
    # This is the form used by the issue report: ctypes views over a bytearray.
    file_bytes = bytearray(b"\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05")
    array = (ctypes.c_uint8 * len(file_bytes)).from_buffer(file_bytes)

    resolver, children = _debugger_children(array)

    # It must not fall through to the generic object resolver, which only
    # exposes special/protected attributes and has no indexed children.
    assert _indexed_children(children) == {
        "0": 1,
        "1": 2,
        "2": 3,
        "3": 4,
        "4": 5,
    }
    assert children["len()"] == 5

    # Expanding an indexed child is part of debugger enumeration, rather than
    # merely presenting synthetic values in get_dictionary().
    assert resolver.resolve(array, "0") == 1
    assert resolver.resolve(array, "4") == 5


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "array, expected",
    [
        ((ctypes.c_int * 3)(-10, 0, 42), {"0": -10, "1": 0, "2": 42}),
        ((ctypes.c_char * 3)(b"a", b"b", b"c"), {"0": b"a", "1": b"b", "2": b"c"}),
        ((ctypes.c_uint8 * 0)(), {}),
    ],
)
def test_ctypes_array_types_are_displayed_as_containers(array, expected):
    _, children = _debugger_children(array)

    assert _indexed_children(children) == expected
    assert children["len()"] == len(array)


def test_nested_ctypes_arrays_can_be_expanded_recursively():
    Row = ctypes.c_uint16 * 2
    Matrix = Row * 2
    matrix = Matrix(Row(10, 20), Row(30, 40))

    _, outer_children = _debugger_children(matrix)
    assert outer_children["len()"] == 2
    assert set(_indexed_children(outer_children)) == {"0", "1"}

    # Each element is itself a ctypes array and must be recognized when the
    # variables UI expands that child.
    _, first_row_children = _debugger_children(outer_children["0"])
    _, second_row_children = _debugger_children(outer_children["1"])

    assert _indexed_children(first_row_children) == {"0": 10, "1": 20}
    assert _indexed_children(second_row_children) == {"0": 30, "1": 40}
    assert first_row_children["len()"] == 2
    assert second_row_children["len()"] == 2

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_notnull_parses_as_is_not_null_with_default_dialect():
    shorthand = parse_one("SELECT * FROM datasets WHERE mmh_trip_start NOTNULL")
    standard = parse_one("SELECT * FROM datasets WHERE mmh_trip_start IS NOT NULL")

    assert shorthand == standard

    predicate = shorthand.args["where"].this
    assert isinstance(predicate, exp.Not)
    assert isinstance(predicate.this, exp.Is)
    assert isinstance(predicate.this.expression, exp.Null)
    assert predicate.this.this.name == "mmh_trip_start"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "operand",
    [
        "trip_start",
        "(trip_start + 1)",
        "COALESCE(trip_start, fallback)",
        '"MixedCase"',
    ],
)
def test_notnull_accepts_postfix_expression_operands_in_postgres(operand):
    shorthand = parse_one(
        f"SELECT * FROM events WHERE {operand} NOTNULL",
        read="postgres",
    )
    standard = parse_one(
        f"SELECT * FROM events WHERE {operand} IS NOT NULL",
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert shorthand == standard


def test_notnull_composes_with_boolean_predicates():
    shorthand = parse_one(
        """
        SELECT *
        FROM events
        WHERE started_at NOTNULL
          AND (finished_at NOTNULL OR cancelled_at IS NULL)
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )
    standard = parse_one(
        """
        SELECT *
        FROM events
        WHERE started_at IS NOT NULL
          AND (finished_at IS NOT NULL OR cancelled_at IS NULL)
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert shorthand == standard
    assert isinstance(shorthand.args["where"].this, exp.And)


def test_original_postgres_query_with_notnull_matches_standard_null_check():
    query = """
    SELECT datasets.a,
           id AS history_id,
           app_users.id AS user_id,
           companies.name AS companyname,
           app_users.email AS email,
           app_users.group_id AS group_id
    FROM datasets
    JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
    JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
    WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
      AND (mmh_trip_start NOTNULL)
    """

    shorthand = parse_one(query, read="postgres")
    standard = parse_one(query.replace("NOTNULL", "IS NOT NULL"), read="postgres")

    assert shorthand == standard

    where = shorthand.args["where"].this
    assert isinstance(where, exp.And)

    predicate = where.expression
    assert isinstance(predicate, exp.Paren)
    assert isinstance(predicate.this, exp.Not)
    assert isinstance(predicate.this.this, exp.Is)
    assert isinstance(predicate.this.this.expression, exp.Null)
    assert predicate.this.this.this.name == "mmh_trip_start"

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import pytest

import narwhals as nw


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("values", "expected"),
    [
        ([1.0, None, None, 2.0], 2),
        ([None, None, None], 0),
        ([1, 1, None, 2, 2, None], 2),
        ([1, 2, 3], 3),
    ],
)
def test_series_n_unique_does_not_count_polars_nulls(
    values: list[Any], expected: int
) -> None:
    # pandas is the compatibility target: missing values are not unique values.
    assert pd.Series(values).nunique() == expected

    pandas_result = nw.from_native(pd.Series(values), series_only=True).n_unique()
    polars_result = nw.from_native(
        pl.Series("value", values), series_only=True
    ).n_unique()

    assert pandas_result == expected
    assert polars_result == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("values", "expected"),
    [
        ([1.0, None, None, 2.0], 2),
        ([None, None], 0),
        ([1, 1, None, 2, 2, None], 2),
    ],
)
def test_expression_n_unique_does_not_count_polars_nulls(
    values: list[Any], expected: int
) -> None:
    pandas_frame = pd.DataFrame({"value": values})
    polars_frame = pl.DataFrame({"value": values})

    pandas_result = (
        nw.DataFrame(pandas_frame).select(nw.col("value").n_unique())["value"][0]
    )
    polars_eager_result = (
        nw.DataFrame(polars_frame).select(nw.col("value").n_unique())["value"][0]
    )
    polars_lazy_result = (
        nw.LazyFrame(polars_frame.lazy())
        .select(nw.col("value").n_unique())
        .collect()["value"][0]
    )

    assert pandas_result == expected
    assert polars_eager_result == expected
    assert polars_lazy_result == expected

import pytest

import esper


class Position:
    def __init__(self, x=0):
        self.x = x


class Velocity:
    pass


def test_create_entity_without_components_creates_an_existing_empty_entity():
    world = esper.World()

    first_entity = world.create_entity()
    second_entity = world.create_entity()

    assert first_entity == 1
    assert second_entity == first_entity + 1
    assert world.entity_exists(first_entity)
    assert world.entity_exists(second_entity)
    assert world.components_for_entity(first_entity) == ()


def test_empty_entity_remains_valid_after_processing_and_can_be_built_later():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    # Empty entities should not disappear merely because the world is processed.
    world.process()
    assert world.entity_exists(entity)

    position = Position(42)
    velocity = Velocity()
    world.add_component(entity, position)
    world.add_component(entity, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity
    assert world.has_components(entity, Position, Velocity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == [(entity, position)]


def test_add_component_rejects_a_never_created_entity_without_creating_it():
    world = esper.World()
    made_up_entity = 123

    # Use None specifically, as in the reported reproduction case.
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(made_up_entity, None)

    assert not world.entity_exists(made_up_entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(made_up_entity)


def test_add_component_rejects_an_entity_that_was_deleted():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    world.delete_entity(entity, immediate=True)

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Position())

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)


def test_empty_entities_can_be_deleted_immediately_or_deferred():
    world = esper.World()

    immediate_entity = world.create_entity()
    world.delete_entity(immediate_entity, immediate=True)
    assert not world.entity_exists(immediate_entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(immediate_entity)

    deferred_entity = world.create_entity()
    world.delete_entity(deferred_entity)
    assert not world.entity_exists(deferred_entity)

    world.process()
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(deferred_entity)

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest

import zarr


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("method_name", "kwargs", "expected"),
    [
        ("empty", {"shape": (2, 3), "dtype": "i4"}, None),
        ("zeros", {"shape": (2, 3), "dtype": "i4"}, 0),
        ("ones", {"shape": (2, 3), "dtype": "i4"}, 1),
        ("full", {"shape": (2, 3), "dtype": "i4", "fill_value": 7}, 7),
    ],
)
def test_group_creation_helpers_accept_positional_name_with_warning(
    method_name: str, kwargs: dict[str, object], expected: int | None
) -> None:
    group = zarr.group()
    name = f"positional_{method_name}"

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        array = getattr(group, method_name)(name, **kwargs)

    assert group[name] == array
    assert array.shape == (2, 3)
    assert array.dtype == np.dtype("i4")
    if expected is not None:
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(array[:], np.full((2, 3), expected, dtype="i4"))


def test_group_create_and_array_accept_positional_name() -> None:
    group = zarr.group()

    # ``create`` is the backwards-compatible alias for ``create_array``.
    created = group.create("created", shape=(3,), dtype="i2")
    assert group["created"] == created
    assert created.shape == (3,)
    assert created.dtype == np.dtype("i2")

    # ``array`` remains deprecated as an API, but its legacy positional name
    # argument must still work during the keyword-only transition.
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", DeprecationWarning)
        array = group.array("array", shape=(4,), dtype="i4")

    assert group["array"] == array
    assert array.shape == (4,)
    assert array.dtype == np.dtype("i4")


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("method_name", "kwargs", "expected"),
    [
        ("empty_like", {}, None),
        ("zeros_like", {}, 0),
        ("ones_like", {}, 1),
        ("full_like", {"fill_value": 9}, 9),
    ],
)
def test_group_like_helpers_accept_positional_name_and_data_with_warning(
    method_name: str, kwargs: dict[str, object], expected: int | None
) -> None:
    group = zarr.group()
    data = np.arange(6, dtype="i2").reshape(2, 3)
    name = f"positional_{method_name}"

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        array = getattr(group, method_name)(name, data, **kwargs)

    assert group[name] == array
    assert array.shape == data.shape
    assert array.dtype == data.dtype
    if expected is not None:
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(
            array[:], np.full(data.shape, expected, dtype=data.dtype)
        )


def test_positional_name_works_for_nested_group_and_keyword_calls_do_not_warn() -> None:
    root = zarr.group()
    nested = root.create_group("foo").create_group("bar")

    # This is the reported usage pattern: a positional name plus keyword-only
    # creation options in a nested group.
    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        positional = nested.zeros("baz", shape=(2, 2), dtype="i4")

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(positional[:], np.zeros((2, 2), dtype="i4"))
    assert root["foo/bar/baz"] == positional

    # The supported keyword-only spelling must remain warning-free.
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        keyword = nested.ones(name="keyword", shape=(2,), dtype="i4")

    assert not any(issubclass(item.category, FutureWarning) for item in caught)
    np.testing.assert_array_equal(keyword[:], np.ones((2,), dtype="i4"))

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", ["spark", "databricks"])
def test_raw_string_parses_in_regexp_replace(dialect):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT regexp_replace('100-200', r'([^0-9])', '')",
        read=dialect,
    )

    regexp_replace = expression.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(regexp_replace, exp.RegexpReplace)
    assert regexp_replace.this.this == "100-200"
    assert regexp_replace.expression.this == "([^0-9])"
    assert regexp_replace.args["replacement"].this == ""


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", ["spark", "databricks"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "prefix, quote",
    [
        ("r", "'"),
        ("R", "'"),
        ("r", '"'),
        ("R", '"'),
    ],
)
def test_raw_string_accepts_supported_prefix_and_quote_forms(dialect, prefix, quote):
    value = r"([a-z]+)\d{2}"

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        f"SELECT {prefix}{quote}{value}{quote}",
        read=dialect,
    )

    raw_string = expression.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(raw_string, exp.RawString)
    assert raw_string.this == value


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", ["spark", "databricks"])
def test_raw_string_preserves_backslashes_literally(dialect):
    value = r"\d+\s+\n\t"

    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(f"SELECT r'{value}'", read=dialect)
    raw_string = expression.expressions[0]

    assert isinstance(raw_string, exp.RawString)
    assert raw_string.this == value

    # A generator may render a raw string as an escaped ordinary string, but
    # that output must retain the raw literal's value when read again.
    rendered = expression.sql(dialect=dialect)
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, read=dialect).expressions[0]
    assert reparsed.this == value


@pytest.mark.parametrize("dialect", ["spark", "databricks"])
def test_raw_strings_work_as_empty_and_multiple_select_expressions(dialect):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT r'', r'first', R'second'",
        read=dialect,
    )

    raw_strings = expression.expressions
    assert len(raw_strings) == 3
    assert all(isinstance(raw_string, exp.RawString) for raw_string in raw_strings)
    assert [raw_string.this for raw_string in raw_strings] == ["", "first", "second"]

import pytest

from sqlglot import parse_one


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "postgres_sql, standard_sql",
    [
        (
            "SELECT * FROM measurements WHERE reading NOTNULL",
            "SELECT * FROM measurements WHERE reading IS NOT NULL",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT * FROM measurements WHERE reading ISNULL",
            "SELECT * FROM measurements WHERE reading IS NULL",
        ),
        (
            """
            SELECT *
            FROM measurements
            WHERE (reading NOTNULL)
              AND ((backup_reading ISNULL) OR (status NOTNULL))
            """,
            """
            SELECT *
            FROM measurements
            WHERE (reading IS NOT NULL)
              AND ((backup_reading IS NULL) OR (status IS NOT NULL))
            """,
        ),
        (
            "SELECT * FROM measurements WHERE (reading + adjustment) NOTNULL",
            "SELECT * FROM measurements WHERE (reading + adjustment) IS NOT NULL",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_postfix_null_predicates_match_standard_null_predicates(postgres_sql, standard_sql):
    """PostgreSQL's ISNULL/NOTNULL postfix forms must retain their null-test semantics."""
    postfix_expression = parse_one(postgres_sql, read="postgres")
    standard_expression = parse_one(standard_sql, read="postgres")

    assert postfix_expression == standard_expression
    assert postfix_expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == standard_expression.sql(dialect="postgres")


def test_notnull_parses_in_the_joined_query_shape_from_the_report():
    postgres_sql = """
        SELECT datasets.a,
               id AS history_id,
               app_users.id AS user_id,
               companies.name AS companyname,
               app_users.email AS email,
               app_users.group_id AS group_id
        FROM datasets
        JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
        JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
        WHERE datasets.companyid = '405'
          AND (mmh_trip_start NOTNULL)
    """

    standard_sql = postgres_sql.replace("mmh_trip_start NOTNULL", "mmh_trip_start IS NOT NULL")

    assert parse_one(postgres_sql, read="postgres") == parse_one(standard_sql, read="postgres")


def test_notnull_keyword_does_not_affect_quoted_identifier():
    postfix_expression = parse_one(
        'SELECT "NOTNULL" FROM data WHERE checked_at NOTNULL',
        read="postgres",
    )
    standard_expression = parse_one(
        'SELECT "NOTNULL" FROM data WHERE checked_at IS NOT NULL',
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert postfix_expression == standard_expression

        stix2.Indicator(pattern=PATTERN)

        labels=["malicious-activity"],
        pattern=PATTERN,
    )
    assert indicator["labels"] == ["malicious-activity"]

    """An SDO whose labels are optional must support both forms."""
    without_labels = stix2.Identity(
        name="Example identity",
        identity_class="organization",
    )
    assert "labels" not in without_labels

    with_labels = stix2.Identity(
        name="Example identity",
        identity_class="organization",
        labels=["partner"],
    )
    assert with_labels["labels"] == ["partner"]


def test_labels_are_not_implicitly_added_to_every_sdo():
    """
    labels must not be inherited as a common property by object types which do
    not define it.
    """
    attack_pattern = stix2.AttackPattern(name="Spearphishing Attachment")
    assert "labels" not in attack_pattern

    with pytest.raises(ExtraFieldsError) as exc_info:
        stix2.AttackPattern(
            name="Spearphishing Attachment",
            labels=["phishing"],
        )

    assert exc_info.value.fields == ["labels"]

import zipfile

import pytest

from ...platforms import EPDPlatform
from ..setuptools_egg import SetuptoolsEggMetadata


def _make_setuptools_egg(tmp_path, python_version):
    """Create a minimal platform-specific setuptools egg."""
    egg_path = tmp_path / (
        "example-1.0-py{0}-win-amd64.egg".format(python_version)
    )
    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(egg_path), "w") as egg:
        egg.writestr(
            "EGG-INFO/PKG-INFO",
            "Metadata-Version: 1.0\n"
            "Name: example\n"
            "Version: 1.0\n"
            "Summary: test package\n",
        )
    return egg_path


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "python_version, expected_python_tag, expected_abi_tag",
    [
        # The old pymalloc ABI suffix must still be retained before Python 3.8.
        ("3.7", "cp37", "cp37m"),
        # Python 3.8 removed the pymalloc ABI suffix.
        ("3.8", "cp38", "cp38"),
    ],
)
def test_repackaged_setuptools_egg_uses_correct_abi_for_python_version(
    tmp_path, python_version, expected_python_tag, expected_abi_tag
):
    egg_path = _make_setuptools_egg(tmp_path, python_version)
    platform = EPDPlatform.from_epd_string("win-64")

    metadata = SetuptoolsEggMetadata.from_egg(str(egg_path), platform)

    assert metadata.python_tag == expected_python_tag
    assert metadata.abi_tag == expected_abi_tag
    assert metadata.platform_tag == "win_amd64"

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def test_clickhouse_with_array_join_as_alias():
    query = parse_one(
        """
        WITH arrayJoin([(1, [2, 3])]) AS arr
        SELECT arr
        """,
        dialect="clickhouse",
    )

    assert len(query.ctes) == 1

    cte = query.ctes[0]
    assert cte.alias_or_name == "arr"
    assert cte.args["scalar"] is True
    assert isinstance(cte.this, exp.Explode)
    assert isinstance(cte.this.this, exp.Array)

    selected = query.expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(selected, exp.Column)
    assert selected.name == "arr"


def test_clickhouse_with_multiple_array_join_expression_aliases():
    query = parse_one(
        """
        WITH
          arrayJoin([1, 2]) AS first_value,
          arrayJoin(['a', 'b']) AS second_value
        SELECT first_value, second_value
        """,
        dialect="clickhouse",
    )

    assert [cte.alias_or_name for cte in query.ctes] == [
        "first_value",
        "second_value",
    ]
    assert all(isinstance(cte.this, exp.Explode) for cte in query.ctes)
    assert [expression.name for expression in query.expressions] == [
        "first_value",
        "second_value",
    ]

import re
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

from mobilus_client.app import App
from mobilus_client.config import Config
from mobilus_client.mqtt_client import MqttClient


def _client_id(client: MqttClient) -> str:
    value = client._client_id
    return value.decode() if isinstance(value, bytes) else value


def test_config_does_not_allocate_a_client_id() -> None:
    config = Config(
        gateway_host="gateway",
        user_login="user",
        user_password="password",
    )

    # A Config can be shared by several connections, so it must not allocate
    # one connection's MQTT identity itself.
    assert config.client_id is None


def test_each_app_mqtt_client_gets_a_distinct_generated_id_from_shared_config() -> None:
    config = Config(
        gateway_host="gateway",
        user_login="user",
        user_password="password",
    )

    first_app = App(config)
    second_app = App(config)

    first_id = _client_id(first_app.client)
    second_id = _client_id(second_app.client)

    assert config.client_id is None
    assert first_id != second_id

    for client_id in (first_id, second_id):
        assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9A-F]{12}", client_id)


def test_generated_client_id_is_used_as_the_client_subscription_topic() -> None:
    config = Config(
        gateway_host="gateway",
        user_login="user",
        user_password="password",
    )
    app = App(config)
    client_id = _client_id(app.client)

    # Config has no generated identity to fall back to. The MQTT callbacks
    # must use the identity belonging to this particular client.
    with patch.object(MqttClient, "subscribe", autospec=True) as subscribe:
        app.client.on_connect(app.client, app.client._userdata, None, 0)

    subscribe.assert_called_once_with(
        app.client,
        [
            (client_id, 0),
            ("clients", 0),
        ],
    )

import json

import pytest

import stix2
from stix2.v21 import observables


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "file_kwargs",
    [
        {
            "name": "example.exe",
            "size": 68 * 1000,
            "magic_number_hex": "50000000",
            "hashes": {
                "SHA-256": "841a8921140aba50671ebb0770fecc4ee308c4952cfeff8de154ab14eeef4649",
            },
        },
        {
            "name": "timestamped-example.exe",
            "size": 68001,
            "mtime": "2020-01-02T03:04:05.000Z",
            "hashes": {
                "SHA-256": "941a8921140aba50671ebb0770fecc4ee308c4952cfeff8de154ab14eeef4649",
            },
        },
    ],
    ids=["file-sco-without-optional-timestamps", "file-sco-with-mtime"],
)
def test_filesystem_store_adds_v21_file_sco(tmp_path, file_kwargs):
    """SCOs have an id but do not have the SDO/SRO ``modified`` property."""
    store = stix2.FileSystemStore(str(tmp_path))
    file_observable = observables.File(**file_kwargs)

    assert "modified" not in file_observable

    # This is the operation reported in the issue.  It must not attempt to
    # access a nonexistent ``modified`` property on the SCO.
    store.add(file_observable)

    object_dir = tmp_path / "file" / file_observable.id
    stored_files = list(object_dir.glob("*.json"))
    assert len(stored_files) == 1

    with stored_files[0].open() as f:
        stored_data = json.load(f)

    assert stored_data["type"] == "file"
    assert stored_data["id"] == file_observable.id
    assert stored_data["name"] == file_kwargs["name"]

    # Confirm the object was written in a form which the store's public source
    # side can discover.
    results = store.query([
        stix2.Filter("id", "=", file_observable.id),
    ])
    assert len(results) == 1
    assert results[0].id == file_observable.id
    assert results[0].name == file_kwargs["name"]

import pytest

from pyupgrade import _fix_escape_sequences


@pytest.mark.parametrize('newline', ('\n', '\r\n'))
def test_opening_triple_quote_line_continuation_is_not_made_raw(newline):
    src = (
        'import textwrap' + newline +
        newline +
        'def test_importerror(tmpdir):' + newline +
        '    p1.write(' + newline +
        '        textwrap.dedent(' + newline +
        '            """\\' + newline +
        '        import doesnotexist' + newline +
        newline +
        '        x = 1' + newline +
        '        """' + newline +
        '        )' + newline +
        '    )' + newline
    )

    assert _fix_escape_sequences(src) == src


@pytest.mark.parametrize('newline', ('\n', '\r\n'))
def test_invalid_escape_after_line_continuation_is_escaped_not_made_raw(newline):
    src = 'value = """\\' + newline + r'\d"""' + newline
    expected = 'value = """\\' + newline + r'\\d"""' + newline

    # Adding an r prefix would turn the opening backslash-newline into literal
    # string contents.  Preserve the continuation and repair only \d.
    assert _fix_escape_sequences(src) == expected


def test_invalid_escape_without_line_continuation_can_still_be_made_raw():
    assert _fix_escape_sequences(r'value = """\d"""') == r'value = r"""\d"""'

from __future__ import unicode_literals

from clldutils.badge import badge


def test_badge_preserves_legacy_positional_format_and_markdown_arguments():
    """The formerly documented positional optional arguments remain supported."""
    assert badge('build', 'passing', 'green', 'png', False) == (
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/build-passing-green.png'
    )


def test_badge_accepts_more_than_three_atomic_label_parts():
    """
    The label URL is composed of atomic hyphen-separated parts, rather than
    being limited to the former subject/status/color triple.
    """
    assert badge(
        'coverage',
        '80%',
        'brightgreen',
        'logo-github',
        markdown=False,
        style='flat-square',
    ) == (
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/'
        'coverage-80%25-brightgreen-logo-github.svg?style=flat-square'
    )


def test_badge_accepts_a_label_with_fewer_than_three_parts():
    """
    Flexibility applies at both ends: callers need not invent a color merely
    because the old function required three positional arguments.
    """
    assert badge('documentation', 'available', markdown=False) == (
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/documentation-available.svg'
    )

    """

        'build system',
        'ready',
        '#00ff00',
        'release candidate',
        markdown=False,
    ) == (
        'https://img.shields.io/badge/'
        'build%20system-ready-%2300ff00-release%20candidate.svg'
    )

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected_sql",
    [
        (
            "select cast('1 day' as interval)",
            "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) FROM events",
            "SELECT CAST(duration AS INTERVAL) FROM events",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT CAST(NULL AS INTERVAL(3))",
            "SELECT CAST(NULL AS INTERVAL(3))",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT '1 day'::interval",
            "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_recognizes_interval_as_a_cast_type(sql, expected_sql):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)
    assert cast is not None

    data_type = cast.args["to"]
    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL

    assert expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == expected_sql

    assert "labels" not in COMMON_PROPERTIES


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

        (Malware, {"name": "Example malware"}),

)

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pytest

from zarr.core.group import AsyncGroup, Group
from zarr.store import MemoryStore


@pytest.mark.parametrize("zarr_format", [2, 3])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("method", "expected"),
    [
        ("empty", None),
        ("zeros", 0),
        ("ones", 1),
        ("full", 42),
    ],
)
def test_group_creation_helpers_create_group_relative_arrays(
    zarr_format: int,
    method: str,
    expected: int | None,
) -> None:
    """All constructors create a child of this group in its Zarr format."""
    store = MemoryStore(mode="w")
    root = Group.create(store, zarr_format=zarr_format)
    group = root.create_group("nested")

    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"path": method, "dtype": "i4", "chunks": (1, 3)}
    creator: Callable[..., Any] = getattr(group, method)
    if method == "full":
        array = creator((2, 3), 42, **kwargs)
    else:
        array = creator((2, 3), **kwargs)

    assert array.shape == (2, 3)
    assert array.dtype == np.dtype("i4")
    assert array.metadata.zarr_format == zarr_format

    # The path supplied to a Group method is relative to that Group.
    assert group[method].shape == (2, 3)
    assert method not in root

    if expected is not None:
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(array[:], np.full((2, 3), expected, dtype="i4"))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("zarr_format", [2, 3])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("method", "expected"),
    [
        ("empty_like", None),
        ("zeros_like", 0),
        ("ones_like", 1),
        ("full_like", 7),
    ],
)
def test_group_like_helpers_support_public_array_prototypes(
    zarr_format: int,
    method: str,
    expected: int | None,
) -> None:
    """The synchronous Group API must accept the public synchronous Array."""
    store = MemoryStore(mode="w")
    root = Group.create(store, zarr_format=zarr_format)
    group = root.create_group("nested")

    prototype_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "shape": (2, 3),
        "dtype": "i4",
        "fill_value": 7,
    }
    if zarr_format == 2:
        prototype_kwargs["chunks"] = (1, 3)
    else:
        prototype_kwargs["chunk_shape"] = (1, 3)
    prototype = group.create_array("prototype", **prototype_kwargs)

    creator: Callable[..., Any] = getattr(group, method)
    array = creator(prototype, path=method)

    assert array.shape == prototype.shape
    assert array.dtype == prototype.dtype
    assert array.chunks == prototype.chunks
    assert array.metadata.zarr_format == zarr_format
    assert group[method].shape == prototype.shape

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


ISSUE_QUERY = """
SELECT datasets.a,
       id AS history_id,
       app_users.id AS user_id,
       companies.name AS companyname,
       app_users.email AS email,
       app_users.group_id AS group_id
FROM datasets
JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
  AND (mmh_trip_start NOTNULL)
"""


def test_postgres_notnull_parses_original_query_as_is_not_null():
    expression = parse_one(ISSUE_QUERY, read="postgres")

    expected = parse_one(
        """
        SELECT datasets.a,
               id AS history_id,
               app_users.id AS user_id,
               companies.name AS companyname,
               app_users.email AS email,
               app_users.group_id AS group_id
        FROM datasets
        JOIN companies ON datasets.companyid = companies.companyid
        JOIN app_users USING (short_user_id)
        WHERE (datasets.companyid = '405')
          AND (mmh_trip_start IS NOT NULL)
        """,
        read="postgres",
    )

    assert expression == expected
    assert expression.sql() == expected.sql()

        (
            "SELECT * FROM t WHERE value NOTNULL",

import zipfile

import pytest

from okonomiyaki.file_formats.setuptools_egg import SetuptoolsEggMetadata
from okonomiyaki.platforms import EPDPlatform, PythonImplementation


def _make_setuptools_egg(path, python_version):
    """Create the minimal setuptools egg required for metadata parsing."""
    egg_path = path / "example-1.0-py{}-win-amd64.egg".format(python_version)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(str(egg_path), "w") as egg:
        egg.writestr(
            "EGG-INFO/PKG-INFO",
            "Metadata-Version: 1.1\n"
            "Name: example\n"
            "Version: 1.0\n"
            "Summary: test egg\n",
        )
    return egg_path


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "python_version, python_tag, expected_abi",
    [
        # Python 3.7 is the boundary before the ABI tag changed.
        ("3.7", "cp37", "cp37m"),
        # Python 3.8 no longer uses the pymalloc "m" ABI suffix.
        ("3.8", "cp38", "cp38"),
    ],
)
def test_repackaging_platform_setuptools_eggs_uses_target_python_abi(
    tmp_path, python_version, python_tag, expected_abi
):
    egg_path = _make_setuptools_egg(tmp_path, python_version)
    platform = EPDPlatform.from_epd_string("win-64")
    python = PythonImplementation.from_string(python_tag)

    metadata = SetuptoolsEggMetadata.from_egg(
        str(egg_path),
        platform=platform,
        python=python,
    )

    assert metadata.python_tag == python_tag
    assert metadata.abi_tag == expected_abi

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected",
    [
        ("SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)", "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"),
        ("select cast('1 day' as interval)", "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"),
        (
            "SELECT CAST('1 day 02:03:04' AS INTERVAL(3))",
            "SELECT CAST('1 day 02:03:04' AS INTERVAL(3))",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_cast_interval_type(sql, expected):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)
    assert cast is not None
    assert isinstance(cast.this, exp.Literal)
    assert cast.this.is_string
    assert cast.this.this.startswith("1 day")

    data_type = cast.args["to"]
    assert isinstance(data_type, exp.DataType)
    assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.INTERVAL

    assert expression.sql(dialect="postgres") == expected


def test_postgres_cast_interval_transpiles_without_losing_type():
    assert transpile(
        "SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)",
        read="postgres",
        write="postgres",
    ) == ["SELECT CAST('1 day' AS INTERVAL)"]

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _cast_target(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="duckdb")
    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)

    assert cast is not None
    return cast.to


def _array_element(data_type, dimensions=1):
    for _ in range(dimensions):
        assert data_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.ARRAY
        assert len(data_type.expressions) == 1
        data_type = data_type.expressions[0]
    return data_type


def test_duckdb_cast_to_array_of_struct():
    expression = parse_one(
        "SELECT CAST([STRUCT_PACK(a := 1)] AS STRUCT(a BIGINT)[])",
        read="duckdb",
    )
    cast = expression.find(exp.Cast)

    assert cast is not None
    assert cast.sql(dialect="duckdb") == (
        "CAST([STRUCT_PACK(a := 1)] AS STRUCT(a BIGINT)[])"
    )

    struct_type = _array_element(cast.to)
    assert struct_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT
    assert len(struct_type.expressions) == 1

    field = struct_type.expressions[0]
    assert field.name == "a"
    assert field.expression.this == exp.DataType.Type.BIGINT


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "type_sql, dimensions",
    [
        ("STRUCT(a BIGINT, b VARCHAR)[]", 1),
        ("STRUCT(a BIGINT)[][]", 2),
        ("STRUCT(a BIGINT[])[]", 1),
    ],
)
def test_duckdb_cast_to_postfix_array_of_struct_preserves_nested_type(type_sql, dimensions):
    target = _cast_target(f"SELECT CAST(value AS {type_sql})")

    struct_type = _array_element(target, dimensions)

    assert struct_type.this == exp.DataType.Type.STRUCT
    assert target.sql(dialect="duckdb") == type_sql

    # The generated type must remain usable in another DuckDB CAST.
    assert _cast_target(f"SELECT CAST(value AS {target.sql(dialect='duckdb')})") == target

import pytest

import esper


class Position:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


class Velocity:
    def __init__(self, x=0, y=0):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y


def test_create_entity_without_components_creates_usable_empty_entity():
    world = esper.World()

    entity = world.create_entity()
    next_entity = world.create_entity()

    assert next_entity == entity + 1
    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.components_for_entity(entity) == ()
    assert not world.has_component(entity, Position)

    position = Position(10, 20)
    world.add_component(entity, position)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.get_component(Position) == [(entity, position)]


def test_empty_entity_can_be_deleted_like_a_populated_entity():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    world.delete_entity(entity, immediate=True)

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.components_for_entity(entity)


def test_removing_last_component_leaves_entity_available_for_later_components():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity(Position(1, 2))

    world.remove_component(entity, Position)

    # An entity's existence is no longer defined by whether it currently has
    # components: it should become an empty entity and remain buildable.
    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.components_for_entity(entity) == ()

    velocity = Velocity(3, 4)
    world.add_component(entity, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity


def test_add_component_rejects_unknown_and_deleted_entities_without_resurrecting_them():
    world = esper.World()
    unknown_entity = 123

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(unknown_entity, Position())

    assert not world.entity_exists(unknown_entity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []

    deleted_entity = world.create_entity()
    world.delete_entity(deleted_entity)

    assert not world.entity_exists(deleted_entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(deleted_entity, Position())

    # A delayed-deleted entity must not be revived by add_component.
    world.process()
    assert not world.entity_exists(deleted_entity)
    assert world.get_component(Position) == []

import ctypes
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import pytest

from _pydevd_bundle import pydevd_resolver, pydevd_xml


def _numeric_children(resolver, value):
    """
    Return the children that the debugger exposes as array indexes.

    get_contents_debug_adapter_protocol() is the representation consumed by
    DAP clients such as Visual Studio. get_dictionary() is also checked below
    because it is used by the legacy variable-expansion path.
    """
    contents = resolver.get_contents_debug_adapter_protocol(value)
    return {
        str(entry[0]): entry[1]
        for entry in contents
        if str(entry[0]).isdigit()
    }


def _assert_ctypes_array_is_debugger_container(array, expected_values):
    type_object, type_name, resolver = pydevd_xml.get_type(array)

    assert type_object is type(array)
    assert type_name == type(array).__name__
    assert resolver is not None
    assert resolver is not pydevd_resolver.defaultResolver

    # The XML protocol must mark the value as expandable. Without this, the
    # variables view only displays the object's special/protected attributes.
    variable_xml = pydevd_xml.var_to_xml(array, "array")
    variable = ET.fromstring(variable_xml)
    assert variable.attrib.get("isContainer") == "True"

    expected_children = {
        str(index): expected_value
        for index, expected_value in enumerate(expected_values)
    }

    # Verify the generic resolver path used for variable expansion.
    dictionary = resolver.get_dictionary(array)
    dictionary_children = {
        str(name): value
        for name, value in dictionary.items()
        if str(name).isdigit()
    }
    assert dictionary_children == expected_children

    # Verify the DAP-specific child enumeration path, including every element.
    dap_children = _numeric_children(resolver, array)
    assert dap_children == expected_children
    assert len(dap_children) == len(array)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "array, expected_values",
    [
        (
            (ctypes.c_uint8 * 5).from_buffer(bytearray(b"\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05")),
            [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
        ),
        ((ctypes.c_int32 * 4)(-10, 0, 20, 30), [-10, 0, 20, 30]),
        ((ctypes.c_double * 3)(1.25, -2.5, 3.75), [1.25, -2.5, 3.75]),
    ],
)
def test_ctypes_arrays_are_enumerated_like_sequence_containers(array, expected_values):
    """ctypes arrays must be expandable and expose indexed DAP children."""
    _assert_ctypes_array_is_debugger_container(array, expected_values)


def test_empty_ctypes_array_is_still_an_expandable_container():
    """
    An empty array has no indexed children, but must not fall back to the
    default object resolver merely because its length is zero.
    """
    empty = (ctypes.c_uint16 * 0)()

    _assert_ctypes_array_is_debugger_container(empty, [])

    _, _, resolver = pydevd_xml.get_type(empty)
    assert _numeric_children(resolver, empty) == {}


def test_nested_ctypes_arrays_are_enumerable_at_each_level():
    """
    Arrays can themselves be element types. Both the outer array and each row
    must be treated as containers, rather than exposing ctypes internals.
    """
    row_type = ctypes.c_uint8 * 3
    matrix_type = row_type * 2
    matrix = matrix_type(row_type(1, 2, 3), row_type(4, 5, 6))

    _, _, outer_resolver = pydevd_xml.get_type(matrix)
    outer_children = _numeric_children(outer_resolver, matrix)

    assert set(outer_children) == {"0", "1"}
    assert len(outer_children) == len(matrix)

    _assert_ctypes_array_is_debugger_container(outer_children["0"], [1, 2, 3])
    _assert_ctypes_array_is_debugger_container(outer_children["1"], [4, 5, 6])

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest
from numpy.testing import assert_array_equal

import zarr


def test_group_factories_accept_legacy_positional_name_and_data_arguments() -> None:
    """The v2 positional calling convention remains usable during deprecation."""
    root = zarr.group()
    group = root.create_group("parent").create_group("child")

    # `create` is the backwards-compatible alias for create_array.
    created = group.create("created", shape=(2, 3), dtype="i4")
    assert created.path == "parent/child/created"
    assert created.shape == (2, 3)

    # `array` is itself deprecated, so ignore that unrelated deprecation while
    # verifying that its name may still be positional.
    source = np.arange(6, dtype="i2").reshape(2, 3)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", DeprecationWarning)
        array = group.array("array", shape=source.shape, data=source, dtype=source.dtype)
    assert array.path == "parent/child/array"
    assert_array_equal(array[:], source)

    # These methods made `name` keyword-only in v3, but must continue to
    # support the v2 positional form and warn about its eventual removal.
    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        empty = group.empty("empty", shape=(2, 3), dtype="i4")
    assert empty.path == "parent/child/empty"
    assert empty.shape == (2, 3)
    assert empty.dtype == np.dtype("i4")

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        zeros = group.zeros("zeros", shape=(2, 3), dtype="i4")
    assert_array_equal(zeros[:], np.zeros((2, 3), dtype="i4"))

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        ones = group.ones("ones", shape=(2, 3), dtype="i4")
    assert_array_equal(ones[:], np.ones((2, 3), dtype="i4"))

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        full = group.full("full", shape=(2, 3), fill_value=17, dtype="i4")
    assert_array_equal(full[:], np.full((2, 3), 17, dtype="i4"))

    # The *_like methods historically accepted both the destination name and
    # source data positionally.
    like_source = np.arange(6, dtype="i2").reshape(2, 3)

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        empty_like = group.empty_like("empty_like", like_source)
    assert empty_like.path == "parent/child/empty_like"
    assert empty_like.shape == like_source.shape
    assert empty_like.dtype == like_source.dtype

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        zeros_like = group.zeros_like("zeros_like", like_source)
    assert_array_equal(zeros_like[:], np.zeros_like(like_source))

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        ones_like = group.ones_like("ones_like", like_source)
    assert_array_equal(ones_like[:], np.ones_like(like_source))

    with pytest.warns(FutureWarning):
        full_like = group.full_like("full_like", like_source, fill_value=9)
    assert_array_equal(full_like[:], np.full_like(like_source, 9))

import pytest

from sqlglot import parse_one


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        # Regression from the issue: arrayJoin's argument contains both an
        # array and a tuple, so the parser must not confuse the inner comma
        # with WITH-expression syntax.
        """
        WITH arrayJoin([(1, [2, 3])]) AS arr
        SELECT arr
        """,
        # The same construct must also work when another scalar WITH
        # expression follows it.
        """
        WITH
          arrayJoin([(1, [2, 3])]) AS arr,
          1 AS one
        SELECT arr, one
        """,
    ],
)
def test_clickhouse_parses_scalar_with_arrayjoin(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="clickhouse")

    # Parsing is the behavior requested by the issue. Rendering also ensures
    # the parser produced a complete statement rather than losing the SELECT
    # clause while processing the scalar WITH expression.
    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="clickhouse").lower()
    assert "with" in rendered
    assert "arrayjoin" in rendered
    assert "select" in rendered
    assert "arr" in rendered

import pytest

import esper


class Position:
    def __init__(self, x=0):
        self.x = x


class Velocity:
    def __init__(self, speed=0):
        self.speed = speed


def test_create_entity_without_components_registers_a_usable_entity():
    world = esper.World()

    entity = world.create_entity()

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.components_for_entity(entity) == ()

    position = Position(10)
    velocity = Velocity(3)
    world.add_component(entity, position)
    world.add_component(entity, velocity)

    assert world.entity_exists(entity)
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Position) is position
    assert world.component_for_entity(entity, Velocity) is velocity


def test_multiple_empty_entities_exist_and_keep_normal_sequential_ids():
    world = esper.World()

    first = world.create_entity()
    second = world.create_entity()

    assert second == first + 1
    assert world.entity_exists(first)
    assert world.entity_exists(second)
    assert world.components_for_entity(first) == ()
    assert world.components_for_entity(second) == ()


def test_add_component_rejects_an_entity_that_was_never_created():
    world = esper.World()
    nonexistent_entity = 123

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(nonexistent_entity, None)

    # A failed add must not silently create the supplied arbitrary ID or
    # partially register its component type.
    assert not world.entity_exists(nonexistent_entity)
    assert world.get_component(type(None)) == []


def test_empty_entity_can_be_deleted_and_cannot_be_recreated_by_add_component():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    world.delete_entity(entity, immediate=True)

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Position())

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)


def test_add_component_rejects_entity_pending_delayed_deletion():
    world = esper.World()
    entity = world.create_entity()

    world.delete_entity(entity)

    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        world.add_component(entity, Position())

    world.process()
    assert not world.entity_exists(entity)
