import asyncio
import logging
import socket
import threading
import time

from aiosmtpd.controller import Controller


class SlowRcptHandler:
    """A handler which remains active until EOF cancels the SMTP task."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.rcpt_started = threading.Event()
        self.rcpt_cancelled = threading.Event()
        self.data_calls = 0
        self.exceptions = []

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, options):
        self.rcpt_started.set()
        try:
            # The client will close its write side while this is pending.
            await asyncio.sleep(30)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            self.rcpt_cancelled.set()
            raise

        envelope.rcpt_tos.append(address)
        return "250 OK"

    async def handle_DATA(self, server, session, envelope):
        self.data_calls += 1
        return "250 OK"

    async def handle_exception(self, error):
        self.exceptions.append(error)
        return "500 handler exception"


def _read_until_eof(sock, timeout=3):
    """Read all pending server output and require a prompt connection close."""
    chunks = []
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    sock.settimeout(0.2)

    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            chunk = sock.recv(4096)
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
        if not chunk:
            return b"".join(chunks)
        chunks.append(chunk)

    raise AssertionError("server did not close the connection after client EOF")


def test_eof_during_slow_rcpt_cancels_cleanly_and_ignores_pipelined_input(caplog):
    """A peer EOF during an awaited command must terminate that SMTP session.

    In particular, queued DATA input must not be interpreted as further SMTP
    commands after the RCPT coroutine was cancelled; doing so was the source
    of the endless ``500 Error: bad syntax`` loop reported in the issue.
    """
    handler = SlowRcptHandler()
    controller = Controller(handler)
    controller.start()

    sock = None
    healthy_sock = None
    try:
        caplog.set_level(logging.ERROR, logger="mail.log")

        sock = socket.create_connection((controller.hostname, controller.port))
        sock.settimeout(2)
        assert sock.recv(4096).startswith(b"220 ")

        # Wait for the slow handler to be entered before closing the write
        # side.  The remaining commands emulate a client which pipelined data
        # and then exited without waiting for any responses or sending QUIT.
        sock.sendall(
            b"HELO embedded-device\r\n"
            b"MAIL FROM:<sender@example.test>\r\n"
            b"RCPT TO:<recipient@example.test>\r\n"
        )
        assert handler.rcpt_started.wait(2), "RCPT handler was not entered"

        sock.sendall(b"DATA\r\nmessage that must be ignored\r\n.\r\n")
        sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)

        assert handler.rcpt_cancelled.wait(2), (
            "EOF did not cancel the in-progress command handler"
        )

        output = _read_until_eof(sock)
        assert b"500 Error: bad syntax" not in output
        assert handler.data_calls == 0
        assert handler.exceptions == []
        assert not any(
            "SMTP session exception" in record.getMessage()
            for record in caplog.records
        )

        # The bad client must not leave the event loop/server unusable.
        healthy_sock = socket.create_connection(
            (controller.hostname, controller.port)
        )
        healthy_sock.settimeout(2)
        assert healthy_sock.recv(4096).startswith(b"220 ")
        healthy_sock.sendall(b"NOOP\r\n")
        assert healthy_sock.recv(4096).startswith(b"250 ")
        healthy_sock.sendall(b"QUIT\r\n")
        assert healthy_sock.recv(4096).startswith(b"221 ")

    finally:
        if sock is not None:
            sock.close()
        if healthy_sock is not None:
            healthy_sock.close()
        controller.stop()

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _assert_lateral_subquery_round_trips(sql, alias):
    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    laterals = list(expression.find_all(exp.Lateral))
    assert len(laterals) == 1

    lateral = laterals[0]
    assert isinstance(lateral.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert lateral.this.alias_or_name == alias

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "LATERAL" in generated.upper()
    assert "LATERAL VIEW" not in generated.upper()

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, read="postgres")
    reparsed_laterals = list(reparsed.find_all(exp.Lateral))

    assert len(reparsed_laterals) == 1
    assert isinstance(reparsed_laterals[0].this, exp.Subquery)
    assert reparsed_laterals[0].this.alias_or_name == alias


def test_postgres_lateral_join_subquery_from_issue():
    sql = """
        SELECT art
        FROM table1
        INNER JOIN LATERAL (
            SELECT art
            FROM table2
        ) table2
        ON table2.art = table2.art
    """

    expression = parse_one(sql, read="postgres")
    join = expression.args["joins"][0]

    assert isinstance(join.this, exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(join.this.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert join.this.this.alias_or_name == "table2"

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "LATERAL" in generated.upper()
    assert "LATERAL VIEW" not in generated.upper()

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, read="postgres")
    reparsed_join = reparsed.args["joins"][0]
    assert isinstance(reparsed_join.this, exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(reparsed_join.this.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert reparsed_join.this.this.alias_or_name == "table2"

"""Regression tests for clients disconnecting during asynchronous commands."""

import asyncio
import socket
import threading
import time

from aiosmtpd.controller import Controller


class SlowRcptHandler:
    """Keeps RCPT processing active until the peer disconnects."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.started = threading.Event()
        self.cancelled = threading.Event()

    async def handle_RCPT(
            self, server, session, envelope, address, rcpt_options):
        self.started.set()
        try:
            # This represents a webhook or another slow external operation.
            await asyncio.sleep(60)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            self.cancelled.set()
            raise


class CancellingRcptHandler:
    """A handler whose in-progress command is cancelled."""

    async def handle_RCPT(
            self, server, session, envelope, address, rcpt_options):
        raise asyncio.CancelledError()


def _read_response(sock):
    data = sock.recv(4096)
    assert data, "SMTP server unexpectedly closed the connection"
    return data


def _smtp_preamble(sock):
    assert _read_response(sock).startswith(b"220")

    sock.sendall(b"HELO example.test\r\n")
    assert _read_response(sock).startswith(b"250")

    sock.sendall(b"MAIL FROM:<sender@example.test>\r\n")
    assert _read_response(sock).startswith(b"250")


def _wait_for_eof(sock, timeout=2.0):
    """Return data received before the server closes the socket."""
    chunks = []
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    sock.settimeout(0.1)
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            data = sock.recv(4096)
        except socket.timeout:
            continue
        if not data:
            return b"".join(chunks)
        chunks.append(data)
    raise AssertionError("server did not close the cancelled SMTP session")


def _assert_server_still_accepts_commands(controller):
    """A bad peer must not wedge the listener or its event loop."""
    with socket.create_connection(
            (controller.hostname, controller.port), timeout=2) as sock:
        assert _read_response(sock).startswith(b"220")
        sock.sendall(b"NOOP\r\n")
        assert _read_response(sock).startswith(b"250")


def test_eof_while_slow_rcpt_is_running_closes_session_without_spin():
    """EOF during a handler must cancel the command instead of looping on EOF."""
    handler = SlowRcptHandler()
    controller = Controller(handler, hostname="localhost", port=8025)
    controller.start()
    try:
        with socket.create_connection(
                (controller.hostname, controller.port), timeout=2) as sock:
            _smtp_preamble(sock)

            sock.sendall(b"RCPT TO:<recipient@example.test>\r\n")
            assert handler.started.wait(2), "RCPT handler did not start"

            # Match a client which has already sent more input, ignores the
            # pending RCPT response, and then sends EOF without QUIT.
            sock.sendall(b"DATA\r\nmessage body\r\n.\r\n")
            sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)

            received = _wait_for_eof(sock)

        assert handler.cancelled.wait(2), "slow handler was not cancelled"
        assert b"500 Error: bad syntax" not in received

        # Most importantly, the EOF must not leave the server's event loop
        # occupied by endlessly processing empty lines.
        _assert_server_still_accepts_commands(controller)
    finally:
        controller.stop()


def test_cancelled_command_does_not_leave_client_connection_open():
    """CancelledError from command processing is a terminal session failure."""
    controller = Controller(
        CancellingRcptHandler(), hostname="localhost", port=8025)
    controller.start()
    try:
        with socket.create_connection(
                (controller.hostname, controller.port), timeout=2) as sock:
            _smtp_preamble(sock)
            sock.sendall(b"RCPT TO:<recipient@example.test>\r\n")

            # A cancellation is not a normal handler error for which a 500
            # response should be sent and the protocol loop continued.
            received = _wait_for_eof(sock)
            assert b"500" not in received

        _assert_server_still_accepts_commands(controller)
    finally:
        controller.stop()

import re

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _parse_postgres(sql):
    return parse_one(sql, read="postgres")


def _assert_lateral_subquery_join(sql, alias=None):
    expression = _parse_postgres(sql)

    join = next(expression.find_all(exp.Join))
    assert isinstance(join.this, exp.Lateral)

    lateral = join.this
    assert isinstance(lateral.this, exp.Subquery)

    rendered = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")

    # PostgreSQL LATERAL joins must not be rendered as the unrelated Hive/Spark
    # LATERAL VIEW construct.
    assert "LATERAL (" in rendered
    assert "LATERAL VIEW" not in rendered

    if alias:
        # PostgreSQL permits both `AS alias` and a bare alias for a subquery.
        # The alias is required for references in the outer query and must survive
        # parsing/generation regardless of which spelling the generator chooses.
        assert re.search(rf"\)\s+(?:AS\s+)?{alias}\b", rendered)

    # Generated PostgreSQL must itself be accepted as PostgreSQL input.
    reparsed = _parse_postgres(rendered)
    reparsed_join = next(reparsed.find_all(exp.Join))
    assert isinstance(reparsed_join.this, exp.Lateral)

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_columns(statement, constraint_type):
    constraint = next(statement.find_all(constraint_type))

    schema = constraint.args.get("schema")
    if schema is not None:
        return schema.expressions

    return constraint.args["expressions"]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected_directions",
    [
        (
            "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), KEY idx_a (a DESC))",
            [True],
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), KEY idx_a (a ASC))",
            [False],
        ),
        (
            """
            CREATE TABLE `foo` (
              a VARCHAR(10),
              b INT,
              c DATE,
              KEY idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c)
            )
            """,
            [False, True, None],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_index_column_ordering_is_parsed_and_round_trips(sql, expected_directions):
    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    columns = _index_columns(expression, exp.IndexColumnConstraint)

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == expected_directions

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    reparsed_columns = _index_columns(reparsed, exp.IndexColumnConstraint)

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == expected_directions


def test_mysql_ordered_index_columns_support_prefixes_and_index_options():
    sql = """
        CREATE TABLE `foo` (
          name VARCHAR(255),
          created_at DATETIME,
          KEY idx_name_created USING BTREE (name(12) DESC, created_at ASC)
            COMMENT 'ordered index'
        )
    """

    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    columns = _index_columns(expression, exp.IndexColumnConstraint)

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [True, False]

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql").upper()
    assert "NAME(12) DESC" in generated
    assert "CREATED_AT ASC" in generated
    assert "USING BTREE" in generated
    assert "COMMENT 'ORDERED INDEX'" in generated


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql",
    [
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, UNIQUE INDEX uq_a (a DESC))",
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, UNIQUE KEY uq_a USING BTREE (a DESC))",
    ],
)
def test_mysql_unique_index_variants_support_descending_columns(sql):
    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    columns = _index_columns(expression, exp.UniqueColumnConstraint)

    assert len(columns) == 1
    assert isinstance(columns[0], exp.Ordered)
    assert columns[0].args.get("desc") is True

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    reparsed_columns = _index_columns(reparsed, exp.UniqueColumnConstraint)

    assert len(reparsed_columns) == 1
    assert reparsed_columns[0].args.get("desc") is True


def test_postgres_create_index_keeps_order_and_nulls_qualifiers():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE INDEX idx_a ON foo (a DESC NULLS FIRST, b ASC NULLS LAST)",
        dialect="postgres",
    )

    index = next(expression.find_all(exp.Index))
    columns = index.args["params"].args["columns"]

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [True, False]
    assert [column.args.get("nulls_first") for column in columns] == [True, False]

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="postgres")
    reparsed_index = next(reparsed.find_all(exp.Index))
    reparsed_columns = reparsed_index.args["params"].args["columns"]

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == [True, False]
    assert [column.args.get("nulls_first") for column in reparsed_columns] == [True, False]

import re

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def _parse_lateral_join(sql):
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="postgres")

    joins = list(expression.find_all(exp.Join))
    assert len(joins) == 1

    lateral = joins[0].this
    assert isinstance(lateral, exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(lateral.this, exp.Subquery)

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "LATERAL VIEW" not in generated
    assert "LATERAL (" in generated

    # Generated PostgreSQL SQL must be parseable and preserve the lateral
    # subquery rather than degrading it into a normal table expression.
    reparsed = sqlglot.parse_one(generated, read="postgres")
    reparsed_join = next(reparsed.find_all(exp.Join))
    assert isinstance(reparsed_join.this, exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(reparsed_join.this.this, exp.Subquery)

    return expression, generated


def test_postgres_inner_join_lateral_subquery_with_alias_and_on_clause():
    expression, generated = _parse_lateral_join(
        "select art from table1 "
        "inner join lateral (select art from table2) table2 "
        "on table2.art = table2.art"
    )

    lateral_subquery = next(expression.find_all(exp.Lateral)).this
    assert lateral_subquery.alias == "table2"
    assert "ON table2.art = table2.art" in generated
    assert re.search(r"\)\s+(?:AS\s+)?table2\s+ON\b", generated)


def test_postgres_left_join_lateral_subquery_can_reference_outer_table():
    _, generated = _parse_lateral_join(
        "SELECT * FROM table1 "
        "LEFT JOIN LATERAL ("
        "SELECT * FROM table2 WHERE table2.id = table1.id"
        ") t ON TRUE"
    )

    assert "LEFT JOIN LATERAL (" in generated
    assert "table2.id = table1.id" in generated
    assert re.search(r"\)\s+(?:AS\s+)?t\s+ON TRUE\b", generated)


def test_postgres_cross_join_lateral_subquery_without_on_clause():
    expression, generated = _parse_lateral_join(
        "SELECT * FROM table1 "
        "CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT art FROM table2 LIMIT 1) t"
    )

    join = next(expression.find_all(exp.Join))
    assert join.kind.upper() == "CROSS"
    assert join.args.get("on") is None
    assert "CROSS JOIN LATERAL (" in generated
    assert "LIMIT 1" in generated
    assert re.search(r"\)\s+(?:AS\s+)?t\b", generated)


def test_lateral_view_generation_remains_distinct_from_postgres_lateral_join():
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT x FROM tbl LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(y) tbl2 AS z",
        read="hive",
    )

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="hive")

    assert generated == "SELECT x FROM tbl LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(y) tbl2 AS z"
    assert "LATERAL VIEW" in generated

import re

import pytest

from sqlglot import expressions as exp
from sqlglot import parse_one


def _index_constraint(expression):
    return next(expression.find_all(exp.IndexColumnConstraint))


def _ordered_columns(constraint):
    schema = constraint.args["schema"]
    columns = schema.expressions

    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in columns)
    return columns


def _assert_index_ordering_round_trip(sql, expected_desc):
    parsed = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    constraint = _index_constraint(parsed)
    columns = _ordered_columns(constraint)

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == expected_desc

    generated = parsed.sql(dialect="mysql")

    # ASC/DESC are ordering modifiers, not aliases such as "a AS DESC".
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated.upper()
    assert " AS ASC" not in generated.upper()

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    reparsed_columns = _ordered_columns(_index_constraint(reparsed))

    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == expected_desc

    return generated


@pytest.mark.parametrize("index_keyword", ["KEY", "INDEX"])
def test_mysql_index_column_ordering_for_key_and_index(index_keyword):
    generated = _assert_index_ordering_round_trip(
        f"""
        CREATE TABLE foo (
          a VARCHAR(10),
          b INT,
          c DATE,
          {index_keyword} idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c ASC)
        )
        """,
        [False, True, False],
    )

    assert re.search(r"\ba\s+ASC\b", generated, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    assert re.search(r"\bb\s+DESC\b", generated, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    assert re.search(r"\bc\s+ASC\b", generated, flags=re.IGNORECASE)


def test_mysql_unnamed_key_and_index_options_keep_ordering():
    generated = _assert_index_ordering_round_trip(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo (
          a VARCHAR(10),
          KEY USING BTREE (a DESC) COMMENT 'descending key'
        )
        """,
        [True],
    )

    assert "USING BTREE" in generated.upper()
    assert "COMMENT 'descending key'" in generated


def test_mysql_ordered_index_with_options_after_key_parts():
    generated = _assert_index_ordering_round_trip(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo (
          a VARCHAR(10),
          b INT,
          KEY idx_ab (a DESC, b ASC) USING HASH VISIBLE
        )
        """,
        [True, False],
    )

    assert "USING HASH" in generated.upper()
    assert "VISIBLE" in generated.upper()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["FULLTEXT", "SPATIAL"])
def test_mysql_special_index_kinds_support_ordered_key_parts(kind):
    column_type = "TEXT" if kind == "FULLTEXT" else "POINT"

    generated = _assert_index_ordering_round_trip(
        f"""
        CREATE TABLE foo (
          a {column_type},
          {kind} KEY idx_a (a DESC)
        )
        """,
        [True],
    )

    assert f"{kind} INDEX" in generated.upper() or f"{kind} KEY" in generated.upper()
    assert re.search(r"\ba\s+DESC\b", generated, flags=re.IGNORECASE)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("sql", "expected_desc"),
    [
        (
            """
            CREATE TABLE foo (
              a VARCHAR(10),
              b INT,
              UNIQUE KEY idx_ab (a DESC, b ASC)
            )
            """,
            [True, False],
        ),
        (
            """
            CREATE TABLE foo (
              a VARCHAR(10),
              b INT,
              UNIQUE (a ASC, b DESC) USING BTREE
            )
            """,
            [False, True],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_unique_indexes_support_ordered_key_parts(sql, expected_desc):
    # UNIQUE is an index form in MySQL and uses the same index-column grammar.
    # It must therefore accept ASC/DESC in its key parts as well.
    parsed = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    generated = parsed.sql(dialect="mysql")

    assert " AS DESC" not in generated.upper()
    assert " AS ASC" not in generated.upper()

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    ordered = list(reparsed.find_all(exp.Ordered))

    assert len(ordered) == 2
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in ordered] == expected_desc


def test_mysql_ordered_index_prefix_key_part_round_trips():
    # A MySQL key part can have a prefix length before its ordering qualifier.
    generated = _assert_index_ordering_round_trip(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo (
          name VARCHAR(100),
          KEY idx_name (name(12) DESC)
        )
        """,
        [True],
    )

    assert re.search(r"\bname\s*\(\s*12\s*\)\s+DESC\b", generated, flags=re.IGNORECASE)

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def parse_postgres(sql):
    return sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="postgres")


def assert_lateral_round_trip(sql):
    expression = parse_postgres(sql)
    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")

    assert "LATERAL VIEW" not in generated
    assert "LATERAL" in generated

    reparsed = parse_postgres(generated)
    assert reparsed.find(exp.Lateral) is not None
    return expression, generated


def test_postgres_lateral_join_subquery_from_issue():
    expression, generated = assert_lateral_round_trip(
        "SELECT art FROM table1 "
        "INNER JOIN LATERAL (SELECT art FROM table2) table2 "
        "ON table2.art = table2.art"
    )

    assert (
        generated
        == "SELECT art FROM table1 INNER JOIN LATERAL "
        "(SELECT art FROM table2) AS table2 ON table2.art = table2.art"
    )

    join = expression.find(exp.Join)
    assert isinstance(join.this, exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(join.this.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert join.this.this.alias_or_name == "table2"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, expected_join",
    [
        (
            "SELECT b.id FROM base AS b "
            "LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT b.id + 1 AS next_id) AS derived ON TRUE",
            "LEFT JOIN LATERAL",
        ),
        (
            "SELECT b.id FROM base AS b "
            "CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT b.id + 1 AS next_id) AS derived",
            "CROSS JOIN LATERAL",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_lateral_subquery_supports_join_types_and_correlation(
    sql, expected_join
):
    expression, generated = assert_lateral_round_trip(sql)

    assert expected_join in generated
    lateral = expression.find(exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(lateral.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert lateral.this.alias_or_name == "derived"


def test_postgres_lateral_subquery_is_supported_as_from_item():
    # LATERAL is legal before a FROM item as well as after an explicit JOIN.
    # This is especially important for correlated derived tables written using
    # PostgreSQL's comma-separated FROM syntax.
    expression, generated = assert_lateral_round_trip(
        "SELECT b.id, derived.next_id "
        "FROM base AS b, "
        "LATERAL (SELECT b.id + 1 AS next_id) AS derived"
    )

    lateral = expression.find(exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(lateral.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert lateral.this.alias_or_name == "derived"
    assert "LATERAL (SELECT b.id + 1 AS next_id) AS derived" in generated


def test_postgres_lateral_subquery_can_be_the_first_from_item():
    expression, generated = assert_lateral_round_trip(
        "SELECT derived.value "
        "FROM LATERAL (SELECT 1 AS value) AS derived"
    )

    lateral = expression.find(exp.Lateral)
    assert isinstance(lateral.this, exp.Subquery)
    assert lateral.this.alias_or_name == "derived"
    assert generated == "SELECT derived.value FROM LATERAL (SELECT 1 AS value) AS derived"


def test_postgres_lateral_subquery_keeps_column_alias_list():
    expression, generated = assert_lateral_round_trip(
        "SELECT derived.id, derived.name "
        "FROM base AS b "
        "JOIN LATERAL (SELECT b.id, b.name) AS derived(id, name) ON TRUE"
    )

    lateral = expression.find(exp.Lateral)
    subquery = lateral.this

    assert isinstance(subquery, exp.Subquery)
    assert subquery.alias_or_name == "derived"
    assert [column.name for column in subquery.args["alias"].args["columns"]] == [
        "id",
        "name",
    ]
    assert "LATERAL (SELECT b.id, b.name) AS derived(id, name)" in generated


def test_hive_lateral_view_remains_lateral_view():
    # PostgreSQL's bare LATERAL and Hive's LATERAL VIEW are separate syntaxes.
    expression = sqlglot.parse_one(
        "SELECT x FROM tbl LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(y) tbl2 AS z",
        read="hive",
    )

    assert (
        expression.sql(dialect="hive")
        == "SELECT x FROM tbl LATERAL VIEW OUTER EXPLODE(y) tbl2 AS z"
    )

import pytest

import sqlglot
from sqlglot import exp


def parse_postgres(sql):
    return sqlglot.parse_one(sql, read="postgres")


def lateral_subquery(expression):
    lateral = expression.find(exp.Lateral)

    assert lateral is not None, "LATERAL must be represented in the parsed expression"
    assert isinstance(
        lateral.this, exp.Subquery
    ), "LATERAL must wrap the parenthesized SELECT as a subquery"

    return lateral


def assert_round_trip(sql, alias):
    expression = parse_postgres(sql)
    lateral = lateral_subquery(expression)

    assert lateral.this.alias_or_name == alias

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "LATERAL" in generated.upper()
    assert "LATERAL VIEW" not in generated.upper()

    reparsed = parse_postgres(generated)
    reparsed_lateral = lateral_subquery(reparsed)
    assert reparsed_lateral.this.alias_or_name == alias

    return expression, generated


def test_postgres_inner_join_lateral_subquery_from_issue():
    # The alias deliberately omits AS, matching the issue's PostgreSQL example.
    sql = """
        SELECT art
        FROM table1
        INNER JOIN LATERAL (
            SELECT art
            FROM table2
        ) table2
        ON table2.art = table2.art
    """

    expression, generated = assert_round_trip(sql, "table2")

    join = expression.args["joins"][0]
    assert isinstance(join.this, exp.Lateral)
    assert join.args.get("on") is not None
    assert "ON table2.art = table2.art" in generated


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "sql, alias, expected_fragment",
    [
        (
            """
            SELECT *
            FROM table1
            LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
                SELECT *
                FROM table2
                WHERE table2.id = table1.id
            ) matching_table2
            ON TRUE
            """,
            "matching_table2",
            "WHERE table2.id = table1.id",
        ),
        (
            """
            SELECT *
            FROM table1
            CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
                SELECT art
                FROM table2
                LIMIT 1
            ) one_table2
            """,
            "one_table2",
            "LIMIT 1",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_postgres_lateral_subquery_supports_join_variants(
    sql, alias, expected_fragment
):
    _, generated = assert_round_trip(sql, alias)

    assert expected_fragment.upper() in generated.upper()


def test_postgres_lateral_subquery_preserves_nested_subquery_and_alias():
    sql = """
        SELECT *
        FROM table1
        JOIN LATERAL (
            SELECT *
            FROM (
                SELECT id
                FROM table2
            ) nested_table2
            WHERE nested_table2.id = table1.id
        ) derived_table2
        ON TRUE
    """

    expression, generated = assert_round_trip(sql, "derived_table2")

    lateral = lateral_subquery(expression)
    nested_subquery = lateral.this.find(exp.Subquery)

    assert nested_subquery is not None
    assert "nested_table2" in generated
    assert "WHERE nested_table2.id = table1.id" in generated

import re

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_constraint(sql):
    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    index = statement.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)

    assert index is not None
    assert index.args["schema"] is not None

    return statement, index


def test_mysql_key_index_columns_preserve_asc_desc_ordering():
    statement, index = _index_constraint(
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c DATE, "
        "KEY idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c))"
    )

    columns = index.args["schema"].expressions

    assert len(columns) == 3
    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in columns)
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [False, True, None]
    assert not list(index.find_all(exp.Alias))

    generated = statement.sql(dialect="mysql").upper()

    assert re.search(r"\bA\s+ASC\b", generated)
    assert re.search(r"\bB\s+DESC\b", generated)
    assert " AS ASC" not in generated
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated

    statement, index = _index_constraint(

    )

    columns = index.args["schema"].expressions

import pytest

from sqlglot import parse, parse_one
from sqlglot import expressions as exp


def _index_columns(statement):
    constraint = statement.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None
    schema = constraint.args.get("schema")
    assert schema is not None
    return schema.expressions


def test_mysql_create_table_composite_index_preserves_asc_and_desc_columns():
    sql = (
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` ("
        "a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c DATE, "
        "KEY idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c)"
        ")"
    )

    statements = parse(sql, dialect="mysql")

    assert len(statements) == 1
    generated = statements[0].sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert generated == (
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` ("
        "a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c DATE, "
        "INDEX idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c)"
        ")"
    )
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated

    columns = _index_columns(parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql"))
    assert len(columns) == 3
    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in columns)
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [False, True, None]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("keyword", ["KEY", "INDEX"])
def test_mysql_index_direction_round_trips_with_using_and_options(keyword):
    sql = (
        f"CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, {keyword} idx "
        "USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index')"
    )

    generated = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql").sql(dialect="mysql")

    assert "INDEX idx USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC)" in generated
    assert "COMMENT 'ordered index'" in generated
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    assert reparsed.sql(dialect="mysql") == generated
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in _index_columns(reparsed)] == [True, False]


def test_mysql_unique_key_accepts_and_round_trips_ordered_index_columns():
    sql = "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, UNIQUE KEY uq_foo (a DESC, b ASC))"

    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    generated = statement.sql(dialect="mysql")

    assert "UNIQUE uq_foo (a DESC, b ASC)" in generated
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    assert reparsed.sql(dialect="mysql") == generated


def test_postgres_create_index_supports_direction_and_null_ordering():
    sql = "CREATE INDEX idx_foo ON foo (a DESC NULLS LAST, b ASC NULLS FIRST)"

    generated = parse_one(sql, dialect="postgres").sql(dialect="postgres")

    assert "a DESC NULLS LAST" in generated
    assert "b ASC NULLS FIRST" in generated
    assert parse_one(generated, dialect="postgres").sql(dialect="postgres") == generated

import pytest

from sqlglot import expressions as exp
from sqlglot import parse_one


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("sql", "expected", "key_parts"),
    [
        (
            "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), KEY idx_a (a DESC))",
            "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), INDEX idx_a (a DESC))",
            ["a DESC"],
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), KEY idx_a (a ASC))",
            "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), INDEX idx_a (a ASC))",
            ["a ASC"],
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, c INT, KEY idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, c INT, INDEX idx_abc (a ASC, b DESC, c))",
            ["a ASC", "b DESC", "c"],
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (name VARCHAR(100), KEY idx_name (name(10) DESC))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (name VARCHAR(100), INDEX idx_name (name(10) DESC))",
            ["name(10) DESC"],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_index_key_ordering_round_trips(sql, expected, key_parts):
    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")

    assert expression.sql(dialect="mysql") == expected

    index = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert index is not None
    assert isinstance(index.args["schema"], exp.Schema)

    parts = index.args["schema"].expressions
    assert [part.sql(dialect="mysql") for part in parts] == key_parts

    # Ordering qualifiers must be modeled as order expressions, not as aliases
    # such as "a AS DESC".
    ordered_parts = [part for part in parts if isinstance(part, exp.Ordered)]
    assert ordered_parts
    assert all(not isinstance(part.this, exp.Alias) for part in ordered_parts)

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql").sql(dialect="mysql") == expected


def test_mysql_ordered_index_key_parts_preserve_index_options():
    sql = (
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a INT, b INT, "
        "KEY idx_a USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index'"
        ")"
    )
    expected = (
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a INT, b INT, "
        "INDEX idx_a USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index'"
        ")"
    )

    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")

    assert expression.sql(dialect="mysql") == expected

    index = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert index is not None
    assert [part.sql(dialect="mysql") for part in index.args["schema"].expressions] == [
        "a DESC",
        "b ASC",
    ]
    assert index.args["options"][0].args["comment"].this == "ordered index"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("sql", "expected", "key_parts"),
    [
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, UNIQUE KEY uq_ab (a DESC, b ASC))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, UNIQUE uq_ab (a DESC, b ASC))",
            ["a DESC", "b ASC"],
        ),
        (
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, UNIQUE (a DESC))",
            "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, UNIQUE (a DESC))",
            ["a DESC"],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_unique_indexes_support_ordered_key_parts(sql, expected, key_parts):
    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")

    assert expression.sql(dialect="mysql") == expected

    unique = expression.find(exp.UniqueColumnConstraint)
    assert unique is not None
    assert isinstance(unique.this, exp.Schema)
    assert [part.sql(dialect="mysql") for part in unique.this.expressions] == key_parts

    assert parse_one(expression.sql(dialect="mysql"), dialect="mysql").sql(
        dialect="mysql"
    ) == expected

from sqlglot import expressions as exp
from sqlglot import parse_one


def _index_parts(statement):
    constraint = statement.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None

    schema = constraint.args.get("schema")
    assert isinstance(schema, exp.Schema)
    assert all(isinstance(part, exp.Ordered) for part in schema.expressions)
    return schema.expressions


def _unique_parts(statement):
    constraint = statement.find(exp.UniqueColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None

    parts = constraint.args.get("expressions")
    assert parts is not None
    assert all(isinstance(part, exp.Ordered) for part in parts)
    return parts


def test_mysql_index_key_parts_support_mixed_asc_desc_and_round_trip():
    sql = """
        CREATE TABLE `foo` (
            `a` VARCHAR(10),
            `b` INT,
            `c` DATE,
            KEY `idx_abc` (`a` ASC, `b` DESC, `c`)
        )
    """

    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    parts = _index_parts(statement)

    assert [part.this.name for part in parts] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in parts] == [False, True, None]

    rendered = statement.sql(dialect="mysql").replace("`", "")
    assert "a ASC" in rendered
    assert "b DESC" in rendered
    assert " AS ASC" not in rendered
    assert " AS DESC" not in rendered

    reparsed_parts = _index_parts(parse_one(rendered, dialect="mysql"))
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in reparsed_parts] == [False, True, None]


def test_mysql_ordered_index_key_parts_work_with_using_and_options():
    sql = """
        CREATE TABLE foo (
            a INT,
            b INT,
            KEY idx_ab USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index' VISIBLE
        )
    """

    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in _index_parts(statement)] == [True, False]

    rendered = statement.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "USING BTREE" in rendered
    assert "a DESC" in rendered
    assert "b ASC" in rendered
    assert "COMMENT 'ordered index'" in rendered
    assert "VISIBLE" in rendered

    reparsed_parts = _index_parts(parse_one(rendered, dialect="mysql"))
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in reparsed_parts] == [True, False]


def test_mysql_unique_key_parts_also_support_asc_desc():
    sql = """
        CREATE TABLE foo (
            a INT,
            b INT,
            UNIQUE KEY uq_ab (a ASC, b DESC) USING BTREE
        )
    """

    statement = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    parts = _unique_parts(statement)

    assert [part.this.name for part in parts] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in parts] == [False, True]

    rendered = statement.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "UNIQUE" in rendered
    assert "a ASC" in rendered
    assert "b DESC" in rendered
    assert "USING BTREE" in rendered
    assert " AS ASC" not in rendered
    assert " AS DESC" not in rendered

    reparsed_parts = _unique_parts(parse_one(rendered, dialect="mysql"))
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in reparsed_parts] == [False, True]

def _index_constraint(expression):
    return next(expression.find_all(exp.IndexColumnConstraint))


def _ordered_key_parts(expression):
    constraint = _index_constraint(expression)
    return constraint.args["schema"].expressions


def test_mysql_create_table_index_key_parts_support_asc_and_desc_round_trip():
    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        CREATE TABLE `foo` (
          a VARCHAR(10),
          b INT,
          c INT,
          KEY idx_abc (a DESC, b ASC, c DESC)
        )
        """,
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    parts = _ordered_key_parts(statement)

    assert all(isinstance(part, exp.Ordered) for part in parts)
    assert [part.this.name for part in parts] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in parts] == [True, False, True]

    rendered = statement.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "a DESC" in rendered
    assert "b ASC" in rendered
    assert "c DESC" in rendered

    reparsed_parts = _ordered_key_parts(sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, dialect="mysql"))
    assert [part.this.name for part in reparsed_parts] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in reparsed_parts] == [True, False, True]


def test_mysql_index_key_part_prefix_can_be_combined_with_direction():
    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        CREATE TABLE foo (
          name VARCHAR(100),
          other_name VARCHAR(100),
          KEY idx_names (name(12) DESC, other_name(8) ASC)
        )
        """,
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    parts = _ordered_key_parts(statement)

    assert all(isinstance(part, exp.Ordered) for part in parts)
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in parts] == [True, False]
    assert all(isinstance(part.this, exp.ColumnPrefix) for part in parts)
    assert [part.this.this.name for part in parts] == ["name", "other_name"]
    assert [part.this.expression.this for part in parts] == ["12", "8"]

    rendered = statement.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "name(12) DESC" in rendered
    assert "other_name(8) ASC" in rendered

    reparsed_parts = _ordered_key_parts(sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, dialect="mysql"))
    assert isinstance(reparsed_parts[0].this, exp.ColumnPrefix)
    assert reparsed_parts[0].args.get("desc") is True
    assert reparsed_parts[0].this.this.name == "name"
    assert reparsed_parts[0].this.expression.this == "12"


def test_postgres_create_index_supports_direction_and_null_ordering_round_trip():
    statement = sqlglot.parse_one(
        """
        CREATE INDEX idx_ordering
        ON foo (a DESC NULLS LAST, b ASC NULLS FIRST)
        """,
        dialect="postgres",
    )

    parts = list(statement.find_all(exp.Ordered))

    assert [part.this.name for part in parts] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in parts] == [True, False]
    assert [part.args.get("nulls_first") for part in parts] == [False, True]

    rendered = statement.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "a DESC NULLS LAST" in rendered
    assert "b ASC NULLS FIRST" in rendered

    reparsed_parts = list(
        sqlglot.parse_one(rendered, dialect="postgres").find_all(exp.Ordered)
    )
    assert [part.args.get("desc") for part in reparsed_parts] == [True, False]
    assert [part.args.get("nulls_first") for part in reparsed_parts] == [False, True]

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_constraint(expression):
    constraint = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None
    assert isinstance(constraint.args.get("schema"), exp.Schema)
    return constraint


def _ordered_columns(expression):
    constraint = _index_constraint(expression)
    columns = constraint.args["schema"].expressions
    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in columns)
    return columns


def test_mysql_create_table_index_column_ordering_round_trips():
    sql = (
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` ("
        "a VARCHAR(10), "
        "b INT, "
        "KEY idx_ab (a ASC, b DESC)"
        ")"
    )

    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    columns = _ordered_columns(expression)

    assert [column.this.name for column in columns] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [False, True]
    assert not list(_index_constraint(expression).find_all(exp.Alias))

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "INDEX idx_ab (a ASC, b DESC)" in generated
    assert " AS ASC" not in generated
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated

    reparsed_columns = _ordered_columns(parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql"))
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == [False, True]


def test_mysql_index_key_parts_allow_prefix_length_direction_and_options():
    # MySQL key parts permit a prefix length before the optional direction:
    # col_name [(length)] [ASC | DESC].
    sql = (
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` ("
        "`a` VARCHAR(20), "
        "`b` INT, "
        "INDEX `idx_a_b` USING BTREE (`a`(4) DESC, `b` ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index'"
        ")"
    )

    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    columns = _ordered_columns(expression)

    assert isinstance(columns[0].this, exp.ColumnPrefix)
    assert columns[0].this.this.name == "a"
    assert columns[0].this.expression.name == "4"
    assert columns[0].args.get("desc") is True
    assert columns[1].this.name == "b"
    assert columns[1].args.get("desc") is False

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "INDEX `idx_a_b` USING BTREE (`a`(4) DESC, `b` ASC)" in generated
    assert "COMMENT 'ordered index'" in generated

    reparsed_columns = _ordered_columns(parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql"))
    assert isinstance(reparsed_columns[0].this, exp.ColumnPrefix)
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == [True, False]


def test_mysql_fulltext_index_direction_keeps_index_kind():
    sql = "CREATE TABLE foo (body TEXT, FULLTEXT KEY body_idx (body DESC))"

    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    constraint = _index_constraint(expression)
    columns = _ordered_columns(expression)

    assert constraint.args["kind"] == "FULLTEXT"
    assert columns[0].this.name == "body"
    assert columns[0].args.get("desc") is True

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "FULLTEXT INDEX body_idx (body DESC)" in generated


def test_postgres_create_index_preserves_nondefault_null_ordering():
    # These are non-default PostgreSQL null-ordering choices, so a generator
    # cannot safely omit them while preserving the index ordering semantics.
    sql = "CREATE INDEX idx_ordered ON foo (a DESC NULLS LAST, b ASC NULLS FIRST)"

    expression = parse_one(sql, dialect="postgres")
    columns = list(expression.find_all(exp.Ordered))

    assert len(columns) == 2
    assert [column.this.name for column in columns] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [True, False]
    assert [column.args.get("nulls_first") for column in columns] == [False, True]

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "a DESC NULLS LAST" in generated
    assert "b ASC NULLS FIRST" in generated
    assert " AS DESC" not in generated
    assert " AS ASC" not in generated

    reparsed_columns = list(parse_one(generated, dialect="postgres").find_all(exp.Ordered))
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == [True, False]
    assert [column.args.get("nulls_first") for column in reparsed_columns] == [False, True]

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import Mock

from aiosmtpd.smtp import SMTP


class BlockingRcptHandler:
    def __init__(self, loop):
        self.loop = loop
        self.rcpt_started = loop.create_future()
        self.cancelled = False

    async def handle_RCPT(self, server, session, envelope, address, rcpt_options):
        self.rcpt_started.set_result(None)
        try:
            await self.loop.create_future()
        finally:
            self.cancelled = True


def test_eof_during_rcpt_cancels_session_without_processing_buffered_commands():
    """An EOF while a command hook is running must terminate the session.

    In particular, commands which the client already pipelined after RCPT must
    not be interpreted after the hook is cancelled, since EOF otherwise makes
    readline() repeatedly return an empty byte string and causes an endless
    stream of ``500 Error: bad syntax`` responses.
    """
    try:
        old_loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        old_loop = None

    loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
    asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)
    protocol = None

    try:
        handler = BlockingRcptHandler(loop)
        writes = []

        transport = Mock()
        transport.get_extra_info.return_value = ("127.0.0.1", 12345)
        transport.is_closing.return_value = False
        transport.write.side_effect = writes.append

        protocol = SMTP(handler, loop=loop)
        protocol.connection_made(transport)

        # Simulate netcat-like input: the client sends an entire SMTP session,
        # including DATA, then closes without waiting for the slow RCPT hook.
        protocol.data_received(
            b"HELO client.example\r\n"
            b"MAIL FROM:<sender@example.com>\r\n"
            b"RCPT TO:<recipient@example.com>\r\n"
            b"DATA\r\n"
            b"message body\r\n"
            b".\r\n"
        )

        loop.run_until_complete(asyncio.wait_for(handler.rcpt_started, 1))

        # EOF must cancel the command currently being processed.
        protocol.eof_received()
        loop.run_until_complete(
            asyncio.wait_for(protocol._handler_coroutine, 1)
        )

        assert handler.cancelled
        assert protocol._handler_coroutine.done()
        assert not protocol._handler_coroutine.cancelled()
        assert protocol.transport is None
        transport.close.assert_called()

        # Only greeting, HELO, and MAIL replies may have been generated.
        # In particular, the buffered DATA lines must not turn into an
        # unbounded sequence of bad-syntax replies after EOF.
        assert not any(b"500 Error: bad syntax" in reply for reply in writes)
        assert len(writes) == 3
    finally:
        if protocol is not None:
            task = protocol._handler_coroutine
            if task is not None and not task.done():
                task.cancel()
                loop.run_until_complete(
                    asyncio.gather(task, return_exceptions=True)
                )
        loop.close()
        asyncio.set_event_loop(old_loop)

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from pre_commit.meta_hooks.check_useless_excludes import check_useless_excludes


def _make_repo_with_deinitialized_submodule_link(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    subprocess.run(
        ('git', 'init', '-q'),
        cwd=tmp_path,
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    )

    link = tmp_path / 'link_to_submodule'
    # This is the state left after cloning without --recursive or after
    # deinitializing a submodule: the link itself is tracked, but its target
    # below the submodule directory is absent.
    os.symlink('submodule/some_file.txt', link)
    subprocess.run(
        ('git', 'add', 'link_to_submodule'),
        cwd=tmp_path,
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    )

    assert link.is_symlink()
    assert not link.exists()

    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return link


def test_check_useless_excludes_accepts_exclude_for_broken_submodule_symlink(
        tmp_path,
        monkeypatch,
        capsys,
):
    _make_repo_with_deinitialized_submodule_link(tmp_path, monkeypatch)

    config = Path('.pre-commit-config.yaml')
    config.write_text(
        '''\
repos:
-   repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.0.1
    hooks:
    -   id: check-symlinks
        exclude: ^link_to_submodule$
-   repo: meta
    hooks:
    -   id: check-useless-excludes
''',
    )

    assert check_useless_excludes(str(config)) == 0
    assert 'does not match any files' not in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_check_useless_excludes_still_honors_hook_file_patterns(
        tmp_path,
        monkeypatch,
        capsys,
):
    _make_repo_with_deinitialized_submodule_link(tmp_path, monkeypatch)

    config = Path('.pre-commit-config.yaml')
    config.write_text(
        '''\
repos:
-   repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.0.1
    hooks:
    -   id: check-symlinks
        files: ^a_different_file$
        exclude: ^link_to_submodule$
''',
    )

    assert check_useless_excludes(str(config)) == 1
    assert (
        "The exclude pattern '^link_to_submodule$' for check-symlinks "
        'does not match any files'
    ) in capsys.readouterr().out

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_constraint(expression):
    constraint = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None
    return constraint


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "columns, expected_desc",
    [
        ("a ASC", [False]),
        ("a DESC", [True]),
        ("a ASC, b DESC, c", [False, True, None]),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_named_index_accepts_and_round_trips_column_directions(columns, expected_desc):
    expression = parse_one(
        f"CREATE TABLE foo (a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c INT, KEY idx ({columns}))",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    index_columns = _index_constraint(expression).args["schema"].expressions

    assert len(index_columns) == len(expected_desc)
    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in index_columns)
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in index_columns] == expected_desc

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert generated == f"CREATE TABLE foo (a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c INT, INDEX idx ({columns}))"

    reparsed = parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")
    reparsed_columns = _index_constraint(reparsed).args["schema"].expressions
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in reparsed_columns] == expected_desc


def test_mysql_ordered_index_columns_support_prefix_lengths():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a VARCHAR(255), b VARCHAR(255), "
        "KEY idx_prefix (a(10) DESC, b(5) ASC)"
        ")",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    columns = _index_constraint(expression).args["schema"].expressions

    assert len(columns) == 2
    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in columns)
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in columns] == [True, False]
    assert all(isinstance(column.this, exp.ColumnPrefix) for column in columns)
    assert [column.this.expression.this for column in columns] == ["10", "5"]

    generated = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert generated == (
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a VARCHAR(255), b VARCHAR(255), "
        "INDEX idx_prefix (a(10) DESC, b(5) ASC))"
    )
    parse_one(generated, dialect="mysql")


def test_mysql_ordered_index_columns_work_with_index_type_and_options():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a INT, b INT, "
        "KEY idx USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC) "
        "COMMENT 'ordered index' VISIBLE"
        ")",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    constraint = _index_constraint(expression)
    assert constraint.args["index_type"] == "BTREE"
    assert [column.args.get("desc") for column in constraint.args["schema"].expressions] == [
        True,
        False,
    ]

    assert expression.sql(dialect="mysql") == (
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a INT, b INT, INDEX idx USING BTREE "
        "(a DESC, b ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index' VISIBLE)"
    )

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_constraint(expression):
    constraint = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None
    return constraint


def test_mysql_index_desc_parses_as_ordered_column_and_round_trips():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), KEY idx_a (a DESC))",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    columns = _index_constraint(expression).args["schema"].expressions

    assert len(columns) == 1
    assert isinstance(columns[0], exp.Ordered)
    assert columns[0].this.name == "a"
    assert columns[0].args["desc"] is True

    sql = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert sql == "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), INDEX idx_a (a DESC))"
    assert "AS DESC" not in sql

    reparsed = parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql")
    reparsed_column = _index_constraint(reparsed).args["schema"].expressions[0]
    assert isinstance(reparsed_column, exp.Ordered)
    assert reparsed_column.this.name == "a"
    assert reparsed_column.args["desc"] is True


def test_mysql_composite_index_preserves_each_asc_desc_qualifier():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c INT, KEY idx_abc (a, b ASC, c DESC))",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    columns = _index_constraint(expression).args["schema"].expressions

    assert len(columns) == 3
    assert all(isinstance(column, exp.Ordered) for column in columns)
    assert [column.this.name for column in columns] == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert [column.args["desc"] for column in columns] == [False, False, True]

    assert expression.sql(dialect="mysql") == (
        "CREATE TABLE foo (a VARCHAR(10), b INT, c INT, INDEX idx_abc (a, b ASC, c DESC))"
    )


def test_mysql_ordered_index_columns_support_prefix_lengths_and_index_type():
    # MySQL index columns may combine a prefix length and a direction qualifier.
    expression = parse_one(

import os
import subprocess

import pytest

from pre_commit.meta_hooks import check_useless_excludes
from testing.fixtures import add_config_to_repo


def _add_broken_submodule_symlink(in_git_dir, name='broken-submodule-link'):
    """Add a tracked symlink whose target disappears like a deinitialized module."""
    root = in_git_dir.strpath
    submodule_dir = os.path.join(root, 'submodule')
    target = os.path.join(submodule_dir, 'file.txt')
    link = os.path.join(root, name)

    os.mkdir(submodule_dir)
    with open(target, 'w') as f:
        f.write('contents\n')

    try:
        os.symlink('submodule/file.txt', link)
    except OSError:
        pytest.skip('symlinks are not supported on this platform')

    subprocess.check_call(('git', 'add', name), cwd=root)

    # Simulate cloning without --recursive / deinitializing the submodule.
    os.unlink(target)
    os.rmdir(submodule_dir)

    assert os.path.lexists(link)
    assert not os.path.exists(link)


def _check_symlinks_config(**hook_options):
    hook = {'id': 'check-symlinks'}
    hook.update(hook_options)
    return {
        'repos': [
            {
                'repo': 'https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks',
                'rev': 'v4.0.1',
                'hooks': [hook],
            },
        ],
    }


def test_broken_symlink_exclude_for_check_symlinks_is_not_useless(
        capsys,
        in_git_dir,
):
    _add_broken_submodule_symlink(in_git_dir)
    add_config_to_repo(
        in_git_dir.strpath,
        _check_symlinks_config(exclude='^broken-submodule-link$'),
    )

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ''


def test_broken_symlink_exclude_is_useless_when_explicit_types_cannot_match_it(
        capsys,
        in_git_dir,
):
    _add_broken_submodule_symlink(in_git_dir)
    add_config_to_repo(
        in_git_dir.strpath,
        _check_symlinks_config(
            exclude='^broken-submodule-link$',
            types=['python'],
        ),
    )

    assert check_useless_excludes.main(()) == 1
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == (
        "The exclude pattern '^broken-submodule-link$' for check-symlinks "
        'does not match any files'
    )


def test_broken_symlink_exclude_is_useless_when_files_pattern_cannot_match_it(
        capsys,
        in_git_dir,
):
    _add_broken_submodule_symlink(in_git_dir)

            exclude='^broken-submodule-link$',
        ),
    )

        "The exclude pattern '^broken-submodule-link$' for check-symlinks "
        'does not match any files'
    )

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_parts(expression):
    constraint = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None

    schema = constraint.args["schema"]
    assert schema is not None

    return schema.expressions


def test_mysql_create_table_index_asc_desc_round_trips():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` (a VARCHAR(10), b INT, KEY idx_ab (a DESC, b ASC))",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    parts = _index_parts(expression)

    assert len(parts) == 2
    assert all(isinstance(part, exp.Ordered) for part in parts)

    assert parts[0].this.name == "a"
    assert parts[0].args["desc"] is True

    assert parts[1].this.name == "b"
    assert parts[1].args["desc"] is False

    sql = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "INDEX idx_ab (a DESC, b ASC)" in sql

    reparsed_parts = _index_parts(parse_one(sql, dialect="mysql"))
    assert [part.this.name for part in reparsed_parts] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [part.args["desc"] for part in reparsed_parts] == [True, False]


def test_mysql_ordered_index_columns_work_with_index_options():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a VARCHAR(10), "
        "b INT, "
        "INDEX idx_ab USING BTREE (a ASC, b DESC) COMMENT 'ordered index' VISIBLE"
        ")",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    parts = _index_parts(expression)

    assert [part.this.name for part in parts] == ["a", "b"]
    assert [part.args["desc"] for part in parts] == [False, True]

    sql = expression.sql(dialect="mysql")
    assert "INDEX idx_ab USING BTREE (a ASC, b DESC)" in sql
    assert "COMMENT 'ordered index'" in sql
    assert "VISIBLE" in sql


def test_postgres_create_index_preserves_order_and_explicit_null_ordering():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE INDEX idx_ab ON foo (a DESC NULLS LAST, b ASC NULLS FIRST)",
        dialect="postgres",
    )

    ordered = list(expression.find_all(exp.Ordered))

    assert len(ordered) == 2
    assert ordered[0].this.name == "a"
    assert ordered[0].args["desc"] is True
    assert ordered[0].args["nulls_first"] is False

    assert ordered[1].this.name == "b"
    assert ordered[1].args["desc"] is False
    assert ordered[1].args["nulls_first"] is True

    sql = expression.sql(dialect="postgres")
    assert "a DESC NULLS LAST" in sql
    assert "b ASC NULLS FIRST" in sql

    reparsed = parse_one(sql, dialect="postgres")
    reparsed_ordered = list(reparsed.find_all(exp.Ordered))

    assert [
        (part.this.name, part.args["desc"], part.args["nulls_first"])
        for part in reparsed_ordered
    ] == [
        ("a", True, False),
        ("b", False, True),
    ]

import pytest

from sqlglot import exp, parse_one


def _index_constraint(expression):
    constraint = expression.find(exp.IndexColumnConstraint)
    assert constraint is not None
    assert isinstance(constraint.args.get("schema"), exp.Schema)
    return constraint


def _index_orders(expression):
    orders = _index_constraint(expression).args["schema"].expressions
    assert all(isinstance(order, exp.Ordered) for order in orders)
    return orders


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "columns, expected_desc",
    [
        ("a DESC", [True]),
        ("a ASC", [False]),
        ("a ASC, b DESC, c ASC", [False, True, False]),
    ],
)
def test_mysql_create_table_index_ordering_round_trips(columns, expected_desc):
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE `foo` ("
        "a VARCHAR(10), "
        "b INT, "
        "c INT, "
        f"KEY idx_a ({columns})"
        ")",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    assert [order.args.get("desc") for order in _index_orders(expression)] == expected_desc

    # Direction qualifiers must remain valid after AST -> SQL generation.
    reparsed = parse_one(expression.sql(dialect="mysql"), dialect="mysql")
    assert [order.args.get("desc") for order in _index_orders(reparsed)] == expected_desc


def test_mysql_descending_index_keeps_existing_prefix_length_syntax():
    # MySQL key parts allow a prefix length and an order direction together.
    # Adding ASC/DESC parsing must not regress the pre-existing key-part form.
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a VARCHAR(20), "
        "b INT, "
        "KEY idx_prefix (a(10) DESC, b ASC)"
        ")",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    first, second = _index_orders(expression)

    assert first.args.get("desc") is True
    assert isinstance(first.this, exp.ColumnPrefix)
    assert first.this.this.name == "a"
    assert first.this.expression.this == "10"

    assert second.args.get("desc") is False
    assert second.this.name == "b"

    reparsed_first, reparsed_second = _index_orders(
        parse_one(expression.sql(dialect="mysql"), dialect="mysql")
    )
    assert reparsed_first.args.get("desc") is True
    assert isinstance(reparsed_first.this, exp.ColumnPrefix)
    assert reparsed_first.this.this.name == "a"
    assert reparsed_first.this.expression.this == "10"
    assert reparsed_second.args.get("desc") is False


def test_mysql_index_ordering_coexists_with_type_and_options():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE TABLE foo ("
        "a INT, "
        "b INT, "
        "KEY idx_ordered USING BTREE (a DESC, b ASC) COMMENT 'ordered index' VISIBLE"
        ")",
        dialect="mysql",
    )

    constraint = _index_constraint(expression)

    assert constraint.args.get("index_type") == "BTREE"
    assert [order.args.get("desc") for order in _index_orders(expression)] == [True, False]

    options = constraint.args.get("options")
    assert len(options) == 2
    assert options[0].args.get("comment").this == "ordered index"
    assert options[1].args.get("visible") is True

    reparsed = parse_one(expression.sql(dialect="mysql"), dialect="mysql")
    reparsed_constraint = _index_constraint(reparsed)
    assert reparsed_constraint.args.get("index_type") == "BTREE"
    assert [order.args.get("desc") for order in _index_orders(reparsed)] == [True, False]


def test_postgres_create_index_preserves_order_and_null_ordering():
    expression = parse_one(
        "CREATE INDEX idx_ordered ON foo (a DESC NULLS FIRST, b ASC NULLS LAST)",
        dialect="postgres",
    )

    orders = list(expression.find_all(exp.Ordered))
    assert len(orders) == 2
    assert [order.args.get("desc") for order in orders] == [True, False]
    assert [order.args.get("nulls_first") for order in orders] == [True, False]

    reparsed = parse_one(expression.sql(dialect="postgres"), dialect="postgres")
    reparsed_orders = list(reparsed.find_all(exp.Ordered))
    assert [order.args.get("desc") for order in reparsed_orders] == [True, False]
    assert [order.args.get("nulls_first") for order in reparsed_orders] == [True, False]

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from pre_commit.meta_hooks.check_useless_excludes import check_useless_excludes


CONFIG = """\
repos:
- repo: local
  hooks:
  - id: check-symlinks
    name: check symlinks
    entry: check-symlinks
    language: system
    types: [symlink]
    exclude: ^link-into-submodule$
"""


def _git(cwd: Path, *args: str) -> None:
    subprocess.check_call(('git', *args), cwd=cwd)


@pytest.fixture
def git_repo(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    _git(tmp_path, 'init')
    _git(tmp_path, 'config', 'user.email', 'tester@example.com')
    _git(tmp_path, 'config', 'user.name', 'Tester')
    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
    return tmp_path


def test_useless_exclude_accepts_broken_symlink_to_uninitialized_submodule(
        git_repo: Path,
        capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str],
) -> None:
    """A symlink remains relevant to check-symlinks after its target vanishes.

    This is the state a checkout has when a submodule was not initialized.
    identify must still classify the dangling link as a symlink, allowing the
    hook-level exclude to be recognized as useful.
    """
    submodule_path = git_repo / 'submodule'
    submodule_path.mkdir()
    (submodule_path / 'target').write_text('contents')
    os.symlink('submodule/target', git_repo / 'link-into-submodule')

    _git(git_repo, 'add', 'link-into-submodule')
    _git(git_repo, 'commit', '-m', 'add symlink')

    # Simulate an uninitialized / deinitialized submodule after the link has
    # been committed: the link itself remains tracked, but is now dangling.
    (submodule_path / 'target').unlink()
    submodule_path.rmdir()

    config = git_repo / '.pre-commit-config.yaml'
    config.write_text(CONFIG)

    assert check_useless_excludes(str(config)) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out == ""

import threading

import anyio
import pytest

from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse


class TransparentMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
        return await call_next(request)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("sync_task", [False, True])
def test_background_task_does_not_keep_base_http_middleware_request_open(sync_task):
    """
    A completed HTTP response must release BaseHTTPMiddleware's request scope,
    even when its background task is still running.

    This models consecutive requests over a keep-alive connection: servers
    cannot start handling the next request until the previous ASGI application
    call has returned.
    """

    async def exercise():
        app = Starlette()
        app.add_middleware(TransparentMiddleware)

        release_background_work = threading.Event()
        task_started = []
        task_finished = []
        request_count = 0

        async def async_work(started, finished):
            started.set()
            while not release_background_work.is_set():
                await anyio.sleep(0.001)
            finished.set()

        def sync_work(started, finished):
            started.set()
            release_background_work.wait()
            finished.set()

        @app.route("/")
        async def endpoint(request):
            nonlocal request_count
            request_count += 1

            started = threading.Event()
            finished = threading.Event()
            task_started.append(started)
            task_finished.append(finished)

            return PlainTextResponse(
                "response-{}".format(request_count),
                background=BackgroundTask(
                    sync_work if sync_task else async_work,
                    started,
                    finished,
                ),
            )

        async def wait_for_thread_event(event):
            while not event.is_set():
                await anyio.sleep(0.001)

        async def run_request(result):
            received_request = False
            response_complete = anyio.Event()
            messages = result["messages"]

            async def receive():

        await release_async.wait()

            release_sync.wait()

            "server": ("testserver", 80),

            messages.append(message)
            if (

                and not message.get("more_body", False)
            ):
                response_finished.set()

        await app(make_scope(), receive, send)

    second_response_finished = anyio.Event()

import threading

import anyio
import pytest

from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.background import BackgroundTask
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.responses import PlainTextResponse


class TransparentMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
        return await call_next(request)


def _http_scope(path="/"):
    return {
        "type": "http",
        "asgi": {"version": "3.0"},
        "http_version": "1.1",
        "method": "GET",
        "scheme": "http",
        "path": path,
        "raw_path": path.encode("ascii"),
        "query_string": b"",
        "headers": [],
        "client": ("testclient", 50000),
        "server": ("testserver", 80),
    }


async def _receive():
    return {"type": "http.request", "body": b"", "more_body": False}


async def _wait_for_threading_event(event):
    while not event.is_set():
        await anyio.sleep(0.001)


@pytest.mark.anyio
@pytest.mark.parametrize("background_kind", ["async", "sync"])
async def test_background_task_does_not_prevent_following_request_with_base_http_middleware(
    background_kind,
):
    """
    Once a response has been sent, a long-running background task must not stop
    another request from being processed by an application using
    BaseHTTPMiddleware. The task must still be allowed to complete rather than
    being cancelled by the middleware's internal task group.
    """

    background_started = threading.Event()
    release_background_tasks = threading.Event()
    background_completed = []
    first_response_sent = anyio.Event()
    second_response_sent = anyio.Event()

    async def async_background_task():
        background_started.set()
        await _wait_for_threading_event(release_background_tasks)
        background_completed.append("async")

    def sync_background_task():
        background_started.set()
        release_background_tasks.wait()
        background_completed.append("sync")

    background_task = (
        async_background_task
        if background_kind == "async"
        else sync_background_task
    )

    async def endpoint(request):
        return PlainTextResponse("ok", background=BackgroundTask(background_task))

    app = Starlette()
    app.add_middleware(TransparentMiddleware)
    app.add_route("/", endpoint)

    async def send_first(message):
        if (
            message["type"] == "http.response.body"
            and not message.get("more_body", False)
        ):
            first_response_sent.set()

    async def send_second(message):
        if (
            message["type"] == "http.response.body"
            and not message.get("more_body", False)
        ):
            second_response_sent.set()

    async with anyio.create_task_group() as task_group:
        task_group.start_soon(app, _http_scope(), _receive, send_first)

        with anyio.fail_after(1):
            await first_response_sent.wait()
            await _wait_for_threading_event(background_started)

        # Keep the first task running while a second request is handled. Before
        # the fix, middleware could either cancel the background task or make
        # later request handling wait for it.
        task_group.start_soon(app, _http_scope(), _receive, send_second)
        with anyio.fail_after(1):
            await second_response_sent.wait()

        release_background_tasks.set()

    assert background_completed == [background_kind, background_kind]

async def test_base_http_middleware_cancels_an_abandoned_downstream_response():
    """
    Middleware is allowed to replace a response returned by call_next(). In
    that case the downstream streaming response is abandoned and must be
    cancelled; otherwise BaseHTTPMiddleware can hang forever waiting for an
    unread memory stream.

    class ReplacingMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
        async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
            await call_next(request)
            return PlainTextResponse("replacement")

    async def endpoint(request):
        return PlainTextResponse("original")

    app = Starlette()
    app.add_middleware(ReplacingMiddleware)
    app.add_route("/", endpoint)

        "type": "http.response.body",

import pytest

from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders


def test_mutable_headers_ior_merges_dict_in_place_and_normalizes_keys():
    headers = MutableHeaders({"Content-Type": "text/plain"})
    alias = headers

    headers |= {
        "X-Request-ID": "abc123",
        "CACHE-Control": "no-cache",
    }

    assert headers is alias
    assert headers["content-type"] == "text/plain"
    assert headers["x-request-id"] == "abc123"
    assert headers["cache-control"] == "no-cache"
    assert headers.items() == [
        ("content-type", "text/plain"),
        ("x-request-id", "abc123"),
        ("cache-control", "no-cache"),
    ]


def test_mutable_headers_ior_replaces_existing_headers_case_insensitively():
    headers = MutableHeaders(
        raw=[
            (b"x-token", b"old"),
            (b"other", b"preserved"),
            (b"x-token", b"duplicate"),
        ]
    )

    headers |= {"X-Token": "new"}

    assert headers["x-token"] == "new"
    assert headers.getlist("X-TOKEN") == ["new"]
    assert headers.raw == [
        (b"x-token", b"new"),
        (b"other", b"preserved"),
    ]


def test_mutable_headers_ior_has_same_result_as_update_for_a_dict():
    values = {"X-One": "1", "x-two": "2", "X-ONE": "replacement"}

    expected = MutableHeaders({"Existing": "value"})
    expected.update(values)

    actual = MutableHeaders({"Existing": "value"})
    actual |= values

    assert actual.items() == expected.items()
    assert actual.raw == expected.raw


def test_mutable_headers_ior_accepts_an_empty_dict_without_changing_headers():
    headers = MutableHeaders(raw=[(b"x-header", b"value")])
    original_raw = headers.raw[:]

    headers |= {}

    assert headers.raw == original_raw
